questionEn: From which two orphan brothers of Banu al-Najjar did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ purchase the plot of land for Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: When Al-Qaswa knelt in their date-drying yard (mirbad), the orphans Sahl and Suhayl offered it as a gift, but the Prophet ﷺ insisted on paying its fair price.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Which companion paid the ten gold dinars required to purchase the land for Al-Masjid an-Nabawi from Sahl and Suhayl?
explanationEn: At the Prophet's ﷺ instruction, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) paid the ten dinars for the plot before construction began.

questionEn: Whose graves were respectfully exhumed and relocated before the foundation of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was laid?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ ordered the pre-Islamic graves of polytheists on the plot to be exhumed, the ruins leveled, and the palm trees cut and aligned toward the Qiblah.

questionEn: What material formed the structural columns inside the original Al-Masjid an-Nabawi built in 1 AH?
explanationEn: The early mosque was built with remarkable simplicity using mud-brick walls, date-palm trunks as columns, and palm fronds (jarid) for the roof.

questionEn: What material did the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions lay beneath the mud-brick walls as the base foundation of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: The foundation of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was built with stone up to about three cubits high before sun-dried mud bricks (labin) were laid atop it.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: How was the roof of the original Al-Masjid an-Nabawi constructed in the first year of Hijrah?
optionsEn: Date-palm fronds coated lightly with clay
explanationEn: The roof consisted of palm branches and fronds (jarid) so light that rainwater sometimes dripped into the prayer hall until later reinforced.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: Which direction did the original Qiblah wall of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi face during the first 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah?
explanationEn: Muslims initially prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis in the north until Allah commanded the Qiblah shift toward the Sacred Mosque in Makkah in 2 AH.

questionEn: How many doors were built into the original mud-brick enclosure of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: The original mosque had three doors: Bab al-Rahmah (Bab Atikah) on the west, Bab Jibril on the east, and a rear door that was moved to the north when the Qiblah changed.

questionEn: What did the Companions do when rain turned the dirt floor of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi into mud during prostration?
optionsEn: They spread small pebbles over the ground
They paved it with marble slabs
explanationEn: After a rainy night left mud on the Prophet's ﷺ forehead, the Companions began spreading small pebbles (hasba) across the floor to keep it clean and firm.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Night Prayer

questionEn: According to an authentic Hadith, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is one of how many mosques to which a Muslim may intentionally undertake a religious journey?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Do not set out on a journey except to three mosques: Al-Masjid al-Haram, this mosque of mine (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi), and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: Which two mosques have a higher prayer reward than Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, or equal/higher status in Hadith?
optionsEn: Only Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah exceeds its 1,000x reward
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ affirmed that one prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is better than 1,000 prayers elsewhere, except Al-Masjid al-Haram where one prayer equals 100,000.

questionEn: After which major expedition in 7 AH did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ carry out the first expansion of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: As the Muslim community grew after Khaybar in 7 AH, the Prophet ﷺ expanded the mosque, doubling its width and extending its length to roughly 100 by 100 cubits.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: Who financed the purchase of the adjacent plot needed for the Prophet's ﷺ expansion of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi after Khaybar?
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ asked who would buy the neighboring plot for a house in Paradise, Uthman ibn Affan (RA) purchased it and donated it to expand the mosque.

questionEn: Which verses were Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Companions reciting together while carrying bricks to build Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Poetic supplications asking Allah to forgive the Ansar and Muhajirun
Silent reflection with no spoken words
explanationEn: While hauling bricks, the Prophet ﷺ joined them in reciting: 'O Allah, there is no true life except the life of the Hereafter; so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirah.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Which companion had his house demolished (with compensation) or moved during Umar ibn al-Khattab's expansion of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: During Umar's (RA) 17 AH expansion, Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) generously donated his adjacent home to allow the mosque to grow.

questionEn: In which direction did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) deliberately refrain from expanding Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 17 AH?
optionsEn: The northern side toward Mount Uhud
The eastern side, out of respect for the apartments of the Mothers of the Believers
explanationEn: Umar (RA) expanded the mosque south, west, and north, leaving the eastern flank untouched because the rooms of the Prophet's ﷺ wives stood there.

questionEn: How did Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) upgrade the building materials of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 29-30 AH?
optionsEn: With fired blue glazed tiles from Persia
With carved stone walls, plaster, and a teakwood (saj) roof
With granite domes and brass pillars
explanationEn: Uthman (RA) replaced the mud bricks and palm fronds with carved stone, lime plaster (jiss), stone columns reinforced with lead, and a durable teakwood roof.

questionEn: Under which Umayyad caliph and Madinah governor were the apartments of the Prophet's ﷺ wives first incorporated inside the expanded mosque walls?
optionsEn: Caliph Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik and Governor Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
explanationEn: Between 88 and 91 AH, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz oversaw Al-Walid's grand reconstruction, bringing the Sacred Chamber inside the mosque footprint and adding four minarets.

questionEn: How many minarets were first constructed at the four corners of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's reconstruction?
explanationEn: Prior to 88-91 AH, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi had no tall minarets; the Umayyad expansion introduced four corner minarets for the call to prayer.

questionEn: Which Abbasid caliph carried out a major northward expansion of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi between 161 and 165 AH?
explanationEn: Caliph Al-Mahdi added ten columns' length to the northern side of the Prophet's Mosque while preserving its historic southern and eastern bounds.

questionEn: What devastating event struck Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 654 AH (1256 CE), destroying its wooden roof and historic Minbar?
optionsEn: A flash flood from Wadi al-Aqiq
A massive fire sparked by a lamp in the storeroom
An earthquake centered in Mount Uhud
explanationEn: In Ramadan 654 AH, a lamp accidentally ignited the storeroom curtains, burning the roof and the original Prophetic Minbar before Mamluk rulers rebuilt the mosque.

questionEn: What natural disaster struck Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 886 AH (1481 CE), prompting Sultan Qaitbay to rebuild the roof and dome in stone?
optionsEn: A sandstorm collapsing the northern colonnade
A locust plague destroying the timber
A volcanic tremor in Harrat Rahat
Lightning striking the southeastern minaret and igniting a fire
explanationEn: Lightning struck the main minaret near the Sacred Chamber in Ramadan 886 AH; Sultan al-Ashraf Qaitbay then sponsored a durable stone restoration.

questionEn: Which Ottoman Sultan commissioned the major 19th-century reconstruction (1849-1861 CE) marked by red stone columns and domes inscribed with calligraphy?
explanationEn: Sultan Abdulmecid I rebuilt most of the Ottoman prayer hall using reddish stone from Jabal al-Jamma and adorned the domes with Qur'anic and poetic calligraphy.

questionEn: In the modern Saudi expansions of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, what distinctive architectural feature sits in the inner courtyards to allow natural daylight and ventilation?
explanationEn: Twenty-seven motorized sliding domes cover the inner courtyards and open smoothly along tracks to circulate fresh air and natural light.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Which gate of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi stands on the western side and traditionally serves as the entrance walkway leading past the Sacred Chamber?
explanationEn: Visitors traditionally enter calmly through Bab al-Salam on the western flank, walk parallel to the Qiblah wall, offer salam at the Sacred Chamber, and exit toward Bab al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which eastern gate of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi opens directly toward the historic cemetery of Madinah?
explanationEn: Bab al-Baqi opens on the eastern side of the mosque right beside the courtyard leading to Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which historic eastern gate of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is named after the angel who brought revelation and visited the Prophet ﷺ there?
explanationEn: Bab Jibril is one of the earliest gates on the eastern wall, located north of the Sacred Chamber where Jibril (AS) visited the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Which gate on the eastern side of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was historically designated for women's entry by Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) dedicated a specific northern-eastern door—Bab al-Nisa—so women could enter and exit the mosque comfortably without crowding.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: What is the historical name of the gate on the western wall of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi also known in early sources as Bab Atikah?
explanationEn: Bab al-Rahmah (Gate of Mercy), located on the western side of the original mosque, was one of the three original doors and sat near the house of Atikah bint Abd al-Muttalib.

questionEn: What blessing did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Allah for Madinah in comparison to Makkah in Sahih al-Bukhari?
optionsEn: Three times the gold of Syria
Twice the blessing (barakah) that Ibrahim (AS) prayed for Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ supplicated: 'O Allah, place in Madinah twice the blessing that You placed in Makkah.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise for someone who enters Al-Masjid an-Nabawi solely to learn or teach goodness?
optionsEn: The reward of a warrior striving in Allah's path (mujahid)
The reward of building ten mosques
The reward of fasting an entire year
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated that whoever comes to the Prophet's Mosque only to learn or teach good holds the rank of a mujahid in Allah's cause.

questionEn: What name did the Prophet ﷺ give to the person who used to sweep and care for Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, for whom he later prayed the funeral prayer at her grave?
optionsEn: Umm Mihjan (a black woman who swept the mosque)
explanationEn: When Umm Mihjan passed away and was buried at night without informing the Prophet ﷺ, he rebuked the Companions for not telling him and went to her grave to offer Janazah prayer.

questionEn: Which tribal leader from Najd was tied to one of the pillars of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi as a captive and embraced Islam after observing the mosque's worship and the Prophet's ﷺ kindness?
explanationEn: Captured and bound to a pillar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for three days, Thumamah watched the Muslims' devotion and the Prophet's ﷺ mercy, then accepted Islam and bathed at a nearby well.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Where in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did the Prophet ﷺ permit the Abyssinian companions to display their spear-play on Eid day?
optionsEn: Inside the courtyard/hall of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
On the roof of the Sacred Chamber
explanationEn: While Aishah (RA) watched from behind the Prophet's ﷺ shoulder, Abyssinian companions performed lawful spear-play in the mosque on Eid, showing joy within Islamic bounds.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Two Eids

questionEn: Which companion was temporarily given a tent inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi so the Prophet ﷺ could visit and tend to his wounds after the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) was wounded in the arm artery at Khandaq, the Prophet ﷺ pitched a tent for him in the mosque beside Rufaydah's medical tent so he could visit him closely.

questionEn: Who was the female companion who set up a nursing tent inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to treat wounded Muslim soldiers?
explanationEn: Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah (RA) cared for wounded companions such as Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in her medical tent within the mosque courtyard.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when a man stood up calling out loudly about a lost red camel?
optionsEn: Announcing lost property or buying and selling inside the mosque
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that mosques are built for the remembrance of Allah and prayer, saying to one announcing a lost camel: 'May Allah not return it to you!'

questionEn: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) tell two men from Taif who raised their voices inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Only poetry is allowed to be spoken loudly
You may speak as loudly as you wish outside Fajr
Had you been residents of Madinah, I would have disciplined you for raising your voices in the Prophet's Mosque
You must leave Madinah before sunset
explanationEn: Umar (RA) upheld the sanctity of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, reminding visitors never to raise their voices near the Prophet's ﷺ mosque.

questionEn: Which companion had his house door—like all others opening directly into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—ordered closed near the end of the Prophet's ﷺ life, except for one specific door?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan's door remained open
Umar ibn al-Khattab's door remained open
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq's (RA) door remained open while all other private doors were closed
explanationEn: During his final illness, the Prophet ﷺ commanded that every small private door opening directly into the mosque be closed except Abu Bakr's (RA) door.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Companions of the Prophet

questionEn: What color are the carpets inside Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah today, distinguishing it visually from the red carpets of the rest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah is carpeted in green, helping visitors identify the blessed boundary between the Sacred Chamber and the Minbar.

questionEn: Approximately how wide (east to west) is the historic area of Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah between the Sacred Chamber and the Minbar?
explanationEn: Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah measures roughly 22 meters from east (the Sacred Chamber) to west (the Minbar) and about 15 meters from north to south (~330 square meters).

questionEn: What does the word 'Al-Rawdah' literally mean in Arabic?
optionsEn: A lush garden or verdant meadow
explanationEn: Al-Rawdah means a flourishing garden; the Prophet ﷺ called the area between his house and his pulpit 'a garden from the gardens of Paradise' (rawdah min riyad al-jannah).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: Which historic pillar inside Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah is known as 'Ustuwana al-Mukhalliqah' (the Perfumed Pillar)?
optionsEn: The northernmost pillar near Bab al-Nisa
The pillar at the entrance of Jannat al-Baqi
The outer courtyard pillar near Bab al-Salam
The pillar standing beside the Prophet's ﷺ Mihrab where the weeping palm trunk originally stood
explanationEn: Located next to Mihrab al-Nabawi, it marks the spot of the palm trunk where the Prophet ﷺ used to lean and pray; it was nicknamed al-Mukhalliqah after someone perfumed it with khaluq.

questionEn: Why was Ustuwana al-Mukhalliqah also called 'Ustuwana al-Hannana'?
optionsEn: Because the palm trunk that once stood there yearned and wept for the Prophet ﷺ
Because the Ansar stored honey beside it
Because birds nested at its capital
Because rainwater always collected at its base
explanationEn: Al-Hannana derives from hanin (yearning), commemorating the date-palm trunk that cried out when the Prophet ﷺ moved from it to the wooden Minbar.

questionEn: Which pillar in Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah did Salamah ibn al-Akwa' (RA) always strive to pray beside because he saw the Prophet ﷺ regularly pray there?
optionsEn: The pillar next to the Mushaf / Ustuwana al-Mukhalliqah
The eastern gate pillar of Bab Jibril
explanationEn: Salamah ibn al-Akwa' (RA) deliberately sought out the pillar near the Mushaf box (al-Mukhalliqah) because he observed the Prophet ﷺ praying there frequently.

questionEn: Which pillar in Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah is named after Aishah (RA) and is also known as 'Ustuwana al-Qur'ah' (Pillar of Drawing Lots)?
optionsEn: The third pillar from the Sacred Chamber / third from the Minbar
The first pillar of the Ottoman courtyard
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said there was a spot in his mosque so blessed that if people knew its worth they would cast lots (qur'ah) to pray there; she later indicated this pillar.

questionEn: What is another well-known name for Ustuwana Aishah (RA) because senior emigrants frequently gathered around it?
explanationEn: Senior Muhajirun companions such as Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ibn al-Zubayr often sat and prayed beside Ustuwana Aishah, earning it the name Ustuwana al-Muhajirin.

questionEn: Which companion stayed awake praying beside Ustuwana Aishah after Aishah (RA) discreetly pointed it out to him?
explanationEn: When Aishah (RA) whispered the location to her nephew Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA), he made it his cherished spot of prayer in Al-Rawdah.

questionEn: Which pillar inside Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah is known as 'Ustuwana al-Tawbah' (Pillar of Repentance)?
optionsEn: The pillar of Ka'b ibn Malik
The pillar of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah
The pillar of Thumamah ibn Uthal
The pillar of Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir (RA)
explanationEn: Positioned near the Sacred Chamber, this pillar commemorates Abu Lubabah (RA), who bound himself to it in remorse until Allah revealed his forgiveness.

questionEn: What regretful act led Abu Lubabah (RA) to tie himself to the Pillar of Repentance in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Making a hand gesture across his throat hinting at the fate awaiting Banu Qurayzah
Sleeping through the Fajr prayer before Badr
explanationEn: Sent as an advisor to Banu Qurayzah, Abu Lubabah (RA) pointed to his throat; realizing he had betrayed a trust of the Prophet ﷺ, he walked straight to the mosque and tied himself to a pillar.

questionEn: Who untied Abu Lubabah (RA) from the Pillar of Repentance after Surah At-Tawbah (9:102) confirmed Allah's acceptance of his repentance?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself after Fajr prayer
explanationEn: Even when his daughter freed him briefly for prayer and bodily needs, Abu Lubabah insisted that only the Prophet ﷺ untie him permanently, which he ﷺ did upon revelation of 9:102.

questionEn: Which pillar directly adjacent to the Sacred Chamber wall marks where the Prophet's ﷺ simple palm-fiber bed was placed during I'tikaf?
explanationEn: During his spiritual retreats (I'tikaf) in the last ten nights of Ramadan, a modest bed of palm fibers (sarir) was set beside this pillar near the wall of Aishah's (RA) room.

questionEn: Which pillar behind Ustuwana al-Tawbah is called 'Ustuwana al-Haras' (Pillar of the Guard) or 'Ustuwana Ali'?
optionsEn: The pillar where Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and other Companions stood guard over the Prophet's ﷺ chamber
The pillar guarding the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal)
The pillar at the entrance of Uhud
The pillar outside the western market
explanationEn: Companions, especially Ali (RA), kept night watch at this pillar until Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:67) revealed: 'And Allah will protect you from the people.'

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse prompted Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to step out of his chamber and tell his guards at Ustuwana al-Haras to go home?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:67 ('And Allah will protect you from the people')
explanationEn: Upon receiving 'Wallahu ya'simuka min al-nas' (5:67), the Prophet ﷺ put his head out and told the Companions guarding him to disperse because Allah had guaranteed his protection.

questionEn: Which pillar north of Ustuwana al-Haras along the line of the Sacred Chamber is called 'Ustuwana al-Wufud'?
optionsEn: The Pillar of Rain, used for Istisqa
The Pillar of Delegations, where the Prophet ﷺ met visiting tribal envoys
The Pillar of Fasting, marking Ramadan's crescent
The Pillar of Treaties, where Hudaybiyyah was signed
explanationEn: Especially during 9 AH (the Year of Delegations), Arab tribal representatives met the Prophet ﷺ by this pillar to learn Islam and pledge allegiance.

questionEn: Which historic pillar stands north of the Sacred Chamber behind the elevated platform known as Dikkah al-Tahajjud?
explanationEn: Ustuwana al-Tahajjud marks the spot behind the Sacred Chamber where the Prophet ﷺ sometimes spread his mat for late-night voluntary prayer (Tahajjud).

questionEn: What is 'Ustuwana Murabba'at al-Qabr' (also linked with Maqam Jibril) today?
optionsEn: A historic pillar enclosed within the walls/grille of the Sacred Chamber
A free-standing pillar in the northern outer piazza
A pillar relocated to Masjid Quba
The minaret base near Bab al-Salam
explanationEn: Located near the northern edge of the Prophet's ﷺ chamber where Jibril (AS) used to enter, it was enclosed inside the Sacred Chamber boundaries when the pentagonal wall was built.

questionEn: How are the historic pillars of Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah visually marked today for visitors inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: They are surrounded by wooden fences
Their Arabic names are inscribed in gold/calligraphy on marble plaques near their upper shafts
explanationEn: Each historic pillar inside the Ottoman section of Al-Rawdah bears a clear calligraphic plaque identifying its historic name, such as Ustuwana Aishah or Ustuwana al-Tawbah.

questionEn: What is the Islamic ruling on wiping, kissing, or seeking blessings directly from the physical stone or marble of the pillars in Al-Rawdah?
optionsEn: It is not from the Sunnah and should be avoided; the blessing lies in praying sincerely in Al-Rawdah
Only pilgrims from Madinah are required to kiss them
It grants the reward of an extra Hajj
It is an obligatory pillar of Ziyarah
explanationEn: Scholars of the Sunnah emphasize that pillars and grilles are not touched for tabarruk; visitors honor Al-Rawdah through humble prayer, dhikr, and following the Sunnah.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about the space between his house and his Minbar?
optionsEn: 'This carpet will remain until the Last Hour'
'Between my house and my pulpit is the center of the earth'
'Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise'
explanationEn: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA), this authentic Hadith establishes the exceptional spiritual rank of Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: Which companion's house wall formed the eastern boundary of Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah?
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ house mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Rawdah specifically refers to the apartment of Aishah (RA), where he passed away and was buried.

questionEn: How did scholars like Ibn Hajar explain the phrase 'a garden from the gardens of Paradise' regarding Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah?
optionsEn: Meaning physical fruits grow beneath its floor
Both spiritually—leading to Paradise through worship—and literally, as a blessed patch honored by Allah
Only as a metaphor for the date trees outside Madinah
Referring exclusively to the Day of Uhud
explanationEn: Classical commentators note that worship there guides believers to Paradise, and many scholars also affirm Allah may literally elevate this blessed spot in the Hereafter.

questionEn: Why did Al-Masjid an-Nabawi introduce regulated time-slot permits for entering Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah?
optionsEn: To charge visitors an entrance fee
To prevent dangerous crowding and enable serene, unhurried prayer in the compact 330-square-meter space
To reserve it solely for Friday prayers
Because only scholars are allowed inside
explanationEn: Because Al-Rawdah is small while millions visit Madinah yearly, organized permits ensure safety, dignity, and quiet worship for every guest.
reference: Ministry of Hajj & Umrah / Nusuk Guidelines

questionEn: What should a Muslim prioritize upon receiving a brief permitted time inside Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah?
optionsEn: Taking selfies and filming long video tours
Praying two calm rak'ahs (if not a prohibited time) and making sincere dua without pushing others
Remaining outside until the permit expires
Shoving to reach the exact same square meter
explanationEn: Quietly offering two rak'ahs of prayer and heartfelt supplication while respecting fellow worshippers preserves both the Sunnah and the serenity of Al-Rawdah.

questionEn: In early Madinah, who used to sit by Ustuwana al-Wufud to welcome incoming delegations and guide them to the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA) and senior Companions assigned to protocol
explanationEn: Companions such as Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA) stood guard or helped organize delegations near Ustuwana al-Wufud when tribes arrived to meet the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What happened to the weeping date-palm trunk after the Prophet ﷺ comforted it upon moving to the wooden Minbar?
optionsEn: It was thrown into Wadi al-Aqiq
He ﷺ embraced it until it quieted, and it was later buried beneath the Minbar area
explanationEn: After embracing the groaning trunk until it calmed like a soothed child, the Prophet ﷺ said it wept for missing the Dhikr it used to hear; it was buried beneath the spot.

questionEn: How did Hasan al-Basri respond with emotion whenever he narrated the Hadith of the weeping palm trunk in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: He ordered all wooden pulpits removed
He wept and said: 'O Muslims, a piece of wood yearned for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—you have more right to long for him!'
He refused to teach inside mosques
explanationEn: Hasan al-Basri's famous reflection reminds believers that hearts should feel even deeper love and longing for the Prophet ﷺ than a lifeless palm trunk.

questionEn: Before the wooden Minbar was crafted, how did the Prophet ﷺ support himself while delivering the Friday khutbah?
optionsEn: He leaned against a date-palm trunk standing near his prayer spot
He sat on a high stone throne
He spoke from the roof of the mosque
He stood inside a sunken pit
explanationEn: For several years in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ stood beside a date-palm trunk (jidh') when delivering sermons before the three-step Minbar was built.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Signs of Prophethood

questionEn: Which pillar marks the western edge of Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah where the Prophet's ﷺ wooden Minbar stood?
optionsEn: The Prophet's ﷺ Minbar itself forms the western boundary of Al-Rawdah
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ Hadith explicitly defines Al-Rawdah as the area stretching from his chamber on the east to his Minbar on the west.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: Why is Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's Ottoman prayer hall distinct from the surrounding modern Saudi halls when viewed from inside?
optionsEn: It features lower painted arches, thick red-painted columns, and calligraphy-adorned domes over the oldest section
It faces Jerusalem instead of Makkah
It has no roof above it
It uses steel trusses and glass walls
explanationEn: The Ottoman core around Al-Rawdah retains its iconic low domes and ornate columns, while the surrounding modern halls feature towering marble arches and massive chandeliers.

questionEn: How many steps did the original wooden Minbar crafted for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi have?
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ original Minbar had three simple wooden steps; he sat on the top step and rested his feet on the second (or stood on the second while speaking).

questionEn: From what type of desert wood was the Prophet's ﷺ original three-step Minbar carved?
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari records that an Ansari woman offered her skilled carpenter slave to build a Minbar from tamarisk wood (tarfa) grown in Al-Ghabah north of Madinah.

questionEn: Which Companion volunteered the services of her enslaved carpenter to build the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar?
optionsEn: An Ansari woman (often identified as the mother of Minah / a companion from Banu Najjar or Banu Malik)
explanationEn: An Ansari woman told the Prophet ﷺ: 'Shall I not have something made for you to sit on, for I have a slave who is a carpenter?' He agreed, and the Minbar was crafted.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: On which step of the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar did Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) sit out of humility after the Prophet ﷺ passed away?
optionsEn: On the very top canopy above the Minbar
One step lower than where the Prophet ﷺ sat
explanationEn: Out of reverence, Abu Bakr (RA) sat one step below the Prophet's ﷺ seat, and Umar (RA) later sat one step below Abu Bakr's.

questionEn: Which Umayyad caliph later added six extra steps to the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar, turning it into a taller nine-step pulpit (before later restorations)?
optionsEn: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (RA) / Marwan ibn al-Hakam during Mu'awiyah's reign
explanationEn: When Marwan moved or raised the Minbar on Mu'awiyah's instruction, six steps were placed beneath the original three so the larger congregation could see and hear.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, what eschatological location did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ connect to his Minbar?
optionsEn: 'My Minbar is in the center of Wadi al-Aqiq'
'My Minbar will be moved to Damascus'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Between my house and my pulpit is a garden of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon my Hawd (Pond).'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: What severe warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ issue regarding taking a false oath beside his Minbar in Madinah?
optionsEn: Whoever swears falsely at this Minbar—even over something as small as a fresh siwak—earns Hellfire
They are barred from Quba for a week
They must pay one gold dinar in charity
explanationEn: To uphold truthfulness and the sanctity of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ warned strictly against lying under oath beside his Minbar.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah (Sahih)

questionEn: Why did Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA) remind visitors who asked about the wood of the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar that he personally witnessed the first day the Prophet ﷺ sat upon it?
optionsEn: Because he was the Caliph of Madinah
Because he was one of the last surviving Companions in Madinah who saw the Prophet ﷺ ascend it
explanationEn: Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (RA) lived to a ripe age in Madinah and eyewitnessed the exact day the Prophet ﷺ prayed upon the new Minbar and then stepped back to prostrate at its base.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform prostration (sujud) on the day he prayed atop the new Minbar to teach the congregation the motions of prayer?
optionsEn: He stepped backward down the Minbar to prostrate on the floor at its base, then returned up it
He prostrated in the air without touching the ground
He stayed seated throughout the prayer
explanationEn: When he reached the time for bowing/prostration, he walked backward down the steps to prostrate on the mosque floor so everyone could follow his prayer cleanly.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: Which Ottoman Sultan gifted the ornate marble Minbar that still stands in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today (1590 CE / 998 AH)?
explanationEn: After the earlier Mamluk Minbar deteriorated, Ottoman Sultan Murad III commissioned the fine carved marble Minbar placed in Al-Rawdah in 998 AH.

questionEn: How many named historic Mihrabs (prayer niches) are famously preserved within the historic core of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Twelve Mihrabs along the western wall
Three main Mihrabs inside the prayer hall (Al-Nabawi, Al-Uthmani, and Al-Tahajjud), plus Al-Sulaymani
explanationEn: Visitors can observe Mihrab al-Nabawi in Al-Rawdah, Mihrab al-Uthmani in the southern Qiblah wall (where the Imam stands today), Mihrab al-Tahajjud north of the Chamber, and Mihrab al-Sulaymani.

questionEn: Did Al-Masjid an-Nabawi have a recessed concave wall niche (Mihrab) during the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Yes, carved out of white marble in 1 AH
No; the first concave Mihrab in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was introduced later by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (88-91 AH)
Yes, built by Salman al-Farsi in 5 AH
explanationEn: During the Prophet's ﷺ time, the Qiblah wall was flat; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz introduced the curved niche marking the exact spot where the Prophet ﷺ led prayer.

questionEn: Where does the Imam of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi normally stand to lead the five daily prayers today?
optionsEn: On the roof beside the Green Dome
At the northern entrance near Bab al-Majidi
In the Uthmani Mihrab (Mihrab al-Uthmani) along the southern Qiblah wall
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ Mihrab sits inside Al-Rawdah slightly behind the southern front line, whereas the Imam today leads prayers from Mihrab al-Uthmani on the expanded Qiblah wall.

questionEn: Why is the Imam's current prayer niche on the southern wall named 'Mihrab al-Uthmani'?
optionsEn: Because it marks the Qiblah wall position established during Caliph Uthman ibn Affan's (RA) southward expansion
Because the Ottoman Sultan Osman I built it
Because Uthman (RA) carved it personally out of wood
Because the Mushaf of Uthman is buried under it
explanationEn: When Uthman (RA) expanded the mosque southward in 29-30 AH, the Imam's front position shifted to that Qiblah wall, hence named after him.

questionEn: Where is 'Mihrab al-Tahajjud' located inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: To the west of the Minbar
Directly north of the Sacred Chamber, behind Fatimah's (RA) historic room
Inside the courtyard near Bab al-Salam
explanationEn: Mihrab al-Tahajjud marks the quiet spot behind the Sacred Chamber where the Prophet ﷺ used to stand in late-night prayer.

questionEn: Which Ottoman Sultan added 'Mihrab al-Sulaymani' (also known as the Hanafi Mihrab) to the west of the Minbar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Built in the 16th century under Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent and later clad in marble, it sits west of the Minbar near the old Hanafi prayer area.

questionEn: What is the raised marble platform inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi from which the Muezzins call the Adhan and repeat the Imam's Takbir?
explanationEn: Al-Mukabbariyah is the elevated platform behind Al-Rawdah where the Muezzins stand to proclaim the Adhan, Iqamah, and Takbirat.

questionEn: During the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, which two companions also served as Muezzins in Madinah alongside Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)?
optionsEn: Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Ubaydah
Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As
Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) and Sa'd al-Qaraz (RA, at Quba)
explanationEn: Bilal (RA) called the first Fajr adhan (to wake sleepers), while the blind companion Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) called the second Fajr adhan at true dawn; Sa'd al-Qaraz called at Quba.

questionEn: Whose dream in Madinah originally introduced the exact wording of the Islamic Adhan to the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari (RA) (confirmed also by Umar ibn al-Khattab RA)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ sought a way to summon believers without horns or bells, Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw the Adhan in a true vision; the Prophet ﷺ approved it and told him to teach it to Bilal.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ ask Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) to teach the words of the Adhan to Bilal (RA) rather than call it himself?
optionsEn: Because Bilal was older than Abdullah
Because Abdullah ibn Zayd was traveling to Makkah
Because Abdullah could not speak Arabic
Because Bilal (RA) had a stronger, more resonant voice
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ recognized Bilal's (RA) powerful, carrying voice (anda minaka sawtan), making him ideal for calling all of Madinah to prayer.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: From where did Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) often climb to call the Fajr Adhan in early Madinah?
optionsEn: A wooden tower in Jannat al-Baqi
The highest rooftop adjacent to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (house of a woman of Banu al-Najjar)
explanationEn: Before minarets existed, Bilal (RA) climbed the tallest nearby roof belonging to a woman of Banu al-Najjar to project the dawn Adhan across Madinah.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: What special practice did the Prophet ﷺ occasionally follow when Bilal (RA) called the Adhan during intense heat in Madinah?
optionsEn: Combining Dhuhr and Maghrib every day
Delaying the Dhuhr prayer slightly until the midday heat eased (ibrad)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Bilal (RA) to wait until the extreme desert heat abated before calling the Iqamah for Dhuhr, as fierce heat is from the breath of Hellfire.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Times of Prayer

questionEn: Who was the famous blind companion of Madinah whose Adhan at Fajr signaled that the pre-dawn Suhoor meal had ended?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Bilal calls the Adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls the Adhan.'

questionEn: What happened to Bilal ibn Rabah's (RA) role as regular Muezzin after the passing of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: He remained Muezzin for forty more years without pause
Overcome with grief, he could barely finish the Adhan and later moved to Greater Syria (Al-Sham)
explanationEn: After the Prophet's ﷺ passing, Bilal (RA) felt unable to remain in Madinah where every call of 'Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah' broke his heart, though he visited again under Umar (RA).
reference: Ibn Asakir & Al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala

questionEn: On the Prophet's ﷺ return to Madinah or during Eid, what did the Companions hold up or place before him in open-air prayers outside the mosque?
optionsEn: An iron-tipped short spear (anazah) planted as a sutrah
explanationEn: Whenever the Prophet ﷺ prayed in an open space (such as the Eid Musalla), Bilal (RA) carried and planted an anazah (short spear) in front of him as a sutrah.

questionEn: Why does the current Imam's Mihrab (Mihrab al-Uthmani) sit south of the Prophet's ﷺ Mihrab inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Because later expansions extended the Qiblah wall southward beyond the Prophet's ﷺ original mosque wall
Because the direction of Makkah shifted eastward
To leave room for carriages inside
explanationEn: As Uthman (RA) and later rulers enlarged the mosque southward toward the Qiblah, the front prayer row moved forward while preserving Mihrab al-Nabawi in Al-Rawdah.

questionEn: Which direction do worshippers face when standing at the Prophet's ﷺ Mihrab inside Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah?
optionsEn: South toward the Kaaba in Makkah
explanationEn: From Madinah, the Qiblah direction toward Makkah is due south (slightly south-southwest), so Mihrab al-Nabawi faces south.

questionEn: What phrase did the Prophet ﷺ say whenever he stood upon the Minbar and faced the congregation before starting his sermon?
optionsEn: He asked everyone to stand up
He faced them and greeted them with 'Assalamu alaykum'
He rang a brass bell for silence
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) reported that when the Prophet ﷺ ascended the Minbar, he greeted the congregation with salam before sitting while Bilal called the Adhan.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of Establishing Prayer

questionEn: What posture did the Prophet ﷺ maintain while delivering the Friday khutbah from his Minbar?
optionsEn: Standing upright, leaning lightly on a staff or bow, with short, focused sermons
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ delivered two standing khutbahs separated by a brief sitting, keeping the sermon concise and the prayer prolonged.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ respond when a man entered Al-Masjid an-Nabawi while he was delivering the Friday khutbah and sat down without praying?
optionsEn: He told him never to pray during a khutbah
He asked him if he had prayed, and told him to stand and pray two brief rak'ahs (Tahiyyat al-Masjid)
He paused the khutbah for thirty minutes
He ordered him to leave the mosque immediately
explanationEn: The man was Sulayk al-Ghatafani (RA); the Prophet ﷺ instructed him—and all Muslims arriving during the Friday sermon—to offer two quick rak'ahs before sitting.

questionEn: What special moment on Friday did the Prophet ﷺ urge Muslims to seek inside the mosque, often noted as being between the Imam sitting on the Minbar and the end of prayer (or the last hour after Asr)?
optionsEn: The Hour of Acceptance of Dua (Sa'at al-Istijabah)
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) reported it as between the Imam sitting on the Minbar and the completion of Jumu'ah prayer, while other authentic reports highlight the final hour before Maghrib.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: Which famous verse was placed in calligraphy inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi reminding worshippers of the etiquette of entering Allah's houses?
optionsEn: Surah An-Nur 24:36 ('In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein')
explanationEn: Surah An-Nur 24:36 celebrates mosques raised in honor where Allah is glorified morning and evening by people whom commerce never distracts from His remembrance.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ make a small raised wooden step or chamber screen (hasir) in the mosque during Ramadan nights before gently halting public congregation for Tarawih?
optionsEn: Because the wood was damaged by rain
Out of fear that the night prayer might become obligatory (fard) upon his Ummah
explanationEn: After praying two or three nights with growing crowds in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ stayed inside on the fourth night so Tarawih would remain a beloved voluntary Sunnah rather than an obligation.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Night Prayer

questionEn: Who revived the regular unified congregation of Tarawih behind a single imam (Ubayy ibn Ka'b) inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Seeing Muslims praying in scattered small groups during Ramadan, Umar (RA) united them behind Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) and famously remarked, 'What an excellent revival/practice this is!'

questionEn: What is the significance of the Prophet's ﷺ custom of sitting inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi after Fajr prayer until sunrise?
optionsEn: He slept on the Minbar until noon
He collected taxes at the eastern wall
He remained remembering Allah with his Companions until the sun rose fully, a practice carrying great reward
He closed the mosque doors to all visitors
explanationEn: Sitting in one's prayer place after Fajr in dhikr until sunrise and then praying two rak'ahs (Duha/Ishraq) is a cherished Sunnah practiced by the Prophet ﷺ in his mosque.

questionEn: Who led the prayers in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during the final days of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ illness?
explanationEn: Despite Aishah's (RA) concern about her father's tender heart, the Prophet ﷺ insisted: 'Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.'

questionEn: On what final morning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lift the curtain of Aishah's (RA) apartment and smile joyfully seeing the Muslims lined up in Fajr prayer behind Abu Bakr (RA)?
optionsEn: Monday morning, 12 Rabi al-Awwal 11 AH, the day of his passing
explanationEn: Seeing his Ummah united in Fajr rows filled the Prophet's ﷺ face with radiant joy—described by Anas (RA) as looking like a page of the Mushaf—shortly before his passing later that morning.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Adhan & Maghazi

questionEn: How many rooms (hujurat) of the Mothers of the Believers originally lined the eastern exterior wall of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Nine modest mud-brick and palm-branch rooms stood along the eastern flank of the mosque for the Prophet's ﷺ wives, as alluded to in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:4).

questionEn: What historic landmark stands near the southeastern corner of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi where the Prophet's ﷺ wives' apartments once stood?
optionsEn: The Sacred Chamber (Al-Hujrah al-Sharifah) beneath the Green Dome
explanationEn: Only Aishah's (RA) apartment—containing the graves of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA)—was preserved inside a sealed enclosure when the remaining apartments were cleared for expansion.

questionEn: Why did Companions like Hasan ibn Thabit (RA) weep when Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz cleared the remaining outer rooms of the Prophet's ﷺ wives during the 88 AH expansion?
optionsEn: Because they opposed building mosques in Madinah
Witnessing those humble mud-brick rooms reminded people of the Prophet's ﷺ simplicity in contrast to worldly luxury
Because the Qiblah was being changed again
Because they wanted to build a palace there
explanationEn: Elders of Madinah (like Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib) wished the modest rooms had been left standing as a living lesson in Prophetic asceticism for future generations.

questionEn: Why was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ buried inside Aishah's (RA) room rather than in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Because Aishah's room was outside Madinah
Because Abu Bakr (RA) testified that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Every prophet is buried where he passes away'
explanationEn: When the Companions differed on where to bury him—his mosque, Baqi, or Makkah—Abu Bakr (RA) resolved it with the Prophet's ﷺ explicit Hadith that prophets are buried right where their souls are taken.

questionEn: Who dug the niche-style grave (lahd) for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ beneath his bed in the Sacred Chamber?
explanationEn: Madinah had two gravediggers: Abu Ubaydah (who dug a straight trench, shaqq) and Abu Talhah (who dug a side-niche, lahd); the Companions prayed for Allah's choice, and Abu Talhah arrived first.

questionEn: How was the Funeral Prayer (Salat al-Janazah) offered for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ inside the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: Offered only by the people of Makkah
Led by Umar ibn al-Khattab in Jannat al-Baqi
Believers entered in small groups sequentially and prayed upon him without a single Imam
explanationEn: Men, then women, then children entered Aishah's (RA) room in small groups to offer Salat al-Janazah individually without anyone standing ahead as Imam.

questionEn: Whose body rests immediately beside Prophet Muhammad ﷺ inside the Sacred Chamber, with his head aligned near the Prophet's ﷺ shoulder?
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr (RA) passed away in 13 AH, he requested to be buried beside his lifelong companion Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, placed slightly back so his head aligned with the Prophet's ﷺ shoulder.

questionEn: Whose permission did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) humbly ask on his deathbed in 23 AH to be buried in the third spot inside the Sacred Chamber?
explanationEn: Even though Aishah (RA) had kept that space for herself, she gladly gave it up out of respect for Umar (RA), saying: 'I will prefer him over myself today.'

questionEn: How did Aishah (RA) adjust her clothing inside her own apartment after Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) was buried there alongside her husband and father?
optionsEn: She opened the chamber to tourists
She began wearing a veil/outer garment out of modesty (haya) before Umar (RA)
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) remarked that before Umar's burial, only her husband and father lay there, so she felt at ease; once Umar—not a mahram—was buried there, she covered fully out of modesty.

questionEn: What unusual geometric shape did Governor Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz build for the outer stone wall enclosing the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: A pentagonal (five-sided) wall with a pointed northern apex
explanationEn: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz deliberately designed the outer wall as an irregular pentagon so it would never resemble the rectangular Kaaba or tempt anyone to perform Tawaf around it.

questionEn: Why is the Sacred Chamber completely sealed without any public doorway into the inner graves today?
optionsEn: Because only rulers enter every Friday
To protect the graves' sanctity and prevent superstitious or idolatrous practices forbidden by Islam
Because the floor collapsed in 1200 AH
Because the key was lost in Baghdad
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ prayed: 'O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped.' Sealing the chamber with layered walls and outer grilles safeguards pure monotheism (Tawhid).

questionEn: In what year did Mamluk Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun construct the very first dome above the Sacred Chamber?
explanationEn: For over six centuries there was no dome over the Sacred Chamber; Sultan Qalawun first erected a wooden dome clad in lead plates in 678 AH.

questionEn: What color was the dome over the Sacred Chamber during various centuries before it was painted green in the 19th century?
optionsEn: Bright orange during the Abbasid era
Natural wood/lead gray, white, and blue/purple in earlier periods
explanationEn: Historically it was known as Al-Qubbah al-Bayda (White Dome) or Al-Qubbah al-Zarqa/al-Fayha (Blue Dome) before Ottoman Sultan Mahmud II ordered it painted green in 1253 AH (1837 CE).

questionEn: Which Ottoman Sultan ordered the dome above the Sacred Chamber to be painted green in 1253 AH (1837 CE), giving it the famous name 'Al-Qubbah al-Khadra'?
explanationEn: After Sultan Mahmud II commissioned the green paint in 1253 AH (1837 CE), the iconic dome became universally known as the Green Dome (Al-Qubbah al-Khadra).

questionEn: What is 'Al-Muwajahah al-Sharifah' inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: The library wing near Bab al-Majidi
The northern entrance leading to Uhud
The southern walkway directly facing the brass grilles of the Sacred Chamber where visitors offer Salam
explanationEn: Walking eastward from Bab al-Salam, visitors pass along Al-Muwajahah al-Sharifah—the front grille screen—to offer peaceful salutations to the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA).

questionEn: How many circular viewing openings (holes) exist on the main brass grille facing the Sacred Chamber at Al-Muwajahah al-Sharifah, and what does each align with?
optionsEn: One single opening for the Prophet ﷺ only
Seven openings for the Seven Fuqaha
Three circular openings aligning with the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA)
Twelve openings for the months of the year
explanationEn: The largest central opening aligns with the resting place of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, followed slightly to the east by the opening for Abu Bakr (RA), and then Umar (RA).

questionEn: What is the proper wording of the salutation a visitor offers when standing politely before the Prophet's ﷺ resting place?
optionsEn: Asking the Prophet ﷺ directly to grant wealth
Reciting Surat al-Fatihah while facing away
'Assalamu alayka ya Rasulallah wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh' (or adding 'ya Nabiyyallah')
Chanting loudly in unison with drums
explanationEn: Scholars cite Ibn Umar's (RA) concise Sunnah greeting: 'Assalamu alayka ya Rasulallah', followed by a half-step right for 'Assalamu alayka ya Aba Bakr' and 'Assalamu alayka ya Umar'.
reference: Sunan al-Bayhaqi & Al-Mughni of Ibn Qudamah

questionEn: Which direction should a visitor face if they wish to raise their hands and make personal Dua to Allah after offering Salam at the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: Directly toward the brass grille with hands raised
Toward the Qiblah (south, facing Makkah), away from the grave
explanationEn: Imam Malik and other classical scholars emphasized turning toward the Qiblah—not the grave—for personal supplication, because Dua is worship directed exclusively to Allah.
reference: Al-Qadi Iyad, Al-Shifa & Fiqh of Ziyarah

questionEn: What clear warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give on his deathbed regarding turning the graves of prophets into places of worship?
optionsEn: 'Offer your five daily prayers toward my chamber'
'May Allah's curse be upon those who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship'
'Always ask the righteous dead for rain'
'Build tall shrines over every companion's grave'
explanationEn: Narrated by Aishah and Ibn Abbas (RA), the Prophet ﷺ warned against building mosques atop graves or worshipping toward them, protecting the purity of Tawhid.

questionEn: What authentic assurance did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about how our Salawat and Salam reach him from anywhere, as well as near his grave?
optionsEn: Allah returns his soul to him so he returns the Salam, and Allah appoints traveling angels to convey Salawat from everywhere
Angels only deliver Salawat on Eid
Only people living in Madinah can send Salawat
One must touch the grille for Salam to be heard
explanationEn: According to Sunan Abi Dawud (Sahih) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (Sahih), Allah conveys every believer's Salawat from across the globe via angels, and the Prophet ﷺ returns the Salam offered to him.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell his Companions: 'Do not make my grave a site of recurring festival (id), and do not turn your houses into graves'?
optionsEn: Because Salawat may only be said once a year
Because houses should have no carpets
To discourage ritualized festive gatherings at his grave while encouraging frequent Salawat from anywhere and prayer inside homes
explanationEn: This Hadith balances deep love with sound creed: send abundant Salawat on the Prophet ﷺ wherever you are, and keep homes alive with voluntary prayer and Qur'an.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Rites (Graded Sahih)

questionEn: When Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) returned to Madinah from a journey, how did he briefly greet the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: He circled the chamber seven times
He shouted poems at the door
He entered the mosque, prayed, walked briefly to the grave saying 'Assalamu alayka ya Rasulallah, Assalamu alayka ya Aba Bakr, Assalamu alayka ya Abatah (O my father)', and left
He stayed clinging to the wall for four hours
explanationEn: Ibn Umar's (RA) dignified, brief, and heartfelt greeting serves as a timeless model of love, restraint, and adherence to the Sunnah.

questionEn: What specific Qur'anic admonition in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:2) did Imam Malik invoke when Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur raised his voice in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: 'O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you'
'Read in the name of your Lord who created'
'And perform Hajj and Umrah for Allah'
'Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet... lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not'
explanationEn: Imam Malik reminded the Abbasid Caliph that the Prophet's ﷺ honor after his passing is just as sacred as in his lifetime, so voices must stay calm and respectful.

questionEn: Which window of the Sacred Chamber is called 'Al-Khawkha' or faces Fatimah's (RA) historic adjacent quarters on the north side?
optionsEn: The roof parapet above Bab al-Salam
The western facade of Masjid Quba
The northern side of the Sacred Chamber enclosure (near Bayt Fatimah)
explanationEn: The northern compartment inside the Sacred Chamber enclosure encompassed the room of Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) and Ali (RA), adjacent to Aishah's (RA) apartment.

questionEn: What sits directly above the inner dome of the Sacred Chamber, visible from across Madinah as a symbol of the Prophet's ﷺ city?
explanationEn: The outer lead-clad masonry dome painted green rises over the inner chamber dome, orienting pilgrims across Madinah toward the southeastern corner of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: What is the 'Maqsurah' surrounding the Sacred Chamber inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: The minaret balcony used by the Muezzin
The outer marble plaza for Friday crowds
The underground water cistern beneath the courtyard
The ornate green-and-gold brass grille enclosure surrounding the pentagonal inner wall
explanationEn: Installed originally in the Mamluk era and renewed later, the Maqsurah grille defines a respectful boundary around the pentagonal walls of the Sacred Chamber.

questionEn: Which two companions did Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz witness during his childhood/youth—or consult among Madinah's elders—when inspecting the collapsed wall of the Sacred Chamber during the 88 AH renovation?
optionsEn: Elders of Madinah such as Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad witnessed the repair
explanationEn: When the outer mud wall briefly gave way during reconstruction in 88 AH, scholars of the Tabi'in in Madinah were present as Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz carefully rebuilt the pentagonal enclosure.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, when the wall of the Sacred Chamber briefly collapsed during Al-Walid's reign, whose foot was uncovered slightly before Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz hastened to cover and rebuild it?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), as identified by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)
explanationEn: When people worried it might be the Prophet's ﷺ foot, the knowledgeable scholar Urwah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) clarified the layout of the three graves and confirmed it was Umar's (RA).

questionEn: What did the Companions do with the Prophet's ﷺ garments and bed inside the Sacred Chamber during his burial?
optionsEn: They buried him in armor and sword
They shrouded him in three white Sahuli cotton garments and placed red velvet/cloth beneath him in the grave due to Madinah's damp soil
They buried him inside a golden coffin
They wrapped him in silk brocade from Persia
explanationEn: His mawla Shuqran placed a red cloak the Prophet ﷺ used to wear beneath him in the lahd because Madinah's soil was moist, and he was shrouded in three white cotton cloths.

questionEn: Who were the close family members who descended into the grave to gently lay Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to rest inside the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Al-Abbas, Al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, Qutham ibn al-Abbas, Usamah ibn Zayd, and Shuqran (RA)
Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Khalid ibn al-Walid
explanationEn: His closest Hashemite kin along with Usamah ibn Zayd and Shuqran lowered the noble body into the lahd and sealed it with unbaked mud bricks.

questionEn: What touching question did Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) ask Anas ibn Malik (RA) right after the Companions finished burying Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'Where is the treasure of the masjid kept?'
'When will we travel back to Makkah?'
'O Anas, how were your hearts able to throw earth over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?'
explanationEn: Anas (RA) wept as he recounted Fatimah's (RA) grief-stricken words, capturing the profound sorrow that enveloped Madinah on that day.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: How long did Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) survive in Madinah after the passing of her father Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ had whispered to her during his final illness, Fatimah (RA) was the first of his family to join him, passing away six months later in Ramadan 11 AH.

questionEn: Why do some historical narrations mention a fourth empty space inside Aishah's (RA) room, known in Madinah tradition?
optionsEn: It was used as a library archive
Tradition recorded in Al-Tirmidhi notes that Isa (Jesus, AS) will be buried beside the Prophet ﷺ upon his return and passing
It was reserved for Imam Malik
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) and narrations in Sunan al-Tirmidhi mention that Isa ibn Maryam (AS) will be buried alongside the Prophet ﷺ in the Sacred Chamber.
reference: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Book of Virtues (Gharib) & Al-Samhudi

questionEn: Which famous gate or corridor near the Sacred Chamber was historically known as 'Khawkhat Al-Baqi' or 'Dakhlat al-Rawdah'?
optionsEn: The road from Madinah to Dhul-Hulayfah
The market alley of Banu Qaynuqa
The corridor along the front Qiblah wall connecting Bab al-Salam past Al-Rawdah and Al-Muwajahah to Bab al-Baqi
The path from Masjid Quba to Uhud
explanationEn: Pilgrims follow this linear eastern flow—entering at Bab al-Salam, passing Al-Rawdah and Al-Muwajahah, and exiting calmly via Bab al-Baqi.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing supererogatory Tawaf (circumambulation) around the Sacred Chamber or Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Permissible only on Mondays and Thursdays
Strictly forbidden (haram/bid'ah); Tawaf is performed exclusively around the Holy Kaaba in Makkah
explanationEn: Islam restricts Tawaf solely to Allah's House, the Kaaba in Makkah; circling any other building or grave violates the Sunnah.

questionEn: When passing before the Sacred Chamber during crowded times, what is the best etiquette if one cannot pause right in front of the grille?
optionsEn: Keep walking smoothly while offering Salam softly and respectfully without blocking or pushing others
Climb onto the marble benches to see inside
Turn around and sit on the walkway
explanationEn: Maintaining calm flow, gentleness, and respect for fellow believers honors the Prophet's ﷺ own character inside his mosque.

questionEn: Which companion had his house located adjacent to the Prophet's ﷺ mosque where the Prophet ﷺ visited him and once heard him reciting Qur'an softly at night?
optionsEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) (or Aishah/Hafsah's quarters nearby)
explanationEn: Hearing Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's (RA) melodious recitation in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ praised him: 'You have been given one of the flutes (sweet melodies) of the family of Dawud.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the house and mosque being illuminated when believers pray and recite Qur'an within Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and their Madinah homes?
optionsEn: Only the mosque should ever have Qur'an recited inside
Homes in Madinah must stay silent at night
Homes where Allah is remembered are like the living compared to the dead for those where He is forgotten
Voluntary prayers are invalid outside Al-Rawdah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged believers to perform some of their voluntary prayers in their homes so their homes are blessed alongside the mosque.

questionEn: Who was the famous companion and poet of the Prophet ﷺ who used a special pulpit set up inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to defend Islam with truthful verse?
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ set up a small minbar inside the mosque for Hassan ibn Thabit (RA) to recite poetry defending the Messenger ﷺ and refuting Quraysh's satires.

questionEn: What comforting assurance did the Prophet ﷺ give Hassan ibn Thabit (RA) when Hassan recited poetry in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit (Jibril)'
explanationEn: Because Hassan's (RA) poetry defended truth and the Messenger ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Jibril (AS) to strengthen him.

questionEn: What happened when Ka'b ibn Abi Ka'b / Ka'b ibn Malik and Ibn Abi Hadrad raised their voices disputing a debt inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: He expelled both men from Madinah
The Prophet ﷺ opened his curtain from Aishah's room and signaled Ka'b to forgive half the debt, settling it peacefully
He canceled all debts across Arabia
He imposed a double fine on both
explanationEn: Overhearing their raised voices inside the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ stepped out, gestured for Ka'b to remit half the debt, and had Ibn Abi Hadrad repay the rest immediately.

questionEn: Which companion was known as the regular keeper of the keys/lanterns or attended the mosque closely, and when did oil lamps first illuminate Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Abu Lahab gifted chandeliers in 1 AH
Oil lamps were banned until 500 AH
Only torches of palm leaves were allowed until the 20th century
Tamim al-Dari (RA) first brought oil lamps from Syria to light Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 9 AH
explanationEn: Before Tamim al-Dari (RA) brought oil lamps, wicks, and hanging ropes from Greater Syria, the mosque was lit by burning palm branches; the Prophet ﷺ joyfully said: 'You have illuminated Islam, may Allah illuminate you!'

questionEn: What was the 'Aghawat' corps historically associated with serving Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and the Sacred Chamber for centuries?
optionsEn: Devoted elder attendants dedicated to guarding, cleaning, perfuming, and maintaining the Sacred Chamber and Al-Rawdah
explanationEn: Established in the medieval Islamic era, the Aghawat served with strict discipline as lifelong caretakers of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and the Sacred Chamber.

questionEn: Where inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was 'Al-Suffah' (the shaded bench/platform) situated after the Qiblah shifted south toward Makkah?
optionsEn: At the rear (northern end) of the mosque
Directly inside the southern Qiblah wall
explanationEn: When the Qiblah changed to the south in 2 AH, the shaded platform at the northern back wall of the mosque became the famous home and school of Ahl al-Suffah.

questionEn: Who were 'Ahl al-Suffah' (Ashab al-Suffah) in early Madinah?
optionsEn: Impoverished emigrants and visiting students who had no home or family in Madinah and lived in the mosque devoting themselves to Qur'an and Hadith
explanationEn: Ahl al-Suffah were guests of Islam—often numbering around seventy at a time—who lived simply in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and preserved immense Prophetic knowledge.

questionEn: Which resident of Al-Suffah became the single most prolific narrator of Prophetic Hadith in Islamic history?
optionsEn: Abu Hurayrah (Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr al-Dawsi, RA)
explanationEn: Accompanying the Prophet ﷺ constantly from 7 AH onward while living at Al-Suffah, Abu Hurayrah (RA) memorized over 5,300 Hadith narrations through Allah's blessing after the Prophet's ﷺ dua for his memory.

questionEn: How did Abu Hurayrah (RA) describe the hunger sometimes endured by Ahl al-Suffah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: They feasted on roasted lamb three times daily
They owned vast date farms in Khaybar
He sometimes fainted between the Minbar and Aishah's (RA) chamber from hunger so severe that passersby mistook it for an illness
They received silver salaries from Quraysh
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) candidly recounted tying stones to his stomach and collapsing from hunger while refusing to compromise his devotion to learning from the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ share food with Ahl al-Suffah whenever charity (sadaqah) or a gift (hadiyyah) was brought to him?
optionsEn: He sent all Sadaqah directly to Ahl al-Suffah without touching it, and invited them to share any personal gift with him
He auctioned gifts in the market
He kept Sadaqah for himself and gave them nothing
He sent all food outside Madinah
explanationEn: Prophets do not consume charity (sadaqah); thus the Prophet ﷺ forwarded charitable meals solely to Ahl al-Suffah while graciously sharing personal gifts alongside them.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari's famous narration of the bowl of milk, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach Abu Hurayrah (RA) generosity toward Ahl al-Suffah?
optionsEn: He told Abu Hurayrah to drink the milk in secret
He sent the milk back to the donor
He asked Abu Hurayrah to call all of Ahl al-Suffah to drink from one bowl of milk until every single one was satisfied before the Prophet ﷺ drank last
He poured the milk onto the sand
explanationEn: Through a blessed miracle of multiplication, dozens of Ahl al-Suffah drank their fill from one cup of milk, with the Prophet ﷺ declaring 'Only you and I remain' before drinking last.

questionEn: Which generous Ansari leader regularly sent massive platters—or hung fresh date bunches in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—and once hosted eighty of Ahl al-Suffah at his home?
explanationEn: The Khazraj chief Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) was legendary in Madinah for feeding scores of Ahl al-Suffah nightly and sending food daily to the Prophet's ﷺ household.

questionEn: Which Ansar custom supported Ahl al-Suffah by hanging bunches of ripe dates inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during harvest?
optionsEn: Selling dates at double price to travelers
Hanging clusters of dates (qinw) on a rope between two pillars for anyone in need to eat
explanationEn: Every harvest, Medinan orchard owners hung clusters of fresh dates between two pillars in the mosque so Ahl al-Suffah and travelers could eat freely; this practice is linked with Surah 2:267 when someone hung inferior dry dates.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed regarding a resident or donor who hung poor-quality dry dates in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for Ahl al-Suffah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:267 ('Do not aim for the bad things to spend therefrom...')
explanationEn: Allah admonished donors not to give inferior things they themselves would dislike, urging believers to spend from the finest of what they earned.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse in Surah Al-An'am (6:52) and Surah Al-Kahf (18:28) defended the poor companions like Ahl al-Suffah when arrogant tribal chiefs asked the Prophet ﷺ to send them away?
optionsEn: 'Today I have perfected for you your religion'
'And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance'
'Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest'
explanationEn: When aristocratic visitors disdained sitting beside impoverished Muslims like Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ammar, Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ never to turn away sincere believers.

questionEn: Who was appointed by the Prophet ﷺ to teach reading, writing, and the Qur'an to Ahl al-Suffah in early Madinah?
optionsEn: Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA) (and Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn al-As / literate Badr captives also taught writing)
explanationEn: Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA) taught literacy and Qur'an at Al-Suffah; he famously declined even a bow gifted by a student, fearing any worldly payment for teaching Allah's Book.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: What remarkable opportunity did literate Makkah captives from the Battle of Badr receive in Madinah to earn their freedom?
optionsEn: By swimming across the Red Sea
Each captive could earn freedom by teaching ten children of the Ansar how to read and write
By building a palace in Quba
explanationEn: Valuing literacy as a pillar of community building, the Prophet ﷺ accepted teaching ten Medinan children as full ransom for educated Badr prisoners.

questionEn: Which companion of Al-Suffah was sent by the Prophet ﷺ on a mission to Najd and was martyred at Bi'r Ma'unah alongside seventy Qur'an reciters?
optionsEn: Al-Mundhir ibn Amr (RA) and Haram ibn Milhan (RA) among the seventy Qurra
explanationEn: Many of the seventy martyred Qur'an scholars (al-Qurra) at Bi'r Ma'unah in 4 AH were devoted learners from Al-Suffah who worked by day gathering firewood to feed their companions and prayed by night.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which companion from Al-Suffah famously answered 'Allah and His Messenger know best' when the Prophet ﷺ asked him about marriage, later wed through teaching what he knew of the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Sahl ibn Sa'd's narration of a poor Companion (often linked to Al-Suffah) who had not even an iron ring
explanationEn: When a poor man in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi had no wealth—not even an iron ring—the Prophet ﷺ married him to a willing woman on the mahr of teaching her the surahs of the Qur'an he memorized.

questionEn: What name was given to the elevated platform or seat inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in later centuries marking the historic zone of Ahl al-Suffah?
optionsEn: Dikkah al-Aghawat / Al-Suffah platform (located northeast of Al-Rawdah)
explanationEn: In the Ottoman reconstruction, a raised stone platform known today near the Aghawat bench marks the northern-eastern area corresponding to the later Suffah.

questionEn: Which companion of Al-Suffah was known as 'Dhul-Bijadayn' (Possessor of Two Coarse Cloaks) because he gave up everything in his tribe to migrate to Madinah?
explanationEn: Stripped of his wealth by his uncle for embracing Islam, Abdullah tore a coarse blanket in two for his garments, lived at Al-Suffah, and later died at Tabuk where the Prophet ﷺ personally lowered him into his grave.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ treat visiting Bedouin who entered Al-Masjid an-Nabawi unaware of mosque etiquette, such as the man who urinated in a corner of the mosque?
optionsEn: He demolished that side of the mosque
He banned all Bedouins from Madinah
He stopped the Companions from shouting at him, let him finish, had a bucket of water poured over the spot, and gently taught him
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ calm wisdom won the Bedouin's heart and taught the Companions that mosques are purified with water and that people are guided with gentleness, not harshness.

questionEn: What remarkable dua did that Bedouin make aloud inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi right after the Prophet's ﷺ gentle response?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, bring a flood upon Madinah'
'O Allah, have mercy on me and on Muhammad, and do not have mercy on anyone else with us!'
'O Allah, close the doors of Quba'
explanationEn: Smiling at the Bedouin's naive exclusivity, the Prophet ﷺ replied gently: 'You have narrowed something very vast (Allah's mercy)!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: Which companion from Al-Suffah used to walk silently behind the Prophet ﷺ carrying his water vessel and slippers whenever he needed them?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) (and Anas ibn Malik / Abu Dharr)
explanationEn: Known as 'Sahib al-Siwak wal-Na'layn' (Keeper of the Prophet's tooth-stick and sandals), Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) enjoyed constant access to the Prophet's ﷺ household and Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when the Companions laughed at the thin calves of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) while he climbed a tree in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'By Him in Whose hand is my soul, those two legs will be heavier on the Scale (Mizan) on the Day of Judgment than Mount Uhud!'
'Height and weight determine rank before Allah'
'Tell him to remain silent in the mosque'
'Never allow him to climb trees again'
explanationEn: This profound teaching in Madinah showed that true weight before Allah lies in faith, sincerity, and Qur'anic devotion rather than outward physique.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the blessing of a community gathering in houses of Allah like Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to recite and study the Qur'an together?
optionsEn: Tranquility descends upon them, mercy envelops them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him
They are exempted from Fajr prayer
Only scholars over sixty may attend
They must finish within ten minutes
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, this Hadith inspires the timeless tradition of Qur'an and Hadith study circles (halaqat) inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Remembrance and Supplication

questionEn: For over fourteen centuries, what continuous educational institution inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi has connected scholars and students from across the Muslim world?
optionsEn: Annual poetry contests without religious subjects
The Halaqat (scholarly study circles) of Qur'an, Hadith, and Fiqh seated beside its pillars
explanationEn: From the Prophet's ﷺ own circles and Ahl al-Suffah to Imam Malik and modern scholars, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's pillars remain a living university of Islamic knowledge.

questionEn: Where is the main scholarly library of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi located today for visitors seeking Islamic manuscripts and books?
optionsEn: Within the mosque complex (above the western/northwestern expansion halls, accessible via Gate 10/library escalators)
Inside the basement of Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Maktabat al-Masjid an-Nabawi houses vast collections of classical manuscripts, Qur'an commentaries, and multilingual Islamic works open to visitors and researchers.

questionEn: What distinctive daily service is provided free of charge throughout Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's halls and courtyards for worshippers?
optionsEn: Chilled and room-temperature Zamzam water dispensers
explanationEn: Thousands of Zamzam water containers are continually replenished inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, connecting the spiritual blessing of Makkah's well with Madinah's worshippers.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: How many motorized shading umbrellas stand across the outer piazzas of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today to shelter worshippers from the sun?
explanationEn: Installed during the modern expansion, 250 automated Teflon-coated umbrellas open at sunrise and fold at dusk, shading roughly 143,000 square meters of outer plaza.

questionEn: How are the 250 courtyard umbrellas of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi equipped to reduce summer heat for pilgrims?
optionsEn: With built-in misting water fans mounted on the umbrella columns
With ice blocks carried by hand
explanationEn: Over 430 misting fans integrated into the umbrella pillars spray fine cooling water vapor across the courtyards during hot afternoons.

questionEn: What is the total prayer capacity of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, its roof, and its shaded outer piazzas during peak Ramadan and Hajj seasons?
explanationEn: Across its indoor halls, rooftop prayer area, and vast paved courtyards, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi accommodates more than a million worshippers at peak gatherings.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What happens inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during the last ten nights of Ramadan in emulation of the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah?
optionsEn: The courtyard umbrellas stay closed all day
Thousands perform I'tikaf (spiritual retreat) and Qiyam al-Layl (Tahajjud) praying through the night
Only travelers from Jeddah may enter
The mosque closes completely from Maghrib to Fajr
explanationEn: I'tikaf in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during Ramadan's final ten nights follows the unbroken example of the Prophet ﷺ, who practiced I'tikaf every Ramadan until his passing.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, how many days did the Prophet ﷺ observe I'tikaf inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in the final Ramadan of his life (10 AH)?
explanationEn: While his normal custom was ten days, in the final year of his life (10 AH) the Prophet ﷺ observed twenty days of I'tikaf inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with him twice.

questionEn: What etiquette does the Prophet ﷺ advise for anyone walking to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when the Iqamah for prayer has already started?
optionsEn: Walk calmly with dignity and serenity; pray what you catch and complete what you missed
Sprint as fast as possible down the aisles
Turn back and pray in the street
Shout to the Imam to wait
explanationEn: Even when eager not to miss a rak'ah, Muslims are taught to walk toward prayer with calmness (sakinah) and composure (waqar).

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, what is the reward for every step a believer takes walking from their hotel or home toward Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: One step erases a sin and the next step elevates a degree in Paradise
Only steps taken inside Al-Rawdah count
Every ten steps equal one dirham
explanationEn: Purifying oneself properly and walking calmly to the mosque turns every single footstep into spiritual purification and elevation.

questionEn: Which supplication is Sunnah to recite when stepping into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with the right foot?
