optionsEn: 'Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik' (O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy), preceded by Salawat
explanationEn: Entering with the right foot while sending Salawat on the Prophet ﷺ and asking Allah to open the doors of His mercy is the Sunnah for entering every mosque, and especially his own mosque.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Prayer of Travelers

questionEn: Which supplication is Sunnah to recite when exiting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with the left foot?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik' (O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty)
explanationEn: Upon leaving the mosque into daily life, the believer steps out with the left foot, sends Salawat, and asks Allah for His lawful bounty.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Prayer of Travelers

questionEn: What short two-rak'ah prayer should a pilgrim offer upon entering Al-Masjid an-Nabawi before sitting down (outside prohibited times according to some schools, or anytime according to Shafi'i)?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When one of you enters the mosque, let him not sit down until he prays two rak'ahs.'

questionEn: What mistake do some visitors make upon first entering Al-Masjid an-Nabawi regarding the order of Tahiyyat al-Masjid and offering Salam at the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: Rushing straight to the Sacred Chamber without first greeting the House of Allah with two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid
Lowering their voice inside the mosque
explanationEn: Classical scholars advise prioritizing two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid (in Al-Rawdah if accessible, or anywhere in the mosque) before walking calmly to offer Salam at the Sacred Chamber.

questionEn: Which companion of Al-Suffah was known for his deep devotion to fasting and night prayer and later became an ascetic scholar who married into the Ansar?
optionsEn: Salman al-Farsi (RA) and Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) among the elders of Al-Suffah
explanationEn: Both Salman al-Farsi and Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) spent time among Ahl al-Suffah, exemplifying asceticism and reliance upon Allah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the humble mud-brick floor and ceiling of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when a companion asked about repairing the roof?
optionsEn: 'An arbor like the arbor of Musa (AS): sticks and reeds—for the affair (of this world) is swifter than that'
'Build a marble palace fifty cubits high'
explanationEn: When asked to fortify the leaking roof, the Prophet ﷺ taught detachment from excessive ornamentation, keeping the mosque simple and functional.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

questionEn: Which companion first introduced wooden railings or a small stone parapet around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's outer courtyard ('Al-Butayha') so people wouldn't disturb the mosque with poetry or chatter?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), who built a designated courtyard space called Al-Butayha
Uthman ibn Affan (RA) at Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Umar (RA) constructed an open courtyard space called Al-Butayha beside the mosque, telling people: 'Whoever wants to chat, recite poetry, or raise their voice, let them step out to Al-Butayha.'
reference: Muwatta Malik, Book of the Qiblah

questionEn: What happened to the height of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's roof when Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) rebuilt it in 17 AH?
optionsEn: He lowered it to three cubits
He replaced it with stone pyramids
He raised the roof height to roughly eleven cubits so the congregation had better air and light
explanationEn: While keeping Umar's (RA) humble materials—mud brick and palm trunks—he elevated the roof to improve airflow and space for the rapidly growing community.

questionEn: What phrase did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) tell the builders during his 17 AH renovation of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi regarding ornamentation?
optionsEn: 'Shelter the people from the rain, and beware of painting it red or yellow lest you distract the worshippers'
'Carve portraits of rulers on the pillars'
explanationEn: Umar (RA) wanted the Prophet's Mosque to prioritize peaceful focus in Salah over distracting visual extravagance.

questionEn: Which famous gate on the northern facade of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is named after King Fahd ibn Abd al-Aziz, featuring monumental twin minarets and ornate bronze doors?
explanationEn: Located along the northern facade of the modern expansion, King Fahd Gate forms the grand northern axis adorned with twin minarets and intricate woodwork.

questionEn: How many tall minarets crown Al-Masjid an-Nabawi following its major modern Saudi expansions?
optionsEn: Ten minarets (each reaching approximately 104 meters in the newer sections alongside historic ones)
explanationEn: From four minarets in the Umayyad era and five in the Ottoman era, the expanded complex now features ten majestic minarets visible across Madinah.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What was the 'Bab al-Uthman' / 'Bab Jibril' distinction on the eastern side of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: They are bridges across Wadi al-Aqiq
Bab Jibril sits opposite the Sacred Chamber's northern side, while Bab al-Baqi sits further south along the eastern wall
Both are on the western wall
explanationEn: On the eastern wall facing Jannat al-Baqi, Bab Jibril, Bab al-Nisa, and Bab al-Baqi each preserve distinct early historical landmarks.

questionEn: Which area inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is known as 'Bab al-Majidi' along the northern historic edge?
optionsEn: The southern gate leading to Quba
The northern gate erected during Sultan Abdulmecid's 19th-century Ottoman renovation
explanationEn: Named after Sultan Abdulmecid I, Bab al-Majidi stood along the northern wall of the Ottoman mosque before later expansions.

questionEn: Which companion of Al-Suffah was a former slave from Rome (Byzantium) who gave up all his accumulated wealth in Makkah just to reach Madinah and the Prophet ﷺ?
explanationEn: When Quraysh demanded Suhayb's (RA) wealth in exchange for letting him emigrate, he revealed where it was hidden; upon hearing this in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Suhayb has made a profitable trade!'

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed honoring Suhayb al-Rumi's (RA) sacrifice to emigrate to Madinah and join the Prophet's ﷺ community?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:207 ('And of the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah')
explanationEn: Sacrificing every earthly possession to reach Madinah earned Suhayb (RA) eternal praise in the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which companion stayed in Al-Suffah after coming from Yemen and later served as one of the earliest governors/scholars of Islam, known for refusing to take bribes?
optionsEn: Mu'adh ibn Jabal / Abu Dharr / Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' (RA) among Ahl al-Suffah's scholars
explanationEn: Among the companions associated with Al-Suffah, Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' (RA) and Abu Dharr (RA) carried strict integrity and Prophetic Hadith across the Muslim world.

questionEn: What remarkable sign of humility did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show when entering Madinah's mosque or sitting among his Companions in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: He sat wherever a space opened in the circle without a raised throne, so strangers had to ask 'Which of you is Muhammad?'
He required visitors to kneel before approaching
explanationEn: Even delegations arriving at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi could not tell him apart by royal dress or seating, testifying to his unmatched humility.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once forbid a companion from wearing a gold signet ring inside Madinah, tossing it aside while teaching simplicity?
optionsEn: Because silver was unavailable in Madinah
Because rings were banned for women too
Because gold rings and silk garments are unlawful for men in Islam
Because the ring belonged to Quraysh
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ wore a simple silver signet ring engraved 'Muhammad Rasul Allah'—later lost in Bir Aris—and forbade men from gold jewelry.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Clothing and Adornment

questionEn: Which door of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was historically called 'Bab Uthman' or 'Bab al-Jana'iz' (Gate of Funerals) on the eastern side?
optionsEn: The western gate leading toward Jeddah
The eastern gate facing Jannat al-Baqi through which funeral biers are carried out after Janazah prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: Today as well, funeral prayers (Salat al-Janazah) are offered after every obligatory prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and biers exit smoothly through the eastern doors toward Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which mosque on the southern outskirts of Madinah was the very first mosque built in the history of the Islamic state in 1 AH?
explanationEn: Upon reaching the settlement of Quba in Rabi al-Awwal 1 AH, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ laid the foundation of Masjid Quba before entering central Madinah.

questionEn: At whose home in Quba did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stay upon arriving from Makkah before moving into central Madinah?
optionsEn: Kulthum ibn al-Hidm (RA) of Banu Amr ibn Awf
explanationEn: While residing with Kulthum ibn al-Hidm (RA) in Quba for several days—and receiving guests in Sa'd ibn Khaythamah's house—the Prophet ﷺ founded Masjid Quba.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Whose nearby home in Quba—nicknamed 'Bayt al-Uzzab' (House of the Bachelors)—did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ use to sit and teach visiting Muslims?
explanationEn: Single emigrants frequently stayed at Sa'd ibn Khaythamah's (RA) home in Quba, where the Prophet ﷺ held gatherings during his stay before Friday.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse in Surah At-Tawbah (9:108) refers directly to a mosque 'founded on righteousness (taqwa) from the first day'?
optionsEn: Surah At-Tawbah 9:108, applied by scholars and Hadith to Masjid Quba (and also Al-Masjid an-Nabawi)
explanationEn: Many Companions and classical commentators cite Surah At-Tawbah 9:108 in praise of Masjid Quba, while Sahih Muslim also records the Prophet ﷺ applying it to his own mosque in Madinah.

questionEn: What remarkable habit of the residents of Quba earned Allah's praise in Surah At-Tawbah 9:108: 'In it are men who love to purify themselves'?
optionsEn: They purified themselves thoroughly with water (combined with stones) after relieving themselves
They bathed in seawater every morning
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ asked the people of Quba why Allah praised their purity, they explained that they followed up dry cleansing with water—establishing a lasting Sunnah of istinja.

questionEn: On which day of the week did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly visit Masjid Quba—either riding or walking?
optionsEn: Only once a year on Eid
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet ﷺ used to go to Masjid Quba every Saturday, riding or on foot, and pray two rak'ahs there.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, which famous Companion strictly maintained the Prophet's ﷺ Saturday habit of visiting Masjid Quba throughout his entire life?
explanationEn: So devoted was Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) to following every Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ that he visited Masjid Quba every Saturday without fail.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer in Makkah and Madinah

questionEn: What condition is mentioned in the Hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) for receiving the reward of an Umrah when praying at Masjid Quba?
optionsEn: Bringing a sacrificial camel from Makkah
Purifying oneself (making Wudu) at home, then coming to Masjid Quba and praying in it
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Whoever purifies himself in his house, then comes to Masjid Quba and prays a prayer therein, will have a reward like that of an Umrah.'

questionEn: Who joined Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at Quba in 1 AH after staying behind three days in Makkah to return people's entrusted valuables?
explanationEn: After fulfilling the Prophet's ﷺ trust by returning deposits to their owners in Makkah, Ali (RA) walked by night to catch up with the Prophet ﷺ in Quba with blistered feet.

questionEn: Which Companion reportedly placed the very first boundary stone for Masjid Quba after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ laid the initial Qiblah stone?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA), followed by Umar (RA) and Uthman (RA)
explanationEn: As the Prophet ﷺ personally carried a heavy stone to mark the Qiblah wall of Masjid Quba, Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA) eagerly placed the next stones alongside him.

questionEn: Who served as the regular Imam of Masjid Quba in the early days before the Prophet's ﷺ arrival, leading senior emigrants like Abu Bakr and Umar (RA)?
explanationEn: Because Salim Mawla Abi Hudhayfah (RA) had memorized the most Qur'an among the first emigrants arriving in Quba, he led the prayer for companions including Umar (RA).

questionEn: Which devoted Ansari companion led prayer at Masjid Quba and used to begin every single rak'ah with Surah Al-Ikhlas ('Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad') before reciting another surah?
optionsEn: Kulthum ibn al-Hidm / an Ansari Imam of Quba narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari
explanationEn: When his congregants asked why he always recited Surah Al-Ikhlas in every rak'ah, he replied: 'Because I love it!' The Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'

questionEn: Who appointed Sa'd al-Qaraz (RA) as the Muezzin of Masjid Quba?
explanationEn: While Bilal and Ibn Umm Maktum called the Adhan at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ appointed Sa'd al-Qaraz (RA) as Muezzin at Masjid Quba.

questionEn: Approximately how far south of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is Masjid Quba situated?
explanationEn: Masjid Quba sits roughly 3.5–5 kilometers south of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—an easy walking distance along the historic Quba walkway today.

questionEn: Which Umayyad governor of Madinah carried out the first monumental stone expansion of Masjid Quba and added its first minaret and courtyard arcades?
explanationEn: During his governorship (87–93 AH), Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz rebuilt Masjid Quba with carved stone, mosaic ornamentation, and its first tall minaret.

questionEn: How many minarets rise above the modern expanded Masjid Quba today?
optionsEn: Four tall corner minarets (with numerous white domes)
explanationEn: Reconstructed beautifully in the late 20th century while honoring its historic footprint, Masjid Quba features four iconic white minarets and over fifty white domes.

questionEn: What is the name of the tree-lined pedestrian avenue recently developed connecting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi directly to Masjid Quba?
explanationEn: Today's pedestrian Quba Walkway allows pilgrims to stroll safely on foot between Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and Masjid Quba in revival of the Prophet's ﷺ Saturday walk.

questionEn: Which area adjacent to Al-Awali and Quba was known as 'Al-Sunh', where Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) lived and tended his household after the Hijrah?
optionsEn: Al-Sunh (in Upper Madinah, eastern outskirts near Quba)
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) lived at Al-Sunh with his Ansari wife Habibah bint Kharijah and rode to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for leadership and prayer.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Where was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) when he received the devastating news of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ passing on Monday, 12 Rabi al-Awwal 11 AH?
optionsEn: At his residence in Al-Sunh on the outskirts of Madinah
explanationEn: Having been reassured earlier that morning that the Prophet's ﷺ fever had eased, Abu Bakr (RA) rode to Al-Sunh, only to rush back upon hearing the tragic news and steady the Ummah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which mosque east of Masjid Quba—originally known as Masjid Bani al-Nadir or Masjid al-Shams—is nicknamed 'Masjid al-Fadih'?
optionsEn: The mosque where the Qiblah changed
The mosque where Companions poured out their jars of date-wine the moment alcohol was prohibited
The mosque built atop Mount Uhud
explanationEn: When the final prohibition of intoxicants (Surah 5:90) was announced in Madinah, Companions gathered at this house/mosque immediately spilled their vessels of fadih (date-wine) into the street.

questionEn: Which historic mosque in Quba marks the residence/prayer spot of Banu Unayf, where the Prophet ﷺ used to pray when visiting Talhah ibn al-Bara'?
explanationEn: Located southwest of Masjid Quba, Masjid Bani Unayf commemorates where the Prophet ﷺ prayed when visiting his sick Companion Talhah ibn al-Bara' (RA).

questionEn: What touching request did the young Ansari companion Talhah ibn al-Bara' (RA) of Banu Unayf make on his deathbed in Madinah?
optionsEn: He asked to delay his burial for two weeks
He asked to be buried in Taif
He asked his family to bury him quickly at night and not disturb the Prophet ﷺ if he feared danger from hostile locals on the road
explanationEn: Out of sheer protective love for the Prophet ﷺ, Talhah (RA) wished not to risk the Prophet's ﷺ safety at night; in the morning the Prophet ﷺ stood over his grave and prayed for Allah to smile upon Talhah.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Ibn Hajar, Al-Isabah

questionEn: Which early mosque sits just north of Masjid Quba in Wadi Ranuna where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ led the very first Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer after leaving Quba?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Jumu'ah (also called Masjid Wadi Ranuna or Masjid Atikah)
explanationEn: On Friday, 12 (or 16) Rabi al-Awwal 1 AH, as the Prophet ﷺ rode from Quba into central Madinah, the time for Jumu'ah arrived in the valley of Banu Salim ibn Awf (Wadi Ranuna), so he led the first Jumu'ah there.

questionEn: Which Medinan tribe resided in Wadi Ranuna and hosted Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for his historic first Friday prayer on his way from Quba to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Banu Salim ibn Awf welcomed the Prophet ﷺ in their valley of Ranuna, where roughly a hundred Muslims gathered for the inaugural Jumu'ah khutbah and prayer.

questionEn: Who had already established the very first Jumu'ah gathering in Madinah even before Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ Hijrah arrival, in the courtyard of Banu Bayadah?
optionsEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) (along with Mus'ab ibn Umayr RA)
explanationEn: Before the Prophet ﷺ migrated, As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) gathered the early Medinan converts at Naqi' al-Khadamat (Hazm al-Nabit) for Friday prayers, with about forty men attending.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah (Sahih)

questionEn: On which day of the week did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrive in Quba during his Hijrah from Makkah?
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Quba on a Monday in Rabi al-Awwal, stayed through Thursday, and departed toward central Madinah on Friday morning.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Which mosque near Quba—often called 'Masjid al-Nur' or 'Masjid Musabbah'—is associated with the Prophet's ﷺ arrival stop before entering Quba or praying Dawn?
optionsEn: Masjid Musabbah (near the southern approach to Quba)
explanationEn: Historically identified in Al-Awali/Quba records, Masjid Musabbah marks a resting spot where the Prophet ﷺ prayed dawn prayer on his early approach.

questionEn: Which mosque in central-west Madinah marks the historic location where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ prayed while facing two different Qiblahs in the same prayer?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Qiblatayn (Mosque of the Two Qiblahs)
explanationEn: Situated in the quarter of Banu Salimah northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Masjid al-Qiblatayn preserves the memory of the revelation turning prayers from Jerusalem to Makkah.

questionEn: Which Medinan clan's neighborhood housed Masjid al-Qiblatayn when the Qiblah command was revealed in 2 AH?
explanationEn: Masjid al-Qiblatayn was originally called Masjid Bani Salimah because it served that Ansari clan on the northwestern side of Madinah.

questionEn: In what Islamic month of 2 AH was the Qiblah changed from Bayt al-Maqdis toward the Kaaba in Makkah?
optionsEn: Rajab (or Sha'ban according to other classical historians) of 2 AH
explanationEn: After praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months in Madinah, Allah revealed Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144 in mid-2 AH directing Muslims to face Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: During which specific daily prayer did the congregation at Masjid Bani Salimah (Qiblatayn) or Quba receive word of the Qiblah change and physically pivot mid-prayer?
optionsEn: Dhuhr or Asr prayer (at Masjid Bani Salimah), and Fajr the next morning (at Masjid Quba)
explanationEn: Narrations describe the Prophet ﷺ turning during Dhuhr/Asr (while leading prayer at Bani Salimah or his mosque), and a messenger calling out at Quba during Fajr the next morning so the congregation turned 180 degrees mid-salah.

questionEn: How many degrees did the praying congregation at Masjid al-Qiblatayn pivot inside the prayer hall when turning from Jerusalem to Makkah?
explanationEn: Because Jerusalem lies north of Madinah and Makkah lies south of Madinah, turning from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Kaaba required rotating roughly 180 degrees so the Imam and rows reversed direction.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage reassured anxious Muslims that the prayers of companions who died before the Qiblah changed to Makkah were completely accepted by Allah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:143 ('And never would Allah have caused your faith [prayers] to be lost')
explanationEn: When Companions asked about brothers like As'ad ibn Zurarah and Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur who passed away praying toward Jerusalem, Allah revealed that their sincere faith and earlier prayers were fully rewarded.

questionEn: Why did Masjid al-Qiblatayn historically preserve two Mihrabs inside its architecture until its late-20th-century renovation?
optionsEn: Because the architect forgot which wall was south
So two separate congregations could pray simultaneously
To commemorate both the original northern Qiblah toward Jerusalem and the permanent southern Qiblah toward Makkah
One was used only in winter and one in summer
explanationEn: For centuries, Masjid al-Qiblatayn displayed a secondary decorative niche on the northern wall opposite the active southern Mihrab; during modern reconstruction the active Makkah Mihrab was kept prominent while a plaque/mark recalls the northern Qiblah.

questionEn: Which famous open-air mosque southwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi stands on the historic 'Musalla' site where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ led Eid and Istisqa (rain) prayers?
explanationEn: Except once during heavy rain, the Prophet ﷺ regularly led Eid prayers and Istisqa (rain-seeking) prayers outdoors at Al-Musalla; later Masjid al-Ghamamah was built on that site.

questionEn: In addition to Eid and Istisqa prayers, what rare funeral prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lead at the Musalla (site of Masjid al-Ghamamah)?
optionsEn: Salat al-Janazah in absentia (Salat al-Gha'ib) for Al-Najashi (Ashamah, the Negus of Abyssinia)
explanationEn: On the very day King Ashamah (Al-Najashi) passed away in Abyssinia, Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ, who walked out with the Companions to the Musalla, lined them up in rows, and offered four-takbir Janazah prayer for him.

questionEn: What distinctive architectural feature distinguishes the exterior of Masjid al-Ghamamah in Madinah?
optionsEn: Dark basalt volcanic stones and a row of white domes over its prayer hall
explanationEn: Restored in the Ottoman era using Madinah's dark basalt stone with white-washed domes, Masjid al-Ghamamah stands gracefully in the southwestern plaza near Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which three small historic mosques named after the Rightly Guided Caliphs sit near Masjid al-Ghamamah around the old Musalla plaza?
optionsEn: Masjid Talhah, Masjid Zubayr, and Masjid Sa'd
Masjid Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Masjid Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Masjid Ali ibn Abi Talib
Masjid Bilal, Masjid Salman, and Masjid Ammar
Masjid Mu'awiyah, Masjid Yazid, and Masjid Marwan
explanationEn: Located steps from Masjid al-Ghamamah, these historic neighborhood mosques mark places where those senior Caliphs led Eid or resided/prayed near the Musalla.

questionEn: Which mosque north of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (in the quarter of Banu Mu'awiyah) is named 'Masjid al-Ijabah' (Mosque of Answered Prayer)?
optionsEn: The mosque where Salman dug the trench
The mosque where the Qiblah changed
The mosque where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ made three great supplications for his Ummah, two of which Allah granted immediately
The mosque where the treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ prayed two rak'ahs at Banu Mu'awiyah's mosque and asked Allah for three things: not to destroy his Ummah by famine (granted), not to destroy them by drowning (granted), and not to cause internal strife among them (withheld).

questionEn: What was the third supplication Prophet Muhammad ﷺ made at Masjid al-Ijabah that Allah, in His divine wisdom, did not grant?
optionsEn: That Muslims would never travel by sea
That rain would fall every day in Madinah
That his Ummah would never experience internal conflict and fighting among themselves
explanationEn: While Allah promised never to annihilate the entire Ummah through global famine or external conquest by a single enemy, He decreed that internal tests and disagreements would remain a trial for believers.

questionEn: Which mosque north of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—also called 'Masjid al-Shukr' or 'Masjid Abi Dharr'—commemorates a remarkably long prostration by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: When Jibril (AS) brought glad tidings that whoever sends one Salawat upon him receives ten blessings from Allah, the Prophet ﷺ fell into a lengthy prostration of gratitude (Sujud al-Shukr) at this spot.

questionEn: Which historic mosque near the southern edge of Madinah (near Anbariya) marks the spot where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reviewed the Muslim army before departing for the Battle of Badr?
explanationEn: At Suqya Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, the Prophet ﷺ inspected the troops marching to Badr, sent back young boys like Umayr ibn Abi Waqqas initially (until Umayr wept and was permitted), and prayed for Madinah's blessings.

questionEn: Which mosque perched on a small rocky hill ('Jabal Dhubab') northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi marks where Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ command tent and banner stood during the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: During the siege of Khandaq in 5 AH, the Prophet ﷺ pitched his red leather dome/tent on Jabal Dhubab overlooking the trench; the mosque built there is known as Masjid al-Rayah.

questionEn: Which small mosque near Jabal Sal' marks the cavern/shelter where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ slept and prayed during the digging of the Trench, and where Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) invited him for a miraculous feast?
explanationEn: Located at the base of Mount Sal' in the Banu Haram quarter, this historic site recalls the Prophet's ﷺ nights during Khandaq and Jabir's (RA) modest meal that fed hundreds.

questionEn: Which grand mosque standing at Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) roughly 10 km southwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is also historically called 'Masjid al-Shajarah'?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Miqat (Dhul-Hulayfah), where pilgrims departing Madinah enter Ihram for Hajj and Umrah
explanationEn: Called Masjid al-Shajarah after the tree beneath which the Prophet ﷺ rested and prayed before entering Ihram, Dhul-Hulayfah is the farthest Miqat from Makkah and the designated Miqat for Madinah.

questionEn: What is the historical name of the famous Madinah well purchased and endowed as a public charity by Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA)?
optionsEn: Bir Ruma (also known today as Bir Uthman)
explanationEn: When the Muhajirun struggled with brackish water in Madinah, only Bir Ruma had sweet water; its owner sold water at high cost until Uthman (RA) purchased it and dedicated it free to all.

questionEn: How did Uthman ibn Affan (RA) persuade the owner of Bir Ruma to sell the well when the owner initially refused to part with the whole well?
optionsEn: He dug a canal draining it
He traded Mount Uhud for it
Uthman first bought half of the well (alternating days) for 12,000 dirhams, then bought the remaining half when his free day drew all the customers
He seized the well by force
explanationEn: On Uthman's (RA) free day, citizens drew enough water for two days; seeing his profits vanish, the owner agreed to sell the second half as well, creating one of the longest-running awqaf in history!

questionEn: What eternal reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise to whoever would buy Bir Ruma and share its sweet water freely with the Muslims?
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (mu'allaq) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi (Hasan), the Prophet ﷺ promised Paradise and a superior well in Jannah to the buyer of Bir Ruma, prompting Uthman (RA) to step forward.

questionEn: What remarkable modern legacy continues today from the historic date palm orchard surrounding Bir Uthman (Bir Ruma) in Madinah?
optionsEn: It only grows wheat for horses
The orchard still functions as a registered Islamic endowment (waqf) producing dates whose proceeds support charity and orphans/poor
It belongs privately to a foreign bank
explanationEn: Maintained for over 1,400 years as a living charitable endowment (waqf), the orchard around Bir Uthman still yields dates and charity in Uthman's (RA) ongoing Sadaqah Jariyah.

questionEn: Which well in Quba/Al-Awali did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ call 'a well from the wells of Paradise' and ask to be washed with seven waterskins from it after his passing?
explanationEn: Narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), the Prophet ﷺ drank from Bir Ghars, blessed it, and instructed: 'When I die, wash me with seven skins of water from Bir Ghars.'

questionEn: Which well near Masjid Quba became famous in Islamic history as 'Bir al-Khatam' (Well of the Signet Ring)?
explanationEn: While Caliph Uthman (RA) sat on the edge of Bir Aris in the sixth year of his caliphate, the Prophet's ﷺ silver signet ring slipped from his finger into the deep well and was never recovered despite draining it for three days.

questionEn: Which four leaders sat together with their feet dangling into Bir Aris in a famous Hadith narrated by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA)?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, and Mu'awiyah
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), Umar (RA), and Uthman (RA)
explanationEn: Sitting on the rim of Bir Aris, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman each received glad tidings of Paradise from the Prophet ﷺ—with Uthman told he would enter Paradise alongside a severe trial.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: What three words were engraved vertically in three lines on the silver signet ring that slipped into Bir Aris?
explanationEn: Read from bottom to top—'Allah' at the top, 'Rasul' in the middle, 'Muhammad' at the bottom—so that Allah's name sat highest, this ring sealed the Prophet's ﷺ letters to kings and was passed to Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman.

questionEn: Which lush date garden right across from Al-Masjid an-Nabawi belonged to Abu Talhah al-Ansari (RA), who donated it immediately upon hearing Surah Aal Imran 3:92?
explanationEn: Hearing 'Never will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love' (3:92), Abu Talhah (RA) walked straight to the Prophet ﷺ and gave away Bir Ha—his dearest orchard whose sweet well water the Prophet ﷺ loved.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise Abu Talhah (RA) to distribute his beloved garden of Bir Ha after he donated it for Allah's sake?
optionsEn: To sell it to merchants from Syria
To distribute it among his own close relatives and cousins
To burn the trees for charcoal
To give it exclusively to strangers outside Madinah
explanationEn: Praising Abu Talhah's generosity as 'a profitable trade,' the Prophet ﷺ advised him to place it among his needy relatives such as Hassan ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA).

questionEn: Where is the historic site of Abu Talhah's (RA) Bir Ha located relative to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today?
optionsEn: At the peak of Mount Uhud
Incorporated within the northern interior expansion of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (near King Fahd Gate)
explanationEn: Originally just north of the early mosque, Bir Ha now lies beneath the grand northern prayer hall of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which ancient Madinah well northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is famous in Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) for the Hadith: 'Water is pure and nothing renders it impure'?
explanationEn: When Companions asked if they could perform Wudu from Bir Budaa'ah even though rainwater runoff carried debris toward it, the Prophet ﷺ taught the foundational fiqh principle that pure abundant water remains pure unless its color, taste, or smell changes.

questionEn: Which well near Quba (also called Bir al-Yasirah) was renamed 'Bir al-Tafilah' or 'Bir al-Adhq' / 'Bir al-Ihn' in early Medinan topography, where the Prophet ﷺ visited Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd?
explanationEn: Historical maps of early Madinah record Bir al-Ihn alongside Bir Ghars and Bir Aris among the seven blessed wells whose water the Prophet ﷺ drank and blessed.

questionEn: Which valley west of Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ hear an angel/voice from his Lord instructing him to pray in, calling it 'a blessed valley'?
explanationEn: Camping in Wadi al-Aqiq on returning toward Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ told Umar (RA): 'A messenger from my Lord came to me tonight and said: Pray in this blessed valley, and say: Umrah within a Hajj.'

questionEn: Which well-known Medinan valley was described in Hadith as flowing 'upon a mound/bank of the mounds of Paradise' alongside Wadi al-Aqiq?
optionsEn: Wadi Buthan (and Wadi Qanat in some narrations)
explanationEn: Early reports preserved in Al-Samhudi and Musnad sources highlight Madinah's major seasonal valleys—Wadi al-Aqiq, Wadi Buthan, and Wadi Qanat—as arteries of life and blessing for the Prophet's ﷺ city.

questionEn: Which companion had his historic palace/home overlooking the green stretches of Wadi al-Aqiq in the Tabi'in era?
optionsEn: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) (along with Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas RA before him)
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) and later the great scholar Urwah ibn al-Zubayr resided along Wadi al-Aqiq, whose archaeological ruins and wells remain visible today.

questionEn: How many date-palm saplings did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally plant with his own hands in Al-Aliyah to help Salman al-Farsi (RA) pay off his freedom contract (mukatabah)?
optionsEn: Three hundred date-palm shoots (alongside a piece of gold the size of an egg)
explanationEn: When Salman's (RA) master demanded 300 date-palm shoots planted and 40 uqiyah of gold, the Prophet ﷺ told the Companions to help him, then planted every sapling himself—and all survived except one planted by Umar, which the Prophet ﷺ replanted so it thrived.

questionEn: What miraculous gift did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ hand Salman al-Farsi (RA) to complete the forty uqiyah of gold needed for his freedom?
optionsEn: A gold nugget the size of a pigeon's/hen's egg that weighed out the full forty uqiyah without diminishing
A chest of Roman silver coins
explanationEn: Passing the egg-sized gold over his blessed tongue and handing it to Salman (RA), the Prophet ﷺ assured him Allah would pay his debt with it; when weighed, it yielded the exact forty uqiyah required.

questionEn: Which Jewish scholar of Banu al-Nadir embraced Islam on the morning of the Battle of Uhud and bequeathed all seven of his Madinah orchards to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: Declaring that 'Muhammad is the best of our people today' even though Uhud fell on a Saturday, Mukhayriq fought beside the Muslims and fell as a martyr; the Prophet ﷺ said 'Mukhayriq is the best of the Jews' and distributed his seven orchards as Sadaqah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do with the seven Madinah orchards bequeathed to him by Mukhayriq?
optionsEn: He sold them for personal palaces
He cut them all down for fuel
He gifted them back to Quraysh
He designated them as perpetual public endowments (Sadaqah/Awqaf) for the poor and needy of Madinah
explanationEn: Those seven gardens (including Al-A'waf, Al-Safiyah, Al-Dalal, Barqah, Husna, Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim, and Al-Mithab) became foundational Islamic awqaf supporting Madinah's poor and the Prophet's ﷺ family.

questionEn: Which of Mukhayriq's seven endowed gardens in Al-Awali was named 'Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim'?
optionsEn: The orchard residence where Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (RA) lived and gave birth to the Prophet's ﷺ son Ibrahim
explanationEn: Located in Al-Awali southeast of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim was the peaceful orchard where Mariyah (RA) raised baby Ibrahim before his passing in infancy.

questionEn: Which district of southern/southeastern Madinah is famously called 'Al-Aliyah' (or Al-Awali), prized in Hadith for its dates?
optionsEn: The western peak of Mount Radwa
The northern desert road to Tabuk
The Red Sea port of Yanbu
The elevated southern-southeastern orchard region of Madinah (including Quba and nearby villages)
explanationEn: Sitting slightly higher in elevation along Madinah's southern slope, Al-Aliyah's fertile volcanic soil produces the celebrated Ajwah dates praised by the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What special protective virtue did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state in Sahih Muslim regarding eating seven Ajwah dates of Al-Aliyah in the morning?
optionsEn: Whoever eats seven Ajwah dates of Al-Aliyah in the morning will not be harmed by poison or magic that day
They make one invisible in battle
They replace the need to sleep for a week
explanationEn: Narrated by Aishah (RA) in Sahih Muslim and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, seven Ajwah dates in the morning serve by Allah's permission as a spiritual and physical shield.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Drinks & Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What physical characteristic distinguishes Madinah's authentic Ajwah dates from larger brown date varieties?
optionsEn: They grow without pits or seeds
They are small-to-medium, dark nearly black, soft, rounded dates with fine wrinkles
They are giant foot-long yellow dates
They are bright green and triangular
explanationEn: Grown uniquely in Madinah's mineral-rich volcanic oasis soil, Ajwah dates are prized across the Muslim world for their dark hue, delicate sweetness, and Prophetic blessing.

questionEn: Which valley flows eastward past the southern side of Mount Uhud, crossing near the resting place of the Martyrs of Uhud?
explanationEn: Wadi Qanat runs along the southern base of Mount Uhud between the mountain and the city, playing a historic role in Madinah's hydrology and Uhud's battlefield topography.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray regarding Madinah's standard units of dry measurement—the Sa' and the Mudd?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, double the weight of gold in Makkah only'
'O Allah, replace the Sa' with Roman coins'
'O Allah, abolish all weights and measures'
'O Allah, bless us in our Madinah, bless us in our Sa', and bless us in our Mudd!'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ specifically supplicated for barakah in Madinah's food measures (Sa' and Mudd) so small amounts of food would nourish families abundantly.

questionEn: Approximately how many Mudds equal one prophetic Sa' of Madinah used for measuring Zakat al-Fitr and Kaffarah?
optionsEn: Four Mudds (where one Mudd equals two average adult cupped hands)
explanationEn: A Prophetic Sa' equals four Mudds—roughly 2.0 to 3.0 kilograms depending on the grain—preserving the exact standard passed down in Madinah.

questionEn: Why did Imam Abu Yusuf (student of Imam Abu Hanifah) revise his view on the exact volume of the Sa' after visiting Madinah?
optionsEn: He read a Roman inscription in Syria
He dreamed of a golden scale
He witnessed the unbroken living practice of Madinah's scholars holding actual inherited Prophetic measures passed down from the Companions
explanationEn: Seeing the physical Sa' and Mudd preserved continuously across Madinah generations convinced Abu Yusuf of the authenticity of Madinah's measurement standard.

questionEn: Which companion had his well/spring visited by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Wadi al-Aqiq/Al-Awali, or which valley did the Prophet ﷺ say should not be polluted?
optionsEn: He banned drinking water before Maghrib
He turned Wadi al-Aqiq into a salt pan
He ordered every well sealed with lead
He forbade urinating in stagnant water and praised Madinah's clean desert springs and valleys
explanationEn: Islamic environmental etiquette in Madinah emphasized safeguarding pure water sources, planting trees, and keeping valleys clean.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about anyone who plants a date-palm shoot or sows a crop in Madinah or anywhere on earth?
optionsEn: Every bite eaten from it by a human, bird, or animal is counted as ongoing charity (sadaqah) for the planter
Planting trees is disliked near mosques
Birds eating dates cancel the owner's reward
Only dates sold for gold count as good deeds
explanationEn: Even up to the Final Hour, the Prophet ﷺ encouraged planting saplings—transforming Madinah's oasis agriculture into acts of worship.

questionEn: Just as Prophet Ibrahim (AS) consecrated Makkah as a Sacred Sanctuary (Haram), who consecrated Madinah as a Sacred Sanctuary?
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declared: 'Ibrahim made Makkah a sanctuary, and I have made Madinah a sanctuary between its two lava plains (labatayha).'

questionEn: Between which two geological boundaries did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define the Haram (Sanctuary) of Madinah?
optionsEn: Between its two volcanic lava tracts (east-west) and between Mount Ayr (south) and Mount Thawr (north)
Between the Red Sea and Najd
Only within the walls of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim specify the Sanctuary's bounds: east-to-west between Harrat Waqim and Harrat al-Wabrah, and south-to-north from Mount Ayr to Mount Thawr behind Uhud.

questionEn: Where is the 'Mount Thawr' mentioned in the Hadith defining the northern boundary of Madinah's Haram?
optionsEn: South of Makkah on the road to Yemen
A small reddish-black hill directly behind (north of) Mount Uhud in Madinah—not the Cave Thawr of Makkah
explanationEn: Many pilgrims confuse Makkah's Jabal Thawr with Madinah's Jabal Thawr; the Hadith refers to a small hill north of Uhud marking the northern limit of Madinah's sanctuary.

questionEn: What environmental protections apply inside the sacred Haram boundaries of Madinah according to authentic Hadith?
optionsEn: Its wild game must not be hunted or frightened, and its naturally growing trees and thorny shrubs must not be cut
No houses may ever be built
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade shedding blood, hunting wild animals, or cutting fresh trees/thorns within Madinah's sanctuary, except green fodder needed for camels or farming tools as permitted.

questionEn: What penalty did Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) enforce when he caught a man cutting wood or hunting inside the Haram of Madinah?
optionsEn: Confiscating the offender's outer garment/equipment (salab) as taught by the Prophet ﷺ
Imprisoning the man for ten years
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) confiscated the clothing/axe of an intruder hunting/cutting trees in Madinah's Haram, refusing to return it after citing the Prophet's ﷺ explicit directive.

questionEn: To what tool did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ compare Madinah in its spiritual power to purify its community?
optionsEn: A blacksmith's bellows (kir) that blows away impurities and leaves pure iron shining
explanationEn: 'Madinah is like the bellows: it expels its dross (impurities/hypocrites) and purifies its good.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: When a Bedouin who had pledged Islam in Madinah asked the Prophet ﷺ to cancel his pledge due to fever, what happened after he left the city?
optionsEn: He walked out of Madinah, and the Prophet ﷺ remarked: 'Madinah is like a bellows—it expels its impurities and brightens its pure'
The Prophet ﷺ rode after him to force him back
explanationEn: Three times the Bedouin asked to break his pledge after falling ill with Madinah fever; the Prophet ﷺ let him go, noting that Madinah filters out those lacking patience for its sanctuary.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray early in 1 AH when the Muhajirun (including Abu Bakr and Bilal) fell severely ill with Madinah fever?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, let us return to Makkah immediately'
'O Allah, make Madinah as beloved to us as Makkah or even more beloved, make it healthy, bless its Sa' and Mudd, and transfer its fever to Al-Juhfah'
'O Allah, dry up all wells in Madinah'
explanationEn: Through the Prophet's ﷺ earnest dua, Allah cured the Companions' homesickness and fever, transforming Madinah into a healthy, deeply beloved home.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, to what living creature did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ compare Faith (Iman) returning to Madinah in the later eras?
optionsEn: 'Like a pearl sinking in the ocean'
'Like a falcon flying to the sea'
'Verily, Faith retreats to Madinah just as a snake retreats to its hole'
'Like a lion fleeing into the forest'
explanationEn: No matter how turmoil spreads across the world, authentic faith remains anchored and finds safe refuge in Madinah al-Munawwarah.

questionEn: What two great calamities did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise will NEVER enter the sanctuary of Madinah?
optionsEn: Al-Masih al-Dajjal (the False Messiah) and the Plague (al-Ta'un)
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari records: 'On the mountain passes/entrances of Madinah are angels; neither the plague nor the Dajjal will enter it.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: How will Madinah be protected when the Dajjal camps outside it on the salt marsh (Al-Jurf / Sabkhah) near the End of Times?
optionsEn: A wall of fire will melt Mount Uhud
The city will fly into the sky
Angels guarding its seven entrances will block him, and Madinah will quake three times to expel every hypocrite out to him
All residents will evacuate to Taif
explanationEn: Even the Dajjal cannot cross Madinah's guarded approaches; instead, three tremors shake hypocrites and disbelievers out of the city to join him, leaving only sincere believers inside.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, how many mountain passes/entrances of Madinah are guarded by angels against the Dajjal?
optionsEn: Every entrance/pass of Madinah (described in Hadith as the 'anqab'—narrow mountain passes/approaches, or seven gates/doors in other versions)
explanationEn: Angels stand with unsheathed swords guarding Madinah's approaches so the Dajjal cannot step inside its protected borders.

questionEn: What serious warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give to anyone who plots evil against the people of Madinah?
optionsEn: 'They will pay a tax of ten dinars'
'Whoever intends harm/deceit against the people of Madinah will dissolve just as salt dissolves in water'
'They must move to Quba for a month'
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) narrated this stark warning protecting the peace and residents of Madinah.

questionEn: What harsh curse is mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim upon anyone who introduces a wicked innovation/crime (ahdatha hadathan) in Madinah or shelters such an offender?
optionsEn: They are forgiven after one day
Upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all mankind; neither obligatory nor voluntary deeds will be accepted from them
They must pray outside Quba once
They simply pay a fine of dates
explanationEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) read this solemn ruling from the scroll kept in his sword scabbard, underscoring how gravely Islam guards Madinah's legal and spiritual integrity.

questionEn: What reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise for anyone who patiently endures the hardship, heat, and trials of living in Madinah until death?
optionsEn: 'They will never need to perform Salah'
'I will be an intercessor (shafi') or witness for him on the Day of Resurrection'
'They will inherit the palaces of Persia'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ encouraged believers not to abandon Madinah despite its desert heat or tough seasons, promising his special intercession for those who remain steadfast there.

questionEn: What heartfelt wish did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) consistently make in his Dua regarding his passing?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, let me retire to a coastal fortress'
'O Allah, spare me from leaving Makkah'
'O Allah, grant me martyrdom in Your path, and make my death in the city of Your Messenger ﷺ!'
'O Allah, let me pass away in Damascus'
explanationEn: When Hafsah (RA) wondered how martyrdom and dying peacefully in Madinah could both happen, Allah answered Umar's (RA) prayer exactly when he was martyred during Fajr prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise anyone who is able to die in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Whoever is able to die in Madinah, let him die there, for I will intercede for whoever dies there'
explanationEn: Narrated by Ibn Umar (RA) in Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah (graded Sahih), this Hadith inspired generations of righteous Muslims to spend their final years in Madinah.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid people from leaving Madinah simply in search of easier luxury elsewhere during later times?
optionsEn: Because boats could not sail from Jeddah
Because 'Madinah is better for them if only they knew!'—predicting regions like Yemen, Syria, and Iraq would lure people away with abundance
Because travel out of Arabia was sinful
Because Madinah had gold mines beneath Baqi
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ foresaw fertile lands opening up across Yemen, Sham, and Iraq, reminding believers that Madinah's spiritual worth far outweighs material ease elsewhere.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: When will Madinah become temporarily empty of inhabitants near the very end of time according to Sahih al-Bukhari?
optionsEn: Immediately after the death of Abu Bakr (RA)
Never; it stays densely populated after the trumpet
Right before the Final Hour, leaving it to wild beasts and birds, until two shepherds from Muzaynah enter seeking their sheep and find it deserted
explanationEn: Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muwatta Malik describe Madinah thriving until the very end of human history, when the last remnants are gathered for Judgment.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ dislike calling the city 'Yathrib' after the Hijrah?
optionsEn: Because it was too hard to pronounce
Because 'Yathrib' comes from a root meaning blame, reproach, or corruption (tathrib), whereas Allah named it 'Tabah' (The Pure/Good)
Because it was a Persian word
Because Makkah was also called Yathrib
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet ﷺ changed the city's name from Yathrib to Tabah and Taybah ('the pure, pleasant, wholesome city').

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse uses the old pre-Islamic name 'Yathrib' specifically on the lips of the panicked hypocrites during the Battle of the Trench?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:13 ('O people of Yathrib, there is no stand for you here, so return!')
explanationEn: The Qur'an records the hypocrites using the old name 'Yathrib' in panic, while Muslims are taught to honor the city as Al-Madinah and Taybah.

questionEn: What does the honorific title 'Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah' mean?
optionsEn: The Enlightened City (Illuminated by the light of Prophethood and Islam)
explanationEn: Madinah is affectionately known across the Muslim world as Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah—the City Illuminated by divine revelation and the Prophet's ﷺ presence.

questionEn: Which famous scholar wrote the classic encyclopedic history of Madinah titled 'Wafa al-Wafa bi Akhbar Dar al-Mustafa'?
optionsEn: Nur al-Din Ali ibn Ahmad al-Samhudi
explanationEn: Living in Madinah in the 9th century AH (15th century CE), Imam al-Samhudi compiled the most detailed topographical and historical work ever written on Madinah's mosques, wells, valleys, and monuments.

questionEn: What are the two major black basalt volcanic lava plains flanking Madinah to the east and west, forming natural defensive barriers?
optionsEn: The Empty Quarter and Rub al-Khali
explanationEn: Madinah sits in a fertile oasis basin cradled between Harrat Waqim on the east and Harrat al-Wabrah on the west—making those rocky lava beds impassable for cavalry during Khandaq.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ not need to dig a defensive trench around the eastern, western, and southern flanks of Madinah in 5 AH?
optionsEn: Because Quraysh promised not to attack from the south
Because the ocean surrounded Madinah on three sides
Because the jagged black lava plains (Harrat Waqim and Harrat al-Wabrah) and dense palm orchards/stone houses naturally fortified those sides
explanationEn: Only the open northern corridor between the two Harras (from Shaykhayn/Uhud toward Mount Sal'/Madhad) was exposed to enemy cavalry, which is where the Khandaq was dug.

questionEn: Which mountain sits directly west-northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, serving as the Muslim army's backstop during the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ positioned the Muslim camp with their backs to Mount Sal' facing the newly dug trench to the north, with Masjid al-Fath later built upon its western slope.

questionEn: Which mountain marks the southern boundary of Madinah's Haram near Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali)?
explanationEn: Standing southwest of Madinah near Wadi al-Aqiq and Dhul-Hulayfah, Jabal Ayr forms the southern pillar of Madinah's sacred boundary opposite Jabal Thawr in the north.

questionEn: What deeply affectionate words did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak in Sahih al-Bukhari when returning from a journey and catching sight of Mount Uhud?
optionsEn: 'Uhud is a cursed mountain of stone'
'Uhud will sink into the sea tomorrow'
'Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it'
explanationEn: Returning from Tabuk or Khaybar, as Mount Uhud came into view, the Prophet ﷺ pointed joyfully to it and expressed mutual love between the believers and Uhud.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What extraordinary spiritual event occurred once when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), Umar (RA), and Uthman (RA) climbed Mount Uhud together?
optionsEn: Mount Uhud split open revealing a spring of milk
Mount Uhud trembled beneath them, and the Prophet ﷺ struck it with his foot saying: 'Be still, Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a Siddiq, and two Martyrs!'
Birds carried them back to Quba
explanationEn: This Sahih al-Bukhari narration foretold the future martyrdoms of both Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and Uthman ibn Affan (RA).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: What is the approximate length of Mount Uhud stretching from east to west north of Madinah?
explanationEn: Rising roughly 1,077 meters above sea level (and ~350 meters above the Madinah plain), Mount Uhud forms a dramatic 7–8 km red-brown granite massif north of the city.

questionEn: Which small hill standing directly south across the valley from Mount Uhud was originally called 'Jabal Aynayn' before the Battle of Uhud?
explanationEn: Named Jabal al-Rumat after the fifty Muslim archers stationed upon it by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in 3 AH to guard the army's rear flank.

questionEn: Where is 'Al-Ghabah' located relative to Madinah, famous in Seerah for pasturing the Prophet's ﷺ milk camels and supplying tamarisk wood for his Minbar?
optionsEn: North of Madinah along the confluence of its valleys (near Al-Aqiq / Wadi Qanat)
explanationEn: Al-Ghabah was a lush wooded lowland north of Madinah; its tamarisk trees supplied the wood for the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' famously pursued raiders there in 6 AH.

questionEn: Which two major historical regions lay on the caravan highway south of Madinah toward Makkah, both associated with key Seerah milestones?
explanationEn: At Al-Rawha, the Prophet ﷺ prayed at a mosque on his way to Badr; at Al-Abwa lies the resting place of his noble mother Aminah bint Wahb.

questionEn: What emotional event occurred at Al-Abwa (between Makkah and Madinah) when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visited his mother Aminah's grave years later?
optionsEn: He relocated her remains to Makkah
He wept deeply—causing those around him to weep—explaining that Allah permitted him to visit her grave
He banned travelers from passing Al-Abwa
He built a golden dome over her grave
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet's ﷺ visit to Aminah's grave at Al-Abwa revealed profound filial tenderness balanced by pure Islamic monotheism.

questionEn: Which town about 150 km southwest of Madinah witnessed the decisive first military victory of the Madinan community in Ramadan 2 AH?
explanationEn: Marching out of Madinah with just over 310 companions, two horses, and seventy camels, the Prophet ﷺ and the believers won the Day of Criterion (Yawm al-Furqan) at Badr.

questionEn: Which oasis about 150 km north of Madinah was conquered in 7 AH after its fortified strongholds fell, ending external threats from the northern forts?
explanationEn: During the expedition of Khaybar (7 AH), Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) received the banner after the Prophet's ﷺ famous declaration, and the oasis's agricultural agreement strengthened Madinah's economy.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What is the historical significance of 'Al-Jurf', located just northwest of Madinah?
optionsEn: It served as the traditional military staging and camping ground for armies departing Madinah northward (such as Usamah ibn Zayd's army in 11 AH)
It was where the Qiblah changed
It was the site of the Prophet's ﷺ birth
It was the main harbor on the Red Sea
explanationEn: Armies marching toward Syria or Tabuk mustered at Al-Jurf, about 5 km northwest of central Madinah, before setting off on long campaigns.

questionEn: Which area just outside Madinah toward Al-Shaykhayn marked where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ spent the night and inspected the Muslim ranks before the Battle of Uhud?
optionsEn: Al-Shaykhayn (two historic ruined forts/hillocks north of Madinah on the road to Uhud)
explanationEn: At Al-Shaykhayn on Friday evening before Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ reviewed the youth—permitting Rifa'ah/Samurah and Rafi' ibn Khadij while sending back younger boys like Ibn Umar and Zayd ibn Thabit until the next battle.

questionEn: Which coastal port on the Red Sea roughly 220 km west of Madinah served historically as Madinah's maritime gateway?
explanationEn: Sitting due west of Madinah on the Red Sea coast, Yanbu connected the Prophet's ﷺ city to maritime trade routes and later pilgrim arrivals.

questionEn: What makes Madinah's climate and oasis setting unique compared to barren valleys like Makkah?
optionsEn: Madinah sits in a fertile oasis basin fed by underground aquifers from volcanic lava fields, famous for lush date-palm groves
It receives daily monsoon floods year-round
It lies inside a tropical rainforest
It sits atop a snow-capped alpine peak
explanationEn: Water trapped beneath the surrounding volcanic basalt beds feeds springs and wells across Madinah, sustaining tens of thousands of date palms—a striking fulfillment of Ibrahim's and Muhammad's ﷺ prayers for its bounty.

questionEn: Which mosque in Madinah is associated with Banu Zafar (also called 'Masjid al-Baghlah') southeast of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, where the Prophet ﷺ sat on a stone and listened to Ibn Mas'ud recite Surah An-Nisa?
explanationEn: Located east of Jannat al-Baqi in the quarter of Banu Zafar, this historic spot recalls where the Prophet ﷺ wept while Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) recited Surah An-Nisa up to verse 4:41.

questionEn: Which historic mosque near Masjid al-Ghamamah is named 'Masjid al-Musalla' or commemorates Abu Bakr's (RA) Eid prayers?
optionsEn: Masjid Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA), located directly northwest of Masjid al-Ghamamah
explanationEn: Preserved as a historic stone-domed monument near the western piazza, Masjid Abu Bakr sits adjacent to Masjid al-Ghamamah where Eid prayers were held.

questionEn: What happened to the Muslim congregation at Masjid Quba on the morning after Surah Al-Baqarah (2:144) changed the Qiblah toward Makkah?
optionsEn: They waited a month for a written letter
A messenger arrived during Fajr prayer announcing the revelation, and the entire congregation rotated mid-prayer from Jerusalem to Makkah
They abandoned Fajr and restarted at Dhuhr
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that while people at Quba were bowing in Fajr, a caller proclaimed the Qiblah change, and they turned straight toward the Kaaba without breaking their prayer.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ decline to destroy 'Masjid al-Dirar' personally and instead order Companions to demolish and burn it upon returning from Tabuk in 9 AH?
optionsEn: Because it was built without stone columns
Because it stood too close to Mount Uhud
Because Surah At-Tawbah (9:107-110) exposed it as a mosque built by hypocrites in Quba solely to cause harm, disbelief, and division among believers
Because it had no water well nearby
explanationEn: Built by Abu Amir al-Rahib's allies near Quba to lure Muslims away from Masjid Quba and plot treason, the Qur'an forbade the Prophet ﷺ from ever standing in it, commanding instead to stand in the mosque founded on Taqwa.

questionEn: Which two righteous Companions did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ dispatch from Dhu Awan (near Madinah) to dismantle Masjid al-Dirar?
optionsEn: Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and Ma'n ibn Adi (or Amir ibn al-Sakan)
explanationEn: Ordered by the Prophet ﷺ right before re-entering Madinah from Tabuk, Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and Ma'n ibn Adi tore down and burned the treacherous structure.

questionEn: Which tree species gave its name to 'Masjid al-Shajarah' at Dhul-Hulayfah?
optionsEn: An acacia/samurah tree beneath which Prophet Muhammad ﷺ rested and put on Ihram
explanationEn: Located on the rim of Wadi al-Aqiq at Dhul-Hulayfah, the Prophet ﷺ regularly halted beneath that samurah tree, prayed two rak'ahs, and proclaimed the Talbiyah before heading toward Makkah.

questionEn: What is the modern popular name for Dhul-Hulayfah, the Madinah Miqat station?
explanationEn: Dhul-Hulayfah became widely known as Abyar Ali due to historic wells dug and maintained along the pilgrim caravan stop south of Madinah.

questionEn: How many Rak'ahs did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray at Dhul-Hulayfah before mounting Al-Qaswa and starting the Talbiyah for Hajj?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs (the regular prayer/Dhuhr shortened or two voluntary rak'ahs at the blessed valley)
explanationEn: Pilgrims departing Madinah today stop at the grand Masjid al-Miqat in Dhul-Hulayfah to bathe (ghusl), wear Ihram garments, pray two rak'ahs (or the obligatory prayer if its time has entered), and make their Umrah/Hajj intention.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, at what exact point at Dhul-Hulayfah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ raise his voice with the Talbiyah ('Labbayk Allahumma labbayk')?
optionsEn: After praying at Masjid Dhul-Hulayfah and mounting his camel at Al-Bayda (once his mount stood upright and set off)
At the foot of Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Narrators reconciled slight variations by explaining he first spoke the Talbiyah quietly upon finishing prayer at the mosque, then raised his voice clearly once his camel stood at Al-Bayda overlooking the valley.

questionEn: Which companion was instructed by the Prophet ﷺ at Wadi al-Aqiq to perform 'Umrah within a Hajj' during the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself received the command from Allah to proclaim 'Umratan fi Hajjah' (Hajj Qiran) in Wadi al-Aqiq
Abu Dharr was ordered to stay behind
Bilal was ordered to return to Quba
Salman was ordered to fast for a year
explanationEn: Camping in Wadi al-Aqiq after leaving Dhul-Hulayfah, the Prophet ﷺ heard a heavenly caller say: 'Pray in this blessed valley and say: Umrah within a Hajj.'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the number of days a Muhajir (emigrant who left Makkah) was allowed to remain back in Makkah after completing Hajj or Umrah?
optionsEn: They were commanded to move back to Makkah permanently
No more than three days after finishing the rites, because Makkah had ceased to be their permanent home after migrating to Madinah
explanationEn: Out of reverence for the irreversible commitment of Hijrah to Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ limited returning emigrants to three days in Makkah post-rites (e.g., Sa'd ibn Khawlah's tragedy of dying in Makkah).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ feel sorrow for Sa'd ibn Khawlah (RA) when he passed away in Makkah?
optionsEn: Because Sa'd had emigrated to Madinah for Allah's sake and the Prophet ﷺ disliked seeing an emigrant die in the land he had migrated away from
Because Sa'd had never prayed in Madinah
Because Sa'd refused to perform Hajj
Because Sa'd lost his sword at Badr
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ visited Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas when ill in Makkah and expressed compassion for Sa'd ibn Khawlah who died in the very city he had left during Hijrah.

questionEn: What pledge did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make to the Ansar of Madinah right after the Battle of Hunayn when some young Ansar feared he might settle back in Makkah after its conquest?
optionsEn: 'I will move the capital back to Makkah next year'
'Life is with you and death is with you; if all mankind walked one valley and the Ansar walked another, I would walk the valley of the Ansar!'
'Stay in Taif while I return to Quba'
explanationEn: Overwhelmed with tears of joy, the Ansar heard the Prophet ﷺ affirm his lifelong loyalty to Madinah: 'Are you not pleased that people go home with sheep and camels while you go home with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to your dwellings?'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the special duty of love toward the Ansar of Madinah as a sign of true faith?
optionsEn: 'Loving the Ansar is only for residents of Quba'
'Only elders need to respect the Ansar'
'The sign of faith (Iman) is loving the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy (Nifaq) is hating the Ansar'
explanationEn: Recorded in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, loving the Ansar who welcomed Islam and sheltered Madinah is an explicit hallmark of genuine faith.

questionEn: Which prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeatedly make for the Ansar, their children, and their grandchildren?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, forgive the Ansar, the children of the Ansar, and the grandchildren of the Ansar!'
'O Allah, transfer them all to Egypt'
'O Allah, give them control over Rome alone'
'O Allah, exempt them from fasting Ramadan'
explanationEn: Repeatedly praying for forgiveness across generations of the Ansar showed the Prophet's ﷺ boundless gratitude for Madinah's hosts.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Among the four main branches of the Ansar in Madinah, which tribe did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare 'the best of the houses of the Ansar'?
optionsEn: Banu al-Najjar (followed by Banu Abd al-Ashhal, Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Banu Sa'idah)
explanationEn: Asked which Ansari houses were best, the Prophet ﷺ ranked Banu al-Najjar first—his maternal relatives through Hashim's wife Salma—while affirming goodness in every house of the Ansar.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: What family connection did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ already share with Banu al-Najjar of Madinah long before the Hijrah?
optionsEn: His uncle Abu Talib governed Madinah
His mother Aminah was born in Persia
His great-grandmother Salma bint Amr (mother of Abd al-Muttalib) belonged to Banu al-Najjar, and his father Abdullah passed away there
His grandfather Hashim lived in Khaybar
explanationEn: Before the Hijrah, young Muhammad ﷺ had visited his maternal uncles of Banu al-Najjar in Madinah with his mother Aminah and Umm Ayman, even learning to swim in their pond/well.

questionEn: Where in Madinah was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ father, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, buried after falling ill on a trade return from Gaza/Syria?
optionsEn: In Dar al-Nabighah (among Banu al-Najjar in Madinah), months before the Prophet's ﷺ birth
explanationEn: Stopping to visit his maternal relatives of Banu al-Najjar on his journey home, Abdullah fell ill and passed away in Madinah at around age 25, leaving Aminah expecting the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recall his childhood visit to Madinah with his mother Aminah when he later migrated there as a Messenger?
optionsEn: He arrived in Madinah from Iraq
He recognized Dar al-Nabighah where his father was buried and the house/pool of Banu Adi ibn al-Najjar where he learned to swim as a six-year-old boy
He had never heard of Madinah before 1 AH
He visited Madinah only after the Conquest of Makkah
explanationEn: Those poignant childhood memories of Madinah—where he stayed with his mother Aminah before losing her at Al-Abwa on the return trip—bound his heart early to Madinah.

questionEn: What two great Arab tribes dominated Yathrib before Islam and suffered decades of bloody civil war before welcoming Islam?
explanationEn: Descended from two Yemeni brothers from Al-Azd, Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj fought exhausting tribal wars—culminating in the Battle of Bu'ath—until Islam united them as the Ansar.

questionEn: What was the 'Battle of Bu'ath' that took place about five years before the Hijrah in Madinah?
optionsEn: A battle between Persia and Rome
A naval battle on the Red Sea
A devastating civil war between Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj in which most of their elder warlords perished
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) remarked that Allah brought about the Battle of Bu'ath beforehand so the proud tribal chiefs would fall and leave the younger generation of Madinah open and yearning for peace under Islam.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Why did the Jewish tribes of Yathrib (such as Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah) indirectly prepare Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj to recognize Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Whenever disputes arose, they used to tell the Arabs: 'Soon a prophet will be sent whose time is near, and with him we shall overcome you'
They taught the Arabs the Arabic Qur'an
They migrated to Makkah every year
explanationEn: When the pilgrims from Yathrib heard Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at Al-Aqabah, they instantly told one another: 'By Allah, this is the very prophet the Jews warned us about—let us not let them beat us to him!'

questionEn: What did Surah Al-Baqarah (2:89) observe about those who had long awaited the coming Prophet in Madinah once he actually arrived?
optionsEn: Although they previously prayed for victory over disbelievers through the expected prophet, when the truth came to them from outside their lineage, many rejected him out of envy
They had never heard of any prophet before
Every single inhabitant immediately accepted him without exception
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:89 highlights the tragedy of recognizing the truth yet rejecting it due to pride—contrasted with sincere Jewish scholars of Madinah like Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) who embraced Islam at once.

questionEn: Who was the foremost Jewish rabbi and scholar of Madinah who accepted Islam immediately upon seeing Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ face and hearing his first public words in Madinah?
explanationEn: Looking closely at the Prophet's ﷺ face upon his arrival, Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) knew instantly 'that his face was not the face of a liar' and embraced Islam after testing him with three prophetic questions.

questionEn: What were the four timeless universal directives Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) heard as the very first public advice spoken by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Build high castles, hoard silver, close your gates, and distrust strangers'
'Leave Madinah, avoid markets, and remain silent'
'Fight every traveler, fast every day, and abandon families'
'Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, uphold ties of kinship, and pray at night while people sleep—and you will enter Paradise in peace'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah (Sahih), those four foundational pillars—peace, generosity, family love, and night devotion—defined the new society of Madinah.

questionEn: Which companion from Al-Khazraj was chosen by the Prophet ﷺ to host the first great Muslim ambassador to Madinah (Mus'ab ibn Umayr RA) before the Hijrah?
explanationEn: Staying in As'ad ibn Zurarah's (RA) home in Madinah, Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) taught the Qur'an so persuasively that almost every household of Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj embraced Islam within one year.

questionEn: Which two powerful chiefs of Banu Abd al-Ashhal in Madinah accepted Islam on the exact same day after listening to Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) recite the Qur'an by a well (Bir Maraq)?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Ubayy and Abu Amir
Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As
Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA) and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
explanationEn: Arriving ready to expel Mus'ab, Usayd ibn Hudayr and then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) listened calmly to the Qur'an, embraced Islam, and led the entire clan of Banu Abd al-Ashhal into Islam by nightfall.

questionEn: What happened to the sacred idols of Banu Salimah in Madinah, such as the wooden idol of Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA), right before the Hijrah?
optionsEn: They placed it inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
Young Muslim converts like Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Mu'adh ibn Amr repeatedly tossed the old man's idol into a refuse pit at night until Amr realized its helplessness and embraced Islam
explanationEn: Finding his wooden idol 'Manaf' smeared in filth every morning despite hanging a sword around its neck to defend itself, Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA) laughed at its powerlessness and declared the Shahadah.

questionEn: Which historic mosque in Madinah marks the residence/site where the Prophet ﷺ prayed at 'Al-Fath' or 'Al-Qubab' during military assemblies—no, specifically which mosque is known as 'Masjid Al-Shaykhayn'?
optionsEn: The mosque inside Cave Thawr in Makkah
The mosque on the road to Uhud where the Prophet ﷺ led Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr prayers before the Battle of Uhud
The mosque at the port of Yanbu
explanationEn: Masjid al-Shaykhayn (also called Masjid al-Badayi' or al-Dir') marks where the Prophet ﷺ put on his armor and reviewed the Medinan ranks on the eve of Uhud.

questionEn: What is 'Masjid al-Isqiyyah' / 'Masjid al-Suqya' famous for besides troop inspection before Badr?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ performed Wudu there and made his celebrated dua asking Allah to place twice the blessing of Makkah upon Madinah
It was the first stone bridge in Madinah
It was where the treaty of Hudaybiyyah was written
It was where Bilal passed away
explanationEn: Historical accounts link the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for Madinah's barakah and purity of water to the site of Masjid al-Suqya.

questionEn: Which ancient well in Madinah was called 'Bir Quba' or located inside/beside Kulthum ibn al-Hidm's orchard?
optionsEn: Bir Adhq (or Bir Gharas nearby) in the Quba groves
explanationEn: Abu Bakr and the Prophet ﷺ rested under the shade near Bir Adhq among the date groves of Quba when they first arrived from Makkah.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ first arrived at Quba in the midday heat, why were some Muslims of Madinah who hadn't seen him before confused between him and Abu Bakr (RA)?
optionsEn: Because they arrived after midnight in darkness
Because they both wore royal crowns
Because they wore similar simple travel garments and Abu Bakr looked slightly older with graying hair until Abu Bakr stood up to shade the Prophet ﷺ with his cloak
Because the Prophet ﷺ spoke only Persian
explanationEn: When the sun shifted onto the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) immediately stepped up to shield him with his shawl, the Ansar recognized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instantly.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Which companion climbed atop a rooftop or palm tree in Quba and shouted at the top of his voice to announce Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ arrival?
optionsEn: A Jewish resident looking from a fort tower (who spotted the white-clad travelers shimmering in the mirage)
explanationEn: Spotting the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) approaching through the heat shimmer, a Jewish lookout shouted: 'O sons of Qaylah (Ansar), here is your long-awaited fortune arriving!'—sparking Madinah's joyful welcome.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: How did the Ansar of Madinah greet Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as he entered the city from Quba on Friday?
optionsEn: With Takbir, joyous hospitality, young girls of Banu al-Najjar singing welcome verses with duff drums, and every clan inviting him to stay with them
By locking their doors and hiding
explanationEn: Every clan held Al-Qaswa's reins pleading 'Stay with us, O Messenger of Allah!', to which he gently replied: 'Let her walk freely, for she is commanded by Allah.'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ decline each clan's eager invitation along the road and let his she-camel Al-Qaswa choose where to stop?
optionsEn: Because he planned to leave Madinah that evening
Because he didn't recognize any clan's name
To honor Allah's decree and prevent any jealousy or hurt feelings among the loving tribes of Madinah
Because Al-Qaswa was wild and untamed
explanationEn: Allowing Al-Qaswa to follow divine guidance ensured unity among Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj before she knelt at the mirbad of Sahl and Suhayl near Abu Ayyub's house.

questionEn: Whose home stood nearest to where Al-Qaswa knelt in central Madinah, earning him the honor of hosting Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for roughly seven months while Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was built?
optionsEn: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (Khalid ibn Zayd, RA)
explanationEn: Abu Ayyub (RA) joyfully carried the Prophet's ﷺ saddlebags inside and hosted him until the mosque and living quarters were completed.

questionEn: Why did Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) refuse to remain on the upper floor of his house above Prophet Muhammad ﷺ after moving upstairs?
optionsEn: He felt deeply uncomfortable walking over a ceiling beneath which divine revelation descended on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
Because he was afraid of heights
Because the upper roof had collapsed
explanationEn: After a water jar broke upstairs and Abu Ayyub and his wife used their own blanket to soak up every drop lest a drip fall on the Prophet ﷺ, he begged the Prophet ﷺ to move upstairs while they stayed below.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Drinks & Ibn Hisham

questionEn: What touching gesture of love did Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) and his wife Umm Ayyub practice every single evening when returning the Prophet's ﷺ leftover dinner tray?
optionsEn: They never tasted the food at all
They placed their fingers on the exact spots in the dish where the Prophet's ﷺ blessed fingers had touched to eat for barakah
They threw the leftovers to stray dogs
They sold the dish to travelers
explanationEn: This tender detail recorded in Sahih Muslim captures the genuine devotion of Madinah's hosts toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questionEn: What unusual observation did Abu Ayyub (RA) make when a garlic-seasoned dish was returned untouched by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained he avoided raw garlic/onions because he conversed intimately with angels who are offended by pungent odors, while permitting Muslims to eat them
Abu Ayyub had forgotten to cook the meal
The Prophet ﷺ declared garlic forever haram
