explanationEn: While raw garlic and onions remain halal, the Prophet ﷺ taught the etiquette of not entering mosques after eating them so neither worshippers nor angels are disturbed.

questionEn: What is the Arabic meaning of the title 'Al-Ansar' given by Allah in the Qur'an to the Muslims of Madinah?
optionsEn: The Helpers (who supported Allah's Messenger ﷺ and sheltered the emigrants)
explanationEn: Immortalized in Surah At-Tawbah (9:100, 9:117) and Surah Al-Hashr (59:9), 'Al-Ansar' honors the Medinan believers who opened their homes, hearts, and wealth to the Muhajirun.

questionEn: What is the Arabic meaning of 'Al-Muhajirun' who arrived in Madinah alongside Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: The Emigrants (who left behind homes, wealth, and kin in Makkah for the sake of Allah)
explanationEn: United with the Ansar in Madinah, the Muhajirun set the supreme example of sacrificing worldly comfort for faith and sincerity.

questionEn: Which Madinan mosque site is known as 'Masjid Bani Bayadah', located near where As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) and early converts prayed?
optionsEn: The neighborhood mosque of Banu Bayadah west/northwest of the central oasis
explanationEn: Al-Samhudi records several tribal mosques across early Madinah—such as Banu Bayadah, Banu Zafar, Banu Salimah, and Banu Haram—where the Prophet ﷺ visited and prayed.

questionEn: How did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) later show special respect to the descendants of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) and the Ansar in Madinah?
optionsEn: He moved all Ansar to Egypt
He placed the Ansar and Muhajirun at the top of the state stipend register (Diwan) and honored the Prophet's ﷺ hosts
explanationEn: When establishing the Diwan in 20 AH, Umar (RA) honored proximity to the Prophet ﷺ, early conversion, and Badr participation above lineage pride.

questionEn: Where did Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA)—the Prophet's ﷺ Madinah host—eventually pass away decades later as an elderly warrior?
optionsEn: During the expedition near the walls of Constantinople (Istanbul), fulfilling his love for striving in Allah's path
explanationEn: Even in his eighties, Abu Ayyub (RA) joined the campaign to Constantinople, citing Surah 9:41 ('Go forth, whether light or heavy'), and was buried near its city walls.

questionEn: Which Madinah landmark is 'Masjid Al-Manaratayn' (Mosque of the Two Minarets) historically known for?
optionsEn: It is inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's basement
A historic site along the old road between Madinah and Wadi al-Aqiq / Al-Anbariya where two stone markers or a mosque stood near Al-Awali/Qanat
It is the ancient name of Masjid Quba
It sits on the shore of the Red Sea
explanationEn: Recorded in classical Madinah itineraries by Al-Samhudi, Masjid al-Manaratayn stood along the western-northern corridor outside the city wall.

questionEn: What was the famous water spring/aqueduct known as 'Ayn al-Zarqa' that brought sweet water into Madinah for centuries?
optionsEn: A historic underground qanat/spring system initiated under Governor Marwan ibn al-Hakam / Mu'awiyah from Quba springs into central Madinah
A saltwater canal from the Red Sea
An ice glacier on Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Developed in the early Umayyad period from natural springs around Quba, Ayn al-Zarqa supplied public drinking fountains (sabil) around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for over a millennium.

questionEn: Which well near Quba did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ refer to when he blessed its water or used it, and what are the famous 'Seven Wells' of Madinah listed by classical scholars?
optionsEn: Aris, Ghars, Ruma, Budaa'ah, Bir Ha, Al-Ihn, and Al-Suqya (or Al-Basah)
Only one well existed in Madinah
Zamzam, Nile, Euphrates, Tigris, Jordan, Barada, and Aqiq
explanationEn: Classical scholars of Madinah such as Al-Samhudi and Ibn al-Najjar documented seven historic wells linked to the Prophet's ﷺ visits, wudu, and blessings.

questionEn: Why is it forbidden in Islamic law to carry weapons for fighting or stir bloodshed inside Madinah's Haram?
optionsEn: Because Prophet Muhammad ﷺ consecrated Madinah as a zone of peace, security, and sanctuary just like Makkah
Because iron did not exist in Arabia
Because horses could not enter the oasis
Because weapons were only allowed on Mondays
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'It is not permissible for anyone to carry weapons in Madinah for fighting.'

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about Madinah's boundaries when comparing them to Makkah's sanctity?
optionsEn: 'Animals may be hunted freely inside Madinah'
'Only Makkah has a Haram; Madinah has none'
'Madinah's Haram covers only the mosque roof'
'Makkah was Ibrahim's sanctuary, and Madinah is my sanctuary; no blood may be shed in it, nor any weapon carried to fight, nor leaves beaten off trees except for fodder'
explanationEn: This crystal-clear Hadith establishes Madinah's legal status as the second Haram (Al-Haram al-Madani).

questionEn: How do classical schools of Fiqh differ slightly on whether hunting or cutting trees inside Madinah's Haram requires a monetary expiation (fidyah/jaza) like Makkah's Haram?
optionsEn: The Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali schools affirm Madinah is a true Haram (with scholars differing on whether a physical penalty applies alongside sin, while Hanafis regard its sanctity as moral/ethical rather than carrying Hajj-style fidyah)
All four schools require sacrificing a camel for picking a single date
None of the schools ever discussed Madinah
All four schools permit hunting inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: While all scholars agree on Madinah's immense sanctity, classical manuals note the nuanced fiqh distinction regarding expiation versus sin.
reference: Al-Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim & Fiqh Encyclopedias

questionEn: Why did Imam Malik ibn Anas famously refuse to ride an animal inside the streets of Madinah even in his old age?
optionsEn: Because horses were banned in Madinah
Because he could not afford a saddle
Out of deep reverence for the soil beneath which the noble body of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ rests
explanationEn: Asked why he walked even when elderly and weak, Imam Malik replied: 'I feel shy before Allah to tread with an animal's hooves upon earth wherein lies the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'

questionEn: What special status do the inhabitants and neighbors of Madinah hold when pilgrims visit the city?
optionsEn: Pilgrims should argue loudly in markets
Pilgrims should look down on local residents
Pilgrims should avoid speaking to anyone
Pilgrims are encouraged to treat Madinah's people with respect, gentleness, and gratitude as neighbors of the Prophet's ﷺ sanctuary
explanationEn: Classical adab books remind visitors that honoring the city of the Messenger ﷺ includes kindness, patience, and upright conduct toward its residents and caretakers.

questionEn: What does the Prophetic name 'Dar al-Hijrah' mean as an enduring title for Madinah?
optionsEn: Abode of Migration (where Muslims migrated to establish Islam securely)
explanationEn: Classical historians and jurists frequently call Madinah 'Dar al-Hijrah wal-Sunnah'—the Abode of Migration and of the Prophetic Sunnah.

questionEn: Which mountain ridge just north of Madinah appears pink-red at dawn and dusk and holds the Prophet's ﷺ promise of mutual love?
explanationEn: Its distinctive reddish volcanic-granite hue and timeless bond with the Prophet ﷺ and its seventy martyrs make Mount Uhud one of Madinah's most moving sights.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Anas ibn Malik's father-in-law or companions when approaching Madinah returning from a journey and seeing the walls of Madinah?
optionsEn: He ordered everyone to close their eyes
He urged his mount faster out of eagerness and love for Madinah
He stopped ten miles outside for a month
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that whenever the Prophet ﷺ returned from travel and caught sight of Madinah's walls, he spurred his camel faster out of sheer love for the city.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Madinah

questionEn: What dua did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recite whenever returning from a journey as Madinah came into view?
optionsEn: 'Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun' (Returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord)
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, returning safely to Madinah inspired gratitude, repentance, and renewed devotion to Allah.

questionEn: Which scholar-companion settled in Madinah and taught that 'He who turns away from the Sunnah of the people of Madinah turns away from guidance' in early hadith transmission?
optionsEn: Early Imams like Malik ibn Anas highlighted Madinah's continuous collective transmission ('Amal Ahl al-Madinah) of daily worship practices like Adhan and weights
explanationEn: Because thousands of Companions lived and died in Madinah, everyday practices like the Adhan, Iqamah, and Sa' measure were passed down publicly across an entire city.

questionEn: What unique feature do the historic mosques of Madinah (such as Masjid Quba, Masjid al-Qiblatayn, and Masjid al-Ghamamah) offer visitors today?
optionsEn: Peaceful spaces to remember Seerah milestones and offer voluntary prayers while remembering that only three mosques warrant dedicated religious travel
Mandatory rituals required to validate Hajj
Substitution for Friday prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
Equal 100,000x prayer reward like the Kaaba
explanationEn: While Masjid Quba carries the specific Sunnah of a Saturday visit and Umrah-like reward for two rak'ahs after wudu at home, visiting Madinah's other historic mosques is a moving historical reflection, not an obligatory Hajj rite.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ call Madinah 'Al-Mahfuzah' or emphasize its protection in Hadith?
optionsEn: Because Allah placed angels guarding its entrances against Dajjal and plague and blessed its security as Dar al-Islam
Because it lies on an island
Because no traveler ever entered it
Because it has a steel dome over the entire city
explanationEn: Protected spiritually by divine decree and angelic guardians, Madinah stands uniquely shielded in Islamic eschatology.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the fruits and dates of Madinah when people first brought the first ripe fruits of the season to him?
optionsEn: He forbade eating fresh dates in summer
He held the first fruit to his eyes/lips, prayed 'O Allah, bless us in our fruits, our Madinah, our Sa', and our Mudd', and handed it to the youngest child present
He saved them only for kings
He threw the first fruit away
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih Muslim, this joyful Medinan Sunnah united gratitude for Allah's provision, love for Madinah, and tender affection for children.

questionEn: Which historical spring/well in Al-Aliyah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visit and drink from when visiting Banu Harithah or Banu Amr ibn Awf?
optionsEn: Bir Al-Basah (near Quba/Baqi), whose sweet water was praised in early Madinah records
explanationEn: Early historians of Madinah list Bir al-Basah among the historic sweet wells blessed by the Prophet's ﷺ visits and ablution.

questionEn: Which Companion donated or cared for the well known as 'Bir Al-Jassah' / 'Bir Ha' near the northern edge of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Abu Talhah al-Ansari (RA), whose beloved garden Bir Ha stood directly across from the northern side of the mosque
explanationEn: Abu Talhah (RA) was among the wealthiest Ansar in Madinah with numerous palm groves, yet Bir Ha was the closest and dearest to his heart—making his charity all the nobler.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to the people of Madinah regarding the water of Madinah's wells versus extravagance?
optionsEn: He charged a silver coin per bucket
He ordered all wells locked behind gates
He encouraged sharing water freely and warned against withholding surplus water from travelers or pastures
He banned sharing well water with horses
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ prohibited selling excess well water in the desert so travelers and flocks would always find mercy.

questionEn: Which historic fortress-village of Banu al-Nadir sat southeast of Madinah near Al-Awali and Quba before their expulsion in 4 AH?
optionsEn: The fortified towers of Banu al-Nadir (southeast of Madinah)
explanationEn: Following Banu al-Nadir's plot against the Prophet's ﷺ life in 4 AH, their fortified compounds southeast of Madinah surrendered peacefully as described in Surah Al-Hashr.

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an is specifically referred to by Ibn Abbas (RA) as 'Surah Bani al-Nadir' because its opening verses chronicle events in Madinah in 4 AH?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hashr recounts the peaceful evacuation of Banu al-Nadir, the principle of distributing fai' wealth fairly, and the supreme praise of both Muhajirun and Ansar.

questionEn: What historic Medinan mosque sits on the northern road near Al-Jurf/Uhud where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ prayed while resting on his return or expeditions?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Mustarah (Mosque of Resting, Banu Harithah)
explanationEn: Located along the old road between Madinah and Mount Uhud, Masjid al-Mustarah marks the spot where the Prophet ﷺ paused to rest and pray on the return from Uhud.

questionEn: Which mosque along the western side of Wadi al-Aqiq / Al-Anbariya is known as 'Masjid al-Anbariyah', built during the late Ottoman era beside the Hijaz Railway station?
explanationEn: Built in 1908 CE next to the historic Hijaz Railway terminal in Al-Anbariya, this stone mosque stands as an architectural landmark of early 20th-century Madinah.

questionEn: What historic transportation project connected Damascus to Al-Anbariya Station in Madinah in 1908 CE to ease pilgrim travel?
explanationEn: Constructed to shorten the arduous forty-day desert journey to just a few days for Hajj pilgrims, the Hijaz Railway reached Al-Anbariya Station in Madinah in 1908 CE.

questionEn: Today, what cultural purpose does the restored historic Al-Anbariya Hijaz Railway Station serve in Madinah?
optionsEn: A private palace closed to everyone
The Madinah Museum (Al-Madinah Museum / Hejaz Railway Museum) showcasing Madinah's history and heritage
explanationEn: Preserved respectfully as a heritage museum, the station exhibits artifacts, historic railway carriages, and scale models of Madinah through the ages.

questionEn: Which major modern facility on the northwestern outskirts of Madinah prints and distributes tens of millions of copies of the Noble Qur'an worldwide?
optionsEn: King Fahd Glorious Qur'an Printing Complex (Mujamma' al-Malik Fahd)
explanationEn: Established in Madinah in 1984 CE, the King Fahd Complex produces verified Mushafs and translations distributed freely to pilgrims and mosques globally.

questionEn: Which renowned international university in Madinah was founded in 1961 CE to teach Islamic sciences and Arabic to students from across the globe?
optionsEn: The Islamic University of Madinah (Al-Jami'ah al-Islamiyyah)
explanationEn: Carrying forward Madinah's timeless heritage as the city of Islamic knowledge, the Islamic University of Madinah hosts students from over 170 nationalities.

questionEn: Which oasis date variety—beside Ajwah—is famously cultivated in Madinah's fertile volcanic soil and loved across the Hijaz?
optionsEn: Apples and pears of cold tundra
Safawi, Anbarah, Barni, Mabroom, and Sukkari/Shalabi dates (especially Barni and Anbarah in Madinah)
explanationEn: Barni dates of Madinah are even praised in classical narrations alongside Ajwah, while Anbarah and Safawi remain staples of Madinah's hospitality.

questionEn: Why is Madinah's soil historically described as dark and stony outside its green palm groves?
optionsEn: Because it is made of ocean coral
Because it sits on white chalk cliffs
Because the city lies on a volcanic basin surrounded by dark basaltic lava fields known as Harrat
Because it was covered by glaciers
explanationEn: Surrounding basaltic plateaus (Harrat Rahat, Waqim, and al-Wabrah) yield dark stones used in Madinah's historic architecture and create natural aquifers beneath the palm oasis.

questionEn: Which famous valley in Madinah did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) warn people about building houses directly inside because of seasonal flash floods?
explanationEn: When torrential desert rains sweep off the surrounding hills, Madinah's valleys (Wadi al-Aqiq, Buthan, and Qanat) swell into rushing seasonal rivers.

questionEn: What remarkable event occurred in Madinah during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) or Prophet's ﷺ lifetime when heavy rain fell continuously for seven days after an Istisqa prayer?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ prayed 'Allahumma hawalayna wa la alayna' (O Allah, around us and not upon us), and the clouds immediately parted into a clear ring over Madinah
The sun vanished for a month
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, when a man returned the very next Friday pleading that houses were collapsing and roads cut off by continuous rain, the Prophet ﷺ smiled and asked Allah to direct rain to the valleys and hills around Madinah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when the clouds instantly parted above Madinah after his Istisqa prayer, leaving Wadi Qanat flowing for a full month?
optionsEn: 'I bear witness that Allah has power over all things and that I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger'
'Rain will never fall in Madinah again'
explanationEn: Seeing the storm clouds roll back to form a crown around Madinah while Wadi Qanat surged with water became a vivid miracle remembered by Anas ibn Malik (RA).

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ stand when he prayed that historic Istisqa (rain) supplication in which he turned his cloak inside-out?
optionsEn: On a ship in the Red Sea
In Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during the Friday khutbah (for the cloud-parting dua), and outdoors at the Musalla (Masjid al-Ghamamah) on another occasion of Istisqa
At the summit of Mount Arafat
explanationEn: Both inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during Friday sermon and outdoors at the Musalla (site of Masjid al-Ghamamah), the Prophet ﷺ modeled complete reliance upon Allah for rain.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ turn his outer cloak (rida') inside-out during the Istisqa prayer at Madinah's Musalla?
optionsEn: As an optimistic physical symbol hoping Allah would likewise transform the drought into abundance and mercy
To keep his shoulders warm in snow
To hide his face from the crowd
explanationEn: The Companions imitated him by reversing their cloaks while making sincere dua and seeking Allah's forgiveness for rain.

questionEn: Which companion was famous in Madinah for telling the story of how the Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain during a severe drought, and within moments a cloud formed like a shield behind Mount Sal'?
explanationEn: Serving the Prophet ﷺ for ten years in Madinah, Anas ibn Malik (RA) witnessed countless prayers and miracles in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and recorded them vividly in Sahih al-Bukhari.

questionEn: What is the historical name of the gate/district south of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi where Masjid al-Ghamamah sits—historically known as 'Al-Manakhah'?
optionsEn: Al-Manakhah (the camel-kneeling and caravan staging ground)
explanationEn: For centuries, caravans arriving in Madinah unloaded and knelt their camels at Al-Manakhah outside the city's old western wall right beside Masjid al-Ghamamah.

questionEn: Which small historic hill/outcrop west of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi near Al-Manakhah was known as 'Jabal Dhubab' (or Jabal al-Rayah)?
optionsEn: The hill of Safa in Makkah
The rocky ridge northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi where the Prophet's ﷺ tent stood during the Battle of the Trench
explanationEn: Rising near the trench sector on the northwestern flank, Jabal Dhubab overlooks the open plain where the Confederates camped in 5 AH.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the reward of fasting or giving charity in Madinah compared to other lands?
optionsEn: Charity in Madinah counts for half
Only prayers inside Quba are accepted
Good deeds inside Madinah carry immense blessing because of its Haram status and association with the Prophet's ﷺ mosque, while sins in sacred places are also more serious
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that while Salah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi has the explicit 1,000x reward, every righteous act performed sincerely in the sacred Sanctuary of Madinah is deeply blessed by Allah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Fiqh of the Two Harams

questionEn: Which classical title describes both Makkah and Madinah together as the two noblest cities in Islam?
explanationEn: United by divine consecration—Makkah by Ibrahim (AS) and Madinah by Muhammad ﷺ—they stand forever as Al-Haramayn al-Sharifayn.

questionEn: What was the 'Hima al-Naqi'' (Protected Pasture of Al-Naqi') established near Madinah by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: A protected state grazing reserve south/southwest of Madinah dedicated to public mounts used in charity and defense
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Umar (RA) continued managing Al-Naqi' (and Al-Rabadhah) carefully for public benefit, instructing its caretaker to admit the camels of needy citizens freely while restraining overly wealthy herds.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Agriculture & Watering

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about the shared public right to three basic natural resources—water, pasture, and fire—when regulating Madinah's economy?
optionsEn: 'Only rulers may own wells and grass'
'Firewood must be taxed at the city gate'
'Muslims are partners in three things: water, pasture, and fire'
explanationEn: This foundational prophetic principle in Madinah prevented monopolies over essential life resources and fostered social equity.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah (Sahih)

questionEn: In which Islamic month and year did the Battle of Uhud take place just north of Madinah?
explanationEn: One year after Badr, Quraysh marched north toward Madinah with 3,000 fighters, meeting the Muslims on the slopes of Mount Uhud in Shawwal 3 AH.

questionEn: Why was the mountain north of Madinah originally named 'Uhud' (meaning 'One / Isolated')?
optionsEn: Because it rises as a single isolated massif separated from the neighboring desert ranges
Because it was climbed once a century
Because one river flowed over its summit
Because only one tree grew on it
explanationEn: Standing apart from nearby ridges across the northern Madinah plain, Mount Uhud's distinctive solitary silhouette gave it its name.

questionEn: Prior to marching out to Mount Uhud, what initial defensive opinion did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ share in consultation (shura) with the Companions?
optionsEn: To remain inside fortified Madinah and fight in its narrow streets if Quraysh entered
explanationEn: Initially favored by the Prophet ﷺ and elders like Abdullah ibn Ubayy (though for different motives), the Prophet ﷺ graciously accepted the enthusiastic majority of young companions—including Badr absentees—who urged marching out to meet Quraysh.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ refuse to take off his double armor once he had put it on before marching toward Uhud, even when young Ansar offered to reconsider?
optionsEn: Because his horse could not turn back
'It does not befit a prophet, once he has put on his coat of mail, to take it off until Allah decides between him and his enemy'
Because the armor straps were rusted shut
explanationEn: This celebrated prophetic maxim taught resolve after consultation (Shura) and decision—echoed in Surah Aal Imran (3:159).

questionEn: How many men abandoned the Muslim army between Madinah and Uhud under the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, leaving about 700 Muslims facing 3,000 Quraysh?
optionsEn: Three hundred men (one-third of the original force of 1,000)
explanationEn: Turning back with 300 followers claiming 'we do not expect a real fight,' Abdullah ibn Ubayy exposed the hypocrisy addressed in Surah Aal Imran (3:167).

questionEn: Which two Medinan clans briefly wavered when Abdullah ibn Ubayy deserted before Uhud, yet Allah strengthened their hearts to stay steadfast?
optionsEn: Banu Harithah (from Al-Aws) and Banu Salimah (from Al-Khazraj)
explanationEn: Surah Aal Imran (3:122) praises Allah's protection over these two clans so they stood firmly beside the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: How many skilled archers did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ station on Jabal Aynayn (Archers' Hill) across from Mount Uhud, and who was their commander?
optionsEn: Two hundred archers, commanded by Salman al-Farsi
Fifty archers, commanded by Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA)
Ten archers, commanded by Abu Sufyan
explanationEn: Stationed on the small rocky mound guarding the mountain pass to the Muslim rear, Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) and his fifty archers held the key to the battlefield.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What strict, unmistakable command did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) and the archers on Archers' Hill before the fighting began?
optionsEn: 'Do not leave your position even if you see birds snatching us—whether you see us victorious or defeated—until I send for you!'
'Charge down the hill as soon as Quraysh drops a single shield'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ foresaw that Quraysh's cavalry under Khalid ibn al-Walid could only outflank the Muslim rear if that narrow pass behind Jabal al-Rumat was abandoned.

questionEn: What tragic mistake turned initial Muslim victory into a painful setback at the Battle of Uhud?
optionsEn: Most of the archers left Jabal al-Rumat to collect spoils when Quraysh retreated, ignoring Abdullah ibn Jubayr's (RA) reminder of the Prophet's ﷺ explicit order
The Muslims ran out of water at Fajr
explanationEn: Seeing the pass suddenly guarded by fewer than ten steadfast archers under Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA), Khalid ibn al-Walid wheeled Quraysh's cavalry behind the hill, overran the remaining archers, and struck the Muslim rear.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Who famously fought for the Prophet's ﷺ own sword at Uhud by asking 'Who will take this sword and give it its full due?'
explanationEn: Asking what its due was—'to strike the enemy with it until it bends'—Abu Dujanah (RA) tied his red headband of courage, stepped into the ranks, and spared an enemy woman (Hind) rather than dishonor the Prophet's ﷺ sword.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which noble uncle of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—known as 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah)—was martyred by Wahshi ibn Harb's javelin at the Battle of Uhud?
explanationEn: Fighting valiantly at the front of the Muslim line, Hamzah (RA) was struck from ambush by Wahshi's spear and honored forever by the Prophet ﷺ as 'Sayyid al-Shuhada' (Master of the Martyrs).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What title did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ bestow upon his martyred uncle Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) at Uhud?
explanationEn: Deeply grieved upon seeing Hamzah's (RA) mutilated body, the Prophet ﷺ honored him as Master of the Martyrs and was restrained by Surah An-Nahl (16:126) from retaliating with mutilation.

questionEn: Which grieving sister of Hamzah (RA) showed extraordinary patience and composure when visiting her brother's body on the Uhud battlefield?
explanationEn: Repeating 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' and praying for Allah's forgiveness for Hamzah (RA), Safiyyah (RA) endured the loss with remarkable fortitude, earning the Prophet's ﷺ praise.

questionEn: Which handsome, noble standard-bearer of the Muslims—formerly Madinah's first ambassador—was martyred at Uhud holding the banner until both hands were severed?
explanationEn: When Mus'ab (RA) fell defending the Prophet ﷺ, an angel appeared in his likeness to carry the banner; after the battle his shroud was so short that covering his head uncovered his feet, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered idhkhir grass laid over his feet.

questionEn: Why did Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) weep years later when looking at his comfortable meal, remembering Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) at Uhud?
optionsEn: Because Mus'ab refused to carry the banner
Because Mus'ab (RA), who once wore the finest clothes in Makkah, died at Uhud possessing only a single rough cloak too short to cover both his head and feet
Because Mus'ab never migrated to Madinah
explanationEn: Khabbab (RA) feared that companions who received worldly ease later in life might have had some reward hastened, whereas Mus'ab (RA) departed to Allah untouched by luxury.

questionEn: Which newlywed companion of Uhud rushed straight to battle on hearing the call without completing his purification bath (ghusl) and earned the title 'Ghasil al-Mala'ikah' (Washed by the Angels)?
explanationEn: Seeing angels washing Hanzalah's (RA) body between heaven and earth after his martyrdom at Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ asked his widow, who explained he had hurried out at dawn upon hearing the war cry in a state of janabah.

questionEn: Which courageous female companion from Madinah picked up a sword and shield at Uhud to physically defend Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, sustaining over a dozen wounds?
explanationEn: Looking left and right amid the chaos of Uhud, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ remarked: 'Wherever I turned to the left or right, I saw Umm Umarah fighting in front of me!'

questionEn: What touching request did Umm Umarah (Nusaybah bint Ka'b, RA) ask of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ right there on the battlefield of Uhud?
optionsEn: 'Pray to Allah that we be your companions in Paradise!'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ immediately prayed: 'O Allah, make them my companions in Paradise!'—to which Umm Umarah (RA) joyously replied: 'I care not whatever befalls me in this world after that!'

questionEn: Which companion shielded Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with his own bare hand and body against incoming arrows at Uhud until his hand was paralyzed?
explanationEn: Receiving over thirty sword, spear, and arrow wounds while carrying the Prophet ﷺ up a rocky ledge of Uhud, Talhah (RA) earned the Prophet's ﷺ praise: 'Talhah has made Paradise obligatory for himself!'

questionEn: Which Ansari companion received seven arrows in his back while crouching as a human shield over Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at Uhud?
optionsEn: Abu Dujanah (RA) (along with Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas shooting beside him)
explanationEn: Both Abu Dujanah (RA) shielding the Prophet's ﷺ body and Abu Talhah al-Ansari (RA) raising his chest and shield to protect him showed unmatched devotion at Uhud.

questionEn: What physical injuries did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ suffer during the fierce melee at the Battle of Uhud?
optionsEn: He broke both legs falling from a tower
A chipped lower-right front tooth (rabaiyah), a cut on his lip/forehead, and two iron helmet links driven into his cheek
He suffered no scratches at all
explanationEn: Knocked into a pit dug as a trap by Abu Amir al-Fasiq, the Prophet ﷺ was wounded in his face and tooth; Fatimah (RA) washed the blood and burned a piece of straw mat to stanch the bleeding.

questionEn: Which companion used his own teeth to pull the two iron helmet rings embedded in Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ cheek at Uhud, losing two of his own front teeth in the process?
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr (RA) rushed to help, Abu Ubaydah (RA) begged to extract the iron links himself with his teeth so as not to hurt the Prophet's ﷺ face, losing two front teeth cleanly with gentle devotion.

questionEn: Who famously sucked the blood from Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ wounded cheek at Uhud and swallowed it—no, wait: who was Malik ibn Sinan (RA), father of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, at Uhud?
optionsEn: He refused to approach the battlefield
He deserted with Abdullah ibn Ubayy
Malik ibn Sinan (RA) wiped and sucked the blood from the Prophet's ﷺ blessed face so it wouldn't touch the earth, then fought until martyred at Uhud
explanationEn: Malik ibn Sinan (RA), father of the famed Hadith scholar Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, fought bravely after tending the Prophet's ﷺ wound and attained martyrdom at Uhud.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ wiped the blood off his face at Uhud and wondered 'How can a people prosper who wound the face of their Prophet?'
optionsEn: Surah Aal Imran 3:128 ('Not for you is any share in the decision—whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them')
explanationEn: Teaching patience and divine sovereignty over hearts, Allah soon guided several of those very adversaries at Uhud—including Khalid ibn al-Walid and Ikrimah—to become champions of Islam.

questionEn: What remarkable statement did Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA)—who had missed Badr—declare before charging back into the fighting at Uhud when others panicked over the rumor of the Prophet's ﷺ death?
optionsEn: 'There is no reason left to pray'
'Let us surrender to Abu Sufyan at once'
'If Muhammad has been killed, the Lord of Muhammad is Ever-Living! By Allah, I smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud!'
explanationEn: Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA) fell with over eighty sword, spear, and arrow wounds—recognizable only by his fingertips to his sister—honored in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:23).

questionEn: Which elderly lame companion insisted on fighting at Uhud—even though Allah excused the disabled—saying 'I hope to tread in Paradise with this lame leg of mine!'?
explanationEn: When his four sons tried to hold him back out of compassion, Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA) appealed to the Prophet ﷺ, fought valiantly, and was buried in the same grave with his brother-in-law Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram.

questionEn: Whose father was martyred at Uhud leaving behind nine daughters and unpaid debts, until the Prophet ﷺ comforted his son Jabir (RA) and miraculously blessed their date harvest to pay off every debt?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram (RA), father of Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gave Jabir (RA) the breathtaking glad tiding that Allah spoke directly to his father Abdullah without a veil, offering him any wish—and Abdullah wished only to return to earth and be martyred in Allah's path again!

questionEn: Which companion was found mortally wounded with twelve wounds by Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) on the Uhud battlefield and sent a final message of steadfast loyalty to the Ansar?
explanationEn: Barely breathing, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (RA) asked Zayd to deliver his salam to the Prophet ﷺ and tell his Ansari brothers: 'You will have no excuse before Allah if the Prophet ﷺ is harmed while an eyelash among you still blinks!'

questionEn: What unusual burial practice did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ order for the ~70 martyrs of Uhud because the exhausted surviving companions could not dig 70 separate graves?
optionsEn: Burying two or three martyrs together in a single grave without washing their bloodied clothes, placing the one who memorized more Qur'an first into the lahd
Cremating the armor and burying ashes
Leaving them unburied on the mountaintop
explanationEn: Battlefield martyrs were buried directly in their bloodstained garments without washing them; eight years later, the Prophet ﷺ stood and prayed over them like one bidding farewell.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid washing the martyrs of Uhud before burying them?
optionsEn: Because Madinah had no water wells
Because they were already washed by rain
Because every wound suffered in Allah's path will come on the Day of Resurrection bleeding the color of blood with the fragrance of musk
explanationEn: Martyrs of the battlefield are buried directly in their garments as timeless witnesses to their sacrifice.

questionEn: Which two close martyrs of Uhud—brothers-in-law and devoted friends in life—were buried together in one grave at Uhud?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram (RA) and Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA)
explanationEn: Honoring their lifelong love for one another in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Bury those two together in one grave, for they loved each other in this world.'

questionEn: What happened roughly forty-six years later during Mu'awiyah's reign when a flood or spring-digging project exposed the shared grave of Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram at Uhud?
optionsEn: Their bodies were found completely intact and supple, as though they had just fallen asleep the day before, with Jabir's father's hand resting on his wound
explanationEn: Eyewitnesses in Madinah led by Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) saw the martyrs' bodies preserved miraculously by Allah decades after Uhud before respectfully re-interring them.

questionEn: Who climbed up to confront Abu Sufyan verbally from the rocky cleft of Mount Uhud when Abu Sufyan shouted 'Hubal is exalted!'?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), answering at the Prophet's ﷺ instruction: 'Allah is Most High and Most Majestic!'
explanationEn: When Abu Sufyan boasted 'We have Al-Uzza and you have no Uzza,' Umar (RA) answered boldly: 'Allah is our Protector and you have no protector!'—affirming that Muslim martyrs are in Paradise while enemy dead are in Hell.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lead the wounded survivors of Uhud out the very next morning (Sunday, 16 Shawwal 3 AH) as far as Hamra al-Asad?
optionsEn: To demonstrate unwavering Muslim morale and deter Abu Sufyan's army from turning back to attack a vulnerable Madinah
explanationEn: Only those who had fought at Uhud were allowed on this courageous march to Hamra al-Asad (~13 km south of Madinah); hearing of their resolve, Quraysh hastened straight back to Makkah—earning Allah's praise in Surah Aal Imran 3:172.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage praises the believers who responded to the call to march to Hamra al-Asad right after suffering wounds at Uhud?
optionsEn: Surah Aal Imran 3:172-173 ('Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them... Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal Wakil')
explanationEn: When intimidated with warnings that Quraysh was gathering again, those heroic survivors simply increased in faith and said 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'

questionEn: What soothing Qur'anic passage in Surah Aal Imran (3:169-170) was revealed to comfort the families of Madinah grieving the ~70 martyrs of Uhud?
optionsEn: 'Every soul will perish forever without provision'
'Never think of those martyred in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, rejoicing in what Allah has given them'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ explained that the souls of the martyrs of Uhud soar freely inside green birds in Paradise, resting beneath lanterns suspended under Allah's Throne.

questionEn: Which small cleft/cave high on the southern slope of Mount Uhud is traditionally pointed out by local Madinah historians as where the wounded Prophet ﷺ took temporary refuge during the battle?
explanationEn: Guided up the rocky gorge by Ali (RA), Talhah (RA), and Abu Bakr (RA), the Prophet ﷺ rested on the rocky ledge while Ali brought water in his shield from Al-Mihras hollow.

questionEn: Where is 'Sayyid al-Shuhada Mosque' situated today in Madinah?
optionsEn: Inside the courtyard of Masjid Quba
At the southern base of Mount Uhud, facing the enclosed cemetery of Hamzah (RA) and the ~70 martyrs of Uhud and Jabal al-Rumat
explanationEn: Serving pilgrims visiting Mount Uhud, Sayyid al-Shuhada Mosque sits directly opposite the fenced martyrs' burial ground and Archers' Hill.

questionEn: How many martyrs of the Muslims fell at the Battle of Uhud—a figure mirrored later in the Qur'anic lesson of Surah Aal Imran 3:165?
explanationEn: Having captured or slain seventy Quraysh fighters at Badr, the Muslims lost seventy noble martyrs at Uhud after the archers' lapse—teaching that obedience to the Prophet ﷺ is the true source of victory.

questionEn: Whose elderly father was accidentally slain in the dust of Uhud by fellow Muslims who mistook him for an enemy—yet his son generously forgave them and donated the blood-money?
optionsEn: Al-Yaman (Husayl ibn Jabir, RA), father of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA)
explanationEn: In the dust of Uhud, Muslims accidentally struck elderly Al-Yaman thinking he was an enemy despite Hudhayfah's cries; Hudhayfah (RA) nobly forgave them and donated the blood-money (diyah) in charity.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What heart-moving promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give regarding the Martyrs of Uhud shortly before his own passing in 11 AH?
optionsEn: He forbade anyone from ever visiting Uhud
He ordered their graves moved inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
He went out to the Martyrs of Uhud and prayed over them as if bidding farewell to the living and the dead, then ascended the Minbar
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) narrated this poignant farewell visit eight years after Uhud, when the Prophet ﷺ affirmed: 'I am going ahead of you as your witness.'

questionEn: How did Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) care for the grave of her uncle Hamzah (RA) at Uhud during her lifetime?
optionsEn: She planted a forest across the entire mountain
She regularly visited Uhud, tidied and marked Hamzah's (RA) grave, and prayed sincerely for the martyrs
She built a tall marble palace over it
explanationEn: Early narrations record Fatimah (RA) visiting the martyrs' resting place at Uhud with quiet dignity and supplicating for her beloved uncle.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell the Ansar widow whose husband, brother, and father had all been martyred at Uhud when she rushed out to meet the returning column?
optionsEn: She cursed the archers on the hill
She demanded the army turn back immediately
She asked only: 'How is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?'—and upon seeing him alive and safe, said: 'Every calamity after you is small!'
explanationEn: This celebrated woman of Banu Dinar embodied the Ansar's unmatched love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ above all earthly ties.

questionEn: Which companion's final wish at Uhud—before his mutilated body was barely recognizable—had been: 'O Allah, let me meet an enemy who kills me and cuts off my nose and ears, so I may tell You on Judgment Day: It was for You and Your Messenger!'?
explanationEn: Sharing that extraordinary prayer with Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) before the battle, Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA) saw his wish fulfilled literally at Uhud and was buried alongside his uncle Hamzah (RA).

questionEn: Which companion's name became forever linked with Jabal al-Rumat because he stood firm with less than ten archers defending the pass until martyred?
explanationEn: Even as forty archers hurried down for spoils, Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) stood his post reciting the Prophet's ﷺ order until he fell fighting bravely.

questionEn: What happened to Wahshi ibn Harb years after he killed Hamzah (RA) at Uhud?
optionsEn: He later embraced Islam in Makkah, lived in regret, and later slayed the false prophet Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab at Yamamah with the very same spear
He was executed by Abu Bakr (RA)
He died at Uhud that same afternoon
explanationEn: Though the Prophet ﷺ forgave Wahshi upon his Islam, he gently asked him to stay out of his sight because seeing him reopened the grief for Hamzah (RA); Wahshi used that same javelin to fell Musaylimah in 12 AH.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an devotes roughly sixty consecutive verses (3:121–179) to analyzing the spiritual, moral, and military lessons of the Battle of Uhud?
explanationEn: Surah Aal Imran gently rebukes the lapse at Archers' Hill, consoles the bereaved, exposes the hypocrites, and teaches believers never to despair after hardship.

questionEn: What mistake regarding Jabal al-Rumat do visitors sometimes make today that contradicts proper Islamic Ziyarah etiquette?
optionsEn: Lowering one's gaze and walking safely
Standing quietly to recall the Seerah and make dua for the martyrs
Climbing the hill to tie ribbons, write petitions on rocks, or gather soil for superstitious blessings
Teaching children about Abdullah ibn Jubayr's loyalty
explanationEn: Remembering the history of Uhud and praying for the martyrs is meaningful and educational, whereas taking stones/dust for blessings or superstitious markings has no basis in Islam.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ greet the Martyrs of Uhud when passing their resting place, and how should pilgrims greet them today?
optionsEn: Offering the Sunnah graveyard salam ('Assalamu alaykum ahl al-diyar min al-mu'minin...') and praying to Allah to have mercy on them
Asking Hamzah (RA) to grant children or wealth
explanationEn: Pure Islamic etiquette directs every supplication to Allah alone while sending salam and praying for forgiveness and high ranks for Hamzah (RA) and his companions.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say 'I fear for you after me not that you will associate partners with Allah, but that you will compete for this world' during his farewell address about the Martyrs of Uhud?
optionsEn: Because Makkah was about to sink
Having just prayed over the Martyrs of Uhud eight years after the battle, he warned the Ummah against worldly greed—the very temptation that drew the archers down at Uhud
Because Madinah had too many mosques
Because Uhud was full of gold mines
explanationEn: Narrated by Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, this final sermon connecting the Martyrs of Uhud to warning against materialism remains deeply relevant.

questionEn: In which Islamic month and year did the Confederates (Al-Ahzab) besiege Madinah in the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq)?
explanationEn: Coalition forces numbering around 10,000 fighters from Quraysh, Ghatafan, and allied tribes marched on Madinah in Shawwal 5 AH, outnumbering the 3,000 defenders.

questionEn: How many total enemy warriors did the Confederate coalition (Quraysh, Ghatafan, Sulaym, and allies) assemble outside Madinah during the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: It was the largest hostile force ever to march on Madinah, testing the Muslim community to the utmost—described in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:10) as 'hearts reaching the throats.'

questionEn: Who first proposed digging a deep defensive trench across Madinah's exposed northern approach during the consultation before Al-Ahzab?
optionsEn: Salman al-Farsi (RA), drawing on Persian siege-defense tactics
explanationEn: Remarking 'O Messenger of Allah, in Persia whenever we feared a cavalry assault, we dug a trench around us,' Salman al-Farsi (RA) introduced a tactic completely unfamiliar to Arabian warfare.

questionEn: Approximately how long was the defensive trench (Khandaq) dug across Madinah's northern corridor between the eastern and western lava fields?
explanationEn: Spanning from Shaykhayn/Harrat Waqim on the east to the slopes of Mount Sal' and Harrat al-Wabrah on the west, the trench averaged roughly 4.5 meters wide and deep enough to halt horses.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ organize the 3,000 defenders to dig the entire northern trench in freezing wind within roughly six to ten days?
optionsEn: By letting only the youth dig while elders watched
By waiting for spring rains to erode a ditch
By assigning each group of ten men a forty-cubit stretch to excavate, while he ﷺ personally hauled dirt alongside them
explanationEn: Shared teamwork—with Muhajirun and Ansar chanting poetic encouragement together while the Prophet ﷺ swung a pickaxe with dust covering his chest—finished the massive trench before Quraysh arrived.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which noble honor did both the Muhajirun and the Ansar playfully claim regarding Salman al-Farsi (RA) during the digging of the Trench, and how did the Prophet ﷺ settle it?
optionsEn: He exiled Salman from both groups
Both groups claimed 'Salman is one of us!'—so the Prophet ﷺ smiled and declared: 'Salman is from us, Ahl al-Bayt (my own household)!'
He told Salman to dig alone
explanationEn: By elevating Salman al-Farsi (RA) into the honor of Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet ﷺ showed that brotherhood in Islam transcends ethnicity and lineage.

questionEn: What extraordinary prophetic visions flashed before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he struck a massive boulder blocking the trench three times with a pickaxe?
optionsEn: He predicted Quraysh would conquer Madinah
He saw Madinah sinking into the sea
Sparks lit up the palaces of Al-Hirah/Persia, the red palaces of Greater Syria (Sham), and the gates of Sana'a in Yemen—promising their future opening to Islam
He saw gold buried inside the boulder
explanationEn: At Madinah's darkest hour of hunger and siege, striking that stubborn rock gave the believers radiant certainty of Islam's future global victory.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tie two stones firmly against his own belly while digging the Khandaq?
optionsEn: To keep his cloak from blowing in the wind
To ease the pangs of severe hunger during days of food scarcity in Madinah
explanationEn: When Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) saw the Prophet ﷺ tie stones over his stomach and faint with hunger—while Companions tied one stone—Jabir hurried home to prepare a modest meal.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What memorable miracle of food multiplication occurred at Jabir ibn Abdullah's (RA) house near Jabal Sal' during the digging of the Trench?
optionsEn: The pot cracked and spilled all the stew
Angel Jibril cooked the meat personally
A single small goat-kid and one sa' of barley—blessed by the Prophet's ﷺ touch and prayer—satisfied all 1,000 diggers with food left over
Only ten elders were fed while others fasted
explanationEn: Though Jabir (RA) privately invited only the Prophet ﷺ and a couple of companions, the Prophet ﷺ called all the trench diggers, instructing Jabir's wife not to uncover the pot or pull bread from the oven until he arrived; every single worker ate until full.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What similar miracle involving a handful of dates occurred during the digging of the Trench through the daughter of Bashir ibn Sa'd (RA)?
optionsEn: A tiny handful of dates spread over a cloth by the Prophet ﷺ multiplied until every digger in the trench ate their fill and dates still overflowed the cloth
Birds ate all the dates before noon
The dates turned into silver coins
explanationEn: Recorded by Ibn Ishaq, this second feeding miracle comforted hungry workers working day and night under winter winds.

questionEn: Which Jewish tribe living inside southern Madinah broke their solemn treaty with the Muslims mid-siege during Khandaq, threatening Madinah's women and children from the rear?
explanationEn: Persuaded by Huyayy ibn Akhtab of Banu Nadir, Banu Qurayzah tore up their defense pact with Madinah at the exact moment 10,000 enemies stood at the northern trench.

questionEn: Which two companions did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send to quietly verify whether Banu Qurayzah had indeed betrayed the treaty during the Battle of the Trench?
optionsEn: Hassan ibn Thabit and Abu Hurayrah
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) and Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) (along with Abdullah ibn Rawahah and Khawwat ibn Jubayr)
explanationEn: Discovering open hostility from Banu Qurayzah, the envoys returned using an agreed code phrase ('Adal and al-Qarah') so public panic wouldn't break out in Madinah.

questionEn: How did Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib (RA)—aunt of the Prophet ﷺ—protect the women and children sheltered inside the fort of Fari' during Khandaq?
optionsEn: When a hostile scout climbed near the women's fortress, she struck him down decisively with a tent pole when Hassan ibn Thabit hesitated, keeping the enemy from discovering the fort was unguarded
She opened the gates and surrendered
explanationEn: Safiyyah's (RA) fearless quick action deterred any infiltration of the unprotected families in southern Madinah while the men held the northern trench.

questionEn: Which prominent Quraysh warrior managed to leap his horse across a narrow point of the Trench and challenge the Muslims—only to be defeated in single combat by Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
explanationEn: Accepting the challenge with the Prophet's ﷺ own sword and turban, Ali (RA) offered Amr Islam first, then defeated him cleanly, shattering the Confederates' hope of breaching the trench.

questionEn: On one intense day of the Battle of the Trench, why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ have to delay the Asr prayer until after sunset—prompting him to pray against the besiegers for distracting them?
optionsEn: Because everyone forgot the direction of Makkah
Because no water existed in Madinah
Continuous enemy arrow volleys and crossing attempts kept the defenders pinned down at the trench without pause until dusk
explanationEn: Praying Asr right after sunset followed by Maghrib, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'They distracted us from the middle prayer (Asr) until the sun set—may Allah fill their houses and graves with fire!' (before later verses codified Salat al-Khawf).

questionEn: Which newly converted companion from Ghatafan—whose conversion was still secret to both Quraysh and Banu Qurayzah—brilliantly sowed mutual distrust among the besieging coalition?
explanationEn: Authorized by the Prophet ﷺ with the wisdom 'War is strategy (al-harb khud'ah),' Nu'aym (RA) visited Banu Qurayzah and Quraysh separately, causing Banu Qurayzah to demand hostages and Quraysh to suspect betrayal.

questionEn: What natural—and divinely sent—force finally broke the 10,000-strong Confederate siege of Madinah after nearly a month?
optionsEn: A freezing, howling gale wind accompanied by unseen angelic hosts that extinguished enemy fires, overturned their cooking pots, and tore down their tents
A volcanic eruption on Mount Uhud
A massive flood from the Red Sea
A sudden peace treaty signed by Abu Sufyan
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:9) celebrates Allah sending a fierce wind and unseen armies; terrified and freezing, Abu Sufyan ordered a chaotic retreat back to Makkah overnight.

questionEn: Which companion volunteered in the pitch-black freezing wind of that final night at Khandaq to crawl across the trench and gather intelligence from Abu Sufyan's camp?
explanationEn: Ordered by the Prophet ﷺ not to shoot or provoke anyone despite having Abu Sufyan right in his sights, Hudhayfah (RA) watched Abu Sufyan flee and miraculously felt warm as in a bath until returning to report.

questionEn: What decisive strategic prediction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ announce right after the Confederates fled from Madinah in 5 AH?
optionsEn: 'No treaty will ever be signed with Makkah'
'From now on we will march against them, and they will never march against us; we will go to them!'
'Quraysh will besiege Madinah every year forever'
explanationEn: Marking the permanent turning point of Arabian history, Quraysh never again mounted an offensive against Madinah after Khandaq.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Who came to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ the very day he returned home from the Trench and began removing his armor, instructing him not to lay down his arms until marching on Banu Qurayzah?
explanationEn: Appearing at the door of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi on a mule with dust on his head, Jibril (AS) told the Prophet ﷺ that the angels had not yet laid down their weapons and were already heading toward Banu Qurayzah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What famous urgency command did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ issue to the Companions on the afternoon following Khandaq regarding Banu Qurayzah?
optionsEn: 'None of you should pray Asr except at Banu Qurayzah!'
'Fast for forty days at Masjid Quba'
'Do not leave your homes for a week'
explanationEn: How the Companions understood that command—some praying Asr on the road before sunset while others delayed until reaching Banu Qurayzah, with the Prophet ﷺ approving both—became a classic principle of Fiqh.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Fear Prayer

questionEn: Who was appointed—at Banu Qurayzah's own request as an old ally of Al-Aws—to pass judgment upon their wartime treason after their surrender?
explanationEn: Mortally wounded from the Khandaq arrow in his arm, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) judged according to their own Torah law (Deuteronomy 20:10-14) for wartime treason—which the Prophet ﷺ affirmed matched Allah's decree from above the seven heavens.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What extraordinary honor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ announce upon the passing of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) shortly after the Banu Qurayzah judgment?
optionsEn: 'The Throne of the Most Merciful (Arsh al-Rahman) shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh!'
explanationEn: Narrated by Jabir (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, seventy thousand angels also descended for Sa'd's funeral in Jannat al-Baqi, yet his body felt so light to carry because angels bore his bier.

questionEn: What is the historic complex of mosques along the western foothills of Mount Sal' where the Battle of the Trench unfolded called today?
explanationEn: Clustered near the trench line on the northwestern side of Mount Sal', these small historic mosques mark command posts and prayer spots from the Battle of the Trench.

questionEn: Which mosque sits highest on the ridge of Mount Sal' within the Seven Mosques complex, marking where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ intensely prayed for victory for three days during the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: Praying from Monday to Wednesday between Dhuhr and Asr until his cloak slipped off and Abu Bakr (RA) comforted him, the Prophet's ﷺ supplication was answered on Wednesday afternoon—hence named Masjid al-Fath.

questionEn: According to Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) in Musnad Ahmad, on which day of the week and between which two prayers was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ victory dua answered at Masjid al-Fath during Khandaq?
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) cherished that blessed moment, noting he often sought to make important personal duas on Wednesday between Dhuhr and Asr in gratitude.

questionEn: Which other historic small mosques are traditionally grouped alongside Masjid al-Fath in the 'Seven Mosques' (Al-Masajid al-Sab'ah) at Khandaq?
optionsEn: Masjid Salman al-Farsi, Masjid Abu Bakr, Masjid Umar, Masjid Ali, Masjid Fatimah (Sa'd ibn Mu'adh), and sometimes Masjid al-Qiblatayn or Masjid al-Rayah
Masjid Badr, Masjid Hunayn, and Masjid Taif
Masjid Quba, Masjid al-Haram, and Masjid al-Aqsa
explanationEn: Today a grand modern Masjid al-Khandaq (Masjid al-Fath) serves worshippers comfortably at the site while preserving the historic hillside shrines/mosques above the trench area.

questionEn: Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ build seven stone mosques at Khandaq during the battle itself?
optionsEn: Yes, all seven were built in marble in 5 AH
They were built inside Mount Uhud
No, they were built before Islam by Rome
No; those small mosques were built in later centuries by subsequent rulers to mark the strategic stations of the Prophet ﷺ and Companions during the siege
explanationEn: Historical clarity reminds visitors that while the events of 5 AH occurred right on those ridges, the masonry mosques standing there were erected later as historical commemorations.

questionEn: What is the proper Islamic attitude when visiting the Seven Mosques / Khandaq site today?
optionsEn: Climbing the old domes to leave padlocks
Praying toward Mount Sal' instead of Makkah
Reflecting gratefully on Allah's deliverance, praying normally in the main Masjid al-Khandaq if desired, and avoiding superstitious rituals on the small historic structures
Believing visiting all seven replaces Umrah
explanationEn: Recognizing the difference between authentic Seerah remembrance and unsubstantiated rituals keeps a pilgrim's Ziyarah faithful to the Sunnah.

questionEn: Which companion—the Prophet's ﷺ beloved poet Hassan ibn Thabit (RA)—stayed inside the fort of Fari' protecting the women and children during Khandaq, and why?
optionsEn: Hassan ibn Thabit (RA), who was physically elderly/unable to fight in close combat and remained inside the family fort
explanationEn: Safiyyah (RA) stood alongside Hassan inside the women's fortress when an enemy scout approached, ensuring Madinah's families remained secure.

questionEn: What moving test of hypocrisy vs sincerity during the Battle of the Trench is vividly described in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:12-20)?
optionsEn: True believers complained that the Prophet ﷺ deceived them
Hypocrites dug the deepest part of the trench alone
Hypocrites made flimsy excuses ('our houses are exposed!') and sneaked home, while true believers declared: 'This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us!'
explanationEn: Contrasting the panic of those with diseased hearts against the steady faith of the believers makes Surah Al-Ahzab one of the most powerful reflections on Khandaq.

questionEn: Which famous verse in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21) immediately follows the description of the Battle of the Trench, presenting the Prophet ﷺ as our supreme role model?
optionsEn: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern (Uswah Hasanah)'
explanationEn: Revealed amid the freezing hunger, betrayal, and terror of Khandaq, 33:21 reminds Muslims that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the ultimate model of courage, trust in Allah, and leadership under pressure.

questionEn: What happened to the Muslim community's morale when the Confederates finally departed from outside Madinah without conquering a single street?
optionsEn: Allah enriched the believers peacefully in Madinah, secured the city permanently from further Quraysh invasions, and turned the tide toward Hudaybiyyah and Makkah
Quraysh returned two weeks later and captured Quba
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:25) sums up the outcome: 'And Allah repelled those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good.'

questionEn: Which warrior of Quraysh—one of their future greatest Muslim commanders—led the elite cavalry detachment outside Madinah's trench before accepting Islam in 7/8 AH?
explanationEn: Seeing how Islam united Madinah and survived even a 10,000-strong siege helped awaken Khalid ibn al-Walid's heart until he rode to Madinah in Safar 8 AH to embrace Islam.

questionEn: Which companion—one of the famous archers at Khandaq—kept watch over the Prophet's ﷺ tent all night long throughout the siege?
optionsEn: Abbad ibn Bishr (RA) (along with other faithful Ansar guards)
explanationEn: Remembering Abbad ibn Bishr (RA), Aishah (RA) once heard his sweet night Qur'an recitation and praised him among the finest of the Ansar.

questionEn: What is the historical name of Madinah's principal cemetery directly east of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and what does 'Al-Gharqad' refer to?
optionsEn: Baqi al-Noor, named after white marble
Baqi al-Gharqad (Jannat al-Baqi), named after the thorny boxthorn bushes (gharqad) that originally grew on that open plain
Baqi al-Bahr, named after a lake
Baqi al-Zaytun, named after olive orchards
explanationEn: Before becoming Madinah's Muslim cemetery in 1 AH, the open stretch east of the mosque was thick with gharqad shrubs; clearing them turned it into Baqi al-Gharqad.

questionEn: Who was the very first Muhajir (Emigrant from Makkah) buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away in 2/3 AH shortly after Badr, Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA) was buried in Baqi; the Prophet ﷺ kissed his forehead weeping and placed a stone at his head to identify the grave.

questionEn: Who was the very first Ansari companion buried in Jannat al-Baqi (according to Ansar narrations), even before Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA)?
optionsEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) (leader of Banu al-Najjar, who passed away in 1 AH while Al-Masjid an-Nabawi was being built)
explanationEn: Historians reconcile both accounts by noting As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) was the first Ansari buried in Baqi (1 AH), while Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA) was the first Muhajir buried there (2/3 AH).

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ place a visible stone at the head of Uthman ibn Maz'un's (RA) grave in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: To prevent rain from touching it
So that he could recognize his brother's grave and bury other members of his family nearby
To build a tall dome over it
explanationEn: This Hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud shows the Sunnah permissibility of placing a simple unembellished marker (stone) to identify a loved one's grave without building structures over it.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Funerals

questionEn: How many Companions of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ are estimated by historians to be buried within Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Roughly 10,000 Companions (alongside countless Tabi'in, scholars, and righteous Muslims across the centuries)
None—all Companions were buried in Makkah
explanationEn: For fourteen centuries, tens of thousands of early believers—including over ten thousand Sahabah—have been laid to rest in the blessed earth of Baqi.

questionEn: Which beloved infant son of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (RA) is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away at around 16–18 months old in 10 AH, Ibrahim was buried in Baqi; on that very day a solar eclipse occurred, and the Prophet ﷺ gently corrected people who thought the sun eclipsed for a human's death.

questionEn: What tender words did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak in tears while holding his dying infant son Ibrahim before burying him in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: 'The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, yet we say only what pleases our Lord; O Ibrahim, by your departure we are deeply saddened'
explanationEn: Teaching balanced prophetic mercy, the Prophet ﷺ showed that natural tears of love and grief do not contradict patience and submission to Allah.

questionEn: Which beloved daughter of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—the 'Lady of the Women of Paradise'—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi (or inside her Madinah quarters/Baqi according to early sources)?
optionsEn: Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) (commonly identified with Jannat al-Baqi, buried at night by Ali RA)
explanationEn: Passing away six months after her father in Ramadan 11 AH, Fatimah (RA) was buried quietly at night in Baqi by Ali (RA) and Al-Abbas (RA) in accordance with her wish for modesty.

questionEn: Which three other noble daughters of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah (RA) all rest in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: While Khadijah (RA) rests in Makkah's Jannat al-Mu'alla, all four of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters—Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah (RA)—passed away in Madinah and rest in Baqi.

questionEn: Which two Mothers of the Believers (wives of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) are NOT buried in Jannat al-Baqi, unlike the rest of his noble wives?
optionsEn: Umm Salamah and Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA)
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA, buried in Makkah) and Maymunah bint al-Harith (RA, buried at Sarif near Makkah)
explanationEn: All other Mothers of the Believers—including Aishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Sawdah, Safiyyah, Juwayriyyah, and Umm Habibah (RA)—passed away in Madinah and rest in Baqi.

questionEn: Where is Aishah bint Abi Bakr (RA), Mother of the Believers and foremost jurist-narrator of Madinah, buried?
optionsEn: In Jannat al-Baqi, after passing away in Ramadan 58 AH
Inside the Sacred Chamber beside Umar (RA)
explanationEn: Humbling herself to give her own remaining space inside her room to Umar (RA), Aishah (RA) requested to be buried alongside her co-wives in Jannat al-Baqi, where Abu Hurayrah (RA) led her funeral prayer.

questionEn: Which grandson of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—known as 'Sayyid Shababi Ahl al-Jannah'—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi beside his grandmother Fatimah bint Asad and near Al-Abbas (RA)?
explanationEn: Passing away in Madinah in 49/50 AH, Al-Hasan ibn Ali (RA) was buried in Baqi near the entrance area where Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) also rests.

questionEn: Which noble uncle of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—whose funeral in 32 AH drew huge crowds in Madinah—is buried near the entrance of Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Honored by Umar and Uthman (RA) as the Prophet's ﷺ surviving uncle, Al-Abbas (RA) passed away in Madinah at age 88 and was laid to rest in Baqi.

questionEn: Which mother of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)—who lovingly raised Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a child after Abu Talib took him in—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi, with the Prophet ﷺ laying her in her grave himself?
explanationEn: Calling her 'my mother after my mother,' the Prophet ﷺ wrapped Fatimah bint Asad (RA) in his own shirt and reclined inside her freshly dug grave in Baqi to soften it before burial.

questionEn: Which three towering early scholars from Ahl al-Bayt (descendants of Al-Husayn ibn Ali) lived and taught in Madinah and are buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Ali Zayn al-Abidin, Muhammad al-Baqir, and Ja'far al-Sadiq (rahimahumullah)
Tariq ibn Ziyad, Musa ibn Nusayr, and Saladin
explanationEn: Great scholars of Madinah's Tabi'in and Atba' al-Tabi'in generations, Zayn al-Abidin, Al-Baqir, and Ja'far al-Sadiq are honored in Sunni and classical Islamic scholarship alike and rest in Baqi.

questionEn: Where in Jannat al-Baqi was the third Rightly Guided Caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (RA), originally buried after his tragic martyrdom in 35 AH?
optionsEn: In Hashsh Kawkab, an orchard plot just east of Baqi that was later incorporated inside the walls of Jannat al-Baqi
Inside the Sacred Chamber beside Umar (RA)
On the peak of Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Because rebels blocked the main cemetery path during the siege of 35 AH, Uthman (RA) was buried at night in Hashsh Kawkab—a plot he had previously admired—which Mu'awiyah later joined seamlessly into Baqi.

questionEn: Which three of the Ten Promised Paradise (Al-Asharah al-Mubashsharah) are buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA)
explanationEn: Alongside Uthman (RA), both Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (32 AH) and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (55 AH, brought from Al-Aqiq) were laid to rest in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which prolific Hadith narrator from Ahl al-Suffah passed away near Al-Aqiq around 57–59 AH and was laid to rest in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: After dedicating his life in Madinah to preserving thousands of Prophetic Hadith, Abu Hurayrah (RA) passed away near Madinah and was buried in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which great Ansari companion and Hadith narrator—famous for narrating over 1,100 Hadith and fighting from Khandaq onward—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away in Madinah in 74 AH as one of the last senior Medinan scholars among the Companions, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) rests in Baqi.

questionEn: Which renowned founder of one of the four Sunni schools of law—known as 'Imam Dar al-Hijrah'—passed away in 179 AH and is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Having barely ever left Madinah except for Hajj, Imam Malik lived, taught in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, compiled Al-Muwatta', and was buried in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which renowned freedman and student of Ibn Umar (RA)—forming part of the 'Golden Chain' (Malik from Nafi' from Ibn Umar)—passed away in Madinah in 117 AH and is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away in Madinah in 117 AH, Nafi' transmitted Madinah's clearest Prophetic scholarship straight to Imam Malik.

questionEn: Which foster mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Banu Sa'd is remembered in Madinah tradition with deep reverence, having visited him later and been honored when he spread his cloak for her?
explanationEn: When Halimah (RA) visited Prophet Muhammad ﷺ years later, he stood up immediately saying 'My mother! My mother!' and spread his own cloak for her to sit upon.

questionEn: Which wet-nurse/servant who raised Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from infancy and emigrated to Madinah—called by him 'my mother after my mother'—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) visited Umm Ayman (RA) in Madinah just as the Prophet ﷺ used to visit her, and she wept because divine revelation from heaven had ceased.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ quietly slip out of Aishah's (RA) house in the middle of the night toward Jannat al-Baqi near the end of his life?
optionsEn: To inspect the city walls against Romans
Angel Jibril (AS) instructed him that his Lord commanded him to go to the people of Al-Baqi and pray for forgiveness for them
explanationEn: When Aishah (RA) quietly followed to see where he went, she saw him stand for a long time in Baqi raising his hands three times in earnest prayer for Allah's forgiveness upon its residents.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Aishah (RA) when he returned from his late-night prayer at Jannat al-Baqi and noticed her out of breath?
optionsEn: He refused to explain where he went
He scolded her harshly and banned her from speaking
He told her Baqi was closed forever
He explained he had been commanded to seek forgiveness for the people of Baqi, adding that whoever asks forgiveness for believers receives great mercy
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ taught Aishah (RA) the exact dua to say when visiting graves, combining spiritual depth with tender reassurance.

questionEn: What remarkable eschatological Hadith in Sahih Muslim describes the resurrection of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), Umar (RA), and the people of Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Jannat al-Baqi will sink into the ocean
Only residents of Syria will rise with him
Nobody from Madinah will rise until ten thousand years later
The Prophet ﷺ will rise first, followed by Abu Bakr and Umar, and then he will go to the people of Al-Baqi so they are gathered with him before the people of Makkah
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan al-Tirmidhi (Hasan), this heartwarming narration highlights the honored companionship between the Prophet ﷺ and those resting in Baqi.

questionEn: According to another authentic narration, how many people from Jannat al-Baqi—or Madinah—will rise on the Day of Judgment with faces shining like the full moon, entering Paradise without reckoning?
optionsEn: Seventy thousand whose faces shine like the moon on the night of a full moon
explanationEn: Mentioned in historical sources (Ahmad / Ibn Hibban / Al-Samhudi) alongside the famous 70,000 Hadith, it illustrates the immense spiritual blessing of resting in Baqi with sincere faith.

questionEn: Why do graves inside Jannat al-Baqi today have no tall marble tombs, domes, or ornate shrines—only low mounded earth and simple uninscribed stones?
optionsEn: Because the cemetery was only opened last year
Because Madinah has no stone quarries
In direct obedience to the Prophet's ﷺ authentic command in Sahih Muslim forbidding plastering over graves, sitting on them, or building structures atop them
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, Jabir (RA) narrated: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade plastering a grave, sitting on it, or building a structure over it,' and Ali (RA) instructed Abu al-Hayyaj to level every raised tomb.

questionEn: How was the height of a Sunnah grave in Jannat al-Baqi traditionally shaped, as seen on Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ own grave?
optionsEn: Slightly raised like a camel's hump (musannam) by about one hand-span (shibr) above ground, with no masonry building over it
explanationEn: Sufyan al-Tammar narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that he saw the Prophet's ﷺ grave raised slightly like a camel's hump—protecting it from being walked upon while keeping it utterly humble.

questionEn: What daily scene unfolds in Jannat al-Baqi right after Fajr and Asr prayers in Madinah today?
optionsEn: Funeral biers carried from Al-Masjid an-Nabawi after Salat al-Janazah are gently buried by volunteers and families while visitors offer Salam from the walkways
People picnic on top of graves
explanationEn: Praying Salat al-Janazah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and walking in the funeral procession (ittiba' al-jana'iz) to Baqi earns one or two 'qirats' of reward—each as great as Mount Uhud!

questionEn: What immense reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise in Sahih al-Bukhari for attending a funeral prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (or any mosque) and following the bier to burial in Baqi?
optionsEn: One Qirat (like Mount Uhud) for attending the Janazah prayer, and two Qirats (each like Mount Uhud) if one remains until burial is completed
explanationEn: Because Janazah prayers happen after almost every daily prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Muslims visiting Madinah can frequently earn this monumental reward by praying Janazah and accompanying the deceased to Baqi.

questionEn: Which prominent Medinan elder companions from the Ansar—besides Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)—found their resting place in Madinah and Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA), Rafi' ibn Khadij (RA), Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA), and Ka'b ibn Malik (RA)
explanationEn: Nearly an entire generation of Madinah's Ansar and Muhajirun elders found their resting place side by side in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn Muslims against sitting on graves or stepping across them when visiting Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Because the dirt stains white garments
Because walking on paths is forbidden
He said sitting on a hot ember that burns through one's clothes to the skin is better for a person than sitting upon a Muslim's grave
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, this strong warning instills deep respect for the dignity of deceased believers, urging visitors to stay strictly on the paved paths.

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ comfort beside a fresh grave in Madinah with the timeless counsel: 'Fear Allah and be patient—patience is truly at the first shock of calamity'?
optionsEn: A grieving mother weeping beside her child's grave in Madinah
explanationEn: Not recognizing him at first from behind, she later hurried to the Prophet's ﷺ door apologizing; he taught that true patience is exercised right when bereavement strikes.

questionEn: What is the Islamic ruling regarding women visiting Jannat al-Baqi or cemeteries?
optionsEn: Women may sleep inside Baqi overnight
Women are required to enter Baqi daily and wail loudly

Scholars differ: some permit calm, veiled visits following Aishah's (RA) and Fatimah's (RA) precedent (provided there is no wailing), while others discourage frequent visits by women citing the Hadith 'Allah cursed women who frequently visit graves'; in Madinah today women respectfully offer Salam from outside the perimeter fence
Women cannot even offer Salam or make dua for the deceased from outside
explanationEn: Respecting local Madinah regulations and scholarly advice, female pilgrims offer the Sunnah graveyard Salam and heartfelt dua for the people of Baqi respectfully from outside the eastern walkway.
reference: Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah & Contemporary Fiqh of Ziyarah

questionEn: What is the authentic Sunnah supplication taught by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to Aishah (RA) when visiting Jannat al-Baqi or the Martyrs of Uhud?
optionsEn: 'Assalamu alaykum ahl al-diyar min al-mu'minina wal-muslimin, wa inna in sha'Allahu bikum la-lahiqun, nas'alullaha lana wa lakum al-afiyah'
'O dwellers of the graves, grant us wealth and health'
'Open your graves and speak to us'
'Woe to us, why did you leave us?'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, this moving greeting affirms peace upon the believers, humility before our own mortality, and supplication to Allah alone for well-being and forgiveness.

questionEn: What crucial distinction in Islamic creed (Aqidah) must every pilgrim observe when praying at Jannat al-Baqi or Uhud?
optionsEn: Ask the saints buried there to pay your debts
Kiss the iron bars of the cemetery gate
