Make Dua TO Allah FOR the deceased (asking Him to forgive and elevate them)—never ask the deceased themselves for help, healing, or intercession directly
Tie strings to the cemetery fence for luck
explanationEn: Supplication (Dua) is pure worship belonging solely to Allah; praying for deceased companions aligns with Surah Al-Hashr (59:10): 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.'

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse in Surah Al-Hashr (59:10) models the exact prayer believers should recite for the Muhajirun, Ansar, and all earlier generations resting in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe'
'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab'
explanationEn: Reciting 59:10 in Madinah unites a pilgrim's heart in love, loyalty, and prayer for the Companions who sacrificed everything to establish Islam.

questionEn: What practices did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ strictly forbid at gravesites, including at Baqi and Uhud, when comforting bereaved families?
optionsEn: Giving charity on behalf of the deceased
Slapping one's cheeks, tearing garments, wailing loudly in despair, and cursing destiny
explanationEn: While gentle tears are a mercy Allah places in tender hearts, screaming and tearing clothes violate patience and contentment with Allah's decree.

questionEn: When walking through Jannat al-Baqi or visiting Mount Uhud, why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say 'Visit the graves, for they remind you of the Hereafter'?
optionsEn: Standing calmly beside humble earthen graves softens hard hearts, curbs worldly arrogance, and inspires sincere repentance
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, after initially forbidding grave visits early on to eliminate pre-Islamic customs, the Prophet ﷺ explicitly recommended visiting graves specifically to remember death and the Hereafter.

questionEn: What should a visitor avoid doing with dust, pebbles, or tree leaves from Jannat al-Baqi, Mount Uhud, or Masjid Quba?
optionsEn: Keeping the area spotless without littering
Collecting dirt, pebbles, or leaves under the belief that they possess magical blessing or healing power
explanationEn: Neither the Companions nor the Tabi'in ever collected cemetery dust for talismans; true spiritual benefit comes from following the Sunnah, praying sincerely, and learning from their lives.

questionEn: What is the proper intention (Niyyah) a pilgrim should make in their heart before traveling to Madinah?
optionsEn: Traveling to visit and pray in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (with the additional blessing of greeting the Prophet ﷺ, visiting Quba, Baqi, and Uhud once there)
Replacing obligatory Hajj with a Madinah trip
Traveling exclusively to touch brass grilles
Traveling solely to take photos for social media
explanationEn: Because Sahih al-Bukhari permits setting out on a religious journey only to the Three Mosques, scholars advise intending the visit to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—through which all noble Madinah Ziyarah naturally follows.

questionEn: Is visiting Madinah and Al-Masjid an-Nabawi an obligatory pillar (rukn) or condition for the validity of Hajj or Umrah?
optionsEn: Yes, seven circuits around Quba are mandatory
Yes, Ihram must be worn inside Baqi
Yes, Umrah is completely invalid without visiting Madinah
No; Hajj and Umrah rites take place in Makkah and the Mashair, while visiting Madinah is a deeply cherished, spiritually rewarding Sunnah journey
explanationEn: Clarifying this prevents unnecessary anxiety for pilgrims unable to travel north, while highlighting how precious visiting the Prophet's ﷺ city is whenever possible.

questionEn: When a pilgrim leaves Madinah after their stay, what recommended practice did classical scholars suggest inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Performing a farewell Tawaf around the Green Dome
Walking backward all the way out of the city
Throwing seven pebbles at Bab al-Salam
Praying two rak'ahs in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, making sincere dua, offering a quiet farewell Salam at the Sacred Chamber, and asking Allah to grant another return
explanationEn: Leaving Madinah with a heart full of gratitude, Salawat, and resolve to live by the Sunnah—without inventing a 'farewell tawaf'—aligns beautifully with Prophetic etiquette.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim dress and conduct themselves throughout Madinah, not only inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: With modesty, cleanliness, gentle speech, patience in crowds, and generosity toward the weak and elderly
explanationEn: Living out Prophetic character in Madinah's streets, hotels, buses, and mosques honors the Prophet ﷺ far more truly than external gestures alone.

questionEn: What time of day is Jannat al-Baqi typically open for men to enter and offer Salam and pray for its deceased?
optionsEn: Only at midnight on the 15th of Sha'ban
Usually briefly after Fajr and after Asr prayers (following the cemetery's regulated schedule)
explanationEn: Opening cleanly after Fajr and Asr allows orderly funeral burials and dignified, quiet visits without night hazards.

questionEn: Why are cameras, loud chatter, and eating/drinking discouraged inside Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: To preserve solemn reverence for the dead, privacy for grieving families burying loved ones, and reflection on the Hereafter
explanationEn: Respecting bereaved families and maintaining quiet contemplation keeps Jannat al-Baqi a sanctuary of peace and reflection.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about sending charity or making Dua on behalf of deceased Muslims buried in Baqi or elsewhere?
optionsEn: Nothing ever benefits the deceased after burial
Sincere Dua, seeking forgiveness, and giving charity (or performing Hajj/Umrah) on their behalf genuinely benefit the deceased by Allah's grace
Only musicians at funerals help them
explanationEn: Confirmed in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (e.g., Sa'd ibn Ubadah digging a well for his deceased mother in Madinah), ongoing charity and sincere prayer bring real joy to the departed.

questionEn: Which Ansari companion asked Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah what best charity he could give on behalf of his mother who passed away suddenly without leaving a will?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA), who dug a water well in Madinah saying 'This is for the mother of Sa'd!'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ approved it immediately and declared 'Providing water is the best charity'—establishing one of Islam's noblest traditions of Sadaqah Jariyah for parents.

questionEn: When visiting Mount Uhud early in the morning, what moving reflection did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding the martyrs resting there?
optionsEn: They traded fleeting earthly safety for eternal closeness to Allah, and 'witnessing for them' means remembering their faithfulness to truth and the Messenger ﷺ
They wished they had stayed home with Abdullah ibn Ubayy
They lost every reward because the battle was hard
explanationEn: Even though Uhud brought painful losses, the Qur'an (3:139-140) uplifted the believers: 'Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are true believers.'

questionEn: What is the best thing to pray for while standing peacefully near the Martyrs of Uhud?
optionsEn: Ask the hill for good business luck
Pray to Allah for their forgiveness and highest stations in Paradise, and ask Allah to keep our own hearts steadfast in obedience to His Messenger ﷺ
Collect sand to carry in your suitcase
explanationEn: Remembering how one moment of disobedience on Jabal al-Rumat changed the tide of Uhud makes praying for steadfast obedience to the Sunnah the deepest lesson of Uhud.

questionEn: What simple Sunnah act can a pilgrim perform every day in Madinah to emulate the Ansar's generosity?
optionsEn: Sharing dates, water, meals, or warm smiles with fellow pilgrims, especially during Iftar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's courtyards
explanationEn: During Ramadan and Mondays/Thursdays in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Madinah residents joyfully compete to invite strangers to share Iftar spreads—continuing the Ansar spirit alive today.

questionEn: What happens in the courtyards of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi just before Maghrib during Ramadan and fasting days?
optionsEn: All gates are locked for three hours
Long rows of Iftar mats are laid out voluntarily by Madinah families and charities offering dates, Zamzam, yogurt, and bread to every visitor equally
Meals are sold at high auction prices
explanationEn: No matter one's country, wealth, or language, sitting side-by-side on the courtyard sufrah in Madinah captures the true brotherhood of the Ansar and Muhajirun.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage fasting Mondays and Thursdays, and what special link do Mondays have to Madinah and his life?
optionsEn: Because rain only fell on Thursdays
Because Quba was closed on Fridays
Because markets were closed on Mondays
He was born on a Monday, revelation began on a Monday, he arrived in Quba/Madinah on a Monday, and passed away on a Monday—and deeds are presented to Allah on Mondays and Thursdays
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, when asked about fasting Monday, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'That is the day on which I was born and the day on which revelation came to me.'

questionEn: Which two graves inside Jannat al-Baqi—besides the Martyrs of Uhud—are remembered in Seerah when the Prophet ﷺ walked past and heard two people being punished in their graves, then placed a split fresh palm branch over them?
optionsEn: The graves of Abu Bakr and Umar (RA)
Two graves (often narrated in Madinah/elsewhere) where one had spread malicious gossip (namimah) and the other failed to shield himself properly from urine splashes
The graves of Uthman and Ali (RA)
The graves of Hamzah and Mus'ab (RA)
explanationEn: This Sahih al-Bukhari Hadith warns believers in Madinah and everywhere to guard their tongues from gossip and safeguard ritual cleanliness.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the cleanliness and purity of Madinah's mosques, including removing even a speck of dirt?
optionsEn: He praised keeping mosques clean, perfumed, and spotless—teaching that removing harm from a mosque is an honored act of devotion
He said dust should never be swept
He forbade using pleasant scents in mosques
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ loved pleasant natural fragrance (such as musk and oud) and personally valued keeping Al-Masjid an-Nabawi clean and welcoming.

questionEn: Which companion—the Prophet's ﷺ freedman and adopted son before adoption rules changed—led expeditions from Madinah and was martyred at Mu'tah in 8 AH, causing the Prophet ﷺ to weep in Madinah?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) (along with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah RA)
explanationEn: Receiving news of the three commanders' martyrdom at Mu'tah via revelation while sitting in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ wept openly and visited Ja'far's family in Madinah to comfort his children and have food prepared for them.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What beautiful Sunnah of community care did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ establish in Madinah on the day Ja'far ibn Abi Talib's (RA) family received news of his martyrdom?
optionsEn: 'Leave them alone for seven days without visiting'
'Prepare food for the family of Ja'far, for there has come to them that which preoccupies them'
'Let the bereaved family cook a banquet for the whole city'
'Hold a loud celebration outside their door'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud and Sunan al-Tirmidhi (Hasan), cooking and sending meals to grieving neighbors became a compassionate Prophetic Sunnah across the Muslim world.

questionEn: Who was appointed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in his final days—at just around eighteen years old—to command the Madinah expedition northward toward Syria, which Abu Bakr (RA) insisted on dispatching after becoming Caliph?
explanationEn: Despite pressure to cancel the expedition after the Prophet's ﷺ passing, Caliph Abu Bakr (RA) walked on foot beside young Usamah's (RA) horse out of Madinah toward Al-Jurf, insisting on fulfilling the Prophet's ﷺ final command.

questionEn: How did Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) show extraordinary humility when walking Usamah ibn Zayd's (RA) army out of Madinah?
optionsEn: He walked on foot while young commander Usamah rode, and humbly asked Usamah's permission to let Umar (RA) remain behind in Madinah to assist him
He rode ahead on a golden chariot
explanationEn: Abu Bakr's (RA) respect for the Prophet's ﷺ appointed young leader—and his calm resolve in protecting Madinah—stabilized Arabia during its greatest crisis.

questionEn: What is the best spiritual takeaway a pilgrim can bring back home from visiting Madinah's landmarks—Masjid Quba, Al-Rawdah, Uhud, Khandaq, and Baqi?
optionsEn: Deepened love for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ expressed through practicing his Sunnah daily, uniting hearts in brotherhood, and preparing sincerely for the Hereafter
Bragging about how many photos were taken
Forgetting daily prayers upon returning home
explanationEn: The true fruit of Madinah Ziyarah appears after returning home: gentler character, steadier prayer, love for the Qur'an, and faithful adherence to the Prophetic way.

questionEn: Which young boy of Madinah—younger half-brother of Anas ibn Malik (RA)—was gently teased by the Prophet ﷺ when visiting his home: 'O Abu Umayr, what happened to the little sparrow (al-nughayr)?'?
optionsEn: Abu Umayr (RA), son of Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym (RA)
explanationEn: When the little boy's pet bird died, the Prophet ﷺ showed remarkable warmth toward children in Madinah by playfully comforting him in his home.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: What remarkable story of faith involved Umm Sulaym (RA) and Abu Talhah (RA) in Madinah when their young infant passed away while Abu Talhah was out?
optionsEn: She washed and shrouded the child calmly, fed Abu Talhah first upon his return so he would gain strength, and broke the news gently as a trust returned to Allah
She hid the death for a whole year
She tore her garments and shouted across the street
explanationEn: When Abu Talhah (RA) told the Prophet ﷺ in the morning at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Allah's blessing on their night—and Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah was born, whose descendants included ten Qur'an scholars!

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid building mosques atop graves in Baqi or elsewhere, even for the most righteous believers?
optionsEn: To protect the purity of Islamic monotheism (Tawhid) so graves never become objects of worship or devotion alongside Allah
Because cemeteries were meant to be forgotten
Because stone was too expensive in Madinah
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim records the Prophet's ﷺ dying counsel warning against turning graves of prophets or righteous people into places of worship.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi regarding every idol and raised tomb structure when sent to enforce the Sunnah?
optionsEn: 'Do not leave any idol without effacing it, nor any high raised grave without leveling it (to the normal hand-span mound)'
explanationEn: Narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) in Sahih Muslim, this establishes the traditional simplicity seen today across Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—known as 'Dhul-Nurayn' (Possessor of Two Lights)—rests in Jannat al-Baqi alongside two of his daughters?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA), husband of Ruqayyah (RA) and then Umm Kulthum (RA)
explanationEn: Both Ruqayyah (RA, 2 AH) and Umm Kulthum (RA, 9 AH) preceded Uthman (RA) into Jannat al-Baqi, where he later joined them in 35 AH.

questionEn: Why did Uthman ibn Affan (RA) remain behind in Madinah during the Battle of Badr in 2 AH, yet still receive a full share of Badr's reward and spoils from Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed him to stay in Madinah to nurse his critically ill wife Ruqayyah (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ daughter
Because Uthman was away in Syria trading
Because Abu Bakr asked him to guard Quba
explanationEn: On the very day Zayd ibn Harithah rode into Madinah announcing the victory of Badr, the Muslims were finishing Ruqayyah's (RA) burial in Jannat al-Baqi.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Who was the beloved wife of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ known as 'Umm al-Masakin' (Mother of the Poor) who passed away in Madinah just months after marriage and rests in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Honored for feeding the destitute of Madinah generously, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah (RA) lived only about eight months after marrying the Prophet ﷺ and was buried in Baqi.

questionEn: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—known as the first of his wives to pass away after him because she had the 'longest arm' in charity—is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away around 20 AH during Umar's (RA) caliphate, Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) earned the Prophet's ﷺ prediction—her 'longest hand' turned out to mean utmost generosity in giving charity to Madinah's poor.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—famous for safeguarding the master written sheets (Suhuf) of the Qur'an compiled under Abu Bakr (RA)—lived and died in Madinah and is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Trusted with the authentic master copy of the Qur'an after Umar's (RA) martyrdom, Hafsah (RA) preserved those scrolls in Madinah until Uthman (RA) requested them to standardize official Mushafs.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: Who was the last surviving Mother of the Believers (wife of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) to pass away in Madinah around 61/62 AH and be buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: Umm Salamah (Hind bint Abi Umayyah, RA)
explanationEn: Wise counselor of Hudaybiyyah and prolific Hadith narrator, Umm Salamah (RA) outlived the Prophet's ﷺ other wives in Madinah and rests in Baqi.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—originally of Banu al-Nadir in Madinah—used to distribute generous charity in Madinah and defended Uthman (RA) during his siege before resting in Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away around 50 AH in Madinah, Safiyyah (RA) left a legacy of quiet generosity and loyalty.

questionEn: Which noble aunt of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—mother of his disciple Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (RA)—passed away in Madinah around 20 AH and rests in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib (RA) passed away peacefully in Madinah during Umar's (RA) caliphate around 20 AH and was laid to rest in Baqi.

questionEn: Where is Aqil ibn Abi Talib (RA), elder brother of Ali (RA) and expert genealogist of Quraysh in Madinah, buried?
explanationEn: Settling in Madinah and remaining respected into Mu'awiyah's era, Aqil ibn Abi Talib (RA) rests in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: Which companion—the great Qur'an scribe and collector Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)—passed away in Madinah around 45 AH and is buried in Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Eulogized by Abu Hurayrah (RA) as 'the scholar of this Ummah' upon his death in Madinah, Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) led both Abu Bakr's and Uthman's Qur'an compilation committees.

questionEn: What deeply moving remark did Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) utter at the burial of Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Whoever wishes to see how knowledge disappears, let him see it thus—today vast knowledge has been buried!'
explanationEn: Despite occasional scholarly debates between them, Ibn Abbas (RA) held Zayd's stirrup out of respect for his Qur'anic mastery and mourned his passing deeply.

questionEn: Which companion buried in Jannat al-Baqi was so revered for his Qur'anic recitation that Allah specifically commanded the Prophet ﷺ to recite Surah Al-Bayyinah to him?
optionsEn: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA), 'Sayyid al-Qurra' (Master of the Qur'an Reciters)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy (RA) 'Allah commanded me to recite Surah Al-Bayyinah to you,' Ubayy wept with awe asking 'Did He mention me by name?' and passed away in Madinah in 29/30 AH.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi about the single greatest verse in the entire Qur'an?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Kursi (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255), upon which the Prophet ﷺ tapped Ubayy's chest saying: 'May knowledge bring you joy, O Abu al-Mundhir!'
explanationEn: Recognized as the foremost authority in Qur'an recitation in Madinah, Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) passed on his mastery directly to Madinah's students.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Prayer of Travelers

questionEn: Where is Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported to be buried according to major historical accounts (alongside Kufah traditions)?
optionsEn: Jannat al-Baqi in Madinah, after returning to Madinah near the end of Uthman's (RA) caliphate in 32 AH
explanationEn: Major early sources state Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) returned to Madinah, reconciled warmly with Uthman (RA), and was buried at night in Baqi next to Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA) as he had requested.

questionEn: Which companion—the great warrior and conqueror of Persia at Al-Qadisiyyah, and one of the Ten Promised Paradise—asked on his deathbed at Al-Aqiq to be shrouded in his old woollen cloak from Badr and carried to Jannat al-Baqi?
explanationEn: Passing away in his home at Al-Aqiq in 55 AH as the last surviving member of the Ten Promised Paradise, Sa'd (RA) was carried on men's shoulders into Madinah and buried in Baqi in his cherished Badr cloak.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Funerals & Ibn Sa'd

questionEn: What touching scene occurred at Masjid al-Mustarah or Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when the funeral bier of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) passed through Madinah in 55 AH?
optionsEn: The Mothers of the Believers (led by Aishah RA) asked for his bier to be brought inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi so they could offer Janazah prayer over him
They insisted he be buried outside Madinah
They forbade anyone from praying over him
They refused to open the mosque doors
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, when some people objected to bringing a bier inside the mosque, Aishah (RA) corrected them: 'How quickly people forget! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself prayed over Suhayl ibn Bayda inside the mosque!'

questionEn: Which companion's funeral inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did Aishah (RA) cite to prove the permissibility of offering Salat al-Janazah inside the mosque?
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim records Aishah's (RA) authoritative ruling from Madinah establishing that praying Janazah inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is completely valid and practiced today after every daily prayer.

questionEn: Which Ansari companion had his wounded eye miraculously restored by Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ blessed hand during the Battle of Uhud?
optionsEn: Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man (RA), whose restored eye became the sharper and healthier of his two eyes
explanationEn: Recorded by Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Hakim, Qatadah (RA) lived in Madinah long after Uhud, with that restored eye outlasting his other eye in clarity.

questionEn: Which heroic Ansari companion stayed beside Prophet Muhammad ﷺ throughout the crisis of Uhud, parrying arrows until his bow broke and receiving the Prophet's ﷺ unique ransom phrase: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you!'?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) (and Abu Talhah al-Ansari shielded him alongside)
explanationEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) testified he never heard the Prophet ﷺ say 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you' to anyone except Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) at Uhud (and also Al-Zubayr at Khandaq).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which companion—cousin of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through his aunt Safiyyah—heard the Prophet ﷺ say 'Every prophet has a disciple (hawari), and my disciple is...' during the Battle of the Trench?
explanationEn: Volunteering repeatedly in the freezing cold of Khandaq to scout Banu Qurayzah's intentions, Al-Zubayr (RA) earned the timeless title 'Hawari Rasulillah' (Disciple of the Messenger of Allah).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which female companion from Madinah—mother of Anas ibn Malik (RA)—carried a dagger in her belt during Hunayn and bravely tended wounded Muslims at Uhud by hauling waterskins?
explanationEn: Along with Aishah (RA) and Umm Sulaym (RA) rolling up their sleeves to carry heavy water pouches to parched warriors at Uhud, Madinah's women displayed tireless courage and compassion.

questionEn: Who was the heroic companion who led the Muslims' surprise counter-raid into Al-Ghabah (just north of Madinah) on foot, outrunning horsemen and single-handedly recovering the Prophet's ﷺ stolen camels?
explanationEn: During the raid of Dhu Qarad (6 AH) right outside Madinah, Salamah (RA) ran effortlessly across the lava hills, pinned down the raiders with arrows until cavalry arrived, and was praised by the Prophet ﷺ: 'The best of our foot soldiers today is Salamah!'

questionEn: What remarkable spiritual commitment did Salamah ibn al-Akwa' (RA) fulfill near the end of his life after living for years in Al-Rabadhah following Uthman's (RA) martyrdom?
optionsEn: He deliberately returned to Madinah just days before his death so he would pass away in the Prophet's ﷺ sanctuary and rest in Jannat al-Baqi
explanationEn: Returning to Madinah in 74 AH after decades in the desert, Salamah (RA) died peacefully days later in Madinah and was buried in Baqi.

questionEn: What happened to Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ horse or camel during the Battle of the Trench when the enemy coalition tried to mock the Muslims outside Madinah?
optionsEn: Enemy horsemen failed completely to cross the trench except Amr ibn Abd Wudd and a couple of riders, who were swiftly repelled
Enemy ships sailed up Wadi al-Aqiq
explanationEn: The five-kilometer Khandaq proved a brilliant engineering triumph under Salman al-Farsi's (RA) counsel and the Prophet's ﷺ leadership.

questionEn: How many total Muslim martyrs fell during the month-long siege of the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) in 5 AH?
optionsEn: None—not a single person was wounded
Only six Muslim martyrs (including Sa'd ibn Mu'adh RA from his fatal wound)
explanationEn: Thanks to Salman's (RA) defensive trench strategy and Allah's protection, casualties on both sides remained remarkably low despite 10,000 besiegers.

questionEn: Which companion—one of the 'Three Who Were Left Behind' from Tabuk—wept sincerely in Madinah for fifty days until Surah At-Tawbah (9:118) announced Allah's forgiveness?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) (alongside Hilal ibn Umayyah and Murarah ibn al-Rabi', RA)
explanationEn: Unlike hypocrites who invented false excuses, Ka'b (RA) told the Prophet ﷺ the plain truth in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi; after 50 agonizing days of social boycott, a rider shouted the glad tiding of Allah's forgiveness from atop Mount Sal'!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: From which mountain in Madinah did a companion shout at the top of his voice to bring Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) the joyful news that Allah had accepted his repentance?
explanationEn: Sitting in prayer on a rooftop in Madinah on the 50th morning, Ka'b (RA) heard the herald's voice booming from Mount Sal': 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!'—and fell immediately into prostration of gratitude.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What did Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) joyfully give away on the spot to the herald who raced on horseback to tell him of Allah's forgiveness?
optionsEn: Both of the outer garments he was wearing, even though he owned no others at that moment
explanationEn: Borrowing two garments from Abu Qatadah (RA) just to walk to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Ka'b (RA) walked in to see the Prophet's ﷺ face shining like the full moon with joy.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What life-changing pledge did Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) make before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi after Surah At-Tawbah (9:118-119) was revealed?
optionsEn: Because Allah saved him specifically through truthfulness, he vowed never to speak anything except the truth for the rest of his life
He vowed never to speak again
He vowed never to fast again
He vowed to move out of Madinah forever
explanationEn: Immediately after 9:118 came 9:119: 'O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful (al-sadiqin)'—and Ka'b (RA) testified that Allah tested and blessed him for keeping that pledge all his life.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—known as 'Abu Khaythamah'—turned back on foot after catching up with the Tabuk expedition days late upon realizing the Prophet ﷺ was enduring scorching heat while he sat in cool shade?
explanationEn: Returning from his cool orchard in Madinah where his wives had chilled water and dates waiting, Abu Khaythamah felt ashamed of his comfort, mounted his camel immediately, and rode through the desert until overtaking the Prophet ﷺ at Tabuk.

questionEn: What happened to the arch-hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul when he died in Madinah in 9 AH after the Tabuk expedition?
optionsEn: He fled to Rome and died at sea
He was buried inside the Sacred Chamber
Out of sheer compassion (before Surah 9:84 forbade it), Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave his own shirt for his shroud and prayed over him before Allah revealed 9:84 forbidding prayer over deceased hypocrites
explanationEn: Revealing 9:84 ('Never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand by his grave'), Allah drew an eternal boundary protecting the dignity of Muslim funeral prayers in Madinah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Funerals & Surah 9:84

questionEn: Where is the resting place of Malik ibn Anas (Imam Dar al-Hijrah) located inside Jannat al-Baqi relative to the graves of the Companions?
optionsEn: Near the grave of his teacher/predecessor scholars and the Prophet's ﷺ infant son Ibrahim (in the eastern/central historic area of Baqi)
explanationEn: Resting among the companions and scholars of the city he refused even to ride an animal inside out of reverence, Imam Malik remains a symbol of Madinah's scholarly soul.

questionEn: What should a visitor notice about the cemetery wall and layout of Jannat al-Baqi today compared to centuries past?
optionsEn: It is enclosed by a clean marble-clad wall with wide paved pedestrian paths separating simple grave rows in complete conformity with the Sunnah
It is submerged under a lake
It has neon signs over every grave
explanationEn: Clean walkways allow large crowds after Fajr and Asr to offer Salam peacefully without stepping upon any believer's grave.

questionEn: When offering Salam at Jannat al-Baqi, which direction does a visitor face when reciting the graveyard greeting vs when making personal Dua?
optionsEn: Sit directly atop a grave mound
Face the cemetery peacefully while offering Salam; for longer personal Dua (raising hands), turning toward the Qiblah (south) is preferred by scholars
Face strictly north toward Mount Uhud for all prayers
explanationEn: Keeping Salam directed toward the deceased and personal raised-hand Dua directed toward the Qiblah mirrors Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ own practice and preserves pure Tawhid.

questionEn: What misconception do some visitors hold about visiting 40 prayers in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 8 consecutive days?
optionsEn: One must stay 40 months in Madinah

While praying every possible prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is deeply virtuous (1,000x reward each), the specific '40-prayer immunity' narration is graded weak by many hadith masters—so pilgrims should never miss Hajj/Umrah duties or stress anxiously if flight schedules allow fewer days
Only 40 prayers ever count; the 41st carries zero reward
Missing one of the 40 prayers invalidates Hajj completely
explanationEn: Every single prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi carries immense reward—better than 1,000 elsewhere—without an artificial minimum quota; travelers should enjoy every prayer calmly with sincerity.

questionEn: Why is it helpful for Duya travelers visiting Uhud to wear comfortable shoes, carry water, and visit early in the morning?
optionsEn: Because Mount Uhud only opens at 2 AM
Because Madinah's daytime sun heats the granite slopes of Uhud intensely, whereas morning hours offer cool air for peaceful reflection at Sayyid al-Shuhada and Jabal al-Rumat
Because water is illegal after noon
Because buses only run in winter
explanationEn: Practical foresight allows pilgrims to reflect serenely on Uhud's Seerah lessons without rushing or suffering heat exhaustion.

questionEn: How does visiting both Mount Uhud and the Battle of the Trench site in one morning enrich a Muslim's understanding of Madinah's history?
optionsEn: It contrasts the painful lesson of disobedience at Uhud (3 AH) with the triumph of unity, strategy, and reliance on Allah at Khandaq (5 AH)
It proves warfare was Madinah's only activity
It shows Quraysh conquered Madinah twice
explanationEn: Seeing the physical terrain—Archers' Hill across from Uhud and Mount Sal' overlooking the northern trench—makes the Qur'anic narratives of Aal Imran and Al-Ahzab come vividly alive.

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an is specifically named 'Al-Ahzab' (The Confederates) because of the siege around Madinah in 5 AH?
explanationEn: Revealed around 5 AH, Surah Al-Ahzab documents the psychological intensity of the Confederate siege and teaches believers patience, modesty, and reverence for the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab (33:56), what timeless command follows the lessons of Madinah's trials—linking every visitor's tongue in Madinah to heavenly worship?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with worthy peace!'
explanationEn: Every Salawat whispered inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi joins the eternal praise of Allah and His angels described in 33:56.

questionEn: Which companion's grave at Uhud was covered by the Prophet's ﷺ own mantle or had fresh idhkhir grass laid over his feet because his single cloak could not cover both his head and feet?
explanationEn: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari that when they pulled Mus'ab's short striped cloak over his head, his feet showed, and when they pulled it over his feet, his head showed—so the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Cover his head and put idhkhir grass over his feet.'

questionEn: What noble promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make regarding the orphans and daughters left behind by the martyrs of Uhud, such as the daughters of Hamzah (RA) and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (RA)?
optionsEn: He personally cared for their families, arranged honorable guardianships, and protected their inheritance rights (inspiring Surah An-Nisa 4:11)
He sent all orphans out of Madinah
explanationEn: When Sa'd ibn al-Rabi's (RA) widow feared his brother would seize all property leaving his two daughters destitute, Allah revealed the Qur'anic laws of inheritance (4:11) in Madinah, securing women's and orphans' financial rights forever.

questionEn: Which verse of the Qur'an was revealed in Madinah directly to protect the daughters of Uhud's martyr Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (RA)?
optionsEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:11 (the foundational verse of Islamic inheritance shares)
explanationEn: Prior to Islam, women and young girls were often excluded from inheritance; Allah answered Sa'd's widow's plea in Madinah by enshrining fixed shares for daughters, mothers, and wives in Surah An-Nisa.

questionEn: What compassionate ruling did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enact in Madinah when Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) married an older experienced woman instead of a young virgin right after losing his father at Uhud?
optionsEn: Learning Jabir married a mature matron specifically to care for his seven/nine orphaned younger sisters from Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ praised his selflessness warmly and prayed for him
He ordered Jabir to leave his sisters alone
explanationEn: Then on the journey home, the Prophet ﷺ bought Jabir's slow camel for gold and gifted it right back to him alongside the gold to help support his orphaned sisters!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ miraculously pay off all the debts left by Jabir's father Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram (RA) after his martyrdom at Uhud?
optionsEn: He told creditors to wait ten years

He walked around Jabir's harvested heaps of dates in Madinah, prayed for blessing, and sat beside them while Jabir measured out every creditor's debt in full—leaving the entire original amount still remaining!
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, not a single date appeared missing from the blessed heap after every Jewish creditor received full repayment.

questionEn: What happens to the souls of children of believers who pass away in infancy—like the Prophet's ﷺ own son Ibrahim resting in Jannat al-Baqi?
optionsEn: They are cared for in Paradise under the guardianship of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Sarah, serving as joyful intercessors/forerunners for their believing parents
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet's ﷺ vision showed Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in a lush meadow surrounded by all children who died on pure fitrah—and he specifically comforted parents of infants that their children await them at Paradise's gates.

questionEn: What comforting Hadith did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ share in Madinah for parents—like the Ansar women who buried three children in Baqi—who endure losing young children with patience?
optionsEn: 'Children cannot meet parents in the Hereafter'
'Parents must wear black for ten years'
'No Muslim loses three children before reaching puberty except that Allah admits them to Paradise by His mercy toward them' (and even two, when Abu Sa'id asked!)
'No reward is given for patience in bereavement'
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, when the women of Madinah asked for a dedicated day of teaching, the Prophet ﷺ came to them and comforted grieving mothers with this mercy-filled promise.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Knowledge & Funerals

questionEn: Why did the women of Madinah specifically ask Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to set aside a separate day to teach them in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'The men have taken all your time from us, O Messenger of Allah—appoint a day of your own for us!'—and he gladly agreed
Because women were banned from entering Madinah
Because men forbade women from learning Qur'an
Because women refused to pray Fajr
explanationEn: Honoring women's eagerness for authentic Islamic knowledge, the Prophet ﷺ regularly taught Madinah's women directly, producing towering scholars like Aishah (RA) and Umm Salamah (RA).

questionEn: Which landmark sits directly south of the Martyrs of Uhud enclosure today, allowing visitors to picture how narrow the gap was that the fifty archers guarded in 3 AH?
explanationEn: Standing just a short walk from the martyrs' resting place, Archers' Hill helps every visitor grasp why leaving that small knoll exposed the entire rear flank.

questionEn: What respectful gesture is shown toward visitors by the layout of Sayyid al-Shuhada Plaza at Uhud today?
optionsEn: Guided climbing tours directly over graves
Shaded walkways, an expansive mosque, educational signage, and a clean perimeter fence around the martyrs' burial ground so visitors can offer Salam peacefully
explanationEn: Preserving dignity and safety while hosting millions of pilgrims yearly, Sayyid al-Shuhada Plaza facilitates reflective, Sunnah-compliant Ziyarah.

questionEn: What should every pilgrim remember when leaving Mount Uhud and heading back toward Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: That Uhud is located inside Makkah
That visiting Uhud replaces Friday prayer
That stones from Uhud cure diseases
That Uhud teaches steadfastness in hardship, obedience to Prophetic guidance even when victory seems won, and love for those who sacrificed everything for our Deen
explanationEn: Integrating Uhud's spiritual lessons into daily life turns a brief historical bus stop into lasting faith renewal.

questionEn: Which wise elder poet of Yathrib met Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Makkah before the First Pledge of Aqabah, listened to the Qur'an, and exclaimed 'This is far nobler than the Wisdom of Luqman!'?
explanationEn: Encountering the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah while performing pilgrimage, Suwayd recognized the majesty of the Qur'an over his cherished Scroll of Luqman before returning to Yathrib.

questionEn: Which young man of Banu Abd al-Ashhal from Yathrib visited Makkah seeking an alliance against Khazraj, heard the Qur'an from Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and declared 'This is better than what we came for!'?
explanationEn: Though his elder companions initially brushed him off, Iyas returned to Yathrib praising Allah and embracing Islam shortly before his premature passing.

questionEn: How many pilgrims from Yathrib met Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at Al-Aqabah in Mina during the 11th year of Prophethood—becoming the very first group of Ansar to embrace Islam?
explanationEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah, Awf ibn al-Harith, Rafi' ibn Malik, Qutbah ibn Amir, Uqbah ibn Amir, and Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Ri'ab pledged faith at Al-Aqabah and carried Islam back to Yathrib.

questionEn: How many representatives from Yathrib returned the next year (12th year of Prophethood) to swear the First Pledge of Al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: Twelve men (ten from Al-Khazraj and two from Al-Aws)
explanationEn: Known as Bay'at al-Nisa (Pledge of Women) because it did not yet stipulate warfare, it bound them to pure Tawhid, honesty, chastity, avoiding infanticide and slander, and obeying the Prophet ﷺ in good.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Who were the two men from Al-Aws who joined the ten men of Al-Khazraj at the First Pledge of Al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA) and Uwaym ibn Sa'idah (RA)
explanationEn: Their presence healed decades of rivalry between Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj in Yathrib, uniting both tribes around the banner of Islam.

questionEn: Who was sent back to Yathrib with the twelve pledgers after the First Pledge of Al-Aqabah as Islam's first ambassador and Qur'an teacher in Madinah?
explanationEn: Once a pampered aristocrat of Makkah, Mus'ab (RA) lived modestly in Madinah teaching the Qur'an with wisdom and gentleness, earning the title 'Al-Muqri' (The Reciter).

questionEn: How many Muslims from Madinah (including two women) secretly gathered at night during Hajj in the 13th year of Prophethood to swear the Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: Seventy-three men and two women (seventy-five total)
explanationEn: Escorted under cover of darkness to the gorge of Al-Aqabah, they pledged to protect Prophet Muhammad ﷺ just as they protected their own families and children.

questionEn: Who were the two heroic Medinan women present at the Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: Nusaybah bint Ka'b (Umm Umarah, RA) and Asma bint Amr (Umm Mani', RA)
explanationEn: Their participation at Al-Aqabah proved that Medinan women stood shoulder to shoulder in pledging allegiance and building the Islamic community.

questionEn: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ accompanied him to the Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah—before his own public conversion later—to ensure the Medinans understood the gravity of their commitment?
optionsEn: Abu Talib (who had already passed away)
explanationEn: Al-Abbas urged the Medinans to either defend the Prophet ﷺ wholeheartedly or leave him safely among his Makkan clan; they affirmed unwavering loyalty without hesitation.

questionEn: Who was the very first Medinan leader to clasp Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ hand at the Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah?
optionsEn: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur (RA) (with Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan first interrupting to ask about their future loyalty)
explanationEn: Before clasping hands, Abu al-Haytham asked whether the Prophet ﷺ might abandon Madinah if Allah granted him Makkah later; smiling, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Rather, blood for blood, ruin for ruin—I am of you and you are of me!'

questionEn: How many clan supervisors (Nuqaba') did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ select from the Ansar at the Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah to organize Madinah's Muslim community?
optionsEn: Twelve Nuqaba' (nine from Al-Khazraj and three from Al-Aws)
explanationEn: Appointing twelve local leaders mirrored the twelve leaders of the Children of Israel, giving Madinah's new community immediate structure before the Hijrah even began.

questionEn: Which prophetic reassurance did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give the Ansar at Al-Aqabah when Al-Abbas ibn Ubadah asked what their reward would be if they kept every word of the pledge?
explanationEn: Hearing the single-word promise 'Paradise!', the Ansar stretched out their hands immediately saying: 'Stretch out your hand, O Messenger of Allah—we will never cancel this pledge nor ask back out of it!'

questionEn: Who was the very first Emigrant (Muhajir) from Makkah to arrive in Madinah ahead of the main Hijrah?
explanationEn: Separated heartbreakingly from his wife Umm Salamah (RA) and infant son by Quraysh clan disputes, Abu Salamah (RA) reached Quba roughly a year before the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Which companion emigrated openly in daylight after telling Quraysh chiefs at the Kaaba: 'Whoever wishes his mother to bereave him, let him meet me behind this valley tomorrow!'?
explanationEn: While most persecuted believers slipped away quietly at night, Umar (RA) girded his sword, circumambulated the Kaaba, prayed two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim, and departed unchallenged with twenty companions.

questionEn: Where did the earliest Muhajirun settle upon reaching Madinah before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrived, and who hosted many of them?
optionsEn: In Quba and Al-Awali, hosted warmly in the homes of Kulthum ibn al-Hidm, Sa'd ibn Khaythamah, and Mubashshir ibn Abd al-Mundhir (RA)
explanationEn: Even before seeing the Prophet ﷺ arrive, Medinan Ansar eagerly drew lots whenever multiple hosts competed to welcome an arriving emigrant!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Which famous guide from Banu al-Dil—trusted for his desert navigation despite not yet being Muslim—led Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) safely along little-known coastal trails to Madinah?
explanationEn: Hiring an honest, skilled non-Muslim guide for critical navigation showed Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ wisdom in taking practical precautions alongside absolute trust (tawakkul) in Allah.

questionEn: Which bounty-hunter from Madlaj overtook Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) on the road toward Madinah, only for his horse's legs to sink into solid desert sand three times?
explanationEn: Witnessing his horse sink repeatedly and realizing Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would prevail, Suraqah asked for a written note of safe-conduct and received the stunning prophecy that he would one day wear the golden bracelets of Khosrow!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: What touching gesture did Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (RA) offer Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) when meeting them on the Hijrah road returning from a trade caravan to Syria?
optionsEn: He refused to speak to them
He warned them to return to Makkah
He gifted them fine white garments to wear as they entered Madinah
explanationEn: Meeting the Prophet ﷺ near the road toward Madinah, Al-Zubayr (RA) gladly dressed the two weary travelers in clean white attire before their arrival in Quba.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Who was the famous Jewish scholar of Yathrib who heard Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrive in Quba, recognized his prophetic signs from the Torah, and converted secretly before proclaiming it before his people?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) (originally named Al-Husayn ibn Salam)
explanationEn: Asking the Prophet ﷺ to ask his community about his standing first (they praised him as 'our chief and scholar'), Abdullah then stepped forward proclaiming the Shahadah—exposing their sudden hypocrisy when they instantly slandered him.

questionEn: Which three profound questions did Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) put to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ upon his arrival in Madinah to verify his prophethood?
optionsEn: How deep is the Red Sea, how old is Uhud, and how many stars exist?
When will gold rain from the sky?
Who built Damascus, Rome, and Alexandria?
What is the first sign of the Hour, what is the first meal of the people of Paradise, and why does a child resemble its father or mother?
explanationEn: Informed immediately by Angel Jibril (AS), the Prophet ﷺ answered all three cleanly: a fire driving people east to west, the caudate lobe of fish-liver, and parental precedence in conception—convincing Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) at once.

questionEn: Who was the young Medinan boy—brought by his mother Umm Sulaym (RA) to serve Prophet Muhammad ﷺ upon his arrival in Madinah—who served him faithfully for ten full years?
explanationEn: Ten-year-old Anas (RA) testified that in ten years of close service in Madinah, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never once struck him, scolded him, or asked 'Why did you do that?' or 'Why did you not do that?'

questionEn: What threefold blessing did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray for young Anas ibn Malik (RA) at Umm Sulaym's (RA) request in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, keep him poor and childless'
'O Allah, send him away from Madinah'
'O Allah, grant him only ten years of life'
'O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You give him!'
explanationEn: Allah answered that dua astonishingly: Anas's orchards bore fruit twice a year, he was blessed with over a hundred children and grandchildren, and lived past a hundred years!

questionEn: What happened to Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ daughters Fatimah (RA) and Umm Kulthum (RA), plus his wife Sawdah (RA), right after he settled in Madinah?
optionsEn: They remained in Makkah for fifteen years
He sent Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Rafi' with camels and 500 dirhams from Abu Bakr to escort his family—alongside Abu Bakr's family including Aishah and Asma—safely from Makkah to Madinah
explanationEn: Even while settling into Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ ensured his household and Abu Bakr's (RA) family were brought safely to Dar al-Hijrah.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ eldest daughter Zaynab (RA) arrive in Madinah later than her sisters?
optionsEn: Because her husband Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi' was still non-Muslim in Makkah until after Badr, when he honored his promise to send Zaynab safely to Madinah
explanationEn: Reunited later in Madinah when Abu al-As accepted Islam and had his earlier marriage upheld, Zaynab's (RA) loyalty and suffering during her escape moved the Prophet ﷺ deeply.

questionEn: Which famous welcome song is preserved in Islamic cultural memory as sung by Madinah's children and women upon welcoming Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (attributed either to the Hijrah arrival or his joyful return from Tabuk)?
optionsEn: 'Tala'al-Badru 'Alayna' (The Full Moon Has Risen Upon Us)
explanationEn: While historians like Ibn Hajar note the poetic verses may also connect with the Prophet's ﷺ joyful return from Tabuk from Thaniyyat al-Wada', they remain timelessly linked to Madinah's love for the Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: What was 'Thaniyyat al-Wada'' (The Pass of Farewell) in Madinah?
optionsEn: A market stall of Banu Qaynuqa
The northern/northwestern ridge-pass outside Madinah (or southern pass in earlier routes) where residents bid farewell to departing travelers and welcomed returning loved ones
explanationEn: Mentioned in Hadith (such as horse-racing distances from Al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wada'), it served as Madinah's traditional gateway of departure and joyful welcome.

questionEn: Which calendar system—starting from the 1st of Muharram of the year of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ migration to Madinah (622 CE)—was later instituted by Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
explanationEn: Consulting senior Companions in 17 AH after Abu Musa al-Ash'ari received undated official letters, Umar (RA) rejected birth or death dates and chose the Hijrah to Madinah because it separated truth from falsehood and established the Islamic community.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and the Companions select the Hijrah to Madinah—rather than the Prophet's ﷺ birth or first revelation—as Year 1 of the Islamic calendar?
optionsEn: Because Muharram was a Makkan trade festival
Because the Hijrah to Madinah marked the decisive establishment of Islam as a free, unified, and sovereign moral community
Because nobody remembered the Prophet's ﷺ birth month
explanationEn: Marking Muharram (when the resolve for Hijrah took shape after Al-Aqabah) as Month 1 of 1 AH anchored Muslim history forever in Madinah.

questionEn: Who was the very first baby born to the Muhajirun in Madinah after the Hijrah—refuting a malicious rumor that Madinah's inhabitants had been bewitched into infertility?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA), born to Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) in Quba
explanationEn: Overjoyed at his birth in Quba, the Muslims raised Takbir across Madinah; Prophet Muhammad ﷺ chewed a date (tahnik) to touch the newborn's palate and named him Abdullah after his grandfather Abu Bakr.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Who was the very first baby born to the Ansar in Madinah after Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ arrival?
optionsEn: Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (RA) (born about 14 months after the Hijrah)
explanationEn: Growing up under the Prophet's ﷺ direct care in Madinah, Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (RA) later narrated the famed Hadith on the halal, haram, and the heart ('Indeed, in the body is a morsel of flesh...').

questionEn: In whose home in Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ formally establish the historic Pact of Brotherhood (Al-Mu'akhah) between the Muhajirun and the Ansar?
optionsEn: The house of Abu Sufyan in Makkah
The home of Anas ibn Malik (RA) (or inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in concurrent reports)
explanationEn: Gathering roughly ninety men—forty-five Muhajirun and forty-five Ansar—Prophet Muhammad ﷺ paired each emigrant with an Ansari brother in a bond deeper than blood.

questionEn: With which noble Ansari companion was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) paired in brotherhood in Madinah?
explanationEn: Immediately offering to split his entire property in half and even divorce one of his two wives so Abd al-Rahman could marry, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (RA) epitomized Ansari generosity—while Abd al-Rahman graciously blessed him and asked only: 'Show me the way to the market!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: How did Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) prosper in Madinah's market on his very first day after declining Sa'd ibn al-Rabi's (RA) offer of half his wealth?
optionsEn: He found buried coins in Baqi
Starting with dried yogurt and butterfat, he traded honestly until within days he had enough gold to pay a marriage dowry (mahr) and host his wedding feast
explanationEn: Becoming one of Madinah's wealthiest yet most humble and charitable merchants, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) later funded entire expeditions and freed thousands of slaves.

questionEn: With which Ansari companion was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) paired in brotherhood in Madinah?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) stayed in Al-Sunh with Kharijah's (RA) clan and later married Kharijah's daughter Habibah, cementing lifelong family ties with Madinah.

questionEn: With which Ansari companion was Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) paired in brotherhood in Madinah?
optionsEn: Itban ibn Malik (RA) (or Uwaym ibn Sa'idah in some narrations)
explanationEn: Umar (RA) and his Ansari neighbor in Al-Awali took turns every other day attending Al-Masjid an-Nabawi so neither missed a single revelation or teaching while still earning a livelihood.

questionEn: How did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and his Ansari neighbor ensure neither missed any teaching from the Prophet ﷺ while working in Madinah's orchards?
optionsEn: They hired someone to take notes for money
They alternated days: one stayed with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ all day and reported everything at night while the other tended the farm, then swapped the next day
They stopped working completely for ten years
explanationEn: That mutual pact in Al-Awali shows how Madinah's early Muslims balanced honest daily labor with an insatiable thirst for sacred knowledge.

questionEn: With which companion was Salman al-Farsi (RA) paired in brotherhood in Madinah?
optionsEn: Abu al-Darda (Uwaymir ibn Zayd al-Ansari, RA)
explanationEn: When Salman (RA) visited Abu al-Darda's house in Madinah and saw him neglecting his wife and sleep for nonstop fasting and night worship, Salman gently advised him: 'Your Lord has a right over you, your soul has a right over you, and your family has a right over you—give each its due!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when Abu al-Darda (RA) told him about Salman al-Farsi's (RA) advice on balancing worship, rest, and family in Madinah?
optionsEn: He ﷺ affirmed warmly: 'Salman has spoken the truth!'
He ordered Abu al-Darda to stop sleeping forever
He told Salman to keep quiet
explanationEn: This celebrated Madinan dialogue established Islamic moderation—harmonizing spiritual devotion with family care and physical rest.

questionEn: With which Ansari companion—whose brother-in-law/companion was also beloved—was Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) paired in brotherhood in Madinah?
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) later established state stipends, Bilal (RA) insisted his stipend be recorded beside his brother-in-Islam Abu Ruwayhah's name out of lifelong affection.

questionEn: With which Muhajir companion was Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) paired when the Prophet ﷺ united the brothers in Madinah according to classic Seerah narrations?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ took Ali's (RA) hand and said: 'You are my brother in this world and the Hereafter!' (or in Muhajir-Ansar pairing, Sahl ibn Hunayf RA)
explanationEn: Both traditions reflect Ali's (RA) unique closeness to the Prophet's ﷺ household as well as strong solidarity with Madinah's Ansar.

questionEn: What extraordinary temporary legal arrangement existed during the earliest period of the Brotherhood Pact (Mu'akhah) in Madinah?
optionsEn: Paired Muhajirun and Ansar brothers inherited directly from each other until Surah Al-Anfal (8:75) restored inheritance solely to blood kin
They could never live in separate houses
explanationEn: By allowing spiritual brothers to inherit while emigrants were completely severed from their Makkan families, Allah protected vulnerable emigrants until Madinah's economy stabilized.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Inheritance & Surah 8:75

questionEn: Which Surah and verse in the Qur'an immortalizes the Ansar's extraordinary selflessness ('Ithar') toward the Muhajirun in Madinah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hashr 59:9 ('They give them preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in poverty')
explanationEn: Even when an Ansari family like Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym (RA) had only enough food for their children, they put the children to sleep and dimmed the lamp so their hungry guest could eat fully—moving Allah to reveal 59:9!

questionEn: What self-sacrificing trick did an Ansari host and his wife use one night in Madinah so their Muhajir guest sent by the Prophet ﷺ would not feel shy eating their children's tiny meal?
optionsEn: They borrowed gold from the market
The wife pretended to fix the oil lamp and put it out, while the couple sat moving their empty hands toward the dish in the dark so the guest thought they were eating with him
They locked the guest outside in the yard
explanationEn: When they arrived at Fajr in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ smiled and told them: 'Allah marveled (laughed with pleasure) at what the two of you did last night for your guest!'

questionEn: When the Muhajirun noticed how deeply the Ansar worked their date orchards and shared harvests with them, what worried the Muhajirun enough to bring to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'We want to return to Makkah immediately'
'O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen people more generous than the Ansar—we fear they may take the entire reward in the Hereafter while leaving us none!'
'The Ansar are charging us too much rent'
explanationEn: Reassuring the Muhajirun warmly, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'No—not as long as you thank them sincerely and pray to Allah for them!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ address the Ansar's voluntary offer to split their date palms equally with the Muhajirun right after Bani Nadir / arrival?
optionsEn: He chopped down half the palms

Instead of taking away the Ansar's ownership of their trees, the Prophet ﷺ arranged for Muhajirun to share in working the land and sharing the fruit, later returning the trees cleanly when Khaybar opened
He confiscated all orchards for the state
He sold the orchards to Yemen
explanationEn: By balancing mutual support with respect for property and grateful return after Khaybar (7 AH), the Prophet ﷺ preserved lasting harmony between Muhajirun and Ansar.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ institute a regular census in early Madinah—asking Companions to 'Write down for me every person who has professed Islam'?
optionsEn: To organize community care, defense readiness, and support for Madinah's growing Muslim population (~1,500 counted in the early census)
To charge entrance fees to the mosque
explanationEn: Narrated by Hudhayfah (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, that early register counted around 1,500 believers in Madinah, demonstrating careful civic administration from the very start.

questionEn: What foundational economic institution did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ establish in Madinah independent of existing monopolies so fair trade could flourish?
optionsEn: A royal customs tollhouse charging 50% tax
A state monopoly banning private trade
Suq al-Madinah (The Prophet's Market), declared a tax-free open market with no permanent reserved stalls or tolls
explanationEn: Planting his foot in an open space (later in Al-Manakhah / northwest of the mosque), the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'This is your market—let it not be narrowed and let no tax (kharaj) be levied upon it!'

questionEn: What sharp ethical reform did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enforce immediately while walking through Madinah's market, dipping his hand into a heap of grain?
optionsEn: He raised the price of the wet grain
He forced buyers to pay blindfolded
Finding wet grain hidden beneath dry grain, he rebuked the seller: 'Whoever cheats us is not of us!'
explanationEn: Regular market inspections by the Prophet ﷺ (and later Umar RA) uprooted fraud, false oaths, hoarding, and usury (riba) in Madinah's commerce.

questionEn: Which two financial practices did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage in Madinah's marketplace to cultivate trust and mercy?
optionsEn: Charging compound interest on late loans
Swearing false oaths to boost sales
Lenience when buying, selling, and collecting debts, and forgiving or deferring payment for a debtor in genuine hardship
explanationEn: 'May Allah have mercy on a person who is generous/lenient when he sells, when he buys, and when he demands repayment' (Sahih al-Bukhari).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ eliminate chronic tribal blood feuds between Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj once he settled in Madinah?
optionsEn: He exiled both tribes to Yemen
He fenced off Al-Aws from Al-Khazraj permanently
He reminded them of their shared brotherhood in Allah whenever old pre-Islamic quarrels flared, healing rifts before swords could be drawn
explanationEn: When Shas ibn Qays tried to spark an old Bu'ath feud with pre-Islamic poetry, the Prophet ﷺ rushed to the scene crying 'Is it the call of Jahiliyyah while I am still among you?!'—moving both tribes to drop their weapons and embrace in tears.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage in Surah Aal Imran (3:103) directly celebrates how Allah united the warring hearts of Madinah's tribes upon Islam?
optionsEn: 'Travel across the earth and look at the sea'
'Remember the favor of Allah upon you—when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers'
explanationEn: Recalled repeatedly in Friday sermons in Madinah, 3:103 reminds Muslims that true unity of hearts is a miracle bestowed by Allah.

questionEn: What historic civic charter did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ draft in 1 AH uniting Madinah's Muhajirun, Ansar, and local Jewish tribes under mutual rights and defense?
optionsEn: The Constitution of Madinah (Sahifat al-Madinah / Al-Wathiqah)
explanationEn: Widely recognized as one of history's earliest written constitutional charters, Sahifat al-Madinah defined shared citizenship, mutual security, religious liberty, and rule of law in Madinah.

questionEn: In the opening clauses of the Constitution of Madinah, how did the document describe the Muslims of Quraysh, Yathrib, and those allied with them?
optionsEn: 'Each clan remains completely sovereign at war with its neighbors'
'They are one single community (Ummah Wahidah) distinct from all other people'
explanationEn: Transforming fragmented tribal clans into 'Ummah Wahidah' shifted allegiance from narrow tribalism to shared faith, justice, and moral responsibility.

questionEn: How did the Constitution of Madinah address the religious rights of the Jewish tribes residing peacefully inside Madinah?
optionsEn: It banned them from owning orchards
It expelled them on Day 1 of 1 AH
It forced immediate conversion under threat of sword
It affirmed 'To the Jews their religion, and to the Muslims their religion,' guaranteeing security and equal justice as long as they upheld the pact
explanationEn: Granting explicit freedom of religion and mutual defense alongside Madinah's Muslims made the Constitution of Madinah a landmark of pluralistic governance.

questionEn: According to the Constitution of Madinah, what shared responsibility applied whenever Madinah faced an external military attack?
optionsEn: All signatories—Muslims and allied Jewish tribes—must bear their own expenses and mutually defend Madinah against external aggression, without aiding Quraysh
Only the Muhajirun had to defend the city
Allied tribes were free to invite Quraysh inside
explanationEn: Mutual defense against outside threats was the core security pledge of the document—later violated when Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah conspired with Quraysh.

questionEn: Under the Constitution of Madinah, who was designated as the final legal arbiter whenever grave disputes arose among the city's diverse tribes?
optionsEn: Allah and Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
The elders of Quraysh in Makkah
explanationEn: Replacing endless cycles of tribal blood-revenge with impartial arbitration by Allah's Messenger ﷺ gave Madinah true rule of law.

questionEn: What clear principle of individual criminal accountability did the Constitution of Madinah establish against pre-Islamic collective punishment?
optionsEn: 'Tribes may raid any neighbor for unpaid debts'
'A wrongdoer acts only against himself and his household'—forbidding collective vengeance against innocent clan members
'Every relative of a criminal must be exiled'
explanationEn: Breaking the pre-Islamic cycle of tribal vendettas, the charter held each offender personally accountable while encouraging clans to pool resources justly for lawful blood-money (ma'aqil) and prisoner ransom.

questionEn: What protection did the Constitution of Madinah grant to Madinah's inner territory itself ('Jawf Yathrib')?
optionsEn: The interior valley of Yathrib was declared a protected, sacred sanctuary (Haram) for all signatories of the charter
It was declared open to bandits
explanationEn: Sanctifying the civic valley forbade violent feuding inside the city and bound residents to collective peace.

questionEn: Which rule in the Constitution of Madinah prevented one neighbor's hasty actions from dragging the whole city into war?
optionsEn: Merchants could bring Makkan troops into Madinah
Every household could start private wars
No ally could declare war or offer protection to Quraysh without the permission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
explanationEn: Centralizing foreign policy and war decisions prevented rogue clan conflicts from destabilizing Madinah.

questionEn: How did the Constitution of Madinah handle ransoming war captives and paying accidental blood-money (diyah) within each tribe?
optionsEn: Each clan retained its mutual solidarity fund (ma'aqil) to ransom captives and pay blood-money with fairness and equity among believers
Only orphans had to pay debts
explanationEn: Reforming existing social-insurance customs rather than discarding what was good, Islam transformed tribal solidarity into equitable community welfare.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do in Madinah to eliminate the pre-Islamic custom of 'Al-Diyah' inequality where noble clans valued their blood higher than humble clans?
optionsEn: He doubled penalties for poor citizens
He established equal justice and equal human worth before the law for all believers, rich or poor
He exempted Quraysh from all laws
He allowed revenge killings without trial
explanationEn: Upholding Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:45) and the Constitution's fairness clause, Islam erased aristocratic legal double standards in Madinah.

questionEn: Which Jewish clan in Madinah was the first to break the Constitution of Madinah in 2 AH after Badr by mocking Muslims, assaulting a Muslim woman in the market, and killing a Muslim defender?
explanationEn: After a goldsmith of Banu Qaynuqa pinned a Muslim woman's skirt causing exposure and a Muslim bystander was killed, the Prophet ﷺ besieged their fortress for 15 nights until they surrendered and departed peacefully northward.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ spare the lives of Banu Qaynuqa in 2 AH and allow them to leave Madinah with their property (minus weapons)?
optionsEn: Following consultation and honoring their departure terms after Abdullah ibn Ubayy pleaded persistently on their behalf
Because they surrendered all their gold to Rome
explanationEn: Displaying measured restraint, the Prophet ﷺ neutralized an internal security threat inside Madinah's marketplace while avoiding unnecessary bloodshed.

questionEn: What treacherous plot led to the peaceful evacuation of Banu al-Nadir from southeastern Madinah in 4 AH?
optionsEn: They built a dam flooding Masjid Quba
While Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visited them seeking their treaty-mandated share for an accidental blood-money payment, their leaders plotted to drop a heavy millstone onto him from a rooftop
explanationEn: Informed through divine revelation, the Prophet ﷺ slipped quietly back to Madinah; after a brief siege, Banu al-Nadir surrendered and departed with whatever their camels could carry except weapons.

questionEn: What historic ruling did Surah Al-Hashr (59:7) establish in Madinah when distributing the properties left behind without combat ('Fai') by Banu al-Nadir?
optionsEn: It goes solely to foreign kings
It must be burned in the desert
It belongs strictly to the wealthiest merchants
Fai wealth is distributed to the Prophet's ﷺ family, orphans, the needy, and stranded travelers—explicitly 'so that wealth does not circulate solely among the rich among you'
explanationEn: With the Ansar's joyful consent, the Prophet ﷺ allotted much of those lands to the impoverished Muhajirun, lifting them out of dependency onto self-sufficiency.

questionEn: Which prominent Medinan hypocrite was exposed in Surah Al-Hashr (59:11) for secretly promising Banu al-Nadir military support ('If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you!'), then abandoning them?
explanationEn: When Banu al-Nadir stood besieged, Abdullah ibn Ubayy stayed comfortably inside Madinah—proving Allah's description of hypocrites as cowards whose promises vanish under test.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid in Madinah when Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to stand up every Friday before the sermon praising him hypocritically, or when he stirred division after the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq?
optionsEn: Even when Umar (RA) asked to execute Abdullah ibn Ubayy for saying 'The honorable will expel the lowly from Madinah,' the Prophet ﷺ famously refused: 'Lest people say Muhammad kills his own companions!'
He canceled Friday prayers in Madinah
He immediately executed every suspected hypocrite
explanationEn: Patience and strategic forbearance preserved Madinah's internal stability and prevented neighboring tribes from misunderstanding Islam.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir (Surah Al-Munafiqun)

questionEn: What remarkable stand did Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy—the sincere believing son of the arch-hypocrite—take at Madinah's city entrance upon returning from Banu al-Mustaliq?
optionsEn: He stood across the road with drawn sword blocking his own father from entering Madinah until his father admitted: 'Muhammad ﷺ is the honored one, and I am the lowly one!'
explanationEn: Yet earlier, when he thought the Prophet ﷺ might order his father's execution, young Abdullah gently offered to carry it out himself lest resentment against another killer fester in Madinah—and the Prophet ﷺ warmly reassured him he would treat his father kindly.

questionEn: What painful trial tested Madinah's social fabric and family honor in 5/6 AH after the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq until Allah revealed ten verses of Surah An-Nur (24:11-20)?
optionsEn: A dispute over Masjid Quba's roof
explanationEn: For an agonizing month, gossip spread by Abdullah ibn Ubayy shook Madinah until Allah personally vindicated Aishah's (RA) pure innocence from above the seven heavens and established strict laws against slander (qadhf).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What inspiring act of forgiveness did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) practice in Madinah right after Allah vindicated his daughter Aishah (RA) in Surah An-Nur (24:22)?
optionsEn: He banished Mistah from Arabia forever
He refused to speak to anyone in Madinah

Even though his needy relative Mistah ibn Uthathah had repeated the rumor, Abu Bakr (RA) resumed supporting Mistah financially immediately upon hearing Allah ask: 'Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?'
explanationEn: Declaring 'Yes, by Allah, I do love that Allah should forgive me!', Abu Bakr (RA) set an eternal standard of magnanimity for Madinah's believers.

questionEn: Which noble Ansari companion and his wife—Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) and Umm Ayyub—modeled the exact standard of Husn al-Zann (thinking well of fellow believers) during the crisis in Madinah?
optionsEn: They spread the rumor to ten neighbors
When Umm Ayyub mentioned the gossip, Abu Ayyub asked: 'Would you ever do such a thing?' She said 'No, by Allah!' He replied: 'And Aishah is even better than you!'
explanationEn: Surah An-Nur (24:12) directly praised believers who reacted immediately by saying: 'This is an obvious falsehood!'

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ set out from Madinah with 1,400 companions in Dhul-Qa'dah 6 AH intending only peaceful Umrah, what landmark treaty was signed outside Makkah before returning to Madinah?
explanationEn: Though some companions initially felt saddened turning back before entering Makkah, Allah revealed Surah Al-Fath (48:1) on the road back to Madinah calling Hudaybiyyah 'a clear victory (Fathan Mubina)'!

questionEn: Which Muslim woman from Makkah escaped to Madinah right after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, leading Allah to reveal Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:10) protecting believing women from being returned to non-Muslim persecution?
optionsEn: Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt (RA)
explanationEn: Walking much of the desert journey alone to reach Madinah, Umm Kulthum (RA) was tested for sincerity per 60:10 and granted permanent sanctuary in Madinah.

questionEn: What diplomatic outreach did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ launch from Madinah right after returning from Al-Hudaybiyyah in late 6 AH / early 7 AH?
optionsEn: Dispatching sealed letters bearing his silver signet ring ('Muhammad Rasul Allah') to major rulers—Heraclius, Khosrow, the Negus, Al-Muqawqis, and regional kings
Closing Madinah's borders to all travelers
Signing a tribute pact with Persia
explanationEn: Peace secured by Hudaybiyyah freed Madinah to fulfill its universal mission, inviting world leaders to Islam with clarity and dignity.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation & Jihad

questionEn: Which Makkan-turned-Muslim commanders rode together voluntarily to Madinah in Safar 8 AH to embrace Islam before the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-As, and Uthman ibn Talhah (RA)
explanationEn: Reaching Madinah independently and greeting the Prophet ﷺ at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, these three brilliant figures accepted Islam and helped transform Arabia.

questionEn: When Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah (RA) secretly sent a letter warning Makkah ahead of the Prophet's ﷺ surprise march from Madinah in Ramadan 8 AH, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ handle him upon catching the letter?
optionsEn: He canceled the march to Makkah
He executed Hatib inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi

He forgave Hatib after hearing his honest explanation (that he only sought protection for his Makkan family, not betrayal), reminding Umar (RA): 'He witnessed Badr—perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you!'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:1) gently admonished believers against secret enemy correspondence while the Prophet's ﷺ mercy preserved brotherhood in Madinah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: In what year did Madinah witness the 'Year of Delegations' ('Am al-Wufud), when tribes from across the Arabian Peninsula streamed into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to accept Islam?
optionsEn: 9 AH (following the Conquest of Makkah and the Battle of Tabuk)
explanationEn: Described in Surah Al-Nasr (110:2) as 'seeing people enter Allah's religion in crowds,' over seventy tribal delegations visited Madinah in 9 AH, received by the Prophet ﷺ near Ustuwana al-Wufud.

questionEn: Which delegation from Najran (southern Arabia) arrived in Madinah in 9 AH and was hospitably allowed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to stay and even offer their own prayer inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi while engaging in theological dialogue?
explanationEn: Welcoming the Najran delegation warmly inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Aal Imran's truths about Isa (AS), offered Mubahalah when they hesitated, and concluded a peaceful protection treaty guaranteeing their churches and freedom.
reference: Ibn Hisham & Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma'ad

questionEn: Which Arab chieftain from the tribe of Tayy traveled to Madinah after his sister's generous release and embraced Islam upon witnessing the Prophet's ﷺ humble compassion in Madinah's streets?
explanationEn: When an elderly needy woman stopped Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in a Madinah street and he stood patiently listening until her need was met, Adi ibn Hatim (RA) recognized instantly that this was a true Messenger, not a worldly king!

questionEn: Which towering Yemeni/Najdi tribal chief—Dimad ibn Tha'labah or Amr ibn Ma'dikarib or Al-Ashajj of Abd al-Qays—was praised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ upon arriving in Madinah for washing up calmly before greeting him rather than rushing in dusty travel clothes?
optionsEn: Al-Ashajj al-Asari (Mundhir ibn A'idh) of the Abd al-Qays delegation from Bahrain
explanationEn: While the rest of his delegation dismounted and rushed eagerly into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Al-Ashajj tied the camels, bathed, put on clean garments, and walked in calmly—earning the Prophet's ﷺ timeless praise: 'You possess two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance (hilm) and deliberation (anah)!'
