questionEn: When the Abd al-Qays delegation from eastern Arabia told the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah they could only reach him safely during the Sacred Months, what essential summary of Islam did he teach them?
optionsEn: To believe in Allah alone, establish prayer, pay Zakah, fast Ramadan, and give one-fifth of lawful spoils—while avoiding intoxicating drinks made in specific hollowed containers
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, the delegation carried those crisp foundations back to Bahrain, making Abd al-Qays one of the earliest communities outside Madinah to establish Jumu'ah prayer!

questionEn: Which mosque outside Madinah became the very second place on earth (after Al-Masjid an-Nabawi/Madinah) where Friday Jumu'ah prayer was established?
optionsEn: Masjid Juwatha (in Bahrain, among the tribe of Abd al-Qays)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) confirmed in Sahih al-Bukhari that the first Jumu'ah after the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah was held at Juwatha, a village of Abd al-Qays in eastern Arabia.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: Which brave tribe's delegation from Taif arrived in Madinah in Ramadan 9 AH after the Siege of Taif, requesting exemptions from Salah and breaking their idol Al-Lat—which the Prophet ﷺ gently refused regarding Salah?
explanationEn: Accepting their request to send Mughirah ibn Shu'bah and Abu Sufyan to demolish Al-Lat so they wouldn't do it with their own hands, the Prophet ﷺ stood firm on Salah: 'There is no good in a religion without prayer (rukū' and sujud)!'

questionEn: What remarkable spiritual hospitality did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show the non-Muslim delegation of Thaqif when they arrived in Madinah in 9 AH?
optionsEn: He hid the Qur'an from them
He banned them from entering Madinah
He imprisoned them in a dungeon
He pitched a special tent for them right inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi so they could witness the beauty of Muslim prayer, brotherhood, and Qur'an recitation firsthand
explanationEn: Hearing the Qur'an recited at Fajr and seeing Muslims stand shoulder-to-shoulder in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi softened Thaqif's hearts to embrace Islam.

questionEn: Which companion from Madinah was sent by the Prophet ﷺ in 9 AH to lead the first Muslim-led Hajj from Madinah to Makkah (while Surah At-Tawbah's opening was proclaimed by Ali RA)?
explanationEn: Leading 300 Muslims from Madinah to Makkah in Dhul-Qa'dah/Dhul-Hijjah 9 AH, Abu Bakr (RA) supervised the Hajj rites while Ali (RA) joined to proclaim Allah's final clearance from polytheist pacts.

questionEn: In 10 AH, how many Muslims accompanied Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he departed Madinah (taking Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah) for the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada')?
optionsEn: Over 100,000 Muslims (joining from Madinah and surrounding tribes along the route)
explanationEn: Departing Madinah on 25/26 Dhul-Qa'dah 10 AH after teaching the rulings of Hajj in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet ﷺ led the largest unified gathering of believers in his lifetime.

questionEn: What deeply emotional event occurred in Madinah during the final weeks after returning from the Farewell Pilgrimage in 11 AH?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ went to Baqi at night to pray for its dead, prayed at Uhud for the martyrs, and delivered his final sermons from the Minbar advising care for the Ansar and warning against idolizing graves
He appointed a king from Rome
He set off on a trade journey to Persia
explanationEn: Every step of those final days in Madinah radiated tender concern for his Ummah's unity, faith, and gratitude toward the Ansar.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What specific final testament regarding the Ansar of Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ deliver from his Minbar wrapped in a cloak during his final illness?
optionsEn: 'I advise you to treat the Ansar well! People will increase while the Ansar will diminish until they are like salt in food; accept good from those of them who do good, and overlook mistakes from those who err'
explanationEn: Even in intense fever days before passing, the Prophet ﷺ stepped out to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi specifically to safeguard the honor of Madinah's Ansar for all future generations.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Who was the last person among the Companions to be alone with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in his final moments—besides Aishah (RA), in whose lap his noble head rested?
optionsEn: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr (RA), whose fresh siwak Aishah (RA) chewed to soften for the Prophet ﷺ before he passed away
explanationEn: Passing away in Aishah's (RA) apartment with his head resting on her chest on Monday, 12 Rabi al-Awwal 11 AH, the Prophet's ﷺ last spoken words were: 'Rather, the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la)!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) steady the stunned community inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when Umar (RA) initially could not accept that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had passed away?
optionsEn: Stepping out from Aishah's chamber onto the Minbar, Abu Bakr recited Surah Aal Imran 3:144 and proclaimed: 'Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has passed away; whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies!'
He agreed that the Prophet ﷺ had only traveled to Taif
He closed Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for a month
He ordered everyone to leave Madinah
explanationEn: Hearing Abu Bakr recite 3:144 ('Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; messengers have passed before him...'), Umar's knees gave way in realization—and the crisis in Madinah immediately stabilized in Tawhid.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What historic meeting hall in Madinah (northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi) witnessed the Ansar and Muhajirun uniting upon Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) as the first Caliph on the day the Prophet ﷺ passed away?
optionsEn: Saqifah Bani Sa'idah (The Portico/Shelter of Banu Sa'idah)
explanationEn: Initially gathered to consider Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA), the Ansar listened with grace as Abu Bakr, Umar, and Abu Ubaydah reminded them of unity—and Umar (RA) initiated the Bay'ah to Abu Bakr (RA), followed by Muhajirun and Ansar together.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Limits and Punishments

questionEn: What garden park landmark stands today near the historic site of Saqifah Bani Sa'idah just west-northwest of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Saqifah Bani Sa'idah Park (an enclosed shaded historical garden west of the northern piazza)
explanationEn: Preserved as a quiet green park near Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's northwestern perimeter, it marks the spot where the Ummah preserved unity after its darkest day.

questionEn: What did Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) say inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during his inaugural acceptance speech the day after Saqifah Bani Sa'idah?
optionsEn: 'No poor person may enter my council'
'I have been given authority over you, though I am not the best of you. If I do well, help me; if I do wrong, correct me. Truthfulness is a trust and lying is betrayal!'
'I will move the capital out of Madinah'
explanationEn: Setting a breathtaking standard of accountable leadership in Madinah, Abu Bakr (RA) promised that the weak would be strong in his sight until their rights were restored.

questionEn: During the Apostasy Wars (Riddah) immediately after the Prophet's ﷺ passing, how did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) defend Madinah when rebel tribes marched on the city expecting it to be defenseless?
optionsEn: He stationed night guards under Ali, Al-Zubayr, Talhah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud around Madinah's approaches, then personally led a bold dawn sortie to Dhul-Qassah routing the attackers
He paid tribute to the rebels
explanationEn: Refusing to compromise even a camel's tether of Zakah, Abu Bakr's (RA) fearless defense of Madinah saved Islam's center and turned the tide across Arabia.

questionEn: Which noble action by Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) during the 'Year of Ashes' (Am al-Ramadah, 18 AH) saved Madinah and surrounding tribes from devastating famine?
optionsEn: He closed the city gates to hungry nomads
He locked Madinah's food reserves solely for officials

Umar vowed not to taste ghee, milk, or meat until the poorest citizen ate well, wrote for grain convoys from Egypt, Syria, and Iraq to Madinah, and personally cooked and served meals to starving refugees camping around Madinah
explanationEn: Even walking around Madinah with oil instead of butter until his skin darkened, Umar (RA) led the people outdoors to Al-Musalla where Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) prayed for rain—and Allah poured mercy across the Hijaz!

questionEn: Whose elderly uncle's hand did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) hold high during the severe drought prayer in Madinah in 18 AH, saying: 'O Allah, we used to seek rain through Your Prophet ﷺ, and now we seek it through the Prophet's ﷺ uncle's dua'?
explanationEn: Rather than calling on a deceased person directly, Umar (RA) strictly asked a living righteous elder—Al-Abbas (RA)—to make dua to Allah before the congregation, modeling pure Tawhid in Madinah.

questionEn: Which two companions served as the chief judges and jurists inside Madinah during the caliphates of Abu Bakr and Umar (RA)?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (under Abu Bakr), and Ali ibn Abi Talib & Zayd ibn Thabit (under Umar)
explanationEn: Even as Islam expanded from Persia to Egypt, Madinah remained the supreme judicial, legislative, and scholarly heart of the Caliphate.

questionEn: How did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) keep himself informed of the hardships of widows, orphans, and travelers in Madinah?
optionsEn: By staying locked inside a stone palace
By banning residents from walking after Maghrib
By personally patrolling Madinah's neighborhoods at night, carrying sacks of flour on his own back to needy tents such as the hungry mother boiling stones in water for her crying children
explanationEn: When his servant Aslam offered to carry the heavy flour sack, Umar (RA) replied: 'Will you carry my burden for me on the Day of Judgment?!'

questionEn: Where in Madinah was Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) fatally stabbed while standing in the Mihrab leading Fajr prayer in Dhul-Hijjah 23 AH?
optionsEn: Inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (at the front prayer niche)
explanationEn: Struck by Abu Lu'lu'ah Fayruz with a double-edged poisoned dagger while reciting Qur'an at Fajr, Umar (RA) pulled Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) forward to complete the prayer so the congregation's Salah wouldn't break.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Who led the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) for Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi before his burial inside the Sacred Chamber?
optionsEn: Suhayb al-Rumi (RA), whom Umar appointed to lead prayers temporarily while the six-man Shura council chose the next Caliph
explanationEn: Umar's (RA) choice of Suhayb al-Rumi (RA)—a former Makkan slave—to lead Madinah's prayers during the transition showed Islam's utter disregard for racial or social elitism.

questionEn: What monumental service to the Qur'an did Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) accomplish inside Madinah around 25–30 AH?
optionsEn: Commissioning Zayd ibn Thabit and a Quraysh committee in Madinah to produce standardized master copies (Al-Mushaf al-Uthmani) from Abu Bakr's/Hafsah's preserved Suhuf and dispatching them to major Islamic centers
Locking the single copy in a vault unread
Translating the Qur'an out of Arabic only
explanationEn: Keeping one master copy in Madinah itself ('Al-Mushaf al-Imam / al-Madani'), Uthman's (RA) historic project preserved the exact Qur'anic text in unbroken unity worldwide.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: Why did Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) forbid his loyal Medinan defenders from fighting the armed rebels besieging his house beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 35 AH?
optionsEn: Because he wanted to abandon Islam
He refused to shed a single drop of Muslim blood inside the Prophet's ﷺ Sacred Sanctuary of Madinah to save his own life
Because he had no friends in Madinah
Because he planned to flee to Rome
explanationEn: Even as Hassan, Hasan ibn Ali, Ibn Umar, and Ibn al-Zubayr stood armed at his door ready to defend him, Uthman (RA) commanded them home and passed away calmly reciting the Qur'an, fasting in Madinah.

questionEn: Where did Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) receive the allegiance of Madinah's Companions after Uthman's (RA) martyrdom before relocating the administrative headquarters to Kufah?
optionsEn: Inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah (35 AH)
explanationEn: Although political turbulence later pushed the administrative seat to Kufah and then Damascus, Madinah remained forever the spiritual, scholarly, and Prophetic capital of Islam.

questionEn: Which companion from Madinah—known as 'The Prophet's ﷺ Scribe of Revelation'—lived beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and recorded verses immediately as they descended?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) (alongside Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'awiyah, Ali, and others)
explanationEn: Just eleven years old at the Hijrah, Zayd mastered reading, writing, and even Hebrew/Syriac letters at the Prophet's ﷺ request in Madinah within weeks, becoming the chief scribe of revelation.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask young Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) in Madinah to learn the script of the Jewish communities ('Kitab Yahud')?
optionsEn: So Zayd could migrate to Europe
To open a bookstore in Makkah
So the Prophet ﷺ could trust his own faithful Muslim scribe to read and write correspondence securely without relying on untrusted interpreters
explanationEn: Mastering the script in just fifteen nights, Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) proved how Madinah's youth embraced learning with extraordinary zeal.

questionEn: Which famous treaty/letter dictated by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah to Ali (RA) or scribes established respectful coexistence with St. Catherine's / Christian monks and peaceful People of the Book?
optionsEn: Protective covenants (such as the Najran Covenant and letters guaranteeing monks' sanctuaries, taxes not exceeding capacity, and zero forced conversion)
explanationEn: Historical records in Ibn Sa'd and Abu Yusuf preserve the Madinan covenants granting Najran Christians full security of life, worship, and churches.
reference: Ibn Sa'd & Abu Yusuf, Kitab al-Kharaj

questionEn: What remarkable reform did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Madinah regarding pre-Islamic debt slavery, servitude, and freeing enslaved people?
optionsEn: He forbade freeing slaves in wills

He encouraged freeing slaves as expiation for sins, commanded masters to feed and clothe servants with what they themselves ate and wore, and forbade calling them 'my slave'—using 'my young man/woman' instead
explanationEn: Companions like Bilal, Zayd ibn Harithah, Salman al-Farsi, and Suhayb al-Rumi rose to become foremost leaders and beloved brothers of the Madinan community.

questionEn: Which companion—once enslaved in Madinah—was praised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ after hearing footsteps ahead of him in Paradise during the Night Journey/dream?
optionsEn: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA), because he never performed Wudu at any hour of day or night without praying two rak'ahs immediately afterward
explanationEn: Asked in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi what deed gave him greatest hope, Bilal (RA) shared his simple, consistent habit of praying two rak'ahs after every Wudu (Tahiyyat al-Wudu).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Night Prayer

questionEn: What compassionate rule did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Madinah when seeing an emaciated camel or overworked beast of burden in an Ansari orchard?
optionsEn: He ordered all camels sold immediately
He tied the camel without water

Entering an Ansari's garden where a weeping camel rubbed its head against him, the Prophet ﷺ stroked its ears gently and rebuked its owner: 'Do you not fear Allah regarding this beast He put in your possession? It complained to me that you starve it and overwork it!'
explanationEn: Animal mercy in Madinah extended even to warning against overloading mounts or taking baby birds from nests without returning them to their mother.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Jihad (Sahih)

questionEn: Which Sahih al-Bukhari incident in Madinah shows Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ joy and gentleness with children inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: He stopped the prayer and scolded the boy
He banned children under fifteen from mosques
He prolonged his prostration (sujud) while leading prayer when young Al-Hasan or Al-Husayn climbed onto his back, waiting patiently until his grandson climbed down on his own
explanationEn: He also carried his little granddaughter Umamah bint Abi al-As on his shoulder while leading prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—putting her down to prostrate and lifting her as he stood!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when he heard a baby crying behind him while leading congregational prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: He shortened the prayer deliberately out of compassion for the mother's anxious heart
He lengthened the recitation by an hour
He asked the mother to leave immediately
He banned mothers from attending Fajr or Isha
explanationEn: 'I stand in prayer intending to prolong it, then I hear the crying of a child, so I shorten my prayer lest I cause hardship to its mother' (Sahih al-Bukhari).

questionEn: Which elderly blind companion in Madinah—Itban ibn Malik (RA)—invited Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to pray in a corner of his house because seasonal floodwaters blocked his path to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Itban ibn Malik (RA), so that the exact spot where the Prophet ﷺ prayed in his home could become his family prayer space (musalla)
explanationEn: Walking all the way to Itban's home in Al-Awali with Abu Bakr (RA), the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Where do you want me to pray?' and led two rak'ahs with the family behind him—showing immense warmth toward Madinah's elders.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise another blind companion—Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA)—NOT to skip congregational prayer at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi if he could hear the Adhan?
optionsEn: Because Madinah had paved sidewalks with lamps
Because blind men were fined coins
Because prayers at home are completely invalid
Asking 'Do you hear the call to prayer?' and hearing 'Yes,' the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Then answer it!'—emphasizing the high priority of congregational prayer for able men
explanationEn: This Sahih Muslim Hadith highlights the spiritual centrality of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's prayer rows in the daily rhythm of Madinah.

questionEn: What special honor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeatedly bestow upon blind companion Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) whenever the Prophet ﷺ marched out of Madinah on expeditions?
optionsEn: Asking him to carry war banners at Badr
Appointing Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) as acting governor and deputy prayer-leader of Madinah more than ten times!
explanationEn: Entrusting the civic administration and daily Imamate of Madinah to a blind companion honored capability, integrity, and dignity above physical sight.

questionEn: Which companion—originally from Daws—came to Madinah with seventy or eighty families right after Khaybar (7 AH) and quickly learned Madinah's Qur'anic culture?
optionsEn: Al-Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi (RA) alongside Abu Hurayrah (RA)
explanationEn: Arriving just as the Muslims returned from Khaybar in 7 AH, the Dawsi emigrants enriched Madinah's community with devotion and scholarship.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct the people of Madinah regarding neighbors—after Angel Jibril (AS) emphasized neighborly rights so repeatedly?
optionsEn: 'Jibril kept advising me about the neighbor so much that I thought he would make the neighbor an heir!'
'Build higher walls to block breeze from your neighbor'
explanationEn: Sharing broth ('increase the water in your broth and give some to your neighbor'), smiling, and never harming a neighbor became hallmarks of Madinah's neighborhoods.

questionEn: Which two Madinah neighborhoods/tribes—Banu Salimah vs Banu al-Najjar—received special counsel when Banu Salimah thought of moving their homes closer to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Banu Salimah, whom the Prophet ﷺ gently advised: 'O Banu Salimah, stay in your homes—your footsteps (walking to the mosque) are recorded for you!'
explanationEn: Even though their neighborhood lay a distance northwest of the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ showed them that every extra step walked toward Al-Masjid an-Nabawi adds eternal reward.

questionEn: What happened when a man of Madinah living quite far from Al-Masjid an-Nabawi refused an offer to buy a donkey to ride to prayer, saying he wanted both his walking steps there and his steps back recorded?
optionsEn: He told him to pray only at home
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warmly reassured him: 'Allah has gathered all of that (both coming and returning steps) for you!'
He told the man only riding counts
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, this encourages Madinah pilgrims staying in hotels slightly further from the Haram courtyard to walk calmly with joy, knowing every step both ways is rewarded.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ handle legal disputes over land, inheritance, or water irrigation between neighbors in Madinah?
optionsEn: With patient mediation—as when Al-Zubayr (RA) and an Ansari neighbor disputed an irrigation channel in Al-Harrah, and the Prophet ﷺ advised Al-Zubayr first to water briefly and release water generously to his neighbor before enforcing Al-Zubayr's full strict right
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa (4:65) was revealed in connection with that very Madinah irrigation case, teaching total willingness to submit happily to the Prophet's ﷺ judgment.

questionEn: What practical public-health and urban cleanliness rule did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enforce in early Madinah regarding courtyards and pathways?
optionsEn: Sweeping courtyards clean, avoiding relieving oneself under shaded trees or on public walkways, and removing harmful obstacles from streets as an act of faith
explanationEn: 'Removing something harmful from the road is a branch of faith (Iman) and an act of charity (Sadaqah)' (Sahih Muslim).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage physical health and lawful recreation among the youth of Madinah?
optionsEn: Encouraging archery, horseback racing (from Al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wada'), running, and swimming while keeping modesty and prayer primary
explanationEn: Even racing affectionately with Aishah (RA) in the desert outside Madinah showed wholesome balance, warmth, and vitality.

questionEn: What famous horse-race route in Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ organize for trained vs untrained horses?
optionsEn: Trained horses raced from Al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wada' (~6–7 miles), while untrained horses raced from Thaniyyat al-Wada' to Masjid Bani Zurayq (~1 mile)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) personally rode in those Madinah races, witnessing the Prophet's ﷺ joyful encouragement of readiness and horsemanship.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once come across companions of Banu Aslam competing in archery in Madinah and encourage them?
optionsEn: In the marketplace/open ground of Madinah, saying: 'Shoot, O sons of Ismail, for your forefather (Ismail AS) was an archer!'
explanationEn: Adding playfully 'I am with Banu so-and-so!', when the opposing team lowered their bows thinking they couldn't beat his side, he smiled: 'Shoot! I am with ALL of you!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ establish clear ethical rules against cruel pre-Islamic customs involving animals in Madinah?
optionsEn: He allowed target practice on tied birds
He forbade branding animals on their faces, shooting live animals as archery targets, and cutting flesh off living beasts
explanationEn: Reforming Madinah's moral culture touched every creature, teaching accountability before Allah for every living soul.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

questionEn: What decisive social reform did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ carry out in Madinah regarding intoxication (khamr)?
optionsEn: Gradual divine legislation—from highlighting harm > benefit (2:219), forbidding praying while intoxicated (4:43), to total prohibition (5:90)—culminating in Companions spilling every wine jar so Madinah's streets ran with discarded date-wine
Taxing wine slightly while encouraging it
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) was pouring drinks at Abu Talhah's house when the herald cried Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:90); Abu Talhah immediately said 'Go out and spill it!'—and not a single Companion hesitated.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when a woman in Madinah suffered from epilepsy and asked him to pray for her healing?
optionsEn: He turned her away without listening

He offered her a choice: 'If you wish, be patient and Paradise is yours; or if you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you'—she chose patience for Paradise, asking only that he pray she wouldn't become uncovered during seizures
explanationEn: Known as Umm Zufar (RA), this noble Black woman of Madinah walked proudly through its streets, pointed out by Ibn Abbas (RA) to his student Ata as 'a woman of the people of Paradise!'

questionEn: What moving lesson in dignity and compassion did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Madinah when a lonely impoverished woman's mind was troubled and she asked him to speak with her privately?
optionsEn: He sent guards to arrest her
He refused to speak to women in public
He dismissed her because she had no wealth
He walked with her gently to whichever lane of Madinah she chose and sat patiently listening until all her needs were relieved
explanationEn: Anas (RA) recorded this in Sahih Muslim to illustrate that not even the highest political and spiritual leader in Madinah ever felt too important for the humblest citizen.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat an old Medinan slave-woman who fell ill and asked to see him, or what did he do for people who passed away owing unpaid debts in Madinah?
optionsEn: Early on he declined praying over a debtor unless someone guaranteed the debt (like Abu Qatadah RA did); later, when Allah enriched Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'I am closer to every believer than his own soul—whoever leaves a debt, it is upon me to pay it, and whoever leaves wealth, it belongs to his heirs!'
He refused burial for all poor people
He imprisoned widows for husbands' debts
He confiscated orphans' toys to pay debts
explanationEn: Madinah's Islamic state thus pioneered public social security, shielding grieving families from crushing debt.

questionEn: Which companion stepped forward in Madinah to guarantee a deceased Muslim's small debt of two dinars so the Prophet ﷺ would lead his Janazah prayer?
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ checked the next day whether Abu Qatadah had actually paid those two dinars and heard 'Yes, I just paid them,' he ﷺ smiled: 'Now his skin has cooled down!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid regarding pre-Islamic mourning practices in Madinah when the daughter of an Ansari or Uthman ibn Maz'un passed away?
optionsEn: Hiring professional wailing women (na'ihah) to scream, slap cheeks, and lament hysterically
explanationEn: Even when women pledged allegiance to Islam in Madinah, one explicit condition in Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:12) was obeying the Prophet ﷺ in good—which he clarified included abstaining from pre-Islamic wailing.

questionEn: What joyful, uplifting social tradition did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage in Madinah for Muslim weddings so marriages would be publicly known and celebrated lawfully?
optionsEn: Announcing the marriage openly, hosting a modest wedding feast (walimah)—even if only with a single sheep or barley/dates—and allowing young girls to beat the duff (hand drum) with joyful, modest songs
Holding secret marriages with no witnesses
explanationEn: When Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) married in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ told him warmly: 'Offer a walimah, even if only with one sheep!'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once instruct Aishah (RA) to send an Ansari singer/entertainer along with a young bride marrying an Ansari groom in Madinah?
optionsEn: Because music with drums is forbidden at weddings
'Verily, the Ansar love joyful celebration (al-lahw/ghazal)!'—encouraging lawful, modest joy at weddings
Because weddings must be completely silent
explanationEn: This Sahih al-Bukhari narration highlights the Prophet's ﷺ balanced warmth toward Medinan culture whenever it stayed within Islamic bounds.

questionEn: Which famous wedding feast (walimah) in Madinah witnessed the revelation of the verses of Hijab (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:53) teaching guests respectful home-visiting etiquette?
optionsEn: The Prophet's ﷺ wedding feast for Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) in 5 AH
The wedding of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
explanationEn: When a few lingering guests stayed chatting long after dinner, Surah Al-Ahzab (33:53) taught Muslims everywhere not to enter homes uninvited, not to linger needlessly after meals, and to speak respectfully from behind a screen.

questionEn: What clear rule of privacy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enforce for every home in Madinah, as taught to visiting guests?
optionsEn: Seeking permission three times before entering (knocking/greeting), standing slightly aside rather than staring straight inside the doorway, and leaving gracefully if told 'Go back'
explanationEn: Grounded in Surah An-Nur (24:27-28), Madinah's home etiquette protected dignity, trust, and family peace.

questionEn: What happened when a man peeked secretly through a crack into the Prophet's ﷺ chamber in Madinah while the Prophet ﷺ held an iron comb (midra)?
optionsEn: He removed all doors in Madinah
The Prophet ﷺ warned him sharply: 'Had I known you were looking, I would have poked your eye with this—seeking permission to enter was ordained solely because of the gaze!'
He invited the peeper inside for dates
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, this fierce defense of home privacy protects personal spaces across every Muslim community.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Seeking Permission

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach his Companions in Madinah to resolve anger or hostility between two estranged Muslims?
optionsEn: 'It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three nights: they meet and this one turns away and that one turns away—and the better of the two is the one who initiates the Salam first!'
explanationEn: Narrated by Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, initiating Salam melts resentment and keeps Madinah's brotherhood alive.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: What simple daily greeting did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ urge Madinah's residents to spread to both people they knew and strangers alike?
optionsEn: Spreading Salam ('Assalamu alaykum')—identified in Sahih al-Bukhari alongside feeding people as 'the best aspect of Islam'
explanationEn: Walking through Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today, hearing 'Assalamu alaykum' exchanged warmly across a hundred nations keeps that exact Medinan Sunnah alive.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when asked in Madinah why he greeted even young children playing in Madinah's streets with 'Assalamu alaykum'?
optionsEn: To instill humility in adults, teach children Islamic manners early, and wrap the entire city in peace and love
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) fondly remembered the Prophet ﷺ smiling and greeting children in Madinah as he walked past them.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah once walked through the marketplace solely to greet people with Salam, telling his companion: 'We only come out for the sake of greeting with Salam so we earn good deeds!'?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) (recorded with Tufayl ibn Ubayy in Muwatta Malik)
explanationEn: Even without needing to buy or sell anything, Ibn Umar (RA) walked Madinah's market streets spreading peace and earning Allah's reward.

questionEn: What touching gesture did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ practice whenever shaking hands with any Companion in Madinah?
optionsEn: He wore gloves to avoid touching people
He never pulled his hand away first until the other person let go, nor did he turn his face away until the speaker finished
He turned his back while people spoke
He refused to shake hands with poor companions
explanationEn: Such attentive presence made every person in Madinah feel deeply valued and heard by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questionEn: Which expedition—the final major military campaign led personally by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Madinah in Rajab 9 AH during extreme summer heat—tested Madinah's commitment to the utmost?
optionsEn: The Expedition of Tabuk (Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Campaign of Hardship)
explanationEn: Marching roughly 700 km north to Tabuk in scorching heat as ripe dates hung ready in Madinah's orchards, 30,000 Muslims proved their devotion without even needing a pitched battle as Byzantine forces withdrew.

questionEn: During the mobilization for Tabuk in Madinah, which Companion donated 1,000 gold dinars (and hundreds of equipped camels) into the Prophet's ﷺ lap, moving him to say: 'Nothing Uthman does after today can harm him!'?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) brought all his household's wealth, Umar (RA) brought half, poor Ansar carried single mudds of dates earned by night labor—and Uthman (RA) equipped a third of the entire army!

questionEn: Who were 'Al-Bakka'un' (The Weepers) in Madinah ahead of the Tabuk campaign, honored forever in Surah At-Tawbah (9:92)?
optionsEn: Seven impoverished sincere Companions who begged the Prophet ﷺ for mounts to join Tabuk and wept openly when he had no mounts left to give them
explanationEn: Allah explicitly absolved them in 9:92, honoring their brokenhearted tears as higher in worth than wealth.

questionEn: Who did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ leave in charge of his family and Madinah when marching north to Tabuk in 9 AH—comforting him with one of the most famous comparisons in Islamic history?
optionsEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), whom the Prophet ﷺ reassured: 'Are you not pleased to be to me as Harun (Aaron) was to Musa (Moses), except that there is no prophet after me?'
explanationEn: When hypocrites whispered that Ali was left behind out of dislike, Ali hurried to catch up outside Madinah and received that immortal reassurance before returning to safeguard Madinah.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—known as 'Abu Dharr al-Ghifari' (RA)—walked alone across the blazing desert on foot carrying his gear after his weak camel collapsed on the way to Tabuk, earning the Prophet's ﷺ moving prediction?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA), of whom the Prophet ﷺ said: 'May Allah have mercy on Abu Dharr—he walks alone, will die alone, and will be resurrected alone!'
explanationEn: Years later during Uthman's (RA) caliphate, Abu Dharr passed away peacefully in exile at Al-Rabadhah east of Madinah with only his wife and child present until a passing caravan (including Abdullah ibn Mas'ud!) arrived to bury him.

questionEn: Which three companions stayed behind in Madinah during Tabuk without any excuse, confessed honestly before the Prophet ﷺ in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and endured a fifty-day boycott until Allah revealed 9:118?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah (RA)
explanationEn: Even when the Christian king of Ghassan wrote tempting Ka'b (RA) to defect from Madinah during his isolation, Ka'b burned the letter immediately in his oven out of pure loyalty to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What remarkable spiritual reality did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ witness upon returning from Tabuk to Madinah regarding those sincere believers who stayed back only due to illness or lack of mounts?
optionsEn: 'Those unable to travel lose all reward'
'Indeed, in Madinah there are men who—whenever you traveled a path or crossed a valley—were right there with you in reward, held back only by valid excuse!'
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, this comforting Hadith teaches that sincere intention (niyyah) unites sick, elderly, or financially unable believers in full spiritual reward alongside those who can travel.

questionEn: What inspiring prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make for the youth and children of Madinah whenever seeing them run up to greet his returning caravan?
optionsEn: He lifted young children onto his camel before and behind him (such as Abdullah ibn Ja'far and Al-Hasan/Al-Husayn), gently wiping their heads with dua and joy
explanationEn: Welcoming children right into the heart of public joy taught Madinah's youngest generation to love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than their own parents.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ demonstrate unmatched gratitude toward the Ansar when distributing spoils or honoring Madinah in his final years?
optionsEn: He moved permanently back to Makkah in 8 AH
He never forgot a single kindness done to him in Madinah—honoring old visitors, praying for their families, and affirming his desire to live and die among them
He forgot the Ansar after Makkah opened
He levied extra taxes on Quba
explanationEn: Even after liberating Makkah—his birthplace—Prophet Muhammad ﷺ returned directly home to Madinah, remaining faithful to his pledge to the Ansar until his final breath.

questionEn: Which foundational pillars of Islamic worship—beyond the five daily prayers—were formally legislated by revelation in Madinah during the first few years after Hijrah?
optionsEn: Fasting the month of Ramadan (2 AH), Zakat al-Fitr and obligatory Zakah (2 AH), and Hajj (9/10 AH)
explanationEn: While Makkan revelation anchored pure Tawhid, the Hereafter, and the five daily prayers, Madinan revelation built the complete social, legal, and communal framework of Islam.

questionEn: What remarkable scene unfolded in Madinah on the first Eid al-Fitr in 2 AH after Ramadan fasting was newly ordained?
optionsEn: They fasted throughout Eid day itself
They traveled to Makkah for Eid
Muslims dressed cleanly, ate odd numbers of dates before heading outdoors to the Musalla (site of Masjid al-Ghamamah), paid Zakat al-Fitr beforehand, and walked one route there and another back
explanationEn: Walking one route to the Eid Musalla and returning via another allowed the Prophet ﷺ to greet more residents of Madinah and testify to Islam's joy across the city.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Two Eids

questionEn: What two sacrificial rams did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ slaughter in Madinah on Eid al-Adha to model Qurbani (Udhiyah) for the Muslim community?
optionsEn: None; sacrifice was only for Makkah
Two horned, white-and-black speckled rams—one for himself and his family, and one on behalf of everyone in his Ummah who could not afford a sacrifice
Ten wild gazelles from Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Practicing Udhiyah right in Madinah taught Muslims worldwide that Qurbani is a joyful Sunnah observed in every town on Eid al-Adha, not solely by Hajj pilgrims.

questionEn: Which companion was appointed in Madinah to oversee Zakat al-Fitr food collection (dates and barley)—leading to the famous Hadith where a mischievous jinn taught him Ayat al-Kursi?
explanationEn: Guarding Madinah's Ramadan Zakat al-Fitr dates three nights in a row, Abu Hurayrah (RA) caught a thief who begged mercy and disclosed that reciting Ayat al-Kursi before sleep brings an angelic protector until dawn—which the Prophet ﷺ confirmed: 'He told you the truth, though he is an inveterate liar!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond in Madinah when a barefoot, starving delegation from Mudar entered Al-Masjid an-Nabawi wearing torn striped wool cloaks?
optionsEn: His face changed with sorrow; he immediately climbed the Minbar after Dhuhr, urged charity, and beamed with joy like gold when an Ansari brought a heavy silver sack and others piled up food and clothes!
He told them to leave Madinah before Asr
He taxed them for entering the mosque
explanationEn: That moving afternoon in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi prompted the Prophet's ﷺ immortal Hadith: 'Whoever starts a good practice (sunnah hasanah) in Islam receives its reward and the reward of everyone who acts upon it!'

questionEn: What humorous and deeply humane moment occurred in Madinah when a companion confessed he had accidentally broken his Ramadan fast by intimacy with his wife?
optionsEn: Unable to free a slave, fast 60 days, or feed 60 poor people, he sat waiting until a huge basket of dates arrived for the Prophet ﷺ—and when told to give it to Madinah's poorest family, he exclaimed 'There is none poorer between its two lava plains than mine!', making the Prophet ﷺ laugh until his back teeth showed and tell him: 'Feed your family with it!'
He was banished from Madinah for sixty years
He was forbidden from entering Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: This celebrated Sahih al-Bukhari incident reveals the warmth, realism, and mercy at the heart of Prophetic jurisprudence in Madinah.

questionEn: What revolutionary women's property and social rights were explicitly safeguarded in Madinah through Surah An-Nisa and the Prophet's ﷺ rulings?
optionsEn: Only men could own orchards in Madinah
Women's independent right to inherit, own and manage wealth, receive their own Mahr (marriage gift), refuse forced marriage, and petition for divorce (khul') in unfair marriages
Brides' fathers kept the entire Mahr by force
explanationEn: When the wife of Thabit ibn Qays (RA) respectfully approached the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah seeking separation (khul') simply due to incompatibility, he mediated fairly by having her return the garden Thabit had gifted her.

questionEn: Which courageous woman of Madinah—Khawlah bint Tha'labah (RA)—pleaded directly with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ about her estranged husband Aws ibn al-Samit until Allah revealed the opening of Surah Al-Mujadilah (58:1)?
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) marveled that from the very same room she could barely hear Khawlah's whispered complaint, yet Allah heard her above the seven heavens ('Qad sami'Allahu qawla allati tujadiluka fi zawjiha'), abolishing unjust pre-Islamic zihar!

questionEn: How did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) later honor elderly Khawlah bint Tha'labah (RA) when she stopped his procession in a street of Madinah to remind him of fearing Allah?
optionsEn: He ordered guards to push her away

He stood patiently listening to her every word until she finished, telling astonished bystanders: 'Do you know who this is? This is Khawlah, whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens—by Allah, if she stood here until nightfall I would not leave except for prayer!'
He fined her for delaying traffic
explanationEn: Umar's (RA) humility before an elderly woman in Madinah's street exemplifies Islamic accountability of rulers.

questionEn: Who was 'Al-Shifa bint Abdullah' (RA), one of the literate female companions in Madinah whom Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) later consulted and appointed to oversee market standards?
optionsEn: Al-Shifa bint Abdullah al-Adawiyyah (RA), who also taught Hafsah (RA) writing and beneficial ruqyah
explanationEn: Respected for her literacy, wisdom, and integrity, Al-Shifa (RA) held public market oversight (hisbah) responsibilities in Madinah under Umar (RA).

questionEn: What remarkable domestic scene did Aishah (RA) describe inside the Prophet's ﷺ modest Madinah apartment when asked what he did at home?
optionsEn: 'He lived in a towering stone mansion'
'He demanded servants wait on him silently all day'
'He used to serve his family (patching his sandals, sewing his clothes, milking his goat), and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to pray'
explanationEn: Far from acting like a distant monarch, the leader of Madinah shared daily chores with humility and warmth.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Adhan & Good Manners

questionEn: How frequently did the hearth-fire actually burn for cooked bread or hot meals in the Prophet's ﷺ modest Medinah chambers according to Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: Three lavish banquets every single day
Gold platters from Rome every evening
Months would pass (up to two consecutive crescent moons) with only 'Al-Aswadan'—dates and water—until Ansar neighbors sent over a little milk
explanationEn: Hearing this from Aishah (RA), her nephew Urwah ibn al-Zubayr asked in awe 'What kept you alive?'—reminding Madinah's visitors of the voluntary simplicity chosen by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Gifts & Heart-Melters

questionEn: What happened when Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ wives once gathered in Madinah asking for slightly wider worldly household allowances after Madinah grew more prosperous?
optionsEn: They all left Madinah for Damascus
He built nine marble palaces immediately

Allah revealed Surah Al-Ahzab (33:28-29) giving them a clear choice between worldly adornment with honorable release or Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter—and every single Mother of the Believers, starting with Aishah (RA), wholeheartedly chose Allah and His Messenger ﷺ!
They traded their rooms for gold
explanationEn: Rather than compromising their simple spiritual household, Aishah (RA) immediately replied: 'Concerning this, would I consult my parents? Indeed I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter!'

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ briefly stay in isolation for 29 days during that month of family reflection (Ila') in 9 AH?
optionsEn: In a small upper-floor attic storage room (Mashrubah) accessible only by a palm-trunk ladder near Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
Inside a luxury castle in Khaybar
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) climbed up to that bare room and wept seeing palm-mat imprints on the Prophet's ﷺ side while Caesar and Khosrow lived in silk, the Prophet ﷺ comforted him: 'Are you not pleased that theirs is this world and ours is the Hereafter?'

questionEn: What gentle hospitality did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show in Madinah to his Ethiopian foster-mother Umm Ayman (RA) and visiting elders from Makkah's past, such as Khadijah's (RA) old friends?
optionsEn: He forgot Khadijah (RA) completely after moving to Madinah
He turned away visitors who arrived unannounced

Whenever an elderly friend of Khadijah (RA) visited Madinah, he stood warmly, spread his cloak, sent her generous portions of slaughtered meat, and smiled: 'Honoring old friendships is part of faith!'
explanationEn: Even Aishah (RA) noted she never felt more loving envy toward anyone than Khadijah (RA) because of how tenderly the Prophet ﷺ honored Khadijah's memory and friends in Madinah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: Who was Zayd ibn Harithah's (RA) young son, loved so deeply by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah that he was affectionately called 'Al-Hibb ibn al-Hibb' (The Beloved, son of the Beloved)?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ used to seat little Usamah (RA) on one knee and little Al-Hasan (RA) on the other in Madinah, embracing both and praying: 'O Allah, love them, for I love them!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which noble Ansari companion—owner of the orchard where the Prophet ﷺ once came for shade and witnessed a miracle of sweet cool water—invited the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) to a surprise lunch in the heat of noon?
optionsEn: Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA) (or Abu Ayyub in parallel reports), who slaughtered a lamb, served fresh dates and sweet water—leading the Prophet ﷺ to remind Abu Bakr and Umar: 'By Him in Whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this blessing on the Day of Judgment!'
explanationEn: Leaving their homes driven solely by hunger in the midday heat of Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar (RA) ate joyfully then reminded each other of gratitude for even a simple shaded meal and cool water.

questionEn: Which Companion of Madinah was nicknamed 'Dhu al-Shahadatayn' (He Whose Testimony Equals Two Witnesses) after defending the Prophet ﷺ in a horse-purchase dispute in Madinah?
explanationEn: When a Bedouin denied selling a horse to the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, Khuzaymah (RA) stepped forward testifying he witnessed it—explaining: 'We believe you in revelation from heaven every morning and evening; how could I not trust you about a horse?'—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to make Khuzaymah's single witness count as two!

questionEn: What important lesson in fair judicial impartiality did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare in Madinah when Quraysh aristocrats tried to ask Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) to intercede for a high-born Makhzumi woman caught stealing?
optionsEn: 'By Allah, if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would surely cut off her hand!'—confirming equal justice regardless of family rank
explanationEn: Delivered straight from the Minbar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, this speech warned that previous nations perished precisely because they punished the weak while sparing the elite.

questionEn: What remarkable legal safeguard did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when two litigants came before him arguing over property or inheritance?
optionsEn: 'Whoever speaks fastest always wins rightly before Allah'

'You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than the other; whoever I rule in favor of taking his brother's right by eloquence, I am only cutting off for him a piece of Hellfire!'
explanationEn: Teaching moral conscience above mere legal technicalities, this Medinan Hadith made litigants weep and voluntarily yield disputed claims out of fear of Allah.

questionEn: What role did 'Bayt al-Mal' (the Public Treasury) play in Madinah as Islam expanded from 2 AH through the Rightly Guided Caliphs?
optionsEn: Collecting Zakah, Jizyah, Kharaj, and one-fifth of spoils (Khums) and distributing stipends transparently to the needy, orphans, travelers, soldiers, and public infrastructure
Charging citizens to pray in mosques
Storing gold solely for private banquets
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) distributed funds evenly down to the last coin, and Umar (RA) created the organized Diwan stipends in Madinah reaching widows, newborns, and elderly citizens alike.
reference: Ibn Sa'd & Abu Yusuf, Kitab al-Kharaj

questionEn: How did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) reform stipends in Madinah for nursing mothers and infants after noticing a weeping baby whose mother had weaned him too early?
optionsEn: He reduced stipends to zero until age twenty
Umar wept in remorse, had a herald announce across Madinah: 'Do not hasten to wean your children—we now grant an infant stipend from Bayt al-Mal for every child born in Islam from birth!'
He banned mothers from walking outdoors
explanationEn: Replacing the rule that gave stipends only after weaning, Umar's (RA) compassionate policy in Madinah stands as one of history's earliest universal child-welfare allowances.

questionEn: Which companion—the great warrior and diplomat Amr ibn al-As (RA)—first embraced Islam alongside Khalid ibn al-Walid after riding to Madinah in 8 AH, and what condition did Amr ask before shaking the Prophet's ﷺ hand?
optionsEn: Amr asked for a palace in Quba

Amr held back his hand asking 'Will my past sins be forgiven?'—and the Prophet ﷺ taught him in Madinah: 'Islam erases everything before it, Hijrah erases everything before it, and Hajj erases everything before it!'
Amr demanded to be made Caliph
explanationEn: That conversation in Madinah gave the Muslim world one of its most hopeful and beloved assurances of Allah's total forgiveness upon sincere repentance and new beginnings.

questionEn: Which Companion was hailed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi as 'Amin hadhihi al-Ummah' (Trustworthy Guardian of this Ummah) when Najran Christians asked for a trustworthy judge?
explanationEn: Even Umar (RA) secretly hoped he might be chosen that morning in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, only to watch joyfully as the Prophet ﷺ stepped out and took Abu Ubaydah's (RA) hand: 'Every nation has a trustworthy guardian, and the trustworthy guardian of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which Medinan scholar-companion was sent by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Madinah to Yemen in 9/10 AH with the historic legal instruction on deriving judgments (Qur'an, Sunnah, then careful Ijtihad)?
explanationEn: An Ansari prodigy of Al-Khazraj in Madinah praised by the Prophet ﷺ as 'the most knowledgeable of my Ummah regarding Halal and Haram,' Mu'adh (RA) walked beside the Prophet's ﷺ mount out of Madinah receiving timeless counsel on gradual da'wah and avoiding oppression.

questionEn: What deeply emotional parting prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ whisper to Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA) as he walked him out past the outskirts of Madinah toward Yemen in 10 AH?
optionsEn: 'O Mu'adh, perhaps you will not meet me again after this year of mine—and perhaps you will pass by this mosque of mine and my grave!'—causing Mu'adh to break down weeping
'I will visit you in Yemen next summer'
explanationEn: True to the Prophet's ﷺ words, Mu'adh (RA) was away teaching in Yemen when the Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH, returning later in tears to pray by the Prophet's ﷺ mosque and grave.

questionEn: Which companion—son of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)—grew up in Madinah observing the Prophet's ﷺ every footstep so closely that he would even pause his camel at the exact trees and spots between Makkah and Madinah where the Prophet ﷺ had halted?
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) remarked: 'No one followed the footsteps of Allah's Messenger ﷺ in his stopping places the way Ibn Umar did!'—making Ibn Umar a living mirror of Medinan Sunnah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat elderly non-Muslim visitors or Jewish residents who lived peacefully under Madinah's treaty—even standing up out of respect when a Jewish funeral procession passed through Madinah?
optionsEn: When Companions said 'It is a Jewish funeral!' the Prophet ﷺ replied firmly: 'Is it not a human soul (alaysat nafsan)?!'
He threw stones at the bier
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, honoring the innate dignity of every human soul exemplified Prophetic grace in Madinah.

questionEn: Which young Jewish boy in Madinah used to serve Prophet Muhammad ﷺ kindly, and what did the Prophet ﷺ do when he heard the boy lay dying?
optionsEn: He visited the boy's home, sat gently by his head, and invited him to Islam; after glancing at his father—who nodded 'Obey Abu al-Qasim!'—the boy pronounced the Shahadah and passed away as the Prophet ﷺ walked out thanking Allah for saving him from Hellfire
He forced the father out of Madinah
He ignored the sick boy completely
explanationEn: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, this tender Madinah visit showcases compassion and sincere concern for human salvation.

questionEn: What remarkable example of neighborly kindness did Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As or Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) practice in Madinah even toward non-Muslim neighbors?
optionsEn: Repeatedly asking his household after slaughtering a sheep in Madinah: 'Have you given a share to our Jewish neighbor?'—quoting the Prophet's ﷺ emphasis on neighborly rights
Refusing to sell food to neighbors
explanationEn: Even decades after the Prophet's ﷺ passing, Companions in Madinah carried forward his warm ethos of neighborly generosity regardless of faith.

questionEn: What remarkable miracle of water occurred in Madinah's marketplace before roughly 300 companions when Asr prayer time arrived?
optionsEn: He summoned icebergs from the north
At Al-Zawra' in Madinah's marketplace, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ placed his hand in a shallow bowl of water and clear springs gushed forth from between his fingers until hundreds performed Wudu and drank!
He turned rocks into silver water jars
He diverted the Nile to Madinah
explanationEn: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari (seeing ~300 companions perform Wudu at Al-Zawra' near Madinah's market from one small vessel), it remains one of the most vividly attested miracles in Madinah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Signs of Prophethood

questionEn: Where in Madinah did the famous miracle of water flowing from between Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ fingers occur before roughly 300 companions?
optionsEn: At Al-Zawra', a landmark near Madinah's market beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: Anas (RA) saw the water bubbling continuously from beneath the Prophet's ﷺ fingers inside a small vessel at Al-Zawra' right as Asr prayer time approached.

questionEn: Which companion had a broken shin healed instantaneously by Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ gentle wipe upon returning wounded to Madinah?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Atik (RA) (and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' RA at Khaybar), whose broken leg healed immediately as if never injured!
explanationEn: When Abdullah ibn Atik (RA) fell down stairs breaking his leg on a night mission and reached Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ told him 'Stretch out your leg,' wiped it softly, and it healed instantly without a trace of pain.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:1-5) was revealed in Madinah after crude delegates shouted impatiently outside the Prophet's ﷺ private apartments?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:1-5, commanding believers never to speak rudely or raise their voices above the Prophet's ﷺ voice
explanationEn: Teaching timeless reverence inside Madinah, Allah declared: 'Those who call out to you from behind the private chambers—most of them do not use reason,' establishing calm dignity inside and around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which tribe's delegation prompted the opening verses of Surah Al-Hujurat (49:2-5) in Madinah by shouting impatiently outside Aishah's (RA) and the Prophet's ﷺ chambers?
explanationEn: Upon hearing 49:2 ('Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet'), the loyal Ansari orator Thabit ibn Qays (RA)—who naturally had a booming voice—feared his deeds were lost and locked himself home weeping until the Prophet ﷺ comforted him: 'You are of the people of Paradise!'

questionEn: Who was the noble Ansari orator of Madinah—Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas (RA)—who wept in fear over Surah Al-Hujurat 49:2 because of his naturally loud voice?
optionsEn: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas (RA), the official Orator (Khatib) of the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah
explanationEn: When Thabit feared his loud speaking voice had voided his deeds, the Prophet ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh/Anas to reassure him: 'He will live praiseworthy, die a martyr, and enter Paradise!'—fulfilled later at Yamamah.

questionEn: What remarkable spiritual transformation occurred in Madinah after the Battle of Hunayn when delegates of Hawazin arrived in Madinah or Al-Ji'ranah—and how did Madinah welcome former enemies who embraced Islam?
optionsEn: Madinah executed every former Makkan adversary
Madinah welcomed former adversaries—such as Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Safwan ibn Umayyah—with open hearts, forgiving past injuries and integrating them as brothers in faith
explanationEn: Echoing Prophet Yusuf's (AS) words—'No blame upon you today; may Allah forgive you'—Islam transformed bitter enemies into devoted servants of the Ummah.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse revealed in Madinah (Surah Al-Nahl 16:126 or Surah Al-Shura 42:40) vs Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 sums up Madinah's vision of human equality?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 ('O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you')
explanationEn: Preached in Madinah and echoed at the Farewell Pilgrimage, 49:13 dismantled racial and tribal supremacy permanently.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react in Madinah when Abu Dharr (RA) once lost his temper and insulted Bilal (RA) by referring to his Black mother ('O son of a black woman!')?
optionsEn: He banished Bilal from Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
The Prophet ﷺ rebuked Abu Dharr sharply: 'Did you taunt him about his mother? Truly you are a man who still has traits of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah) in him!'
explanationEn: Immediately heartbroken with remorse, Abu Dharr (RA) laid his own cheek flat in the dust of Madinah begging Bilal (RA) to step upon it—and Bilal forgave and embraced his brother in tears.

questionEn: What enduring lesson did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give the people of Madinah when he heard someone boast of ancestry or mock another's skin color?
optionsEn: 'Allah has removed from you the arrogance of pre-Islamic Ignorance and its boasting about ancestors: a person is either a pious believer or a miserable sinner; all people are children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust'
'Boasting about ancestry is encouraged on Fridays'
explanationEn: This Madinan teaching forged one unified brotherhood out of Arabs, Persians, Abyssinians, Romans, and Jews alike.

questionEn: What crucial role did women of Madinah play in the early Islamic community beyond their homes?
optionsEn: They played no part in Seerah history
They narrated hundreds of Hadith, gave sanctuary/advice, carried water and tended wounded at Uhud and Khaybar, traded in markets, and pledged allegiance directly to the Prophet ﷺ
They were forbidden from speaking to scholars
They were barred from mosques and learning
explanationEn: From Aishah's (RA) juristic authority to Umm Umarah's (RA) bravery and Rufaydah's (RA) nursing tent in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, women were vital pillars of Madinah.

questionEn: Which companion's house in Madinah was called 'Dar al-Qurra' (House of the Reciters) because early Makkan emigrants stayed there learning Qur'an upon arrival?
optionsEn: The home of Makhramah ibn Nawfal / Rifa'ah ibn Abd al-Mundhir / Sa'd ibn Khaythamah (and in later tradition Abu Ayyub & As'ad ibn Zurarah's quarters)
explanationEn: Early Madinah homes opened spontaneously into schools of Qur'an recitation and mutual hospitality for newly arriving emigrants.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ choose NOT to build a royal palace, keep bodyguards (once Surah 5:67 descended), or wear gold crowns in Madinah even after becoming sovereign leader of all Arabia?
optionsEn: Because he lived solely as a servant-messenger of Allah ('Abdun Rasul'), choosing simplicity, accessibility, and closeness to the poor until his final day
Because gold didn't exist in Arabia
Because he planned to move to Persia
explanationEn: When an envoy once trembled in awe upon entering his presence in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ calmed him warmly: 'Be at ease—I am not a king; I am only the son of a woman of Quraysh who used to eat dried meat!'

questionEn: What happened to Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ personal armor on the very day he passed away in Madinah in 11 AH?
optionsEn: It was pawned to a Jewish merchant in Madinah for thirty sa's of barley to feed his household
It was buried inside a golden chest
It was stored in a treasury of silver coins
explanationEn: Even as ruler of the Arabian Peninsula, the Prophet ﷺ died leaving no dinar, dirham, or estate—only his white mule, his weapons, and land dedicated to public charity—testifying to utter purity of heart.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Buying and Selling

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare regarding any property left behind by Prophets—guiding Abu Bakr (RA) when handling Fadak and the Prophet's ﷺ Madinah orchards?
optionsEn: 'We prophets are not inherited from; whatever we leave behind is public charity (Sadaqah)'
explanationEn: Maintaining the Prophet's ﷺ household expenses respectfully from those charitable endowments while keeping the surplus for Madinah's needy, Abu Bakr (RA) fulfilled the Prophet's ﷺ exact directive.

questionEn: Which prophetic virtue of Madinah did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) preserve by keeping Madinah as the spiritual standard even while vast empires opened in Syria, Iraq, and Egypt?
optionsEn: Consulting senior Companions inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi on major crises, enforcing justice equally, and returning victorious delegations straight to Madinah's simple mosque
explanationEn: Even governors of mighty provinces like Egypt and Syria answered directly to Umar (RA) sitting humbly inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: What moving scene unfolded in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when the spoils of Persia—including Khosrow's royal crown and jewelled bracelets—arrived before Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) in Madinah?
optionsEn: Umar threw the bracelets into the sea

Umar (RA) summoned elderly Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) to put on Khosrow's golden bracelets inside Madinah, fulfilling the exact prophecy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had promised him on the lonely Hijrah road years earlier!
Umar kept the crown for himself
explanationEn: Seeing Suraqah (RA) wear Khosrow's bracelets in Madinah moved Umar and the Companions to tears of awe at Allah's truthfulness and the fulfillment of His Messenger's ﷺ promise.

questionEn: Which companion—the Persian seeker Salman al-Farsi (RA)—told Muslims in Madinah how his long journey through Syria, Mosul, Nisibis, and Amorium ended the day he recognized the three prophetic signs in Quba and Madinah?
optionsEn: Salman al-Farsi (RA), who verified that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ accepted gifts (at Quba), refused charity (at Quba), and bore the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders (in Baqi/Madinah)
explanationEn: Testing each of the three signs taught him by his dying Christian monk mentor, Salman (RA) flung himself weeping in joy at the Prophet's ﷺ feet near Baqi and became one of Islam's brightest lights.

questionEn: How did Salman al-Farsi (RA) summarize his true noble identity when proud nobles in Madinah or Iraq boasted of their tribal pedigrees?
optionsEn: 'My father is Islam; I have no father other than Islam—Salman son of Islam!'
'I am a prince who rules over Madinah'
explanationEn: Embodying Madinah's universal brotherhood, Salman al-Farsi (RA) proved that sincerity and truth grant nobility higher than any tribe.

questionEn: Which companion from Madinah or Makkah—Abu Bakr's freedman Bilal (RA)—was affectionately called by Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) 'Our Master (Sayyiduna)'?
optionsEn: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA), as Umar (RA) famously said: 'Abu Bakr is our master, and he freed our master—meaning Bilal!'
explanationEn: That unforgettable tribute in Madinah honored Bilal (RA) not by earthly wealth or tribe, but by his unyielding patience and devotion to Allah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: What is the enduring message of Madinah's transformation from war-torn Yathrib into 'Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah' within a single decade?
optionsEn: Tribal rivalry can never be healed
Wealth without character builds strong societies
When hearts unite around Allah, revelation, justice, and Prophetic mercy, fractured tribes can become a beacon of peace, knowledge, and brotherhood for all humanity
Only military forts create lasting peace
explanationEn: Every brick of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, every grove of Quba, and every page of Sahifat al-Madinah still speaks this timeless lesson to pilgrims visiting Madinah today.

questionEn: What title was given to the seven towering second-generation jurists (Tabi'in) who preserved and taught Islamic law in Madinah during the 1st–2nd century AH?
optionsEn: Al-Fuqaha al-Sab'ah (The Seven Jurists of Madinah)
explanationEn: Learning directly from Aishah, Ibn Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Hurayrah (RA), these seven scholars made Madinah the premier seat of jurisprudence.

questionEn: Which grandson of Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)—raised in Madinah by his aunt Aishah (RA)—was one of the renowned Seven Jurists of Madinah?
optionsEn: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr
explanationEn: Known for piety, deep knowledge of Aishah's (RA) Hadith, and cautious humility in saying 'I do not know,' Al-Qasim shaped Madinah's scholarly ethos.

questionEn: Which son-in-law of Abu Hurayrah (RA) and towering Tabi'i jurist—nicknamed 'Sayyid al-Tabi'in' (Master of the Successors)—sat daily in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for forty years without ever missing the opening Takbir in congregation?
explanationEn: Living modestly as an oil merchant in Madinah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib refused royal favors and taught unbroken Fiqh and Hadith inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which nephew of Aishah (RA) and son of Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) served as one of the Seven Jurists of Madinah and a pioneer historian of the Seerah?
explanationEn: Narrating extensively from his aunt Aishah (RA) and writing foundational early letters on the Seerah, Urwah also resided along Wadi al-Aqiq near Madinah.

questionEn: What extraordinary example of patience (sabr) did the Madinah jurist Urwah ibn al-Zubayr display when his leg was amputated due to gangrene on the very same night his young son Muhammad died?
optionsEn: He wept hysterically for three years
He praised Allah calmly: 'O Allah, You gave me four limbs and took one, and gave me several sons and took one—Yours is all praise!'
He refused to pray ever again
explanationEn: While refusing an intoxicant as anesthetic and instead reciting dhikr during the surgery, Urwah (RA) embodied the steadfast spirit of Madinah's scholars.

questionEn: Which son of Abu Bakr's (RA) Ansari brother-in-Islam (Kharijah ibn Zayd) was among the Seven Jurists of Madinah and renowned for inheritance law (Fara'id)?
explanationEn: Son of the great Qur'an scribe and inheritance expert Zayd ibn Thabit (RA), Kharijah mastered Medinan legal verdicts and partnership rulings.

questionEn: Which blind yet extraordinarily perceptive scholar of Madinah—teacher of Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz—belonged to the Seven Jurists of Madinah?
optionsEn: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud
explanationEn: Combining mastery of Hadith, Fiqh, and refined Arabic literature, Ubaydullah mentored Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz during the latter's years in Madinah.

questionEn: Who were the remaining two scholars completing the classic list of the Seven Jurists of Madinah alongside Sa'id, Urwah, Al-Qasim, Kharijah, and Ubaydullah?
optionsEn: Sulayman ibn Yasar (freedman of Maymunah RA) and Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith (or Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar in alternate lists)
explanationEn: Sulayman ibn Yasar served as Maymunah's (RA) trusted student, while Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman was famed as 'Rahib Quraysh' (Ascetic of Quraysh) for his intense devotion in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which great scholar of Madinah—Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar—became an intimate moral advisor to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz when Umar governed Madinah?
optionsEn: Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, grandson of Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
explanationEn: Inheriting his grandfather Umar's fearless honesty and his father Ibn Umar's love for the Sunnah, Salim urged Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz to uphold absolute justice.

questionEn: How did Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz govern Madinah during his 87–93 AH tenure before becoming Caliph in Damascus?
optionsEn: He exiled all scholars from Madinah
He closed Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to students
He formed an advisory council of ten leading jurists of Madinah (including the Seven Fuqaha), telling them: 'I will not decide a matter without consulting you!'
explanationEn: That collaborative golden era in Madinah turned the city into a model of consultative governance and justice.

questionEn: Which renowned Madinah scholar—Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri—was the first to undertake systematic state-sponsored compilation of Prophetic Hadith at the request of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz?
explanationEn: Fearful that knowledge might fade as elders passed away, Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to Madinah instructing Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri and Abu Bakr ibn Hazm to record authentic Hadith systematically.

questionEn: Which celebrated title was given to Imam Malik ibn Anas (93–179 AH) because he spent almost his entire life teaching inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi without emigrating?
optionsEn: Imam Dar al-Hijrah (Imam of the Abode of Migration)
explanationEn: Teaching for nearly fifty years inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—often seated right near the Prophet's ﷺ chamber area—Imam Malik drew students from Spain, Egypt, Iraq, and Khorasan to Madinah.

questionEn: What is the name of Imam Malik ibn Anas's monumental Hadith and legal compendium compiled in Madinah—one of the earliest surviving written collections in Islamic history?
explanationEn: Refined over forty years in Madinah and vetted by seventy scholars of Madinah, Al-Muwatta' became the bedrock of Maliki jurisprudence and early Hadith literature.

questionEn: How did Imam Malik ibn Anas prepare physically and spiritually every single time before sitting to narrate Hadith of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah?
optionsEn: He narrated casually while riding fast horses
He forbade students from writing notes
He performed complete ablution (Wudu), wore his finest clean garments, combed his beard, applied perfume, and sat with solemn dignity—never narrating Hadith while standing or rushing in the street
explanationEn: Asked why he took such care, Imam Malik replied: 'I love to exalt and honor the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!'

questionEn: What happened once when a scorpion stung Imam Malik ibn Anas sixteen times during a Hadith lesson in Madinah?
optionsEn: His face turned pale, yet he never interrupted his Hadith narration until finishing the gathering out of reverence for the Prophet's ﷺ words
He stopped the class immediately and fled
explanationEn: Explaining afterward why he endured sixteen stings silently, Imam Malik showed generations of students what true adab toward the Prophetic Sunnah looks like.

questionEn: What foundational principle of Islamic legal theory ('Usul al-Fiqh') is uniquely prominent in Imam Malik's Madinan school?
optionsEn: 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (The Living Consensus Practice of the People of Madinah)
explanationEn: Imam Malik argued that continuous everyday communal practices—like the wording of the Adhan, dropping 'Bismillah' aloud vs softly, or weights like the Sa'—inherited publicly by thousands in Madinah carry the weight of mass transmission (mutawatir).

questionEn: Which young scholar traveled all the way from Makkah/Gaza to Madinah as a teenager, memorized Imam Malik's Al-Muwatta' before arriving, and studied directly under Malik in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Welcomed warmly by Imam Malik in Madinah, young Al-Shafi'i read Al-Muwatta' aloud with such eloquence that Malik urged him to continue reading all day, shaping Islamic jurisprudence forever.

questionEn: What polite response did Imam Malik ibn Anas famously give Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid when the Caliph asked to hang Al-Muwatta' inside the Kaaba and enforce it as the sole law across the empire?
optionsEn: He humbly declined, explaining: 'The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ dispersed across lands carrying diverse authentic Hadith; let each region follow the sound knowledge that reached them!'
He agreed immediately and banned all other scholars
He moved to Baghdad to write laws for the Caliph
explanationEn: Imam Malik's intellectual humility in Madinah protected healthy scholarly diversity within the Sunni tradition.

questionEn: What clear rule did Imam Malik ibn Anas consistently teach in his Madinan legal manuals regarding standing at the Prophet's ﷺ grave vs making personal Dua?
optionsEn: Stand for hours gripping the grille while making personal Dua toward the grave
Offer calm, brief Salam while facing the Sacred Chamber, and then face the Qiblah (toward Allah's House) when raising hands for personal Dua—avoiding prolonged standing or crowding around the grave
explanationEn: In authentic Maliki works such as Al-Mudawwanah and Al-Mabsut (and noted by Ibn Taymiyyah and Al-Qadi Iyad), Imam Malik upheld turning toward the Qiblah for personal Dua to preserve pure Tawhid and Sunnah simplicity.
reference: Ibn Rushd, Al-Bayan wal-Tahsil & Al-Qadi Iyad

questionEn: What clear distinction did Imam Malik ibn Anas make in Madinah regarding Madinah residents vs visiting travelers offering Salam at the Prophet's ﷺ grave?
optionsEn: He disliked residents of Madinah standing by the grave every single day unnecessarily (since they enter the mosque daily), whereas greeting politely upon arriving from or departing on a journey follows Ibn Umar's (RA) Sunnah
He banned travelers from ever visiting Madinah
He required bowing deeply at the grille
He encouraged crowds to sleep against the wall
explanationEn: Imam Malik's balanced counsel preserved both heartfelt respect for the Prophet ﷺ and dignity inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi without turning visits into unprescribed routines.

questionEn: Which great Hadith master—author of Sahih al-Bukhari—spent prolonged time studying and writing his early masterpiece 'Al-Tarikh al-Kabir' by moonlight beside the Prophet's ﷺ grave in Madinah?
explanationEn: Arriving in Madinah at around age eighteen, young Al-Bukhari wrote biographies of Hadith transmitters at night beneath the moonlight in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—known as 'Hibr al-Ummah' (Scholar of the Ummah) and 'Tarjuman al-Qur'an' (Interpreter of the Qur'an)—was prayed for by the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Allah, grant him deep understanding of the religion and teach him Tafsir'?
explanationEn: Growing up around the Prophet's ﷺ household in Madinah through his aunt Maymunah (RA), young Ibn Abbas (RA) eagerly questioned senior Companions after the Prophet's ﷺ passing until becoming Islam's foremost Qur'anic exegete.

questionEn: How did young Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) demonstrate extraordinary humility and respect while seeking Hadith from senior Ansar Companions in Madinah?
optionsEn: He demanded elders walk to his house
He paid scribes to gather rumors

He would wait silently outside an Ansari companion's door in the midday wind rather than disturb his afternoon rest until the elder emerged astonished: 'O cousin of Allah's Messenger, why didn't you send for me?!'
explanationEn: Replying 'I have greater right to come to you, for knowledge is walked to, not summoned!', Ibn Abbas (RA) modeled adab for every seeker of knowledge in Madinah.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Aishah bint Abi Bakr (RA)—served in Madinah for nearly fifty years after the Prophet's ﷺ passing as a supreme jurist, mufti, and narrator of over 2,200 Hadith?
explanationEn: Senior Companions themselves came to Aishah's (RA) door in Madinah whenever complex rulings stumped them—with Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) testifying: 'Never did a Hadith confuse us Companions and we asked Aishah, except we found knowledge of it with her!'

questionEn: Which great scholarly contribution in Madinah came from Fatimah bint Qays, Umm Salamah, and Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman (rahimahunnallah)?
optionsEn: Preserving and transmitting Madinah's authentic Prophetic Hadith and legal rulings—Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman was specifically praised by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as one of the most knowledgeable living authorities on Aishah's (RA) narrations
explanationEn: Madinah nurtured remarkable female scholars from the Sahabiyyat through the Tabi'at whose narrations fill Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, and Al-Muwatta'.

questionEn: Which Madinah scholar of the Tabi'in—grandson of Abu Bakr—was appointed judge (Qadi) of Madinah by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and helped gather written Hadith collections?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm
explanationEn: Belonging to a distinguished Ansari-connected scholarly family in Madinah, Ibn Hazm received Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's historic decree to write down all Prophetic Sunnah.
