questionEn: Which scholar of Madinah—Rabia ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, nicknamed 'Rabi'at al-Ra'y'—was the primary teacher of Imam Malik in legal reasoning inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Teaching in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's pillars where even elder Tabi'in attended his circle, Rabi'ah honed Malik's sharp juristic intellect.

questionEn: What touching story illustrates the generosity of Rabi'at al-Ra'y's parents in Madinah when his father returned after twenty-seven years away in distant campaigns?
optionsEn: His mother had invested his father's parting savings into educating young Rabi'ah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi; seeing his son teaching a packed circle of scholars including Imam Malik, his father wept joyfully knowing knowledge was worth far more than gold!
His father forced him to leave Madinah
explanationEn: That famous Madinah story highlights how families sacrificed worldly luxuries so their children could study beside the Prophet's ﷺ pillars.

questionEn: Which towering 14th-century scholar—Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah—spent time in Madinah and authored 'Zad al-Ma'ad' detailing the Prophet's ﷺ life, journeys, worship, and Madinan jurisprudence?
explanationEn: Written partly while traveling and reflecting deeply on the Hijaz, Zad al-Ma'ad remains one of the richest guides to Prophetic practice in Makkah and Madinah.

questionEn: Which famous 15th-century Shafi'i jurist and Hadith master—Imam al-Nawawi—authored 'Al-Idah fi Manasik al-Hajj wal-Umrah', featuring a classic section on the etiquette of visiting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Imam al-Nawawi's gentle, structured instructions for entering Bab al-Salam, greeting the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar (RA), and facing the Qiblah for Dua have guided millions of pilgrims.

questionEn: Which Tabi'i freedman of Maymunah (RA) was one of Madinah's greatest preachers and Hadith narrators, often counseling worshippers inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Ata ibn Yasar (brother of Sulayman ibn Yasar)
explanationEn: Remembered for his piety, fasting, and moving sermons inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Ata ibn Yasar transmitted key narrations including Abu Sa'id al-Khudri's and Zayd ibn Thabit's Hadith.

questionEn: Which famous grandson of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)—Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin)—taught in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and secretly supported a hundred destitute Madinah families every night?
explanationEn: No one in Madinah knew where those nightly sacks of flour came from until Zayn al-Abidin passed away and calluses from carrying heavy sacks were discovered on his shoulders!

questionEn: What noble example of forgiving an insult did Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) show inside Madinah when a man verbally abused him in front of onlookers?
optionsEn: He imprisoned the man for ten years
He challenged him to a sword duel
Rather than retaliating, he calmly gave the man his own robe and ordered gifts sent to him, melting the man's hostility into tears
explanationEn: Living right beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Zayn al-Abidin embodied the gentleness and forbearance of his forefather Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questionEn: Which renowned early Medinan historian—author of 'Kitab al-Maghazi' (The Book of Expeditions) and key source preserved by Ibn Hisham—gathered eyewitness accounts from Madinah's elders?
optionsEn: Muhammad ibn Ishaq (and before him Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Al-Zuhri)
explanationEn: Interviewing children and grandchildren of Badr, Uhud, and Khandaq participants in Madinah, Ibn Ishaq preserved the narrative backbone of the Seerah.

questionEn: What is the name of the famous Madinah reading (Qira'ah) of the Holy Qur'an transmitted by Imam Nafi' al-Madani through his two celebrated students Qalun and Warsh?
explanationEn: Recited widely across North and West Africa (via Warsh) and Libya/Tunisia (via Qalun), Qira'at Nafi' traces straight back through Madinah's Tabi'in to Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Zayd ibn Thabit (RA).

questionEn: Roughly how many of the 114 Surahs of the Noble Qur'an are classified by scholars as 'Madani' (revealed after the Hijrah to Madinah)?
optionsEn: Approximately 28 Surahs (accounting for over a third of the Qur'an's length, filled with legal, social, and historical guidance)
explanationEn: Scholarly convention defines Madani verses as everything revealed after the Hijrah to Madinah—shaping family law, economics, interfaith relations, worship details, and statecraft.

questionEn: Which was the very first complete Surah revealed in Madinah immediately following the Hijrah (according to classical consensus reported by Ibn Abbas RA)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (with Al-Mutaffifin bridging the Hijrah transition around Madinah's market)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah lays out the comprehensive blueprint of the new Medinan Ummah: faith vs hypocrisy, Qiblah, fasting, Hajj, charity, family justice, and abolition of usury.

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an—revealed in Madinah—explicitly mentions 'Al-Madinah' by name four times in Surah At-Tawbah and Surah Al-Ahzab/Al-Munafiqun?
optionsEn: Surah At-Tawbah (9:101, 9:120), Surah Al-Ahzab (33:60), and Surah Al-Munafiqun (63:8)
explanationEn: These Medinan verses directly mention 'the people of Al-Madinah' and 'the hypocrites in Al-Madinah,' rooting Madinah's spiritual trials forever in Allah's Book.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:100), what supreme divine promise does Allah pronounce over the First and Foremost among the Muhajirun and Ansar of Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Allah is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever'
explanationEn: Known as the verse of 'RadiyAllahu anhum wa radu anh,' 9:100 permanently seals the honor of Madinah's Muhajirun, Ansar, and all who follow them in excellence (ihsan).

questionEn: Which verse in Surah At-Tawbah (9:120) rebuked those who stayed behind comfortably in Madinah while Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the believers endured hardship on expedition?
optionsEn: 'It was not [proper] for the people of Madinah and those surrounding them of the Bedouins that they remain behind after [the departure of] the Messenger of Allah or prefer themselves over his self'
explanationEn: Revealed around Tabuk, 9:120 promises that every thirst, fatigue, hunger, or footstep endured for Allah's sake is written down as a righteous deed.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 62) is named 'Al-Jumu'ah' after the weekly Friday congregation established in Madinah?
explanationEn: Commanding believers to hasten to Allah's remembrance and pause trade the moment the Friday Adhan sounds, Surah Al-Jumu'ah recalls an early Friday in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when a Syrian trade caravan arrived drumming during the sermon!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: What dramatic incident inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi prompted the revelation of Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:11 ('And when they saw a transaction or diversion, they rushed to it and left you standing')?
optionsEn: Dihyah al-Kalbi's trade caravan arrived from Syria beating drums during the Prophet's ﷺ Friday sermon, and almost the entire congregation rushed out to buy scarce food—leaving only twelve men standing with him!
A fire broke out on the roof
A ship sank in Wadi al-Aqiq
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ noted afterward that had those last twelve (including Abu Bakr and Umar RA) also walked out, the valley would have burned with punishment—teaching timeless focus during Jumu'ah in Madinah.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 63) exposes the double-faced speeches of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and the hypocrites of Madinah, warning believers not to let wealth or children distract them from remembering Allah?
explanationEn: Revealed during the return from Banu al-Mustaliq after Abdullah ibn Ubayy threatened 'the honorable will expel the lowly from Madinah,' Allah vindicated young Zayd ibn Arqam's report word-for-word.

questionEn: Which young Ansari boy in Madinah overheard Abdullah ibn Ubayy's arrogant boast ('Wait until we return to Madinah—the mighty will drive out the weak!') and reported it truthfully to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy swore false oaths denying he ever said it, young Zayd (RA) felt deeply embarrassed until Allah revealed Surah Al-Munafiqun (63:8), and the Prophet ﷺ gently pinched Zayd's ear smiling: 'Allah has confirmed your truthfulness, O boy!'

questionEn: Which Surah revealed in Madinah (Chapter 47) is named after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself?
explanationEn: Revealed in Madinah around 1–2 AH (also called Surah Al-Qital), Surah Muhammad contrasts the believers who obey truth with those whose deeds Allah invalidates.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 8, Al-Anfal) was revealed right after the Battle of Badr to teach Madinah's community humility in victory and fair distribution of spoils?
explanationEn: Clarifying that victory at Badr came solely from Allah—not numbers—Surah Al-Anfal ordered one-fifth (Khums) set aside for Allah, the Messenger, kin, orphans, the needy, and stranded travelers.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 48) was revealed on the road back from Al-Hudaybiyyah to Madinah, bringing the Prophet ﷺ joy 'dearer to him than everything upon which the sun rises'?
explanationEn: Promising clear triumph, the conquest of Makkah, and Allah's pleasure with those who pledged beneath the tree (Bay'at al-Ridwan), Surah Al-Fath transformed returning pilgrims' disappointment into celebration in Madinah.

questionEn: Which Madinan verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:275–281) abolished usury/interest (Riba) cleanly in Madinah's economy, warning those who refuse to abandon Riba of 'war from Allah and His Messenger'?
explanationEn: Proclaimed in Madinah and finalized at the Farewell Pilgrimage, abolishing Riba protected Madinah's vulnerable borrowers from predatory debt traps.

questionEn: What is the longest single verse in the entire Noble Qur'an—revealed in Madinah—regulating written contracts, witnesses, and honest debt documentation?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Dayn (The Verse of Debt, Surah Al-Baqarah 2:282)
explanationEn: Covering an entire page of the Mushaf, Ayat al-Dayn reflects how carefully Madinah's legal culture safeguarded commercial fairness and prevented disputes.

questionEn: Which Madinan verse—frequently recited as the final or near-final legal revelation shortly before the Prophet's ﷺ passing in Madinah (2:281)—reminds every believer of returning to Allah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:281 ('And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged')
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated this was the very last verse revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ before his passing in Madinah nine or more days/weeks later.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 5, Al-Ma'idah) contains the famous verse of perfection revealed at Arafat ('Today I have perfected for you your religion...') as well as Madinah's detailed dietary and covenant laws?
explanationEn: Opening with 'O you who believe, fulfill all contracts/covenants!', Surah Al-Ma'idah codified Wudu, Tayammum, halal food, and justice toward even adversaries.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 24, Al-Nur) established home privacy, guarding the gaze, modesty, protection against slander, and the luminous 'Verse of Light' (24:35)?
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) urged Madinah's families and women especially to learn and teach Surah Al-Nur for its moral guardianship of family honor.

questionEn: Which Madinan verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256) declares the timeless principle of religious conscience in Islam: 'There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion'?
explanationEn: Revealed in Madinah when some Ansari parents wanted to force their older children who had been raised among Banu al-Nadir to embrace Islam against their will, Allah forbade religious coercion.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 66, Al-Tahrim) addressed personal household harmony inside the apartments along Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's eastern wall, teaching repentance and the examples of Asiyah and Maryam (AS)?
explanationEn: Offering sincere spiritual counsel directly to the Prophet's ﷺ household, Surah Al-Tahrim concludes by holding up Asiyah (wife of Pharaoh) and Maryam (mother of Isa) as eternal models for all believing men and women.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 110, Al-Nasr) signaled to discerning elders like Ibn Abbas and Umar (RA) in Madinah that Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ earthly mission was nearing its triumphant completion?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Nasr ('When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest...')
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) asked elders about 110:1 and only young Ibn Abbas (RA) recognized it as the announcement of the Prophet's ﷺ approaching departure, Umar praised him warmly inside Madinah.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Umm Salamah (RA)—had her moving dua taught by the Prophet ﷺ answered in Madinah when she lost her beloved first husband Abu Salamah from an Uhud wound?
optionsEn: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; Allahumma'jurni fi musibati wa akhlif li khayran minha'—after which Allah replaced Abu Salamah with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself!
She refused ever to remarry or speak
explanationEn: Thinking 'Who could ever be better than Abu Salamah?', Umm Salamah (RA) faithfully recited the dua in Madinah and saw Allah grant her the noblest husband in all creation.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Sawdah bint Zam'ah (RA)—generously gifted her scheduled turn with the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah to Aishah (RA) in her later years so she could remain honored as his wife until Paradise?
explanationEn: Remembered in Madinah for her cheerful warmth, tall stature, and remarkable generosity, Sawdah (RA) once playfully told the Prophet ﷺ she couldn't keep up with his long night Tahajjud because of her age, making him smile.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith (RA)—brought immense blessing upon her entire tribe of Banu al-Mustaliq in Madinah upon marrying the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Upon her marriage, the Muslims of Madinah immediately freed over a hundred captured families of Banu al-Mustaliq, saying: 'How can we hold the in-laws of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in captivity?!'
She asked for a castle in Yemen
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) remarked: 'I know of no woman who was a greater blessing to her people than Juwayriyyah!'

questionEn: What deeply moving spiritual lesson did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach Juwayriyyah (RA) in her Madinah apartment beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi regarding quality vs quantity of Dhikr?
optionsEn: He told her to stop praying Duha

Leaving her praying at Fajr and returning mid-morning to find her still sitting in Dhikr, he taught her four concise words ('SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, adada khalqihi, wa rida nafsihi, wa zinata arshihi, wa midada kalimatihi') weighed heavier than hours of repetition
He forbade morning Dhikr inside chambers
He instructed her to pray only once a week
explanationEn: Pilgrims visiting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today still treasure this exact morning adhkar taught inside Juwayriyyah's (RA) chamber!

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA)—used to tan leather and weave crafts with her own hands in Madinah solely to give all the proceeds in charity to the poor?
explanationEn: Even when Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) sent her massive 12,000-dirham annual state stipend in Madinah, Zaynab covered it with a cloth and had her servant distribute every single coin to needy orphans and relatives before dusk!

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—Umm Habibah (Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan, RA)—lived in Madinah after returning from Abyssinia and refused to let her visiting father Abu Sufyan sit on the Prophet's ﷺ folded bedding before his conversion?
optionsEn: Umm Habibah (RA), telling her surprised father gently: 'It is the bedding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you are an idolater who is impure!'
explanationEn: Even loving her father deeply, Umm Habibah (RA) placed reverence for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ above blood ties—long before Abu Sufyan later embraced Islam at Makkah's Conquest.

questionEn: What remarkable scene occurred in Madinah's mosque when Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) passed away leaving generous bequests—and how much did he leave to each surviving Badr veteran and to the Mothers of the Believers?
optionsEn: He bequeathed 400 gold dinars to each surviving Badr veteran (around 100 men, including Uthman and Ali RA who gladly accepted it as pure halal wealth!) plus an orchard sold for 400,000 dirhams to the Mothers of the Believers
He buried his wealth in the sea
He left everything to Roman governors
explanationEn: Known for saying 'My wealth grew so fast that if I lifted a stone I feared finding gold or silver beneath it,' Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) feared entering Paradise crawling behind poorer companions and gave ceaselessly in Madinah.

questionEn: Which companion—the great warrior Talhah ibn Ubaydullah (RA)—earned the nicknames 'Talhah al-Khayr' (Talhah the Good) and 'Talhah al-Fayyad' (Talhah the Overflowingly Generous) in Madinah?
optionsEn: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah (RA), who once sold land for 700,000 dirhams and stayed awake all night anxiously distributing every single dirham to Madinah's poor before dawn!
explanationEn: Honored as 'a living martyr walking on the earth' by the Prophet ﷺ after shielding him at Uhud, Talhah's (RA) generosity sustained countless households of Banu Taym and Madinah.

questionEn: Which beloved Madinah companion—Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA), one of the Twelve Nuqaba' of Al-Aqabah—pledged to speak truth without fearing any critic's blame, and later served as first Muslim Qadi of Jerusalem?
explanationEn: Living his early Islamic years teaching Qur'an at Al-Suffah in Madinah, Ubadah (RA) carried Madinah's integrity straight to Syria and Palestine.

questionEn: Which Ansari companion from Madinah—Abu Ayyub's neighbor? No, which companion known as 'The Possessor of Two Lights' (Dhul-Nur) had his staff shine like a lamp lighting the pitch-black rainy night as he walked home from Isha prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA) (along with Abbad ibn Bishr RA)
explanationEn: Leaving Al-Masjid an-Nabawi on a pitch-dark rainy night after chatting with the Prophet ﷺ, Usayd and Abbad watched one's staff glow like a bright lantern until their paths split—when both staffs lit their separate ways home to Madinah's lanes!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Ansar

questionEn: What breathtaking spiritual experience happened to Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA) one night in his date courtyard in Madinah while reciting Surah Al-Baqarah beside his tethered horse?
optionsEn: His horse startled repeatedly whenever he recited; looking up into the night sky, he saw a glowing canopy filled with lamp-like lights ascending—which the Prophet ﷺ explained next morning were Angels descending to listen to his Qur'an!
A storm blew away his dates
His horse swam across a river
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ smiled telling Usayd (RA) in Madinah: 'Recite, O Ibn Hudayr! Had you continued until morning, the people would have seen the angels clearly without a veil!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—known for his booming warm smile and kindness to neighbors—never saw the Prophet ﷺ pass him in Madinah without greeting him warmly, and once asked 'Have I ever seen him without a smile?'?
explanationEn: Jarir (RA) testified in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never barred me from entering upon him since I embraced Islam, nor did he ever look at me except with a smile!'

questionEn: What deeply moving moment occurred in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ asked Anas ibn Malik (RA) to take a gift or comfort a simple rural friend named 'Zahir ibn Haram', who used to bring desert gifts to the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah?
optionsEn: He ignored Zahir because Zahir was poor

Walking behind Zahir in Madinah's market, the Prophet ﷺ playfully hugged him from behind calling out 'Who will buy this slave?!'—when Zahir saw who it was and pressed his back fondly against the Prophet's ﷺ chest, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Before Allah, you are not cheap—before Allah you are precious!'
explanationEn: This unforgettable street scene in Madinah captures the Prophet's ﷺ humor, affection, and honoring of ordinary working believers.

questionEn: Which companion in Madinah—known as Nu'ayman ibn Amr al-Ansari (RA)—was famous for lighthearted practical pranks that made Prophet Muhammad ﷺ smile, yet stood firmly as a veteran of Badr?
explanationEn: Once bringing honey on credit as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ and telling the seller to collect payment from the Prophet ﷺ himself, Nu'ayman's harmless humor never crossed into sin or cruelty—and the Prophet ﷺ defended his love for Allah and His Messenger.

questionEn: What gentle lesson did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ model in Madinah regarding laughter and humor among Companions?
optionsEn: He told companions to mock strangers
He smiled warmly, laughed lightly without boisterous roaring, joked kindly, and spoke nothing but the absolute truth even when teasing
He encouraged lying as April jokes
explanationEn: Whether gently teasing an old woman ('No old woman enters Paradise—because Allah makes them youthful again!') or playfully calling Abu Turab ('Father of Dust'), his warmth humanized Madinah's community.

questionEn: Where and why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ affectionately give Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) his beloved nickname 'Abu Turab' (Father of Dust) in Madinah?
optionsEn: After Ali fell off a cliff in Yemen

Finding Ali (RA) napping peacefully on the dusty pebble floor inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with dust on his back after a brief family disagreement with Fatimah (RA), the Prophet ﷺ brushed the dust gently off him saying: 'Sit up, O Abu Turab!'
explanationEn: Far from feeling offended, Ali (RA) cherished 'Abu Turab' above every other title because it came straight from the Prophet's ﷺ tender lips inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi!

questionEn: What sweet memory did Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA) share in Madinah about Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) whenever guests visited Ali's (RA) home?
optionsEn: Living right beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, Fatimah (RA) ground barley with her own hands until her palms blistered and hauled heavy water skins leaving marks on her neck—and when she asked her father for a servant, he taught her and Ali (RA) the 'Tasbih Fatimah' (33 SubhanAllah, 33 Alhamdulillah, 34 Allahu Akbar) before sleep as better than any servant!
She owned fifty mansions in Madinah
explanationEn: Known forever across the Ummah as 'Tasbih al-Zahra / Tasbih Fatimah,' that precious nightly Dhikr was gifted in Madinah to strengthen weary hearts.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: What should a Muslim say first when approaching Al-Masjid an-Nabawi on foot and catching their first glimpse of its green dome and white minarets?
optionsEn: Rush straight through crowds pushing others
Recite abundant Salawat upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and enter with humility, gratitude, and serenity
explanationEn: Approaching the Prophet's ﷺ sanctuary with soft Salawat prepares the heart for focused worship inside.

questionEn: Why are separate, spacious prayer halls and designated gates provided for women inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Because women are barred from praying inside the mosque
To prevent women from reading Qur'an
So female worshippers can pray peacefully in dignity, comfort, and privacy, with dedicated access to scheduled Rawdah visits
Because women cannot attend Friday prayer
explanationEn: Far from excluding women, the Prophet ﷺ famously said in Madinah: 'Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from entering the mosques of Allah!'

questionEn: What compassionate ruling did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi about women attending night prayers like Fajr and Isha?
optionsEn: Allowing entry only once every ten years
Forbidding women from ever entering mosques
Requiring women to shout during prayer
Permitting them freely when wearing modest, unadorned clothing without heavy perfume, while reminding them that private prayer at home holds even greater tranquility
explanationEn: Honoring both spiritual eagerness and modesty, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi today welcomes hundreds of thousands of women daily with organized comfort.

questionEn: How does the Nusuk permit system (or Duya app reminder for Rawdah visits) help pilgrims entering Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah today?
optionsEn: It sends people to Makkah instead
It schedules calm timed entries (typically allowing one slot per periodic window) so visitors have peaceful space to pray two rak'ahs and make dua safely without dangerous crushing
explanationEn: Following permit rules honestly—arriving slightly early, being patient in queues, and exiting smoothly when marshals signal—is part of good Islamic adab in Madinah.

questionEn: During a scheduled visit to Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah, what if a pilgrim does not speak fluent Arabic—does Allah accept Dua in one's native language?
optionsEn: Yes! While obligatory Salah uses Arabic Qur'an/adhkar, personal Dua (supplication) inside Al-Rawdah or anywhere in Madinah can be poured out to Allah sincerely in any language
Silent dua in the heart is invalid
No, Allah only hears Arabic dua inside Al-Rawdah
explanationEn: Pouring one's heart out sincerely in whatever language one understands best makes Dua deeply personal and heartfelt.

questionEn: Why is it helpful to prepare a written or mental list of Duas—for parents, family, friends, Ummah, and forgiveness—before entering Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and Al-Rawdah?
optionsEn: To trade lists with security guards
Because silent mental dua is forbidden
Because reading a prayer list is mandatory for Salah
Because awe, emotion, or brief time limits in Al-Rawdah can easily make a pilgrim forget people they promised to pray for
explanationEn: Having a heartfelt Dua list ready helps every precious minute in Madinah's blessed spaces count.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah practice regarding 'Salawat al-Ibrahimiyyah' inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Repeating Salawat only once a month
Inventing loud musical chants with drums
Reciting the complete Salawat taught by the Prophet ﷺ himself ('Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ala ali Muhammad...') abundantly, especially on Fridays and inside his mosque
Facing away from Makkah during Tashahhud
explanationEn: When Companions in Madinah asked 'How do we send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah?', he taught them Salawat al-Ibrahimiyyah, still recited in every prayer worldwide.

questionEn: What special reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise in Sahih Muslim for sending a single Salawat upon him?
optionsEn: 'Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings (mercy) upon him ten times!'
explanationEn: Combined with Friday's heightened virtue ('Increase Salawat upon me on Friday, for your Salawat is presented to me'), Madinah echoes softly with Salawat every day.

questionEn: Why should a visitor to Madinah never overlook praying regular Sunnah prayers (Rawatib) and Duha inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi alongside the five obligatory prayers?
optionsEn: Because Duha may only be prayed on Mount Uhud
Because the 1,000x reward virtue applies to voluntary prayers as well as obligatory prayers in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (while voluntary prayers at home/hotel also retain their own Sunnah beauty)
Because voluntary prayers are barred in Madinah
Because only Fard prayers exist in Islam
explanationEn: Balancing voluntary worship inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with quiet Qur'an reading and remembrance makes every hour in Madinah deeply restorative.
reference: Al-Nawawi, Al-Majmu' & Fiqh of the Two Harams

questionEn: Which two short Surahs did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly recite in the two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr and the two Sunnah rak'ahs after Maghrib?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kafirun (109) in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) in the second rak'ah
Surah Al-Baqarah and Surah Aal Imran
explanationEn: Opening and closing the day's Sunnah prayers with pure Tawhid—sincerity and rejection of idolatry—mirrors the Prophet's ﷺ own daily routine in Madinah.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Prayer of Travelers

questionEn: What should a Muslim do if they arrive in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during one of the congregational prayers when the Iqamah is called?
optionsEn: Pray silently facing the wrong direction
Insist on finishing two Sunnah rak'ahs first while the Imam recites Al-Fatihah
Join the congregational Fard prayer immediately—never start a separate voluntary Sunnah prayer once the Iqamah for the Fard prayer has begun
Walk out of the mosque until Dhuhr
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explicitly taught in Sahih Muslim: 'When the Iqamah for prayer is called, there is no prayer except the prescribed (Fard) prayer!'
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Prayer of Travelers

questionEn: What thoughtful courtesy should a pilgrim observe regarding prayer mats, shoes, and bags inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Carry shoes cleanly in a dedicated shoe bag (or place them neatly in numbered shoe racks), avoid blocking walkways or emergency aisles, and keep personal belongings compact
Leave loose shoes scattered in the prayer rows
Spread luggage across five prayer spots
explanationEn: Cleanliness, order, and consideration for cleaners and fellow worshippers reflect true Prophetic adab.

questionEn: Why is avoiding flash photography, loud video calls, and filming strangers' faces crucial inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and Al-Rawdah?
optionsEn: To protect worshippers' privacy and khushu' (spiritual focus), follow mosque regulations, and keep worship sincere without showing off (riya')
explanationEn: Keeping phones tucked away in silent mode lets the heart truly experience the stillness of the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque.

questionEn: What moving spiritual reminder did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about humility in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi: 'Allah has revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one boasts over another or oppresses another'?
optionsEn: It reminds pilgrims that standing shoulder-to-shoulder in Madinah—kings and laborers, elders and youth—erases all worldly pride
It teaches wealthy visitors to sit separately
It restricts front rows solely to VIPs
explanationEn: Narrated by Iyad ibn Himar (RA) in Sahih Muslim, humility before Allah and gentleness toward people lie at the heart of Madinah's brotherhood.

questionEn: How does visiting Madinah BEFORE vs AFTER performing Umrah/Hajj in Makkah affect a pilgrim's spiritual journey?
optionsEn: Visiting Madinah before Hajj invalidates Hajj
Only visiting in winter is valid
Visiting Madinah after Umrah is forbidden

Both orders are completely valid in Islam! Visiting Madinah before Makkah settles the heart in Seerah and calm before Ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah; visiting Madinah after Makkah offers serene gratitude and reflection after the intense rites of Makkah
explanationEn: Pilgrims arriving from Madinah toward Makkah enter Ihram conveniently at Miqat Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali), while those arriving after Makkah find Madinah a peaceful haven of reflection.

questionEn: If a pilgrim travels from Madinah to Makkah via the Haramain High-Speed Railway intending Umrah, when and where must they enter the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: After checking into their Makkah hotel

In their hotel in Madinah (bathing and wearing Ihram garments beforehand) and making the Niyyah/Talbiyah right before or as the train passes parallel to Miqat Dhul-Hulayfah (announced onboard), NOT waiting until arriving in Makkah!
explanationEn: Because the high-speed train crosses the Miqat zone rapidly shortly after departing Madinah Station, preparing Ihram beforehand and making Niyyah at the onboard Miqat announcement prevents crossing the Miqat without Ihram.

questionEn: Approximately how long does the modern Haramain High-Speed Railway take to connect Madinah and Makkah across the ~450 km route?
explanationEn: Passing through King Abdullah Economic City and Jeddah, the Haramain train turned the arduous nine-day Hijrah camel journey into a smooth two-hour trip.

questionEn: When walking through Madinah's markets to buy gifts like Ajwah dates, prayer rugs, or Oud/Musk for loved ones back home, what Prophetic spirit should guide purchases?
optionsEn: Fairness without harsh haggling, avoiding deceit, buying within one's means without debt, and remembering that gifts strengthen love ('Tahadu tahabbu' — Exchange gifts and you will love one another)
Spending every day shopping and missing congregational prayers
explanationEn: Keeping Salah at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi first—while buying modest, thoughtful gifts like Ajwah dates—preserves the spiritual focus of Madinah.

questionEn: Which fragrant scent did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ especially love in Madinah and use before prayers, Friday gatherings, and meeting delegations?
optionsEn: Pure Musk and pleasant natural Oud/perfumes (Al-Misk wal-Tib)
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) and Anas (RA) testified to the Prophet's ﷺ unforgettable pleasant scent in Madinah, saying he never refused a gift of pure perfume.

questionEn: What is the traditional Sunnah grooming and cleanliness etiquette encouraged on Fridays before heading to Jumu'ah prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Taking a Friday bath (Ghusl), wearing clean neat clothes, trimming nails/using siwak, applying mild perfume (for men), arriving early on foot calmly, and listening attentively to the Khutbah
Chatting on phones during the Khutbah
Arriving just as the Imam finishes Salam
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught that whoever bathes on Friday, walks early, sits close without separating two people, and listens silently has sins between that Friday and the next forgiven!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid speaking—even telling a neighbor 'Be quiet!'—while the Imam is delivering the Friday Khutbah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Because speaking Arabic is banned on Fridays
Because the Imam cannot read notes
Because listening attentively to the Friday sermon is obligatory, and saying even 'Hush!' distracts oneself and loses the complete reward of Jumu'ah
explanationEn: If someone beside you talks during the khutbah in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, a silent gentle gesture without speaking preserves your full Jumu'ah reward.

questionEn: Which Surah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ frequently recite in full on Fridays during the Jumu'ah prayer—paired with Surah Al-Ghashiyah—or in Fajr on Fridays (Al-Sajdah and Al-Insan)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fil and Surah Al-Masad every Friday
Surah Al-A'la (87) & Surah Al-Ghashiyah (88) in Jumu'ah (or Al-Jumu'ah & Al-Munafiqun), and Surah Al-Sajdah (32) & Surah Al-Insan (76) in Friday Fajr
explanationEn: Hearing Surah Al-Sajdah and Surah Al-Insan echoed melodiously in Friday Fajr inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi connects today's worshippers directly with the Prophet's ﷺ own Friday dawn in Madinah.
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Friday Prayer

questionEn: Why do visitors at Fajr on Fridays inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi perform a sudden collective prostration (Sujud al-Tilawah) during the first rak'ah?
optionsEn: Because the Imam recites Surah Al-Sajdah (Chapter 32), which contains an obligatory/recommended verse of prostration (32:15), before rising to complete the rak'ah
Because Friday Fajr has three rak'ahs
explanationEn: Knowing this ahead of time helps first-time visitors follow the Imam smoothly during Friday Fajr without confusion!

questionEn: What remarkable architectural museum right beside the southern courtyard of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (near Gate 7 / Dar al-Madinah or Al-Masjid an-Nabawi Exhibition) helps visitors visualize Seerah history?
optionsEn: The International Fair and Museum of the Prophet's ﷺ Biography and Islamic Civilization (and Dar Al-Madinah Museum)
explanationEn: Using accurate scale models of Madinah's old neighborhoods, wells, and the Prophet's ﷺ chamber, these educational exhibitions deepen a pilgrim's appreciation of Seerah landmarks.

questionEn: What unique service inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi supports elderly, injured, or disabled pilgrims wishing to move smoothly across the vast courtyards?
optionsEn: Free wheelchair availability and motorized electric golf-cart shuttles operating along designated courtyard lanes
Elderly visitors must stay outside Madinah
explanationEn: Assisting elderly parents or fellow travelers gently across the Haram courtyards reflects the deepest spirit of Madinah hospitality.

questionEn: Why are translation booths and multilingual religious guidance counters placed around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's courtyards and gates?
optionsEn: To provide accurate Qur'anic translations, Fiqh answers, and Sunnah Ziyarah guidance in dozens of world languages free of charge
explanationEn: Pilgrims uncertain about a ruling or lost from their group can approach the official guidance desks inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi anytime.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What does the Prophet's ﷺ authentic Hadith about 'Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of his giving up food and drink' remind fasting visitors in Madinah?
optionsEn: That shouting is allowed while fasting
That spiritual purity—guarding the tongue from backbiting, anger, and rudeness—matters far more than outward rituals alone
That eating dates breaks fasting at night
That fasting is abolished in Madinah
explanationEn: In Madinah's sacred atmosphere, curbing impatience and speaking gently transforms every fast and every prayer.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi about the true measure of strength when men wrestled or boasted in strength?
optionsEn: 'The strong person is not the one who overcomes people in wrestling; rather, the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry!'
explanationEn: Amid busy crowds in Madinah's elevators, queues, and hotel lobbies, self-restraint in anger is true Prophetic strength.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: Which companion asked Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah for brief life-changing advice—and received the three-word reply repeated three times: 'Do not get angry (La taghdab)'?
optionsEn: An Ansari/companion (Abu Hurayrah narrated the man asking 'Advise me!')
explanationEn: Repeating 'La taghdab' three times showed that mastering anger protects faith, family peace, and community harmony in Madinah and everywhere.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when a young man walked into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and asked bluntly for permission to commit adultery (zina)?
optionsEn: He ordered him beaten outside the gate

While Companions shouted at him, the Prophet ﷺ gently called him close, asked calmly 'Would you like it for your mother? Your daughter? Your sister? Your aunt?'—awakening his empathy, then placed his hand on the youth's chest praying: 'O Allah, forgive his sin, purify his heart, and guard his chastity!'
explanationEn: Recorded in Musnad Ahmad (Sahih), the young man testified afterward that nothing had ever become more detestable to him than immorality—a masterpiece of Prophetic mercy in Madinah.

questionEn: Which brief four-part counsel did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach his young cousin Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) while riding behind him on a mount in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Guard Allah (His limits) and He will guard you; guard Allah and you will find Him before you; when you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah!'
explanationEn: Instilling pure Tawakkul and Tawhid into a young boy's heart in Madinah created one of the most beloved Hadith in Islamic education.

questionEn: What moving nightly routine did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ practice in Madinah right before sleeping on his modest mat?
optionsEn: Leaving lights blazing all night in noise
Sleeping atop gold cushions without Dhikr

Dusting the bed three times, lying on his right side with his hand under his right cheek, reciting Ayat al-Kursi, the last two verses of Al-Baqarah, and blowing gently into his cupped hands with the Three Quls (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, Al-Nas) to wipe over his body three times
explanationEn: Practicing this gentle bedtime Sunnah inside one's Madinah hotel room fills even rest with remembrance and protection.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: What happens to a Muslim's heart when leaving Al-Masjid an-Nabawi at night after Isha under the glowing minarets and open courtyard umbrellas?
optionsEn: Gratitude for walking the very ground trodden by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar, Aishah, and thousands of Companions, paired with renewed resolve to live their legacy
explanationEn: Madinah al-Munawwarah is not merely a destination on a map—it is a lifelong standard of love, mercy, scholarship, and devotion to Allah.

questionEn: Which renowned Companion of Madinah—known as 'Al-Bahr' (The Ocean of Knowledge)—answered complex Qur'anic and legal questions from visitors arriving from all corners of the Muslim world?
explanationEn: Even senior Companions like Umar (RA) regularly invited young Ibn Abbas (RA) into consultative councils in Madinah out of admiration for his Qur'anic insight.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of Companions

questionEn: Which scholar of Madinah—grandson of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)—was famous for living with utmost simplicity in coarse wool clothes while advising rulers truthfully?
explanationEn: When Caliph Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik visited Madinah and offered Salim (RA) anything he wished, Salim replied: 'I feel shy before Allah to ask anyone else while standing inside the House of Allah!'

questionEn: Which son of Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA)—Aban ibn Uthman—served as governor of Madinah and became one of the earliest Tabi'i scholars to teach Hadith and Seerah in Madinah?
explanationEn: Respected by scholars of Madinah for judicial fairness and early Maghazi narrations, Aban bridged the generation of the Companions and Tabi'in.

questionEn: Which renowned Madinah scholar—Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi—was a leading Tabi'i exegete of the Qur'an who regularly taught Tafsir inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: Born to a survivor of Banu Qurayzah who embraced Islam sincerely, Muhammad ibn Ka'b grew into one of Madinah's foremost authorities in Qur'anic exegesis.

questionEn: Which famous Tabi'i jurist of Madinah—Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib—refused to marry his brilliant daughter to the Umayyad crown prince, choosing instead a humble, devoted student of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Kathir ibn Abi Wada'ah (his faithful student who had just buried his own wife)
explanationEn: Walking his daughter personally to his poor student's modest home in Madinah with two dirhams' dowry, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib placed character and sacred knowledge above royal wealth—and his daughter proved deeply learned in Hadith and Fiqh.

questionEn: Which famous scholar of Madinah—Abu al-Zinad Abdullah ibn Dhakwan—compiled the legal rulings agreed upon by the Seven Jurists of Madinah?
explanationEn: Transmitting the verdicts of Madinah's Tabi'in masters accurately, Abu al-Zinad preserved the classical jurisprudence that Imam Malik later systematized.

questionEn: Which great scholar of Madinah—Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari—served as Qadi of Madinah and transmitted the opening Hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari ('Actions are judged by intentions') from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi?
explanationEn: Born and raised in Madinah, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari carried the unbroken chain of 'Innama al-a'malu bil-niyyat' from Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) on the Minbar of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Where did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) famously narrate the foundational Hadith 'Indeed, deeds are only by intentions (Innama al-a'malu bil-niyyat)'?
optionsEn: On a ship in the Red Sea
From atop the Minbar of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah
explanationEn: Delivered on the Prophet's ﷺ own Minbar in Madinah—and linking directly to migrating 'to Allah and His Messenger'—this Hadith opens Sahih al-Bukhari itself.

questionEn: What profound warning about sincerity in Hijrah did that very first Hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari give Madinah's residents?
optionsEn: 'Whoever's migration (Hijrah) was for Allah and His Messenger, his migration is for Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's migration was for worldly gain or a woman to marry, his migration is for what he migrated for!'
explanationEn: Every pilgrim visiting Madinah today draws fresh inspiration from Umar's (RA) Minbar sermon: purify your intention solely for Allah!

questionEn: Which Egyptian scholar—Abdullah ibn Wahb—and which Andalusian scholar—Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi—traveled vast distances to Madinah to study Al-Muwatta' directly under Imam Malik?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Wahb (from Egypt) and Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi (from Cordoba, Spain)
explanationEn: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi's recension became the most famous surviving edition of Imam Malik's Al-Muwatta', carrying Madinah's scholarship all the way to Spain and North Africa.

questionEn: What nickname did Imam Malik affectionately give his devoted Egyptian student Abdullah ibn Wahb when writing letters to him?
optionsEn: 'The Mufti of Egypt' and 'The Jurist of Egypt'
explanationEn: Through students like Ibn Wahb, Ibn al-Qasim, and Ashhab, Imam Malik's Madinah school spread effortlessly across Egypt and the Maghrib.

questionEn: Which great scholar of Madinah—Muhammad ibn Maslamah's or Zubayr's line? No, which descendant of Abu Bakr (RA)—Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir—was celebrated in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for weeping out of awe whenever narrating Hadith?
explanationEn: Known as one of Madinah's greatest ascetics and Hadith masters, Ibn al-Munkadir often spent nights praying gently and caring tenderly for his mother in Madinah.

questionEn: What touching exchange occurred in Madinah between the two ascetic brothers Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir and Umar ibn al-Munkadir?
optionsEn: While Umar stayed up all night in voluntary prayer, Muhammad spent the night massaging his elderly mother's aching feet—saying 'I would not trade my night with my mother for Umar's entire night of Tahajjud!'
They refused to help at home
They left Madinah without telling their mother
They argued over inheritance in court
explanationEn: This classic Madinan story teaches believers that serving aging parents with love stands among the highest acts of worship.

questionEn: Which famous scholar-traveler of the 14th century (1326 CE) visited Madinah and left detailed eyewitness descriptions of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's pillars, gates, Rawdah, and Qur'an reciters?
optionsEn: Ibn Battuta (and earlier Ibn Jubayr in 1184 CE)
explanationEn: Both Ibn Jubayr's and Ibn Battuta's travelogues vividly document Madinah's medieval architecture, scholar circles, and pilgrim hospitality.
reference: Rihlat Ibn Battuta & Rihlat Ibn Jubayr

questionEn: Which major early Hadith master compiled 'Sunan al-Tirmidhi' and traveled across the Hijaz—what is the famous status of Madinah in the 'Six Authentic Hadith Books' (Kutub al-Sittah)?
optionsEn: Only Baghdad scholars appear in Sahih Muslim
Madinah banned writing Hadith until 1000 CE
None of the Six Books include Hadith from Madinah
Hundreds of foundational chains in all Six Books—especially Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Malik's Muwatta', and Abu Dawud—originate directly in Madinah's unbroken circle of Companions and Tabi'in
explanationEn: From Aishah, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri to Al-Zuhri, Nafi', and Imam Malik, Madinah formed the golden trunk of Sunni Hadith preservation.

questionEn: What remarkable scene did Abu Hurayrah (RA) witness inside Madinah's marketplace that made him tell shoppers: 'You are sitting here while the inheritance of Muhammad ﷺ is being divided inside the Mosque!'?
optionsEn: Silk robes were being given away

Seeing people absorbed in market trading, he hurried them into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—where they saw only circles studying Qur'an, Hadith, and Fiqh, prompting Abu Hurayrah to remind them: 'That IS the inheritance of the Prophets!'
A chest of gold coins was being auctioned
explanationEn: This unforgettable story in Madinah reminds every Muslim that sacred knowledge—not silver or gold—is the true inheritance left behind by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questionEn: What famous Hadith narrated by Abu al-Darda (RA) echoes Abu Hurayrah's lesson about seeking knowledge inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: 'Scholars are the heirs of the Prophets; the Prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, rather they left behind knowledge—so whoever takes it has taken an abundant share!'
explanationEn: Recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, it remains the charter of Madinah's scholarly circles.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Knowledge

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 22, Al-Hajj, containing both Makkan and Madinan verses) opens Hajj's call to humanity and guarantees Allah's defense of mosques where His name is remembered?
explanationEn: Verses 22:39–40—revealed in Madinah as the earliest permission for oppressed believers to defend themselves—explicitly state permission was granted to safeguard monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which Allah's name is mentioned.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 59, Al-Hashr) concludes with the magnificent Names of Allah (59:22–24: Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, Al-Salam, Al-Mu'min...)?
explanationEn: Revealed in Madinah after the evacuation of Banu al-Nadir, Surah Al-Hashr moves from civic history straight to soaring contemplation of Allah's majesty and His Most Beautiful Names.

questionEn: Which Madinan verse in Surah Al-Hashr (59:18) is frequently recited in Friday sermons at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi urging self-accountability for tomorrow?
optionsEn: 'O you who believe, fear Allah—and let every soul look closely at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (the Hereafter)!'
explanationEn: Paired with 59:19 ('Do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget their own souls'), this Madinan reminder awakens pilgrims' hearts.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 60, Al-Mumtahanah) teaches believers fair, kind, and just conduct ('Al-Birr wal-Qist') toward peaceful non-Muslims who neither fought them nor expelled them from their homes?
explanationEn: Revealed in Madinah (when Asma bint Abi Bakr RA asked whether to treat her visiting non-Muslim mother kindly), Allah confirmed: 'Treat her kindly (sili ummaki)!'—enshrining kindness toward peaceful relatives of other faiths.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 61, Al-Saff) asks believers 'Why do you say what you do not do?' and compares those standing united for truth to 'a solidly joined structure (bunyanun marsus)'?
explanationEn: Revealed in Madinah around Uhud, Surah Al-Saff calls believers to integrity between speech and action and disciplined unity in ranks.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 64, Al-Taghabun) reminds families in Madinah that while spouses and children can sometimes test one's priorities, pardoning, overlooking, and forgiving ('ta'fu wa tasfahu wa taghfiru') invites Allah's own forgiveness?
explanationEn: Revealed when some new emigrants' families tried to hold them back from joining the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, Allah taught mercy and forgiveness rather than harsh estrangement.

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 65, Al-Talaq) lays down compassionate waiting-period housing and support laws during divorce—and gives the famous promise for whoever fears Allah: 'He will make for them a way out (makhraja) and provide from where they never expected'?
explanationEn: Addressing even the most painful family transitions in Madinah with dignity and patience, 65:2–3 anchors believers in absolute trust in Allah (Tawakkul).

questionEn: Which Madinan Surah (Chapter 98, Al-Bayyinah) summarizes the essence of pure faith: worshipping Allah sincerely, establishing prayer, and giving Zakah?
explanationEn: It is the very Surah Allah commanded Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to recite directly to Madinah's master reciter Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)!

questionEn: What moving story from Madinah involved Abu Lubabah, Ka'b ibn Malik, or Abu Qays ibn Sirmah al-Ansari (RA) when fasting rules were still strict in early 2 AH?
optionsEn: Working all day in his Madinah date orchard, Abu Qays fell asleep exhausted before breaking his fast—since sleeping initially forbade eating until next sunset, he fainted midday in hunger, leading Allah to reveal Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187 permitting eating and drinking throughout Ramadan nights until the white thread of dawn!
Fasting was moved to winter only
explanationEn: That compassionate concession revealed in Madinah lifted immense hardship off working families across the entire Muslim world forever.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse revealed in Madinah (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:186) sits right in the middle of the verses about Ramadan fasting—reassuring believers of Allah's nearness?
optionsEn: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me—indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the supplicant when he calls upon Me!'
'Only priests may pray on your behalf'
'Prayer is heard only once a year'
explanationEn: Notice how 2:186 uniquely omits 'Say (Qul)'—Allah answers directly without intermediary: 'I am near!'—making Ramadan and Madinah's nights peak seasons for intimate Dua.

questionEn: What beloved Sunnah of Suhoor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ practice and strongly urge in Madinah—calling it 'a blessed meal'?
optionsEn: Fasting continuously without breaking at Maghrib (wisal)
Eating a late pre-dawn Suhoor meal shortly before Fajr (even if just a sip of water or a few dates), noting: 'Take Suhoor, for in Suhoor there is blessing (barakah)!'
explanationEn: When some companions in Madinah tried fasting two days nonstop (wisal), the Prophet ﷺ gently forbade it out of mercy toward his Ummah.

questionEn: With what simple food did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ routinely break his fast at sunset inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi before praying Maghrib?
optionsEn: Fresh ripe dates (rutab); if unavailable, dry dates (tamr); and if unavailable, a few sips of water
Heavy three-course meat platters before Maghrib
Waiting until after Isha to eat
explanationEn: Breaking the fast gently with dates and water right at Maghrib allows worshippers in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to stand comfortably in Maghrib prayer on time.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ celebrate the arrival of Ramadan inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when addressing the Companions?
optionsEn: He closed Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for thirty days

He gave them glad tidings: 'Ramadan has come to you—a blessed month! Allah has made fasting it obligatory upon you; in it the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and rebellious devils are chained!'
He complained that fasting was too difficult
explanationEn: Hearing those glad tidings echo across Madinah today fills Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with electric spiritual joy on the first night of Ramadan.

questionEn: What special charity is paid in Madinah and worldwide right before Eid al-Fitr prayer, measured in Madinah's traditional units (one Sa' of dates, barley, raisins, or staple grain)?
explanationEn: Instituted in Madinah in 2 AH to purify the fasting person from idle speech and ensure poor neighbors rejoice on Eid morning without begging.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Zakat al-Fitr

questionEn: Which companion—the great jurist Abdullah ibn Umar (RA)—taught how strictly early Madinah observed the timing of Zakat al-Fitr?
optionsEn: Waiting until three months after Eid
Distributing it one or two days before Eid so it reached the poor before the Eid prayer at Al-Musalla
explanationEn: Practiced faithfully in Madinah, timely Zakat al-Fitr ensured every household shared in Eid joy.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Zakat al-Fitr

questionEn: What inspiring habit did Aishah (RA) report about Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ generosity throughout the year in Madinah—and especially when Ramadan arrived?
optionsEn: He was always the most generous of people, and in Ramadan when Jibril (AS) met him nightly to review the Qur'an, he became 'more generous in goodness than the blowing wind!'
He stopped giving charity during Ramadan
explanationEn: That Prophetic example still inspires Madinah's legendary Ramadan hospitality across every courtyard of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Where in Madinah did Angel Jibril (AS) meet Prophet Muhammad ﷺ every night during Ramadan to review the entire revealed Qur'an?
optionsEn: Inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and the Prophet's ﷺ chamber, Jibril (AS) met Prophet Muhammad ﷺ every single night of Ramadan to review the entire revealed Qur'an together
Inside a Roman library in Syria
explanationEn: Reviewing it once every Ramadan—and twice in the final Ramadan of 10 AH—ensured absolute precision in Madinah's Qur'anic preservation.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

questionEn: What is the traditional practice of 'Khatm al-Qur'an' inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi during the 29th night of Ramadan?
optionsEn: Completing the entire recitation of the Noble Qur'an during Tarawih/Qiyam followed by a deeply moving collective Dua al-Khatm by the Imam
Closing the mosque early on the 29th night
explanationEn: Hundreds of thousands stand weeping softly in the courtyards and halls of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi on Khatm night, praying for mercy and guidance.

questionEn: Which dua did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach Aishah (RA) in Madinah specifically for Laylat al-Qadr during the last ten nights of Ramadan?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma innaka Afuwwun tuhibbul-afwa fa'fu anni' (O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me!)
explanationEn: Concise, humble, and infinitely rich, this Madinah-taught dua remains on every worshipper's lips during the last ten nights in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visibly transform his worship routine inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi whenever the last ten nights of Ramadan began?
optionsEn: He tightened his waist-wrapper (shadda mi'zarahu), stayed awake in worship through the night, and gently woke his family to join in prayer
He slept from Maghrib to Fajr
explanationEn: Narrated by Aishah (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, his whole household came alive with prayer during those blessed nights.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Laylat al-Qadr

questionEn: What touching gesture did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show toward his daughter Fatimah (RA) and Ali (RA) at night in Madinah when knocking gently on their door beside the mosque?
optionsEn: He locked their door from outside
'Will you two not get up and pray?'—waking them tenderly for Tahajjud
He forbade Ali from praying at night
explanationEn: Encouraging family members with love toward night prayer filled the neighborhood around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with quiet devotion.

questionEn: What balanced counsel did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when he saw a rope tied between two pillars and asked whose it was?
optionsEn: He tied three more ropes for everyone
Learning it belonged to Zaynab (RA) to hold herself up when exhausted in night prayer, he untied it immediately saying: 'Let one pray while energetic; when tired, let him sit or sleep!'
He banned sitting during voluntary prayer
explanationEn: This Sahih al-Bukhari Hadith inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi teaches sustainable, joyful devotion rather than self-punishing exhaustion.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gently correct Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA) in Madinah when Abdullah vowed to fast every day and finish the entire Qur'an every single night?
optionsEn: Warning 'Your eye has a right over you, your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you,' he guided him toward balanced fasting (at most every other day, like Dawud AS) and finishing the Qur'an calmly across a week or month
He ordered Abdullah to never sleep again
explanationEn: Even when pilgrims feel overwhelmed with zeal in Madinah, Prophetic wisdom reminds them: consistent, heartfelt deeds outlast burnout.

questionEn: What beloved phrase in Sahih al-Bukhari summarizes Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ teaching in Madinah on steady, lifelong spiritual habits?
optionsEn: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent, even if they are small'
'Stop all worship once you return home from Madinah'
explanationEn: Bringing home one small, steady daily Sunnah from Madinah—like two rak'ahs of Duha, morning adhkar, or one page of Qur'an—keeps Madinah's light burning all year.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise when seeing a Companion praying hastily ('pecking like a crow') inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi without pausing calmly in bowing and prostration?
optionsEn: He ordered him never to pray in public
He told him to skip Ruku'

Saying 'Go back and pray, for you have not prayed!' three times until the man begged to be taught, the Prophet ﷺ taught the essential pillar of Tuma'ninah (tranquil stillness in every posture of Salah)
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari as the Hadith of 'Al-Musi' Salatahu,' it teaches every visitor to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi to slow down and savor stillness before Allah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi about straightening prayer rows (taswiyat al-sufuf) shoulder-to-shoulder and foot-to-foot?
optionsEn: 'Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of the perfection/establishment of prayer—lest Allah cause your hearts to differ!'
'Only front rows need to be straight'
'Leave wide gaps so strangers never stand close'
explanationEn: Standing shoulder-to-shoulder across every nationality inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi visually embodies unity of hearts.

questionEn: Which virtue of the 'first row' (al-saff al-awwal) inside mosques like Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ highlight—while warning against pushing or hurting others to reach it?
optionsEn: 'Women must crowd into men's front rows'
'Only wealthy patrons may stand in front'

'If people knew what (reward) lies in the Adhan and the first row, and found no way except drawing lots, they would draw lots for it!'—while etiquette requires arriving early rather than stepping over seated people
'Push people aside when arriving late to seize the first row'
explanationEn: Arriving early calmly with dignity—never stepping over shoulders on Friday—honors both the virtue of early rows and the dignity of fellow Muslims.

questionEn: Which companion—the great Hadith master Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA)—narrated the famous Madinah Hadith about 'Whomever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if unable, with his tongue; if unable, with his heart—and that is the weakest of faith'?
explanationEn: Narrated in Sahih Muslim after Marwan ibn al-Hakam changed Eid prayer order in Madinah before Abu Sa'id gently corrected him publicly, it remains a pillar of Islamic civic responsibility.

questionEn: What kind, constructive manner did Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) show when correcting Governor Marwan in Madinah on Eid day?
optionsEn: Speaking firmly yet respectfully to uphold the Prophetic Sunnah (praying Eid first, then delivering the khutbah) without sparking violence
explanationEn: Standing up respectfully for the Sunnah inside Madinah exemplified balanced scholarly courage.

questionEn: Which famous prayer for entering Madinah or asking for beneficial knowledge did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recite daily after Fajr in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa amalan mutaqabbalan' (O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, pure wholesome provision, and accepted deeds!)
explanationEn: Narrated by Umm Salamah (RA) in Sunan Ibn Majah (Sahih), reciting this concise morning dua after Fajr inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi aligns work, study, and worship beautifully.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of Establishing Prayer (Sahih)

questionEn: What touching dua did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) in Madinah when Abu Bakr asked for a supplication to recite inside his own prayer?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wa la yaghfirul-dhunuba illa Anta, faghfir li maghfiratan min indika warhamni, innaka Antal-Ghafurur-Rahim'
explanationEn: Even the greatest Companion after the Prophets—Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)—was taught to humble himself before Allah asking forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: Which frequent dua did Anas ibn Malik (RA) testify was the supplication Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recited most often in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Give us only this world and ignore the Hereafter'
'Rabbana atina fil-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina adhabal-nar' (Our Lord, grant us good in this world, good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire)
explanationEn: Walking across Al-Masjid an-Nabawi's courtyards repeating this comprehensive Qur'anic dua (2:201) follows the Prophet's ﷺ own most cherished prayer.

questionEn: Which heartfelt dua did Umm Salamah (RA) report Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recited most frequently inside her chamber in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Ya Muqallib al-qulub, thabbit qalbi ala dinik' (O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion!)
explanationEn: Hearing even the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beg Allah to keep his heart steadfast inspires humble vigilance in every visitor to Madinah.

questionEn: What moving scene occurred in Madinah when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visited the sick, attended funerals, and helped widows—summarized by Anas (RA) as 'He was never asked for anything for Islam except that he gave it'?
optionsEn: He hoarded herds solely for himself

A visiting man once received an entire valley-full of sheep between two mountains from the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah/Ji'ranah, returning to his tribe crying: 'O my people, embrace Islam, for Muhammad gives like one who has no fear of poverty!'
explanationEn: Generosity rooted in absolute trust in Allah won whole tribes to Islam without a single sword drawn.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say in Madinah when asked which deeds in Islam are best—highlighting peace and kindness alongside worship?
optionsEn: 'Feeding the hungry and greeting with Salam both those whom you know and those whom you do not know'—and in another Hadith, 'That people are safe from your tongue and your hand'
explanationEn: Combining inner devotion in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi with outward kindness to every pilgrim captures the true spirit of Islam in Madinah.

questionEn: What simple gesture did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare counts as charity (Sadaqah) even for someone in Madinah who has zero money to give?
optionsEn: 'Smiling in the face of your brother is charity, guiding a lost traveler is charity, removing a stone/thorn from the road is charity, and a kind word is charity!'
explanationEn: Every pilgrim in Madinah—even with empty pockets—can give abundant charity every hour simply through warmth, patience, and helpfulness.

questionEn: Which companion—one of the 'Seven Most Prolific Hadith Narrators' (Al-Mukthirun)—all lived in or received their core knowledge in Madinah?
optionsEn: Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Umar, Anas ibn Malik, Aishah bint Abi Bakr, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Jabir ibn Abdullah, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA)
explanationEn: All seven towering pillars of Prophetic Hadith preservation lived and learned directly beside the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah!

questionEn: Approximately how many Hadith did Abu Hurayrah (RA), Ibn Umar (RA), Anas (RA), and Aishah (RA) together preserve from Madinah's prophetic years?
optionsEn: Over 12,000 narrations combined (accounting for the majority of the Sunnah's core foundation)
explanationEn: Their tireless memory and faithfulness inside Madinah ensured Muslims everywhere still hear the Prophet's ﷺ voice clearly fourteen centuries later.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Allah in a heartfelt Madinah dua recorded in Sahih Muslim when longing for future believers who would love him centuries later?
optionsEn: 'No one after 100 AH can love me'
'I wish I could see our brothers!'—explaining to his Companions: 'You are my Companions; our brothers are those who will come after me and believe in me without ever having seen me!'
'Only people born in 1 AH are my brothers'
explanationEn: Whenever a modern pilgrim stands quietly inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi sending Salam upon the Prophet ﷺ, they fulfill his own longing for his beloved future brothers and sisters!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say one's love for him in Madinah or anywhere must practically look like—rather than empty slogans?
optionsEn: 'Love is proven solely by loud shouting'

'Whoever revives my Sunnah has truly loved me, and whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise' (and Sahih Bukhari: 'None of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child, and all mankind')
'Love means inventing new rituals never taught'
explanationEn: True love for the Messenger ﷺ shines through honoring his character, following his Sunnah, and obeying Allah sincerely.

questionEn: What promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give a simple Bedouin who came to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi asking anxiously: 'When is the Hour?'—and admitted he hadn't amassed huge extra prayers, only love for Allah and His Messenger?
optionsEn: 'A person will be with those whom he loves (Al-mar'u ma'a man ahabb)!'
'Go away until you memorize ten books'
'Love brings no closeness in the Hereafter'
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) testified: 'Nothing ever made the Muslims rejoice after Islam as deeply as those words: A person will be with those whom he loves!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: How does visiting Madinah help couples and families strengthen love and mercy inside their own homes?
optionsEn: By recalling the Prophet's ﷺ own tenderness in his Madinah apartments—where he raced with Aishah (RA), helped with chores, listened kindly, and declared: 'The best of you are the best to their families!'
By insisting husbands never help at home
By encouraging cold silence toward spouses
explanationEn: Bringing Madinah's domestic gentleness back home transforms marriages and families worldwide.

questionEn: Which historic well or garden in Madinah is remembered when reciting Surah Al-Kawthar or remembering the Prophet's ﷺ Hawd (Cistern) on the Day of Judgment?
optionsEn: The Prophet's ﷺ Hadith linking his Minbar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi directly to his Hawd ('My Minbar is upon my Hawd')—from which faithful followers of his Sunnah will drink water whiter than milk and sweeter than honey
explanationEn: Praying in Al-Rawdah beside his Minbar fills the believer's heart with hope to drink from his blessed hand at Al-Hawd on the Day of Resurrection.

questionEn: Approximately how many years did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reside in Madinah from his arrival in Rabi al-Awwal 1 AH until his passing in Rabi al-Awwal 11 AH?
optionsEn: Approximately ten lunar years (about 10 years, completing 23 years of total Prophethood following 13 years in Makkah)
explanationEn: In just one decade in Madinah, Allah transformed a divided oasis town into the spiritual axis of human history.

questionEn: What happened to the age of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when Allah took his noble soul in Aishah's (RA) chamber in Madinah?
optionsEn: Sixty-three lunar years old (matching the ages of Abu Bakr and Umar RA when each later passed away!)
explanationEn: Remarkably, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA), and Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) all passed away at age 63 and now rest side-by-side beneath the Green Dome.

questionEn: Why does the Adhan never cease echoing in Madinah or across the globe every second of every day?
optionsEn: Because Madinah uses loudspeakers only on Fridays

Because Allah fulfilled His promise in Surah Al-Inshirah (94:4): 'And We raised high for you your mention!'—uniting Allah's Tawhid with 'Muhammadur-Rasulullah' from Madinah's minarets across every time zone
Because no other city calls the Adhan
Because bells ring instead of voices
explanationEn: Standing in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi as the Adhan rises softly over Madinah lets every Muslim feel part of that unbroken global testimony.

questionEn: Which historical event in 1805–1818 CE or 1916–1925 CE shaped modern governance of Madinah, leading eventually to the massive modern custodian expansions of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: From early modern defense and restoration through the unification of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the 1920s–1930s, launching the largest architectural expansions in Madinah's history
explanationEn: Starting with King Abdulaziz's 1951 expansion project and continuing through King Fahd and modern custodianship, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi expanded more than hundredfold over its original footprint.

questionEn: Approximately how many square meters did Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ original 1 AH Al-Masjid an-Nabawi measure compared to the expanded complex today?
optionsEn: Roughly 1,050 square meters originally (about 30 x 35 meters), expanding today to hundreds of thousands of square meters across indoor halls, roofs, and shaded piazzas
10 square meters originally vs 100 square meters today
Exactly the same size since 1 AH
explanationEn: Standing inside the Ottoman/Rawdah section lets visitors visualize the modest scale of the Prophet's ﷺ original mosque nestled inside today's vast sanctuary.

questionEn: What is the best attitude for a Muslim to carry when returning to daily work, family, and community after completing their Ziyarah in Madinah?
optionsEn: Treating Ziyarah as a one-time badge of pride
Gentleness, truthfulness, steady prayer, love for knowledge, compassion for the weak, and continual Salawat upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
Harshness toward people who haven't traveled yet
explanationEn: The greatest proof of an accepted, blessed visit to Madinah is returning home a humbler, kinder, and more faithful follower of Allah's Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: Which closing verse from Surah Al-Saffat (37:180–182) beautifully seals any reflection, study circle, or journey in Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Subhana Rabbika Rabbil-izzati amma yasifun, wa salamun alal-mursalin, wal-hamdulillahi Rabbil-alamin'
explanationEn: Glorifying Allah above all imperfection, sending peace upon all Messengers, and praising the Lord of all worlds sums up Madinah's eternal message.

questionEn: Which companion—the great warrior and Ansari leader Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA)—had a special flag/banner in Madinah and later moved to Hawran in Syria during Umar's caliphate?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA), chief of Al-Khazraj
explanationEn: Remembered in Madinah for unmatched hospitality toward Ahl al-Suffah and digging a public well for his deceased mother, Sa'd (RA) left an enduring charitable legacy in Madinah.

questionEn: Which famous companion in Madinah—Abu Qatadah al-Ansari (RA)—was praised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as 'the best of our horsemen' (khayru fursanina)?
explanationEn: Hero of Dhu Qarad outside Madinah alongside Salamah ibn al-Akwa' (RA), Abu Qatadah also narrated key everyday Hadith on prayer etiquette (such as praying Tahiyyat al-Masjid before sitting).
reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Jihad & Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What remarkable scene did Abu Qatadah (RA) narrate in Sahih Muslim about Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ gentle tenderness toward animals inside a Madinah home?
optionsEn: He threw away the vessel permanently

When a domestic cat approached a basin of ablution water, the Prophet ﷺ tilted the vessel kindly so the cat could drink, explaining: 'Cats are not impure; they are among those who constantly go around among you!'
He chased the cat out with stones
explanationEn: Even small creatures inside Madinah homes experienced the Prophet's ﷺ gentleness and practical Fiqh mercy.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim al-Ansari (RA), son of Umm Umarah—narrated the most detailed step-by-step description of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ Wudu?
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, his eyewitness demonstration in Madinah taught generations of Muslims how to perform Wudu calmly and thoroughly.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—Humran ibn Aban—witnessed Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) demonstrate Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ exact Wudu beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, followed by the promise of forgiveness?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA), narrating that whoever performs Wudu cleanly like this and prays two rak'ahs without letting worldly thoughts distract them has all past minor sins forgiven!
explanationEn: Standing in Madinah's courtyard after performing unhurried Wudu and praying two focused rak'ahs connects a pilgrim straight to Uthman's (RA) beloved Hadith.

questionEn: Which companion—the great Ansari poet Ka'b ibn Zuhayr—rode into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 9 AH after years of past hostility, sought pardon, and recited his famous poem 'Banat Su'ad' before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr (RA), upon whom the Prophet ﷺ gifted his own striped Yemeni cloak (Al-Burdah)!
explanationEn: That famous moment inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi gave birth to the celebrated tradition of 'Qasidat al-Burdah' (Poem of the Cloak) praising the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questionEn: What moving tribute to the Prophet's ﷺ Companions in Madinah appears in Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's famous poem 'Banat Su'ad' recited in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Initially praising only the Muhajirun, when the Ansar looked subtly at him, Ka'b added verses honoring the Ansar's unmatched courage and protection of Madinah!
explanationEn: Praising both the Muhajirun and the Ansar together won unanimous admiration inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: Which famous 13th-century poet later composed the renowned poem 'Al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah' (widely known as Qasidat al-Burdah) praising Prophet Muhammad ﷺ out of love and spiritual healing?
explanationEn: Inspired by Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's historic cloak gift in Madinah, Al-Busiri's poem became one of the most cherished expressions of prophetic devotion across Islamic lands (evaluated always alongside pure Tawhid).

questionEn: Which companion—one of the young Medinan scribes and scholars, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA)—received explicit permission from Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah to write down everything he heard from him?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA), author of 'Al-Sahifah al-Sadiqah'
explanationEn: When some companions wondered if writing everything while the Prophet ﷺ spoke in anger or joy was safe, the Prophet ﷺ pointed to his lips: 'Write! By Him in Whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of here except truth!'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Knowledge (Sahih)

questionEn: Which famous Ansari companion—Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' (RA) or Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA)—lived to see Madinah's children grow into teachers and narrated the thrilling story of building the Trench and the Prophet's ﷺ white face shining like the moon?
explanationEn: Too young to fight at Badr, Al-Bara' (RA) participated from Uhud/Khandaq onward and described the Prophet ﷺ hauling dirt at Khandaq with dust covering his abdomen while reciting poetry with the Ansar.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

questionEn: What moving description did Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) give of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ appearance in Madinah when wearing a red-striped Yemeni cloak (hullah hamra')?
optionsEn: 'He wore heavy gold crowns and silk'
'I have never seen anyone more handsome than him—his hair reached his earlobes, and he was the bravest and most generous of all people!'
