explanationEn: Every vivid physical and moral detail preserved by Madinah's youth helps believers love the Prophet ﷺ as if seeing him before them.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare in Madinah regarding the virtue of guiding even one person to goodness or Islam?
optionsEn: 'By Allah, that Allah guides even a single person through you is better for you than possessing fine red camels!' (and 'Whoever guides to good has a reward equal to the one who does it')
explanationEn: Delivered as Ali (RA) carried the banner—and echoed across Madinah's da'wah—this principle motivates pilgrims to share authentic Islamic guidance gently with others.

questionEn: Which timeless verse of the Qur'an—revealed in Madinah in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2)—serves as the golden rule for every volunteer, steward, and pilgrim inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: 'And cooperate in righteousness and piety (birr wa taqwa), and do not cooperate in sin and aggression!'
explanationEn: Helping a lost elderly pilgrim, sharing water, holding doors gently, and keeping the mosque spotless bring 5:2 to life every minute in Madinah.

questionEn: Which heartfelt closing reflection connects the city of Makkah and the city of Madinah in every Muslim's spiritual journey?
optionsEn: Makkah is the Qiblah of our bodies—where our prayers face Allah's House—and Madinah is the school of our hearts—where we learn how to walk with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ back to Allah
Only one of the two cities matters in Islam
Makkah and Madinah have no spiritual bond
explanationEn: Together, Al-Haramayn al-Sharifayn anchor the believer in pure worship of Allah and faithful following of His beloved Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: What final personal commitment does Duya's Madinah Knowledge Door invite every pilgrim to carry forward after completing these 1,000 reflections?
optionsEn: Forgetting Madinah's lessons upon boarding the return flight

Turning historical knowledge of Madinah into living practice: daily Salah with tranquility, sincere Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ, love for the Qur'an, generosity toward neighbors, and reverence for Allah's sanctuaries
explanationEn: May Allah accept every step taken in Madinah al-Munawwarah, forgive our shortcomings, and gather us with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his noble Companions in Al-Firdaws al-A'la!

questionEn: Which famous companion in Madinah—Abu Lubabah or Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA)? Specifically, which Ansari companion taught the Prophet's ﷺ exact method of sending Salawat ('Allahumma salli ala Muhammad...') inside Madinah?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) (alongside Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari RA), who asked 'O Messenger of Allah, we know how to give you Salam—how should we send Salawat upon you?'
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) lived and died in Madinah/Kufah transmitting Salawat al-Ibrahimiyyah straight from the Prophet's ﷺ lips.

questionEn: Which famous Medinan companion—Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari (RA)—was sitting with Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) in Sa'd's assembly in Madinah when he asked the Prophet ﷺ how to send Salawat upon him?
optionsEn: Abu Mas'ud Uqbah ibn Amr al-Ansari (RA)
explanationEn: Recorded in Sahih Muslim, that assembly in Sa'd ibn Ubadah's (RA) Madinah courtyard gifted the Ummah the complete Salawat formula still recited in every Salah.

questionEn: What remarkable scene of humility did Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari (RA) experience in Madinah when he was beating an enslaved servant and heard a firm voice behind him: 'Know, O Abu Mas'ud, that Allah has more power over you than you have over him!'?
optionsEn: Turning around to see Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Mas'ud immediately dropped the whip and declared: 'He is free for the sake of Allah!'—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to say: 'Had you not done so, the Fire would have touched you!'
He sold the servant to Syria
He argued with the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: That unforgettable Medinan lesson transformed household dignity and accountability before Allah.

questionEn: Which companion of Madinah—known as 'Al-Bara' ibn Malik' (RA), brother of Anas ibn Malik—had a remarkable gift of answered prayer praised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah?
optionsEn: Al-Bara' ibn Malik (RA), of whom the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Many a disheveled, dusty person turned away from doors—if he swears by Allah (making dua), Allah surely fulfills it! One of them is Al-Bara' ibn Malik!'
explanationEn: Simple, fearless, and pure-hearted, Al-Bara' (RA) fulfilled that promise even during the fiercest battles of early Islam.

questionEn: Which famous companion in Madinah—Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani (RA)—narrated the Hadith of 'Rain at Hudaybiyyah' and the key Madinah Hadith on honest lost-property announcements (Luqatah)?
explanationEn: Teaching strict honesty in Madinah, Zayd ibn Khalid (RA) preserved the Prophet's ﷺ rule to announce any found item publicly for a full year before touching it, and never to touch stray camels.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Lost Property

questionEn: Which noble Ansari companion—Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (RA)—was one of the very last Companions to pass away in Madinah (around 88–91 AH at nearly 100 years old), carrying living eyewitness memories of the Prophet ﷺ into the Umayyad era?
explanationEn: Passing away in Madinah after witnessing the building of the Prophet's ﷺ Minbar, Sahl (RA) connected third-generation Tabi'in directly to the first days of Madinah.

questionEn: Which two historic wells or valleys near Madinah are mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari as places where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ halted along the route between Makkah and Madinah, marked today by heritage awareness?
optionsEn: Wadi al-Aqiq and Dhul-Hulayfah (along with Al-Rawha, Al-Abwa, and Quba)
explanationEn: Every valley and well along the Makkah–Madinah corridor carries echoes of the Hijrah and the Farewell Pilgrimage.

questionEn: What gentle etiquette did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach in Madinah regarding yawning, sneezing, and speaking kindly inside gatherings at Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Cover the mouth calmly when yawning without loud noise, praise Allah ('Alhamdulillah') when sneezing so listeners reply 'YarhamukAllah,' and speak softly with clear, unhurried words
explanationEn: Even small daily manners practiced in Madinah's mosque circles polished believers into models of grace.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

questionEn: Why did Aishah (RA) describe Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ speech in Madinah by saying 'He did not rattle words rapidly like you do—his words were so clear and measured that anyone who wished to count them could count them'?
optionsEn: Because he shouted as fast as possible
Because he spoke with unhurried clarity, repeating profound points three times when needed so every listener in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi understood completely
Because he spoke only in whispers
Because he refused to answer questions
explanationEn: Clarity, patience, and repeating important truths gently define authentic Islamic teaching from Madinah onward.

questionEn: Which beloved Madinan companion—Abu Dujanah or Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA)—narrated the famous Hadith on sincere desire for martyrdom: 'Whoever sincerely asks Allah for martyrdom will reach the ranks of the martyrs even if he dies upon his bed!'?
optionsEn: Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) (hero of Badr and Uhud, and resident of Quba/Madinah)
explanationEn: Narrated by Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) in Sahih Muslim, this comforting Hadith honors sincere intention in every age.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise in Madinah to any believer who wakes up each morning saying 'Radiytu billahi Rabban, wa bil-Islami dinan, wa bi-Muhammadin nabiyyan'?
optionsEn: 'I guarantee—taking him by his hand—to lead him into Paradise!' (and in Sunan Abi Dawud/Muslim, Paradise becomes guaranteed for him)
'He receives a gold coin at noon'
explanationEn: Recited morning and evening by pilgrims in Madinah, this short pledge of contentment in Allah, Islam, and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ fills the heart with serenity.

questionEn: Which famous Madinah scholar—Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak—visited Madinah, studied Imam Malik's Al-Muwatta', and wrote movingly about preferring spiritual sincerity in the Two Sanctuaries?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak (the great scholar-warrior-merchant of Khorasan who regularly visited Makkah and Madinah)
explanationEn: Even while funding impoverished scholars in Madinah anonymously, Ibn al-Mubarak wept over Madinah's scholarly humility and Imam Malik's devotion.

questionEn: What timeless prayer of Ibrahim (AS) and Muhammad ﷺ captures the ultimate spiritual purpose of visiting both Makkah and Madinah?
optionsEn: Asking Allah to accept our humble deeds ('Rabbana taqabbal minna, innaka Antas-Sami'ul-Alim'), keep our hearts firm upon Islam, and unite us in peace beneath the banner of truth
Seeking fame among neighbors back home
Treating pilgrimage as a contest of luxury
explanationEn: May every question in this Madinah Knowledge Door spark lifelong love for Allah's Messenger ﷺ, his noble Companions, and the luminous city of Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah.
